root.title: Practical MIP Solver Mechanisms
root.top_down_role: Operational mechanisms that transform, process, diagnose, extend, and validate practical mixed-integer optimization solves; formulation theory, cutting-plane theory, branching theory, and decomposition theory remain in their owning chapters.

children.title: Solver Execution-State Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Problem representations, solve stages, retained artifacts, and execution controls shared by practical solver subsystems.

children.title: Problem State Layers
children.top_down_role: Representations maintained across transformation, presolving, search, and postsolve.

children.title: Original-Transformed State Correspondence
children.top_down_role: User-facing and solver-facing problem representations.

children.title: Original Problem State
children.top_down_role: User-facing model objects, identifiers, data, and retained submission artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Original Problem State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-facing definition of the user model before transformations or presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the submitted mixed-integer optimization problem be represented by \(O=(X,F,f,I)\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the variable domain, \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is the feasible set, \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the minimization objective, and \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) indexes variables constrained to be integral. The original problem state is \(S_O=(O,D_O)\), where \(D_O\) contains names, bounds, coefficients, constraint senses, objective data, and user annotations expressed in the submitted coordinates, before solver-introduced substitutions, auxiliary variables, or presolve reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The original state is the submitted MIP and its user-coordinate metadata before solver transformations, auxiliary variables, substitutions, or presolve reductions.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\) is not required; the state also represents infeasible submissions.
The optimization convention is minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_O\) is the authoritative state in the submitted variable and constraint coordinates.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Standard abstract representation of a submitted MIP state.
Solver-specific original-state semantics require an authoritative implementation reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no citation supports the claimed authoritative contents and lifecycle semantics of an original solver state.

children.title: Transformed Problem State
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing objects created through normalization, reformulation, or reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformed Problem State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Internal solver state after representation-changing transformations and before or during presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an original state \(S_O\), a transformed problem state is \(S_T=(T,D_T,\Gamma)\), where \(T=(Y,G,h,J)\) is the solver's internal mixed-integer model, \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\), \(G\subseteq Y\) is its feasible set, \(h\) is its objective, and \(J\) indexes internal integral variables. The transformation record \(\Gamma\) stores the substitutions, auxiliary-variable definitions, constraint replacements, scaling data, and status information required to relate \(T\) to \(S_O\). The dimensions and model objects may differ: generally \(p\neq n\), and transformed constraints need not correspond one-to-one with submitted constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transformed state is the solver's internal model plus metadata recording substitutions, auxiliaries, reformulations, scaling, and links to the submitted model.
assumptions_latex: A submitted state \(S_O\) has been accepted by the solver.
Each recorded transformation has specified forward or recovery semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_T\) is expressed in internal coordinates and is interpreted relative to \(S_O\) through \(\Gamma\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Internal reformulation states conventionally include a transformed model and transformation metadata.
Exact transformed-state contents and lifecycle are solver-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope fit, but the components of the transformed state and the asserted recovery obligations are solver-dependent and have no cited source.

children.title: State Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Mappings between submitted objects and their transformed counterparts.

knowledge_statements.title: State Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility- and objective-preserving relation between submitted and internal problem states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_O\) and \(F_T\) be the feasible sets of the original and transformed problems. A state correspondence is a relation \(C\subseteq F_O\times F_T\) and objective conversion \(\alpha:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) such that \(C\) is total in both directions, \(\forall x\in F_O\ \exists y\in F_T:(x,y)\in C\) and \(\forall y\in F_T\ \exists x\in F_O:(x,y)\in C\), and \(h(y)=\alpha(f(x))\) whenever \((x,y)\in C\). If \(\alpha\) is strictly increasing, corresponding feasible points preserve objective order; consequently, the projections of optimal pairs in \(C\) are optimal for their respective problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correspondence relates feasible original and transformed points in both directions while preserving objective values up to a strictly increasing conversion.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\) is strictly increasing for optimality preservation.
Integrality requirements are included in \(F_O\) and \(F_T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is optimal in \(F_O\) if and only if any corresponding objective-matched \(y\) is optimal in \(F_T\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Equivalence of reformulations is expressed by feasibility and objective preservation.
A source specific to solver transformation correspondence is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically plausible and its optimality claim follows under the stated bidirectional totality and strictly increasing objective conversion, but no source establishes this as the intended solver-state correspondence.

children.title: Global-Local State Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Globally persistent and search-node-local information.

children.title: Global Problem State
children.top_down_role: Information valid throughout the active search tree or retained solve state.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Problem State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound state valid throughout the active search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a branch-and-bound search with active-node set \(\mathcal{N}\), the global problem state is \(G=(M_G,B_G,C_G,P_G,U_G,\mathcal{N})\). Here \(M_G\) is the common transformed model, \(B_G\) are globally valid bound changes, \(C_G\) are globally valid constraints, \(P_G\) is globally shared inference or presolve data, and \(U_G\) is the incumbent objective bound and associated solution information. Global validity means that every feasible solution represented by any node \(v\in\mathcal{N}\) satisfies every restriction in \(B_G\cup C_G\); updating \(G\) may therefore affect all active and subsequently created nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global state contains the common transformed model, globally valid bounds and constraints, shared inference data, incumbents, and the active search tree.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{N}\) is the current set of active search nodes.
All global deductions are valid for every node subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every active node inherits \(M_G\), \(B_G\), \(C_G\), \(P_G\), and the incumbent bound \(U_G\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Branch-and-bound solvers distinguish globally valid data from node-local data.
State components and update semantics vary among solver implementations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the global-state leaf, but the selected state tuple, inheritance claim, and meaning of globally shared inference data require authoritative branch-and-bound solver documentation.

children.title: Local Problem State
children.top_down_role: Information restricted to a search node or its descendant subtree.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Problem State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-specific search state layered over inherited global information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search node \(v\), its local problem state is \(L_v=(v,\pi(v),B_v,C_v,P_v,R_v)\), where \(\pi(v)\) is its parent, \(B_v\) are bound changes valid only in the subtree rooted at \(v\), \(C_v\) are locally valid constraints, \(P_v\) is node-local inference or propagation data, and \(R_v\) is the node relaxation state. The effective node problem is obtained by combining the global model and restrictions with all local restrictions on the root-to-\(v\) path. Local data may be discarded when its subtree is closed unless it is separately proved globally valid and promoted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local state stores node-specific bounds, constraints, inference data, and relaxation information layered over global data and inherited along its subtree.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is a node of the current rooted search tree.
Local restrictions are valid throughout the subtree rooted at \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible region at \(v\) equals the global feasible region intersected with inherited root-to-\(v\) local restrictions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Tree-search nodes carry path-specific domains and relaxation state.
Exact inheritance and disposal rules require solver-specific documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the local-state leaf and distinguishes path-local restrictions correctly, but its exact inheritance, storage, and disposal semantics are unsupported by a cited solver reference.

children.title: State Promotion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing whether locally discovered information can become globally persistent.

knowledge_statements.title: State Promotion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for moving node-local deductions into globally shared state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\) be a bound change, constraint, or inference derived while processing node \(v\), and let \(F_G\) be the feasible set defined by the current global state. Promotion of \(q\) from \(L_v\) to the global state is valid exactly when \(F_G\subseteq V(q)\), where \(V(q)\) is the set of points satisfying \(q\). A derivation that uses any unpromoted path restriction must establish this inclusion independently; validity only on the subtree feasible set \(F_v\) is insufficient. If \(F_v\subseteq V(q)\) but \(F_G\nsubseteq V(q)\), then \(q\) must remain local to \(v\) and its descendants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local deduction may become global only if every globally feasible solution satisfies it; validity merely within the current subtree is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\subseteq F_G\) is the feasible set at node \(v\).
\(V(q)\) denotes the validity region of deduction \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Promotion is sound if and only if \(F_G\subseteq V(q)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Global promotion requires validity over the global feasible region.
Implementation-specific promotion boundaries and admissible certificates require sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition expresses the standard semantic test for global validity, but the exact if-and-only-if promotion boundary and treatment of inference objects need a source tied to practical solver state management.

children.title: Presolve-Postsolve Solution Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Solution spaces connected by recorded reductions.

children.title: Presolved Solution State
children.top_down_role: Solution artifacts expressed in the reduced or transformed problem space.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolved Solution State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate solution represented in the reduced model's coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let presolve produce a reduced problem \(P'=(Y,F',h,J)\) and a reversible reduction log \(\Lambda\). A presolved solution state is \(Z'=(y,h(y),\sigma',\tau')\), where \(y\in Y\) is a reduced-coordinate candidate, \(\sigma'\) records its reduced-model feasibility and integrality status, and \(\tau'\) records the tolerances under which those statuses were assessed. When \(\sigma'\) declares primal feasibility, \(y\in F'\) under \(\tau'\), including the required integrality tests for indices in \(J\). Variables and constraints removed by presolve need not have explicit values or activities in \(Z'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolved solution state records a reduced-coordinate candidate, objective, feasibility and integrality status, and the tolerances used to assess it.
assumptions_latex: Presolve outputs a reduced model \(P'\) and reduction log \(\Lambda\).
Statuses are interpreted using recorded tolerances \(\tau'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z'\) describes a solution only in the coordinates and semantics of \(P'\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Presolved candidates inhabit reduced coordinates and require reduction metadata for recovery.
No supplied locator directly supports solver solution-state semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits a reduced-coordinate solution state, but the proposed tuple, recorded statuses, tolerances, and assumed reversible log are not supported by a cited presolve implementation or authoritative text.

children.title: Postsolved Solution State
children.top_down_role: Recovered solution artifacts expressed in the submitted problem space.

knowledge_statements.title: Postsolved Solution State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovered candidate expressed in original variables after reversing presolve reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an original problem \(O=(X,F,f,I)\), a postsolved solution state is \(Z=(x,f(x),\sigma,\tau,\rho)\), where \(x\in X\) assigns every original variable, \(\sigma\) records original-model feasibility and integrality status, \(\tau\) records the applicable original-coordinate tolerances, and \(\rho\) records recovery diagnostics. It is obtained by applying the inverse reduction sequence to a presolved state and then evaluating the original constraints, bounds, integrality conditions, and objective. A successful postsolve requires \(x\in F\) under \(\tau\) and objective consistency with the presolved value after accounting for recorded objective offsets and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A postsolved state assigns all original variables and records original-model validation, objective consistency, tolerances, and recovery diagnostics.
assumptions_latex: An original problem \(O\) and a presolved state \(Z'\) are available.
The reduction log supplies the required recovery operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful \(Z\) is a validated original-coordinate solution corresponding to \(Z'\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Postsolve reconstructs and validates solutions in original coordinates.
Exact objective and tolerance reconciliation is solver-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but complete original-variable assignment, validation procedure, tolerance reconciliation, and objective consistency rules are solver-dependent and uncited.

children.title: Solution Recovery Mapping
children.top_down_role: Recorded reduction information used to connect reduced-space solutions with original-space artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Recovery Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse replay of presolve transformations to recover original-variable values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a presolved candidate \(y\) and an ordered reduction log \(\Lambda=(r_1,\ldots,r_k)\). Initialize \(z_k:=y\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), apply the recovery operator \(R_i\) stored with reduction \(r_i\), setting \(z_{i-1}:=R_i(z_i)\); each operator restores eliminated variables, reverses substitutions or scaling, and transfers objective offsets as specified by its record. If an operator's precondition fails or required data are absent, return recovery failure. Otherwise set \(x:=z_0\), evaluate \(x\) against the original bounds, constraints, integrality requirements, and objective, and return \(x\) only if all required validation tests pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover an original solution by reversing reductions in last-in-first-out order, then validate all original bounds, constraints, integrality conditions, and objective data.
assumptions_latex: Every reduction \(r_i\) has a recovery operator \(R_i\) with stored parameters.
The log order matches the order in which reductions were applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On success, the output \(x\) is an original-coordinate candidate corresponding to \(y\); otherwise the algorithm reports failure.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Composed reductions are recovered by applying recorded inverses in reverse order.
Recovery operators and validation conventions require an authoritative solver reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind and reverse replay is plausible, but not every presolve system is represented by individually stored recovery operators of this form; an authoritative source is required.

children.title: Recovery Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where incomplete records, numerical issues, or incompatible artifacts limit recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which reduced-coordinate feasibility does not ensure recoverable original feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solution recovery is not guaranteed from a reduced vector \(y\) alone. Consider the original feasible set \(F=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x_1+x_2=1\}\). Eliminating \(x_2\) yields the unrestricted reduced variable \(y=x_1\). If the reduction log omits the substitution \(x_2=1-y\), no deterministic recovery rule based only on the declaration \(y=x_1\) can certify which value of \(x_2\) satisfies the deleted equation. More generally, recovery reaches its failure boundary when required inverse metadata are absent, a recovery precondition is violated, or finite-precision reconstruction fails original-model validation; reduced feasibility alone then provides no postsolve certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced feasibility does not guarantee recovery when inverse metadata are missing, recovery preconditions fail, or reconstructed values fail original-model validation.
assumptions_latex: Presolve may eliminate variables or constraints.
Recovery must certify feasibility in the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without adequate inverse data and successful validation, \(y\in F'\) does not certify the existence of a returned \(x\in F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Recovery requires inverse transformation data and original-model validation.
The concrete failure taxonomy is not supported by the supplied source locators.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct content kind, but the example depends on excluding access to the deleted original equation as well as omitting recovery metadata. The intended information model and broader failure taxonomy require sourcing before the claim can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Solve-Stage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operational stages through which solver-owned state is created, transformed, used, and released.

children.title: Presearch Transformation Stages
children.top_down_role: Stages preceding enumerative search.

children.title: Transformation Stage
children.top_down_role: Creation of solver-native representations before reduction processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Stage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presearch construction of a solver-native model from the submitted formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an accepted original state \(S_O\). Initialize the internal model as a structural copy of the submitted variables, constraints, and objective. Apply a finite ordered sequence of declared reformulations, which may normalize constraint senses, introduce auxiliary variables, replace supported expressions by solver-native representations, scale data, or encode logical structure. After each operation \(t_i\), append to a transformation record \(\Gamma\) its forward semantics, recovery data, and original-object correspondence. Reject the transformation if it cannot preserve the specified feasibility and objective correspondence. Output the transformed state \(S_T\) together with \(\Gamma\), or report an unsupported or invalid model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert the submitted model into solver-native form while recording each reformulation's correspondence and recovery data; reject transformations that cannot preserve semantics.
assumptions_latex: The submitted model passes syntax and domain checks.
Each transformation \(t_i\) has declared semantic and recovery rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a transformed state \(S_T\) with correspondence metadata \(\Gamma\), or an explicit transformation failure.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Solver front ends construct internal representations through semantics-preserving reformulations.
Transformation-stage scope and ordering are implementation-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the transformation-stage container, but the stage ordering, mandatory recovery data, correspondence checks, and failure behavior are implementation-dependent and have no supporting citation.

children.title: Presolve Stage
children.top_down_role: Pre-search simplification, tightening, structural recognition, and reduction activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Stage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative presearch reduction of the transformed model with recoverability tracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a transformed problem \(P_0\) and initialize the reduction log \(\Lambda:=()\). For rounds \(r=0,1,\ldots\), apply sound reduction operators to \(P_r\), such as bound tightening, fixed-variable elimination, redundant-constraint deletion, coefficient strengthening, or substitution. For every accepted reduction \(q_r\), record its validity conditions and recovery operator in \(\Lambda\), and form \(P_{r+1}:=q_r(P_r)\). Stop when a prescribed resource limit is reached, no enabled operator changes the model, or infeasibility or unboundedness is certified. Output the reduced problem and \(\Lambda\), together with any certified terminal status, for handoff to search or postsolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply sound model reductions, recording validity and recovery information, until convergence, a limit, or a certified terminal status.
assumptions_latex: Each accepted reduction preserves the required solution correspondence.
Every elimination needed for postsolve records sufficient recovery data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stage returns \((P',\Lambda)\) for search, or a certified infeasible or unbounded terminal status.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: MIP presolve iteratively applies sound reductions while retaining postsolve information.
No supplied locator directly documents practical MIP presolve lifecycle semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the presolve-stage leaf, but the reduction-log model and the conditions under which presolve may certify infeasibility or unboundedness require an authoritative, specifically located source.

children.title: Presearch Stage Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of transformed, reduced, and recorded recovery artifacts into root processing.

assumptions_latex: The original minimization MIP is \(P=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X,\ x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\}\).
Presearch produces a transformed model \(P'\) and a reconstruction map \(R\) defined on solutions of \(P'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P'\), \(R\), all valid transformed-domain deductions, and any incumbent expressed in the coordinates of \(P'\) constitute the search input state.

notation.meaning: Map reconstructing an original-space solution from a transformed-space solution.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly specifies a solver-independent presearch handoff contract.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract contract between presolve or transformation and branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presearch handoff is valid when the transformed problem \(P'\) and reconstruction map \(R\) preserve the required solution semantics: every accepted transformed solution \(y\) yields \(R(y)\in X\) with the corresponding original objective value, and the transformed optimum determines the original optimum. The handoff state consists of \(P'\), \(R\), transformed variable and constraint domains, globally valid deductions, and any incumbent translated consistently into transformed coordinates. Search may begin only after these objects form a mutually consistent state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presearch hands search an equivalent transformed model, a valid reconstruction map, consistent global deductions, and any incumbent represented in transformed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Presearch Stage Handoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the handoff container, but no inspectable source supports this solver-independent contract. The transformed objective and the precise sense in which it corresponds to the original objective are also not defined, so the preservation claim cannot be reliably assessed.

children.title: Root-Tree Search Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Root-specific and general node-processing regimes.

children.title: Root Processing Stage
children.top_down_role: Root-specific relaxation work, global strengthening, initialization, and early primal activity.

assumptions_latex: The root-node relaxation \(Q_0\) is a valid relaxation of the current MIP.
An incumbent value \(U\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is available for minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Root processing either certifies termination or returns a strengthened root state whose bound remains valid for every feasible integer solution.
review_flags: Locator supports tree-based integer programming but may not specify this complete solver-stage convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization branch-and-bound root processing with valid global strengthening.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 An Optimal Subtree of a Tree p. 83

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the active problem with the root relaxation \(Q_0\). Repeatedly solve or reoptimize the root relaxation, apply globally valid propagation and cutting operations, and optionally run primal heuristics to update \(U\). Let \(L_0\) be the resulting valid lower bound. Stop at the root if infeasibility is certified or if \(L_0\ge U\). Otherwise output the strengthened root relaxation, its bound, the incumbent, and the globally valid deductions needed to initialize the search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the root, solve and strengthen the relaxation, seek incumbents, and either terminate by infeasibility or bound dominance, or initialize the search tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Root Processing Stage

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 An Optimal Subtree of a Tree p. 83

children.title: Tree-Search Stage
children.top_down_role: Repeated node processing under evolving local domains and global search state.

assumptions_latex: The current problem is a minimization MIP, and every active node \(v\in\mathcal A\) represents a subproblem whose integer-feasible points are contained in its relaxation \(Q_v\).
Every nonempty node relaxation considered by the algorithm has an attained finite optimum and is solved exactly; its optimal value is a valid lower bound \(L_v\) for the node.
The incumbent value \(U\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the objective value of the best known integer-feasible solution, with \(U=+\infty\) when no incumbent exists.
Every branching disjunction used at a node covers all integer-feasible points represented by that node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\), a finite incumbent is globally optimal; if no incumbent exists, the MIP is infeasible.

notation.meaning: Relaxation and optimal relaxation value at node v.
Optimal relaxation solution at node v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact branch-and-bound tree-search stage for minimization MIPs with exactly solved, bounded node relaxations.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 An Optimal Subtree of a Tree p. 83

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: While \(\mathcal A\ne\varnothing\), select a node \(v\) and solve \(Q_v\). Prune \(v\) if \(Q_v\) is infeasible. Otherwise let \(x_v\) be an optimal relaxation solution and let \(L_v\) be its objective value. Prune \(v\) if \(L_v\ge U\). If \(x_v\) is integer feasible, update the incumbent using \(x_v\) and prune \(v\). Otherwise, after incorporating any newly found integer-feasible incumbent, choose a valid disjunction whose children cover all integer-feasible points represented by \(v\), create those children, and insert every child not already certified infeasible or dominated by \(U\) into \(\mathcal A\). Output the incumbent when \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree search exactly solves each selected node relaxation, prunes infeasible or bound-dominated nodes, accepts and prunes an integer-feasible relaxation optimum, and otherwise branches with a covering disjunction. Exhausting the active nodes proves the incumbent globally optimal or proves infeasibility when no incumbent exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Search Stage

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 An Optimal Subtree of a Tree p. 83

children.title: Root-to-Tree Transition
children.top_down_role: Handoff of root artifacts, bounds, cuts, incumbents, and search initialization into enumeration.

assumptions_latex: Root processing has produced a strengthened root subproblem with valid lower bound \(L_0\).
The root is neither certified infeasible nor prunable by the incumbent bound \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initialized active-node set covers every unresolved integer-feasible solution and carries only deductions valid in the scope assigned to each node.

notation.meaning: Root lower bound and incumbent upper bound.

review_flags: The exact retained solver artifacts are implementation-dependent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary between root processing and ordinary node processing.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 An Optimal Subtree of a Tree p. 83

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A root-to-tree transition is admissible when \(L_0<U\), unresolved integer-feasible points remain, and the initialized active set \(\mathcal A_0\) covers all such points. One may set \(\mathcal A_0\) to the processed root or to children of a valid root disjunction. Global cuts and deductions may be inherited by every node; local deductions may be inherited only by descendants within their validity scope. The incumbent and all node bounds must use a common objective convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transition initializes active nodes covering every unresolved solution while preserving the scope of cuts, deductions, bounds, and the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-to-Tree Transition

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 An Optimal Subtree of a Tree p. 83

children.title: Postsolve-Cleanup Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-space artifacts and release of solve-specific state.

children.title: Postsolve Stage
children.top_down_role: Recovery and validation of original-space solution or certificate artifacts.

assumptions_latex: Search terminates with a transformed-space incumbent \(y^*\) and status \(s\).
Presearch retained a valid reconstruction map \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Postsolve returns \(x^*=R(y^*)\) when an incumbent exists and reports status and certificates only after translating them to the original model.

notation.meaning: Transformed-space incumbent and reconstructed original-space solution.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports postsolve reconstruction semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstruction and validation after solving a transformed MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an incumbent \(y^*\) exists, apply retained transformations in reverse dependency order to compute \(x^*=R(y^*)\). Verify that \(x^*\) satisfies the original variable domains and constraints within the declared numerical tolerances, and recompute its original objective value. Translate any reported bound, status, or certificate to the original model's conventions. If reconstruction or validation fails, do not report \(x^*\) as an original-model feasible solution; output a reconstruction failure status instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve reverses transformations, validates the reconstructed original solution, recomputes its objective, and translates statuses and certificates to original-model conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Stage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the postsolve-stage leaf, but no source is supplied for reverse reconstruction, numerical validation, or translation of bounds and certificates. In particular, a reconstruction map for primal solutions alone does not establish that every status or certificate can be translated to the original model.

children.title: Cleanup Stage
children.top_down_role: Release or reset of solve-specific data after termination.

assumptions_latex: Postsolve has completed or recorded a terminal reconstruction failure.
The solver state is partitioned into disposable artifacts \(D\) and explicitly retained artifacts \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cleanup produces a quiescent state containing \(K\) and no live artifact from \(D\), without changing the already determined mathematical result.
review_flags: Cleanup is an implementation lifecycle concept not supported by the supplied mathematical locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical cleanup contract, independent of memory-management implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cleanup begins only after required postsolve outputs have been materialized. It releases or invalidates every artifact in \(D\), including transient node relaxations, local work arrays, and temporary algorithm contexts, while preserving every artifact in \(K\). No retained object may contain an unresolved dependency on a released object. Cleanup must not alter the returned original-space incumbent, its recomputed objective, the terminal status, or any certificate already designated as an output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cleanup removes transient search data while preserving designated outputs and retained artifacts, with no dangling dependencies or changes to the mathematical result.
knowledge_statements.title: Cleanup Stage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed lifecycle and ownership contract. The statement is also procedural and therefore fits an algorithm or operational principle more naturally than a condition in this exact stage container. Source support is needed before selecting and repairing the mathematical role.

children.title: Retained-State Boundary
children.top_down_role: Artifacts preserved beyond cleanup for reporting, restart, or reoptimization.

assumptions_latex: The completed solve has artifact set \(S\).
A retention policy specifies a subset \(K\subseteq S\) and the model version against which each retained artifact is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only \(K\) may remain accessible after cleanup, and reuse is admissible only while every artifact's validity predicate holds.

notation.meaning: Completed solver state and retained subset.
Validity predicate for artifact a under model version M.

review_flags: No supplied locator defines a retained-state boundary for persistent MIP solvers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating persistent solver state from solve-local state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The retained-state boundary is the pair consisting of a selected subset \(K\subseteq S\) and validity predicates \(V_a\) for all \(a\in K\). After cleanup, artifacts in \(S\setminus K\) are inaccessible, whereas an artifact \(a\in K\) may be inspected or reused for model version \(M\) only if \(V_a(M)\) holds. The boundary must include sufficient ownership and version information to prevent retained artifacts from depending on discarded solve-local state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retained-state boundary identifies persistent artifacts and their model-version validity conditions; all other solve-local state becomes inaccessible after cleanup.
knowledge_statements.title: Retained-State Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the boundary leaf and the record is internally coherent, but the proposed pair of a retained subset and per-artifact validity predicates is an uncited abstraction rather than an established solver-state definition. An inspectable source is required.

children.title: Persistent Solve Regimes
children.top_down_role: State-retention regimes spanning more than one uninterrupted solve.

children.title: Restart-Resume Continuation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Controlled restarts, interruptions, and continuation of search.

children.title: Restart Regimes
children.top_down_role: Fresh or partially fresh search launches after deliberate solver-state reset.

assumptions_latex: A previous solve state \(S	extsubscript{old}\) and a current model \(M	extsubscript{new}\) are available.
The restart policy identifies which artifacts remain valid for \(M	extsubscript{new}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A restart creates a new search state and imports only artifacts whose validity for the current model has been established.

notation.meaning: Previous solve state and current model.

review_flags: Restart semantics vary across solver implementations and lack a directly relevant supplied source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent-solver restart, distinguished from resuming a paused search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restart regime constructs a fresh search state \(S_{\mathrm{new}}\) for \(M_{\mathrm{new}}\) rather than continuing the prior active-node process. It may import an incumbent, solution candidates, globally valid constraints, or other artifacts from \(S_{\mathrm{old}}\) only after their feasibility, objective convention, scope, and model-version validity have been checked. Active nodes, node-local deductions, and bounds are discarded unless the regime separately certifies their validity for the current model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart initializes a new search and selectively imports only artifacts proven valid for the current model, rather than continuing the old active tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition distinguishes restart from resume in a plausible way, but restart semantics and which artifacts can survive vary materially by solver. No source establishes the asserted fresh-state and default-discard rules. The assumptions also use nonstandard subscript notation inconsistent with the notation table.

children.title: Resume Regimes
children.top_down_role: Continuation from a retained interruption point with compatible search state.

assumptions_latex: A paused search state \(S_t\) contains an active-node set \(\mathcal A_t\), incumbent, bounds, and scoped deductions.
The mathematical model and all semantics governing those objects are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resume continues from \(S_t\) only if its invariants remain valid; otherwise the solver must invalidate affected artifacts or restart.
review_flags: Resume invariants are solver-state semantics not directly covered by the supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation of an interrupted, materially unchanged branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A paused solve is resumable when every node in \(\mathcal A_t\) still represents the same subproblem, every stored bound remains valid under the same objective and tolerances, the incumbent retains its feasibility and value, and each deduction retains its original validity scope. Resume restores \(S_t\) and continues the node-selection loop without reinitializing the tree. Failure of any invariant requires invalidating the affected artifacts or entering a restart regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resume continues an interrupted tree only when nodes, bounds, incumbent, tolerances, and scoped deductions retain exactly their prior semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Resume Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits a resumability leaf, and the listed invariants are plausible, but no source defines this exact continuation contract or establishes that unchanged model and tolerance semantics suffice for all retained solver state.

children.title: Retained Search Artifacts
children.top_down_role: Search information eligible for preservation across a stop or relaunch.

assumptions_latex: Each stored artifact \(a\) has provenance, validity scope, and a model-version predicate \(V_a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An artifact is reusable in model version \(M\) exactly when \(V_a(M)\) holds and all dependencies required by \(a\) are also retained and valid.

notation.meaning: Artifact-validity predicate for model version M.

review_flags: The artifact taxonomy and validity metadata are implementation-dependent and unsupported by supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent artifacts potentially reused across interruption, restart, or reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A retained search artifact is solver state preserved beyond its originating solve together with provenance, dependency, scope, and model-version metadata. Such artifacts may include incumbents, solution pools, global cuts, conflict information, pseudocost statistics, bases, active nodes, or bounds. For a current model version \(M\), artifact \(a\) is reusable if and only if \(V_a(M)\) holds and every retained dependency of \(a\) is valid; otherwise \(a\) must be discarded, recomputed, or revalidated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retained search artifact is persistent solver data accompanied by enough provenance, scope, dependencies, and validity metadata to decide whether it can be reused.
knowledge_statements.title: Retained Search Artifacts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the artifact leaf, but the artifact taxonomy and required metadata are uncited and implementation-dependent. The statement checks only every retained dependency, whereas the conclusion requires all dependencies to be retained and valid; that distinction must be resolved using a source-backed validity model.

children.title: Continuation Invalidators
children.top_down_role: Changes or losses that prevent safe continuation from retained state.

assumptions_latex: A retained artifact \(a\) was derived under model version \(M\).
The model or solver semantics change from \(M\) to \(M'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Continuation with \(a\) is invalid whenever the change makes its validity predicate false; affected dependents must also be invalidated.
review_flags: Exact invalidation rules depend on artifact type and solver implementation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic boundary for continuing with persistent branch-and-bound state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A change is a continuation invalidator for artifact \(a\) precisely when \(V_a(M)=\mathrm{true}\) but \(V_a(M')=\mathrm{false}\). Typical mechanisms are altered feasible regions invalidating node coverage or incumbents, altered objectives invalidating objective-dependent bounds and priorities, changed integrality invalidating relaxations or branching semantics, and changed tolerances invalidating stored acceptance decisions. Invalidation propagates to every retained artifact whose correctness depends on \(a\); unaffected artifacts may remain reusable only after their predicates are checked independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any model or semantic change that falsifies an artifact's validity predicate invalidates that artifact and all dependent retained state.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Invalidators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, and the predicate-based formulation is internally plausible. However, no source supports the proposed invalidator taxonomy or dependency-propagation rule, and the validity predicates currently encode rather than independently characterize the substantive invalidation conditions.

children.title: Parametric Reoptimization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Reuse after modifications that preserve most model structure.

children.title: Objective-Change Reoptimization
children.top_down_role: Reuse after modifications to objective coefficients, priorities, offsets, or sense.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F=\{x:Ax\le b,\ \ell\le x\le u,\ x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\}\) is unchanged.
The objective changes from \(c^\top x\) to \(d^\top x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility-based artifacts may remain valid, whereas every objective-dependent bound or pruning decision must be recomputed or separately certified under \(d\).
review_flags: The supplied objective locator does not directly establish solver reoptimization rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reoptimization after changing only a linear minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(F\) is unchanged, every stored point \(\bar x\in F\) remains feasible, but its incumbent value must be replaced by \(d^\top\bar x\). Constraints and deductions valid solely from \(F\) remain valid. Any relaxation bound, reduced-cost inference, node pruning decision, objective cutoff, or search priority depending on \(c\) is not automatically valid for \(d\) and must be recomputed or independently certified. Reoptimization may reuse exactly the retained artifacts passing these validity tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After only the objective changes, feasible solutions and feasibility deductions remain usable, but objective values, bounds, pruning decisions, and objective-dependent artifacts require validation or recomputation.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Change Reoptimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits objective-change reoptimization, and the main distinction between feasibility-only and objective-dependent artifacts is plausible. The cited objective-modeling section does not establish solver reoptimization, pruning-invalidation, reduced-cost, or artifact-reuse rules, so a directly relevant source is required before the formulation can be accepted.

children.title: Bound-Change Reoptimization
children.top_down_role: Reuse after variable-domain modifications that preserve model structure.

assumptions_latex: The original minimization MIP is \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax\ge b,\ \ell\le x\le u,\ x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\}\).
Only variable bounds change, producing \(P'=\min\{c^Tx:Ax\ge b,\ \ell'\le x\le u',\ x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reoptimization retains an old incumbent \(\bar x\) only if \(\ell'\le \bar x\le u'\). An old node region \(R_v\) is discarded if \(R_v\cap[\ell',u']=\varnothing\); otherwise its relaxation must be resolved unless its recorded bound is independently valid for \(R_v\cap[\ell',u']\). Under bound tightening, every valid lower bound for the old node remains a valid, possibly weak, lower bound for the restricted node. Under bound relaxation, an old lower bound need not remain valid. The algorithm rebuilds invalid node bounds, rechecks stored solutions, resumes branch-and-bound, and returns a valid incumbent and global bound for \(P'\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization MIPs with unchanged objective, matrix, right-hand side, and integrality declarations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the modified bounds, first test every stored solution and node against the new box \([\ell',u']\). Preserve only artifacts whose validity follows under the new feasible region; resolve all affected relaxations before using their bounds for pruning. Bound tightening preserves old node lower bounds, whereas bound relaxation generally does not. Resume search only after the active-node list and incumbent have been made valid for \(P'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After bounds change, recheck incumbents and nodes. Tightening preserves old lower bounds, but relaxation may invalidate them; affected relaxations must be solved again.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Change Reoptimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf and the bound-tightening monotonicity claim is mathematically plausible, but no source supports the artifact-validation and resume procedure or its solver-dependent scope.

children.title: Reusable Search Artifacts
children.top_down_role: Incumbents, bases, reductions, cuts, or search records that remain compatible after a change.

assumptions_latex: Each stored artifact was generated for a specified MIP, node region, relaxation, and numerical tolerance.
The modified solve may change objective coefficients, bounds, rows, columns, or integrality declarations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An artifact may be reused only with an explicit validity test. A feasible solution \(x\) is reusable as an incumbent exactly when it satisfies every current constraint and integrality requirement. A node lower bound \(L_v\) is reusable only when \(L_v\le\min\{c'^Tx:x\in R_v\cap F'\}\). A cut \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta\) is globally reusable only when it is valid for every \(x\in F'\); a local cut additionally requires its original node domain. Branching history and pseudocosts may guide search heuristically, but cannot certify feasibility, pruning, or optimality without renewed validation.

notation.meaning: Region and stored lower bound of node v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic validity of incumbents, node bounds, cuts, and heuristic search statistics across related MIP solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reusable search state separates certifying artifacts from heuristic artifacts. Certifying artifacts must satisfy their defining feasibility or validity predicates for the current instance. Heuristic statistics may be transferred without preserving correctness claims, provided they affect only search ordering or candidate selection. Any transferred object used to prune a node, establish a bound, or declare optimality must be validated for the current feasible set and objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incumbents, bounds, and cuts require current-instance validity checks. Heuristic statistics may guide search, but cannot certify pruning or optimality by themselves.
knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Search Artifacts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is defensible, but the taxonomy and reuse rules for incumbents, cuts, node bounds, and heuristic statistics require an inspectable solver or reoptimization source.

children.title: Artifact Invalidation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Modification classes that make retained optimization artifacts unsafe or obsolete.

assumptions_latex: An artifact \(a\) has a validity domain \(D(a)\) consisting of model instances for which its defining claim is true.
A model transformation maps an old instance \(M\) to a current instance \(M'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact reuse boundary is \(M'\in D(a)\). In particular, an incumbent is invalidated by any change making it infeasible; an objective-dependent node bound is invalidated when the new objective or an enlarged feasible region destroys its lower-bound inequality; a cut is invalidated when it is not valid for the current feasible set; and a local artifact is invalidated outside its node domain. If membership in \(D(a)\) cannot be verified, the artifact may be retained only as noncertifying heuristic information and must not support pruning, bounds, feasibility, or termination.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for transferring certifying and heuristic artifacts after a MIP modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Artifact reuse is correctness-preserving precisely inside the artifact's validity domain. Outside that domain, or when membership cannot be established, the artifact loses any certifying role. Feasibility certificates, lower bounds, cuts, and local-node information have distinct validity domains; therefore a solver must invalidate them separately rather than treating the entire saved state as uniformly reusable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An artifact remains certifying only when the modified instance lies in its validity domain; otherwise it must be discarded or downgraded to heuristic use.
knowledge_statements.title: Artifact Invalidation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role matches the container, but the validity-domain formalism and claimed downgrade behavior are uncited and may vary by artifact and solver.

children.title: Reoptimization after Structural Changes
children.top_down_role: Reuse after variables or constraints are added, removed, or altered.

assumptions_latex: The original MIP is \(M\), and structural editing produces \(M'\) by adding, deleting, or altering variables or constraints.
A saved artifact is reused only after its semantic references and validity predicate are checked against \(M'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Construct a correspondence between surviving rows, columns, variables, and node restrictions of \(M\) and \(M'\). Delete artifacts referencing removed or altered objects. Recheck every incumbent against \(M'\), every global cut for validity on the feasible set of \(M'\), and every local bound or cut on its mapped node domain. Rebuild relaxations whose matrices, objectives, or domains changed. Search may then resume from the validated state; otherwise it restarts from a clean root. The output must be certified solely by artifacts valid for \(M'\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent-solver reuse after adding, deleting, or altering MIP rows or columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Structural reoptimization begins by mapping unchanged model objects into the modified instance. Saved state is partitioned into valid, invalid, and unmappable artifacts. Invalid or unmappable certifying artifacts are removed; surviving incumbents, cuts, node domains, and bounds are revalidated. A relaxation affected by a structural edit is rebuilt before its value is used for pruning. The solver resumes only from the resulting valid state and otherwise performs a clean restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After structural edits, map unchanged objects, discard broken references, revalidate certifying artifacts, rebuild affected relaxations, and resume only from valid state.
knowledge_statements.title: Reoptimization after Structural Changes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits structural reoptimization, but object mapping, artifact deletion, relaxation rebuilding, and clean-restart behavior are implementation-dependent and unsupported by a source.

children.title: Cross-Instance Solve Sequences
children.top_down_role: State reuse across related instances and rolling solve sequences.

children.title: Scenario Solves
children.top_down_role: Related instances differing through designated scenario data or parameter sets.

assumptions_latex: Scenarios \(s\in S\) define MIPs \(P_s=\min\{c_s^Tx:x\in F_s,\ x_{I_s}\in\mathbb Z^{|I_s|}\}\).
Each scenario has a known transformation from a common base model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(s\in S\), instantiate the scenario data, validate any transferred state against \(P_s\), solve until the scenario stopping rule holds, and record an incumbent \(x_s\), objective value \(z_s\), global bound \(L_s\), and termination status. No incumbent or bound from scenario \(r\) may certify scenario \(s\) unless its feasibility or bound predicate is valid for \(P_s\). The scenario collection is complete only when every requested \(s\) has an independently interpretable result record.

notation.meaning: Scenario incumbent value and global lower bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite deterministic collections of related minimization MIPs, each requiring its own validity and termination record.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scenario solve evaluates a finite family of related MIPs by repeated model transformation and optimization. For each scenario, transferred state is validated under that scenario's objective, feasible set, and integrality declarations. Results are stored separately, including incumbent, global bound, and termination status, so that an incomplete solve is not confused with a proved optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve each scenario as its own MIP, validating transferred state and recording its incumbent, bound, and termination status separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Solves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits scenario solves, but no source establishes the proposed per-scenario workflow, transferred-state validation policy, or required result record.

children.title: Sequence Solves
children.top_down_role: Ordered solve series in which later instances inherit context from earlier instances.

assumptions_latex: A sequence \((P_k)_{k=0}^{K}\) of related minimization MIPs is presented in order.
The result and validated state of \(P_{k-1}\) are available before solving \(P_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solve \(P_0\) from an initial state. For each \(k=1,\ldots,K\), apply the model update, classify saved artifacts by validity for \(P_k\), discard or downgrade invalid artifacts, and initialize search with the remaining state. Run until the stopping rule for \(P_k\) holds and emit \((x_k,z_k,L_k,\sigma_k)\), where \(\sigma_k\) is the termination status. Correctness for \(P_k\) may depend only on certificates valid for \(P_k\), not merely on their validity for an earlier sequence member.

notation.meaning: Incumbent value and global lower bound for instance k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered related MIPs solved incrementally, with per-instance certification and termination records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence solve processes related MIPs in their prescribed order. Before solving each new instance, it applies the update and validates inherited state. Invalid certifying artifacts are removed or made heuristic-only. Each instance then receives its own incumbent, bound, and status, and no earlier certificate is used unless it remains valid for the current instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process related MIPs in order, validate inherited state at every transition, and report separate incumbents, bounds, and statuses for each instance.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequence Solves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the state-transition procedure and artifact downgrade policy lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Cross-Instance State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reusable model, relaxation, primal, or search artifacts across related instances.

assumptions_latex: Instances \(P\\) and \(P'\) have an explicit mapping between corresponding variables, constraints, and objective data.
A stored state object records the model objects and domain on which its claim depends.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transfer an artifact \(a\) from \(P\) to \(P'\) only if its references map into \(P'\) and its validity predicate holds after mapping. A mapped feasible solution must satisfy all constraints and integrality declarations of \(P'\). A mapped lower bound must bound the current objective over its current domain. A mapped cut must remain valid for the current feasible set, with local cuts restricted to mapped node domains. Search-order statistics may be transferred without certification, but all correctness claims for \(P'\) must be independent of unvalidated state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving transfer of solutions, bounds, cuts, and heuristic statistics between related MIP instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cross-instance reuse is governed by semantic validity after model mapping. Object identity alone is insufficient: each certifying artifact must retain both meaningful references and a true defining predicate in the destination instance. Heuristic state may influence search decisions, but unvalidated transferred state cannot establish feasibility, pruning, bounds, optimality, or termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer state only through a valid model mapping; certifying artifacts must retain their defining truth, while heuristic state cannot prove correctness.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Instance State Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the container, but the transfer requirements are uncited. The first assumption also contains malformed math text for the source instance, written as P followed by a doubled backslash instead of a properly closed math delimiter.

children.title: Sequence Drift Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Accumulated instance changes that reduce or invalidate the value of retained state.

assumptions_latex: A sequence \((P_k)\) is solved by transferring state from \(P_{k-1}\) to \(P_k\).
The change set \(\Delta_k\) identifies altered objectives, bounds, rows, columns, integrality declarations, and object mappings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse crosses its correctness boundary at the first \(k\) for which a transferred certifying artifact lacks a valid mapping or fails its defining predicate on \(P_k\). Large numerical or combinatorial drift may additionally make valid heuristic state ineffective, but poor effectiveness alone does not invalidate correctness. When \(\Delta_k\) prevents complete validation, the solver must remove affected certifying state or restart. A quantitative drift threshold can control performance policy only after the solver specifies a metric \(d(P_{k-1},P_k)\) and threshold \(\tau\); it is not a universal mathematical constant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness and performance boundaries as successive MIP instances diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sequence drift has two distinct boundaries. The correctness boundary is semantic: it is crossed when a transferred certificate is no longer valid or mappable. The performance boundary is policy-dependent: even valid heuristic state may cease to help as instances diverge. Any automatic restart based on \(d(P_{k-1},P_k)>\tau\) therefore requires a declared metric and solver-specific threshold, while invalid certifying state must always be removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Drift invalidates correctness when transferred certificates fail; performance degradation is separate and any restart threshold depends on an explicitly chosen metric and policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequence Drift Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the correctness/performance distinction is plausible, but neither the formulation nor the restart-policy claims have source support.

children.title: Solver Control Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Controls governing computational effort and the interpretation of returned solve status.

children.title: Computational Resource Limits
children.top_down_role: Whole-solve and subsystem resource limits.

children.title: Time Limits
children.top_down_role: Wall-clock, CPU, deterministic, or subsystem time budgets.

assumptions_latex: A solve starts at wall-clock time \(t_0\) and has time budget \(T\ge0\).
The measured elapsed time \(E(t)\) and included solver phases are fixed by the stated timing convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The time-limit condition is \(E(t)\ge T\). At the first permitted interruption point satisfying this condition, the solver terminates with time-limit status and returns the best currently valid incumbent \(\bar x\), if one exists, together with the current valid global bound \(L\). For minimization, the report may assert \(L\le z^\star\le c^T\bar x\) only when both quantities are available and valid. Reaching the time limit alone certifies neither feasibility of a missing incumbent nor optimality of an existing one.

notation.meaning: Elapsed time under the declared timing convention.
Optimal value of the minimization MIP.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic stopping semantics for a minimization MIP under a declared elapsed-time accounting convention.

source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A time limit is reached when elapsed time under the declared accounting convention meets or exceeds \(T\). The solver stops at the next permitted interruption point and reports time-limit termination. Any returned incumbent and global bound retain their ordinary meanings, but the limit status itself supplies no optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When measured elapsed time reaches the budget, the solver stops at an interruption point and returns available valid bounds and incumbents without implying optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Time Limits

source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Time Limits, but the cited running-time section does not specifically support solver time-limit accounting, interruption points, termination status, or returned incumbent and bound semantics.

children.title: Memory Limits
children.top_down_role: Memory budgets affecting search storage, relaxations, pools, and auxiliary data.

assumptions_latex: The solver has memory budget \(M\ge0\) measured by a declared memory-accounting function \(U(t)\).
Policies for disk offloading, state compression, and emergency reserve are specified separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The memory-limit condition is \(U(t)\ge M\). Before an allocation that would violate the budget, or at the next detectable safe point, the solver must apply its declared policy: release optional state, offload state, checkpoint and stop, or terminate with memory-limit status. Any reported incumbent or global bound must have been validated before termination. Memory exhaustion does not by itself prove infeasibility, unboundedness, or optimality, and failure to preserve a valid search frontier may prevent later resumption from retaining the previous global bound.

notation.meaning: Memory usage under the declared accounting convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory-budget stopping semantics, excluding any solver-specific choice of accounting metric or recovery policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A memory limit is reached when accounted usage meets the configured budget or a pending allocation would exceed it. The solver follows a declared recovery or termination policy while preserving only claims already supported by valid state. A memory-limit status is a resource outcome and carries no implication of optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the memory budget, the solver follows its declared recovery or stopping policy; valid saved results remain meaningful, but the status proves no optimization conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Memory Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Memory Limits, but no source supports the threshold semantics, recovery alternatives, frontier-preservation claim, or termination behavior.

children.title: Node Limits
children.top_down_role: Budgets on processed, created, open, or depth-restricted search nodes.

assumptions_latex: A branch-and-bound solve maintains a count \(N\) under a declared node-counting convention.
The configured node budget is \(N_{\max}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node-limit condition is \(N\ge N_{\max}\). Once it holds, the solver performs no further counted node processing and terminates at the next permitted control point with node-limit status. It returns any valid incumbent \(\bar x\) and current global lower bound \(L\). For a minimization MIP, \(L\le z^\star\le c^T\bar x\) holds when both are available. The limit status alone does not establish optimality unless the active search frontier is empty or the ordinary optimality-gap condition is already satisfied.

notation.meaning: Number of processed nodes under the declared convention.
Optimal value of the minimization MIP.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound termination under an explicit processed-node budget and counting convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node limit bounds the number of branch-and-bound nodes processed under a declared counting convention. When the count reaches \(N_{\max}\), processing stops at the next control point. The returned incumbent and global bound remain valid if their underlying artifacts remain valid, but node-limit termination is not itself an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop branch-and-bound when the declared processed-node count reaches its budget; report valid incumbent and bound information without claiming optimality solely from the limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Node Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Node Limits, but a generic branch-and-bound chapter does not establish the proposed counting threshold, control-point behavior, status semantics, or solver output guarantees.

children.title: Iteration Limits
children.top_down_role: Budgets on relaxation or numerical iterations at whole-solve or subsystem scope.

assumptions_latex: An iterative solver phase maintains a nondecreasing iteration counter \(K\) under a declared counting convention.
The configured iteration budget is \(K_{\max}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), with its scope identified as local, phase-wide, or solve-wide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration-limit condition is \(K\ge K_{\max}\). When it holds, the affected algorithmic phase performs no additional counted iterations and returns control with iteration-limit status or invokes a separately declared fallback. Any relaxation value used as a node bound must satisfy the solver's validity requirements despite early termination; an unfinished relaxation cannot be treated as optimally solved merely because its iteration budget was exhausted. At solve termination, only previously validated incumbents and global bounds may be reported as certificates.

notation.meaning: Counted iterations in the stated scope.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping an iterative MIP subalgorithm or solve under an explicit counter and scope convention.

source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An iteration limit is reached when the declared counter meets \(K_{\max}\) within its specified scope. The affected procedure then stops or invokes a declared fallback. Early termination does not make an unfinished relaxation optimal, so only bounds satisfying the relevant validity conditions may enter branch-and-bound certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the scoped iteration counter reaches its budget, stop or use a declared fallback; unfinished relaxations cannot automatically supply valid optimal bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Limits

source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Iteration Limits, but the cited running-time section does not support scoped iteration counters, fallback behavior, or the asserted handling of prematurely terminated relaxations.

children.title: Limit Scope Precedence
children.top_down_role: Interactions among global budgets, local budgets, and the first exhausted control.

knowledge_statements.title: Limit Scope Precedence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic precedence rule for nested solver-resource limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_g\) be a global resource limit and let \(L_s\) be the corresponding limit for a subordinate solve. If resource consumption is \(r\), the subordinate solve must stop when \[r\ge L_{\mathrm{eff}},\qquad L_{\mathrm{eff}}=\min\{L_g^{\mathrm{rem}},L_s\},\] where \(L_g^{\mathrm{rem}}\) is the global budget remaining when the subordinate solve starts. A subordinate setting cannot enlarge the remaining global budget; an explicitly documented solver override is required for any different precedence rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested solve is governed by the smaller of its local limit and the remaining global limit, unless the solver explicitly documents another precedence rule.
assumptions_latex: \(L_g,L_s\in[0,+\infty]\) measure the same resource.
Resource consumption \(r\) is nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{eff}}=\min\{L_g^{\mathrm{rem}},L_s\}\).

notation.meaning: resource consumed by the subordinate solve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the leaf, but the minimum-of-limits rule is not universal across nested solver operations and requires an inspectable solver-manual source defining scope and precedence.

children.title: Progress-Based Termination Criteria
children.top_down_role: Progress- and solution-oriented termination families.

children.title: Gap Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping based on absolute or relative separation between primal and dual progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual termination test for a minimization MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_P\in\mathbb R\) be the objective value of a feasible incumbent and let \(z_D\in\mathbb R\) be a valid global lower bound, so \(z_D\le z^*\le z_P\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_r\ge0\), gap termination is permitted when \[z_P-z_D\le\varepsilon_a\quad\text{or}\quad \frac{z_P-z_D}{\max\{1,|z_P|\}}\le\varepsilon_r,\] according to the enabled absolute or relative test. This certifies the corresponding objective-gap bound, not exact optimality unless the tolerance is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when a feasible incumbent and valid global bound differ by no more than an enabled absolute or relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with finite incumbent \(z_P\).
The bound \(z_D\) is globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_P-z^*\le z_P-z_D\), with the configured absolute or relative bound satisfied.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute-gap claim is standard, but the exact relative-gap denominator and the disjunction between enabled tests are solver-specific. The cited duality-gap section does not reliably establish this precise termination formula without full-text inspection.

children.title: Solution-Count Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping based on accepted, improving, or stored solution counts.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Count Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination after a prescribed number of accepted incumbent solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer limit \(K\ge1\). Let \(N(t)\) count accepted feasible incumbent events up to solver state \(t\), using a declared convention for whether repeated objective values or duplicate solutions count. Solution-count termination occurs at the first state \[\tau=\inf\{t:N(t)\ge K\}.\] The returned incumbent, if any, is feasible under the solver's acceptance tolerances, but the stopping condition alone supplies neither an optimality certificate nor a bound on its objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop after the configured number of accepted feasible-solution events; this criterion alone does not certify solution quality or optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb N\) and \(K\ge1\).
The solver specifies which feasible-solution events increment \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination occurs at \(\tau=\inf\{t:N(t)\ge K\}\).

notation.meaning: number of counted feasible-solution events by state t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but what constitutes a counted solution event is solver-specific and no manual locator supports the proposed semantics.

children.title: Stall Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping after insufficient progress over a configured observation window.

knowledge_statements.title: Stall Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progress-window stopping rule with an explicitly chosen progress metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(t)\) be a declared solver-progress metric sampled at ordered states, let \(W\ge1\) be a window length, and let \(\delta\ge0\) be a minimum material improvement. With improvement defined by a nonnegative function \(I(q(t-W),q(t))\), stall termination is permitted at the first eligible state \(t\) satisfying \[I(q(t-W),q(t))\le\delta.\] The status records failure to achieve configured progress; it does not imply infeasibility, unboundedness, or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when a declared progress metric improves by at most the configured amount over a specified window; this is not a conclusive solve certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb N\) and \(W\ge1\).
The metric \(q\), sampling states, and improvement function \(I\) are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(q(t-W),q(t))\le\delta\) triggers a nonconclusive stall stop.

notation.meaning: declared progress metric at state t
maximum improvement classified as a stall

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly treats stalling as nonconclusive, but the metric, sampling sequence, window, inequality, and trigger semantics are implementation-dependent and unsupported by a cited manual.
