children.title: Competing Termination Criteria
children.top_down_role: Status selection when multiple progress-oriented stopping conditions become active.

knowledge_statements.title: Competing Termination Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-trigger semantics for simultaneously enabled stopping predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1(t),\ldots,C_m(t)\) be enabled termination predicates on solver state \(t\). The abstract stopping state is \[\tau=\inf\{t:\bigvee_{i=1}^m C_i(t)\}.\] If several predicates first hold at \(\tau\), the reported status is selected by a documented priority map \(P\) applied to \(\{i:C_i(\tau)\}\). Status priority changes only the reported reason; it does not invalidate any independently verifiable certificate present at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The earliest enabled criterion stops the solve; simultaneous triggers require a documented status-priority rule, while any valid certificate remains valid.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is evaluated on the solver's declared event sequence.
A deterministic priority map \(P\) is defined for simultaneous triggers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau=\inf\{t:\bigvee_i C_i(t)\}\), with status \(P(\{i:C_i(\tau)\})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract first-trigger construction fits the leaf, but real solvers may evaluate criteria asynchronously or report statuses according to implementation-specific precedence. An authoritative manual locator is required.

children.title: Conclusive Solve Status Certificates
children.top_down_role: Conclusive status families returned after completed processing.

children.title: Optimal Statuses
children.top_down_role: Conclusive outcomes reporting an established optimal solution value.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and tolerance-qualified optimal statuses for minimization MIPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization MIP with optimum \(z^*\), an exact optimal status is certified by a feasible point \(\bar x\) and a valid global lower bound \(L\) satisfying \[f(\bar x)=L.\] Then \(f(\bar x)=z^*\). If instead \(f(\bar x)-L\le\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon>0\), the artifacts certify only \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. Consequently, a tolerance-based solver status must not be interpreted as exact optimality without its tolerance qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent matching a global bound certifies exact optimality; a positive residual certifies only tolerance-qualified optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is feasible for the original MIP.
\(L\le z^*\) is a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x)=L\Rightarrow f(\bar x)=z^*\); more generally, \(f(\bar x)-L\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow f(\bar x)-z^*\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Infeasible Statuses
children.top_down_role: Conclusive outcomes reporting absence of feasible solutions in the relevant problem space.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global infeasibility certification in finite branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a finite branch-and-bound partition whose active leaf regions \(R_1,
\ldots,R_m\) cover every integer-feasible candidate of the original problem. If each leaf has a verifiable certificate that \(R_i\) contains no feasible point and no unexplored leaf remains, then \[\bigcup_{i=1}^m(R_i\cap F)=\varnothing,\] where \(F\) is the original constraint set. Hence the MIP is infeasible. Failure to find an incumbent without complete exclusion is not an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasibility is conclusive only when certificates exclude every region containing a possible integer-feasible point; absence of an incumbent is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The leaf regions cover all integer-feasible candidates.
Every leaf exclusion is valid for the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap(\mathbb R^{n_c}\times\mathbb Z^{n_i})=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: leaf region in the exhaustive search partition
numbers of continuous and integer variables

children.title: Unbounded Statuses
children.top_down_role: Conclusive outcomes reporting an improving direction without a finite objective bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive unboundedness certificate for a minimization MILP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization MILP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax\le b,\ x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\}\), let \(\bar x\) be feasible. If a direction \(d\) satisfies \[Ad\le0,\qquad d_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|},\qquad c^Td<0,\] then \(\bar x+kd\) is feasible for every integer \(k\ge0\), and \(c^T(\bar x+kd)\to-\infty\). Thus the MILP is unbounded below. An unbounded relaxation alone does not certify that the original MILP is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and an integrality-compatible improving recession direction certify MILP unboundedness; an unbounded relaxation by itself does not.
assumptions_latex: The model is a linear minimization problem.
\(\bar x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\) and \(A\bar x\le b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{c^Tx:Ax\le b,\ x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\}=-\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated feasible-point and integrality-compatible recession-direction conditions are a coherent sufficient certificate for the displayed MILP, and the certificate kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the exact formulation.

children.title: Conclusive Status Artifacts
children.top_down_role: Solutions, rays, proofs, or logs associated with interpretation of a conclusive status.

knowledge_statements.title: Conclusive Status Artifacts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal abstract artifact bundles supporting conclusive MIP statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conclusive status is represented by a status label together with checkable artifacts: \[\mathcal A_{\mathrm{opt}}=(\bar x,L),\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{inf}}=(\{R_i,\pi_i\}_{i=1}^m,\text{coverage}),\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{unb}}=(\bar x,d).\] Here the optimal bundle contains primal feasibility and a matching global bound; the infeasible bundle contains exhaustive regions and valid exclusion certificates \(\pi_i\); and the unbounded bundle contains a feasible point and an improving feasible ray. Logs or status codes without the corresponding validity conditions are not mathematical certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conclusive statuses require checkable primal-bound, exhaustive-exclusion, or feasible-ray artifacts; a status code alone is not a mathematical certificate.
assumptions_latex: Artifact validity is checked against the original model.
Arithmetic and feasibility tolerances are recorded with the artifacts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each valid bundle certifies respectively optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.

notation.meaning: artifact bundles for the three conclusive statuses

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits an artifacts leaf, but the bundle taxonomy combines branch-and-bound infeasibility artifacts and linear feasible-ray artifacts without restricting the overall scope to the problem classes where those bundles are sufficient. No source supports the combined representation.

children.title: Nonconclusive Solve Status Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Nonconclusive and numerically ambiguous solve outcomes.

children.title: Limit Statuses
children.top_down_role: Nonconclusive outcomes caused by exhaustion of a configured computational budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Limit Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics of termination caused by a finite computational limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(t)\) be cumulative use of a declared computational resource and let \(L<+\infty\) be its limit. A limit status is applicable when the solve stops because \[R(t)\ge L\] before a conclusive certificate has been established. The status identifies the stopping cause, not the mathematical disposition of the model. Any incumbent may provide a feasible solution, and any valid global bound may provide a gap certificate, but neither is implied merely by the limit status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limit status says a resource budget stopped the solve before a conclusive certificate; incumbent and bound availability must be reported separately.
assumptions_latex: \(R(t)\) is the resource counter used by the configured limit.
No conclusive certificate was established before the limit trigger.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limit status alone implies neither optimality, infeasibility, unboundedness, nor incumbent existence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role and nonconclusive interpretation fit the leaf, but resource accounting, trigger timing, and precedence relative to a conclusive result are solver-specific and lack a manual citation.

children.title: Interruption Statuses
children.top_down_role: Outcomes caused by user, application, system, or callback interruption.

knowledge_statements.title: Interruption Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics of externally requested or asynchronously induced termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(t)\) denote receipt of an external stop event, such as a user request, callback decision, or process signal. An interruption status is applicable when termination occurs at the first handled state \[\tau=\inf\{t:E(t)=1\}\] and no conclusive status has precedence. The interruption explains why execution ended but asserts no model conclusion. Feasibility of a returned incumbent and validity of a returned bound remain separately checkable properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interruption status records an external stop event, not a conclusion about the model; returned incumbents and bounds need separate validation.
assumptions_latex: The solver distinguishes external interruption from internal resource limits.
Status precedence is documented when a conclusive certificate exists simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Interruption alone certifies only that an external stop event caused termination.

notation.meaning: indicator that an external stop event has been received
first solver state handling the interruption

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonconclusive interpretation is appropriate, but the classification of callbacks, signals, user requests, handling states, and simultaneous-status precedence depends on solver behavior and is unsupported by an authoritative locator.

children.title: Ambiguous Statuses
children.top_down_role: Outcomes whose available evidence does not support one conclusive interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between unresolved solver outcomes and mathematical conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose termination yields neither a valid feasible incumbent with matching global bound, nor exhaustive infeasibility exclusions, nor a feasible improving ray. Then the returned status is mathematically ambiguous among the remaining possibilities, even if diagnostics suggest infeasibility, unboundedness, or numerical failure. Formally, absence of all conclusive artifact predicates \(C_{\mathrm{opt}},C_{\mathrm{inf}},C_{\mathrm{unb}}\) gives \[
eg C_{\mathrm{opt}}\land
eg C_{\mathrm{inf}}\land
eg C_{\mathrm{unb}},\] which does not imply any one of their negated model properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without an optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness artifact, diagnostics cannot be promoted to a definite mathematical conclusion.
assumptions_latex: Artifact predicates are evaluated against the original model.
No independent exact certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of all conclusive certificate predicates leaves the model disposition unresolved.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is defensible and the logical warning is sound, but the three artifact predicates inherit problem-class-specific certificate assumptions and no authoritative solver or optimization source supports the proposed ambiguous-status taxonomy.

children.title: Incumbent Availability
children.top_down_role: Presence and usability of primal solutions under nonconclusive termination.

assumptions_latex: The reported solver state corresponds to a minimization MIP with feasible set \(F\).
Feasibility and integrality tolerances are fixed before interpreting the returned point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Incumbent availability yields a valid primal bound \(c^\top \hat x\), but does not certify optimality.

notation.meaning: MIP feasible set under the declared acceptance tolerances

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes possession of a feasible incumbent from the solver's nonconclusive termination reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonconclusive solve status has incumbent availability precisely when the solver returns a point \(\hat x\) accepted as belonging to \(F\). For a minimization problem, such a point supplies the primal bound \(c^\top\hat x\). The termination status alone does not imply that an incumbent exists: a time, node, memory, or user-interruption limit may occur before any feasible point is found. Conversely, availability of \(\hat x\) certifies neither global optimality nor a particular optimality gap unless a valid dual bound is also reported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limited or interrupted solve has an incumbent only if it returns an accepted feasible point; that point gives a primal bound but not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Availability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no citation supports the solver-specific meaning of incumbent availability, acceptance tolerances, or primal-bound semantics.

children.title: Numerical Status Qualification
children.top_down_role: Numerical conditions that weaken or qualify the reported solve outcome.

assumptions_latex: The solver reports feasibility, integrality, and optimality tolerances together with any numerical warning.
All residuals are evaluated using the solver's stated scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A qualified status supports only the claims whose residual and tolerance tests are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treats numerical qualification as a restriction on what may be inferred from a solver status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reported status \(s\) is numerically qualified by residual vector \(r\) and tolerance vector \(\tau\). A feasibility claim is accepted only when every applicable scaled primal, bound, and integrality residual satisfies \(r_i\leq\tau_i\); an optimality claim additionally requires the solver's stated dual and complementarity tests. If a numerical warning, unresolved instability, or failed residual test accompanies \(s\), then \(s\) must not be interpreted as an unqualified exact-arithmetic conclusion, even when its textual label is otherwise conclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interpret a solver status only through its residual tests, tolerances, scaling, and numerical warnings; a textual label alone is not an exact-arithmetic certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Status Qualification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed numerical qualification. Moreover, requiring dual and complementarity tests for every MIP optimality claim is too broad; MIP solvers commonly certify optimality through valid global bounds and a closing gap. Solver-specific status and residual semantics require an authoritative citation.

children.title: Presolve Reduction-Propagation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Global and local mechanisms that simplify models, contract domains, expose discrete structure, and retain recoverable relationships to the submitted problem.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Preprocessing and Probing Techniques for Mixed Integer Programming Problems
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Preprocessing and Probing Techniques for Mixed Integer Programming Problems

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Mahajan, Wiley Encyclopedia of Operations Research and Management Science, 2011

children.title: Feasibility-Preserving Structural Reductions
children.top_down_role: Reductions justified through explicit feasibility structure and recoverable variable relationships.

children.title: Row Feasibility Classification
children.top_down_role: Constraint-level redundancy and immediate infeasibility recognition.

children.title: Redundant Row Detection
children.top_down_role: Recognition of constraints removable without changing the relevant feasible set.

assumptions_latex: Each variable satisfies finite bounds \(l_j\leq x_j\leq u_j\).
The tested row is \(\alpha\leq a^\top x\leq\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\alpha\leq L\) and \(U\leq\beta\), deleting the row preserves the bounded-domain feasible set.

notation.meaning: minimum row activity over the variable-bound box
maximum row activity over the variable-bound box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval-activity redundancy test relative to current variable bounds.

source_refs.locator: 8.1 Implicit equalities and redundant constraints p. 99
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the interval activity bounds \[L=\sum_{j:a_j\geq0}a_jl_j+\sum_{j:a_j<0}a_ju_j,\qquad U=\sum_{j:a_j\geq0}a_ju_j+\sum_{j:a_j<0}a_jl_j.\] These are the exact minimum and maximum of \(a^\top x\) over the variable-bound box. Hence the row \(\alpha\leq a^\top x\leq\beta\) is redundant relative to that box whenever \(\alpha\leq L\) and \(U\leq\beta\). Removing such a row cannot remove or add any point satisfying the current variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute minimum and maximum row activity from variable bounds. The row is redundant when its entire activity interval lies within the row bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Row Detection

source_witnesses.locator: 8.1 Implicit equalities and redundant constraints p. 99
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Infeasible Row Detection
children.top_down_role: Recognition of individual constraints or row activities that establish inconsistency.

assumptions_latex: Each variable satisfies finite bounds \(l_j\leq x_j\leq u_j\).
The tested row is \(\alpha\leq a^\top x\leq\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U<\alpha\) or \(L>\beta\), the bounded-domain MIP is infeasible.

notation.meaning: minimum possible row activity over the bound box
maximum possible row activity over the bound box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-activity certificate of infeasibility for a single ranged row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) and \(U\) be the minimum and maximum of \(a^\top x\) over the current variable-bound box, computed by sign-aware endpoint selection. If \(U<\alpha\), no bounded point can satisfy the lower row bound. If \(L>\beta\), no bounded point can satisfy the upper row bound. Either strict separation is therefore a directly checkable certificate that the row, and consequently the full MIP containing it, is infeasible under the current bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row proves infeasibility when its greatest possible activity is below its lower bound or its least possible activity exceeds its upper bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Row Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-separation certificate is mathematically standard and the certificate content kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no source or locator for the interval-activity infeasibility test.

children.title: Row Classification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical, domain, or locality conditions affecting whether a row classification is valid.

assumptions_latex: The activity enclosure \([L,U]\) is computed from current variable bounds.
The row requires \(a^\top x\in[\alpha,\beta]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Inclusive containment gives redundancy, strict separation gives infeasibility, and all remaining interval configurations are undecided by this test.

notation.meaning: attainable activity interval over the bound box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and tolerance-aware boundaries separating redundant, infeasible, and undecided rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In exact arithmetic, classify the row as redundant when \([L,U]\subseteq[\alpha,\beta]\), and infeasible when \([L,U]\cap[\alpha,\beta]=\varnothing\), equivalently \(U<\alpha\) or \(L>\beta\). Boundary contact such as \(U=\alpha\) or \(L=\beta\) is feasible and is not strict infeasibility. Every other overlap is undecided by interval activity alone. With comparison tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), a sound implementation must use consistently relaxed redundancy tests and conservative strict-separation tests rather than silently treating near equality as exact separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Containment means redundant, strict disjointness means infeasible, boundary contact remains feasible, and partial overlap is undecided; tolerances must be applied conservatively.
knowledge_statements.title: Row Classification Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-arithmetic classification is sound, but the tolerance-aware part does not state explicit inequalities and does not establish which relaxed tests preserve exact feasibility. This implementation-sensitive claim needs authoritative source support.

children.title: Sparse-Object Reduction Family
children.top_down_role: Reductions exploiting determined or sparsely connected rows and columns.

children.title: Fixed Object Reductions
children.top_down_role: Elimination or simplification of variables or constraints determined by fixed values.

assumptions_latex: A variable \(x_k\) has equal finite bounds \(l_k=u_k=v\).
The original objective and constraints are affine in \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Substitution and later assignment \(x_k=v\) preserve feasibility, integrality, and objective values.

notation.meaning: coefficient of the fixed variable in row i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine fixed-variable elimination with exact postsolve recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(l_k=u_k=v\), replace every row term \(a_{ik}x_k\) by the constant \(a_{ik}v\), shift the corresponding row bounds by \(-a_{ik}v\), and add \(c_kv\) to the objective constant. Delete \(x_k\) after checking that \(v\) belongs to its declared domain, including integrality when applicable. Store the recovery assignment \(x_k:=v\). If a shifted row becomes empty, classify its constant feasibility before continuing. Output the reduced model together with the recovery assignment and objective offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitute a variable fixed by equal bounds, shift row bounds and the objective constant, delete it, and record its value for postsolve recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Object Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-variable algorithm is plausible, but no cited source supports it. The title says fixed objects while the record covers only fixed variables, so source-backed clarification of the intended terminal scope is also needed.

children.title: Empty Object Reductions
children.top_down_role: Treatment of rows or columns lacking active incidences.

assumptions_latex: An empty row has no variable coefficients.
An empty column variable retains its domain, bounds, and linear objective coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The prescribed row test and one-variable optimization either preserve an optimizer or certify infeasibility or unboundedness.

notation.meaning: objective coefficient of the empty-column variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve rules for coefficient-free rows and columns in a minimization MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an empty row, test whether \(0\in[\alpha_i,\beta_i]\); delete the row if true and declare infeasibility otherwise. For an empty column \(x_j\), solve \(\min\{c_jx_j:x_j\in D_j\}\), where \(D_j\) is its bounded or integral domain. If this scalar problem is unbounded below, declare the MIP unbounded; otherwise select a minimizing value, add its contribution to the objective constant, delete the column, and record the selected value. When \(c_j=0\), any domain value may be recorded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete a feasible empty row, reject an infeasible one, and optimize an unconstrained empty-column variable over its domain before deleting and recording it.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Object Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the empty-row and empty-column rules. The empty-column scalar problem may also be infeasible when its retained domain is empty; the statement handles only an attained minimum or unboundedness and therefore omits a necessary case.

children.title: Singleton Object Reductions
children.top_down_role: Reductions involving rows or columns with exactly one active incidence.

assumptions_latex: A singleton row has the form \(\alpha\leq ax_j\leq\beta\) with \(a\neq0\).
The current domain of \(x_j\) is bounded and may require integrality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intersecting the derived interval with the current domain preserves exactly the solutions satisfying the singleton row.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singleton-row bound propagation, including sign reversal and integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the implied real interval \([\min\{\alpha/a,\beta/a\},\max\{\alpha/a,\beta/a\}]\) and intersect it with the current domain of \(x_j\). If \(x_j\) is integral, replace the implied endpoints by their inward integer roundings. An empty intersection certifies infeasibility; a singleton intersection fixes \(x_j\); otherwise update its bounds. After the update, delete the singleton row because the revised domain enforces it. Store any fixing or bound change needed by postsolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton row becomes a bound interval after sign-aware division; intersect it with the variable domain, apply integer rounding, and detect fixing or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Singleton Object Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singleton-row reduction fits the leaf and is broadly correct, but it has no citation. The integer case should explicitly identify ceiling of the lower endpoint and floor of the upper endpoint rather than relying on the undefined phrase “inward integer roundings.”

children.title: Sparse-Object Recovery Records
children.top_down_role: Postsolve information retained when sparse-object reductions remove model components.

assumptions_latex: Every presolve deletion or substitution has an exact inverse reconstruction rule.
Recovery records are retained in reverse-applicable order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful reverse replay produces an original-model point \(x\) with objective \(c^\top x=\bar c+\bar c^{\top}y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postsolve reconstruction certificate for fixed, empty, and singleton reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse-object recovery record stores the eliminated object identifier, its inverse assignment or bound rule, affected coefficients or row bounds, domain information, and objective offset. Given a reduced solution \(y\), replay records in reverse elimination order to construct \(x\). Each replay step must restore the eliminated variable or row so that its original bounds, integrality requirement, and incident constraints hold. The completed record stack is a verifiable recovery certificate when direct evaluation confirms original-model feasibility and the objective identity \(c^\top x=\bar c+\bar c^{\top}y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery records store inverse transformations and objective offsets; reverse replay reconstructs an original feasible solution whose constraints, domains, and objective can be checked directly.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Object Recovery Records

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed recovery-certificate fields or guarantee. The objective identity is internally inconsistent because \(\bar c\) is defined as a scalar offset but is also used as the coefficient vector in \(\bar c^{\top}y\).

children.title: Variable-Elimination Calculus
children.top_down_role: Variable elimination through explicit and implied relationships.

children.title: Variable Substitution
children.top_down_role: Elimination using an explicit recoverable relationship for a variable.

assumptions_latex: An exact equality implies \(x_k=\gamma+q^\top z\).
All domain restrictions induced by the substitution are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(x_k\) and reconstructing it by \(x_k=\gamma+q^\top z\) preserves feasible solutions and objective values.

notation.meaning: remaining variables occurring in the defining equality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact affine substitution with domain transfer and postsolve reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select an equality that can be solved as \(x_k=\gamma+q^\top z\). Replace every occurrence of \(x_k\) in the objective and remaining constraints by this affine expression, remove the defining equality and the column of \(x_k\), and transfer the bounds and domain of \(x_k\) to valid restrictions on \(z\). If \(x_k\) is integral, retain the induced integrality or congruence condition unless it is already implied. Store the affine recovery formula, and output the transformed model only when substitution is algebraically exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve an exact equality for one variable, substitute it everywhere, preserve its induced domain restrictions, and store the affine formula for reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Substitution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches exact affine variable substitution and correctly notes induced domain and congruence restrictions, but no cited source supports the MIP-specific equivalence and reconstruction claims.

children.title: Variable Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Elimination through a compact relation involving a limited set of model objects.

assumptions_latex: An equality \(ax_i+bx_j=d\) has \(a\neq0\).
Substitution preserves every induced bound and domain restriction on \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregation \(x_i=d/a-(b/a)x_j\) gives an exact reduced representation when all induced domain conditions are retained.

notation.meaning: coefficients and right-hand side of the defining equality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-variable affine aggregation distinguished from multiaggregation over several surviving variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(ax_i+bx_j=d\) with \(a\neq0\), represent the eliminated variable by \(x_i=d/a-(b/a)x_j\). Substitute this expression into all other rows and the objective, then delete the defining equality and \(x_i\). Intersect the domain of \(x_j\) with the restrictions induced by the bounds and domain of \(x_i\). For integral variables, divisibility or congruence conditions must be retained unless automatically satisfied. The inverse record reconstructs \(x_i\) from the surviving value of \(x_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-variable equality can replace one variable by an affine function of the other, provided bounds, integrality, and any congruence restrictions are preserved.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Aggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-variable aggregation formula is plausible, but no source supports its domain-transfer and congruence requirements. The statement is predominantly a presolve procedure, so an authoritative source is also needed to justify using representation rather than algorithm as the terminal content kind.

children.title: Variable Multiaggregation
children.top_down_role: Elimination through a broader linear relation involving multiple retained variables.

assumptions_latex: An exact equality yields \(x_k=\gamma+\sum_{j\in J}q_jx_j\) with \(|J|\geq2\).
All induced bounds, integrality conditions, and congruences are representable in the reduced model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiaggregation is equivalent to the original formulation under projection and affine reconstruction.

notation.meaning: indices of surviving variables in the affine expression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine elimination of one variable using two or more surviving variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent \(x_k\) by \(x_k=\gamma+\sum_{j\in J}q_jx_j\), where \(|J|\geq2\), and substitute this expression into every other row and the objective. Delete \(x_k\) and its defining equality only after transferring its bounds and domain to the variables indexed by \(J\). If \(x_k\) is integral, preserve the induced integrality or congruence restriction. Store the affine expression for reverse reconstruction. The transformation is exact when projection of the original feasible set onto the surviving variables equals the reduced feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiaggregation eliminates one variable as an affine function of several survivors while retaining all induced bounds, integrality conditions, and a reconstruction formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Multiaggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiaggregation statement is plausible under its strong representability assumption, but no source supports the projection-equivalence, induced-domain, or congruence claims. Its procedural form also raises an unresolved algorithm-versus-representation content-kind question.

children.title: Elimination Fill Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural density, numerical quality, and recovery costs associated with elimination choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Fill Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural cost of an exact equality-based variable elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let pivot row \(p\) be an equality containing variable \(x_j\), and let \(S_i\) denote the support of row \(i\). Substitution of \(x_j\) into every other incident row \(i\) produces support contained in \((S_i\setminus\{j\})\cup(S_p\setminus\{j\})\). Hence its structural fill is bounded by \[\Delta_j=\sum_{i\ne p:\,j\in S_i}\left|(S_p\setminus\{j\})\setminus S_i\right|.\] An exact elimination reduces one column and at least one row but may increase nonzeros by as much as \(\Delta_j\); cancellation can only reduce this bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact substitution removes a variable but can create coefficients wherever the pivot row contains variables absent from other incident rows.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{pj}\ne 0\) and row \(p\) is an equality.
The substitution preserves the variable domain and permits reconstruction of \(x_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{fill}(j)\le \Delta_j\), with possible strict inequality from coefficient cancellation.

notation.meaning: structural upper bound on introduced nonzeros

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The structural support bound is plausible and fits the property container, but no cited source supports the presolve-specific fill formula or its interpretation.

children.title: Structural Equivalence-Dominance Classes
children.top_down_role: Recognition and consolidation of equivalent or dominated model objects.

children.title: Parallel Structure
children.top_down_role: Rows or columns related through proportional coefficient patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive parallelism of ranged linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For ranged rows \(\ell_k\le a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le u_k\), rows \(1\) and \(2\) have parallel structure when there exists \(\lambda>0\) such that \(a_2=\lambda a_1\). After normalization, row \(2\) is equivalent to the interval restriction \(\ell_2/\lambda\le a_1^{\mathsf T}x\le u_2/\lambda\). Their conjunction is therefore represented by \[\max\{\ell_1,\ell_2/\lambda\}\le a_1^{\mathsf T}x\le\min\{u_1,u_2/\lambda\}.\] It is infeasible exactly when the resulting lower bound exceeds the resulting upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel rows share a positive scalar multiple of the same normal and can be intersected as bounds on one linear form.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) belongs to the common variable domain \(X\).
Infinite endpoints are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two parallel rows are equivalent on \(X\) to their normalized interval intersection.

notation.meaning: permitted interval for the row activity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-parallel-row definition and interval intersection are mathematically coherent and fit the container, but the record supplies no evidence.

children.title: Duplicate Structure
children.top_down_role: Rows, columns, or logical objects with equivalent active content.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplication of normalized linear rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two linear rows are duplicates when, after multiplication of one row by a positive scalar, their coefficient vectors and both activity bounds coincide. Equivalently, for some \(\lambda>0\), \(a_2=\lambda a_1\), \(\ell_2=\lambda\ell_1\), and \(u_2=\lambda u_1\). For every \(x\) in the common domain, one row is satisfied if and only if the other is satisfied. Consequently, deleting either row preserves the feasible set, although row names and associated metadata require a reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate rows impose exactly the same normalized activity interval, so either row may be removed without changing feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Both rows use the same variables and variable domain.
Scaling uses \(\lambda>0\), so inequality directions are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in X:\ell_1\le a_1^{\mathsf T}x\le u_1\}=\{x\in X:\ell_2\le a_2^{\mathsf T}x\le u_2\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duplicate-row characterization is precise and appropriately classified as a definition, but it has no supporting citation.

children.title: Dominated Structure
children.top_down_role: Model objects rendered unnecessary by stronger or preferable alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominated Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy among positively parallel ranged rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose rows \(1\) and \(2\) are positively parallel with \(a_2=\lambda a_1\) and \(\lambda>0\). Row \(1\) dominates row \(2\) precisely when its normalized activity interval is contained in that of row \(2\): \[[\ell_1,u_1]\subseteq[\ell_2/\lambda,u_2/\lambda].\] Then every point satisfying row \(1\) also satisfies row \(2\), so row \(2\) is redundant in their conjunction. If neither normalized interval contains the other, neither row alone dominates, and consolidation requires their interval intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among parallel rows, the tighter normalized activity interval dominates the wider one and makes the wider row redundant.
assumptions_latex: \(a_2=\lambda a_1\) for some \(\lambda>0\).
Both rows are interpreted over the same domain \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Normalized interval containment implies \(F_1\subseteq F_2\), permitting deletion of row \(2\).

notation.meaning: points in the common domain satisfying row k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Normalized interval containment correctly expresses redundancy for positively parallel ranged rows, but no source supports the stated dominance convention or reduction.

children.title: Consolidation Safety Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Objective, domain, numerical, or recovery conditions limiting structural consolidation.

knowledge_statements.title: Consolidation Safety Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of deleting structurally similar rows or columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Structural equality of coefficient rows or columns is insufficient for consolidation unless bounds, integrality, objective coefficients, and a solution-reconstruction map are also preserved. For example, consider \(\min\{y:x+y\ge1,\ x,y\in\{0,1\}\}\). The columns of \(x\) and \(y\) in the constraint matrix are identical, but deleting \(x\) and retaining only \(y\) yields \(\min\{y:y\ge1,\ y\in\{0,1\}\}=1\), whereas the original optimum is \(0\). Thus duplicate-column consolidation based only on matrix structure is unsafe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical matrix columns cannot be merged solely by structure; differing objectives, bounds, or domains can change the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The example is a minimization problem.
Naive consolidation deletes one identical column without encoding its objective or domain choices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matrix-column equality alone does not imply optimization equivalence under consolidation.

notation.meaning: binary decision variables in the counterexample

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is correct and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the broader safety claim concerning bounds, integrality, objectives, metadata, and reconstruction lacks evidence.

children.title: Sparsity-Fill Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Reduction choices that balance elimination against matrix density.

children.title: Matrix Sparsification
children.top_down_role: Reduction choices intended to decrease active matrix incidence or storage.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Sparsification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sparsification of a linear equality subsystem by row operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an equality subsystem \(Ax=b\). Initialize \((\bar A,\bar b)=(A,b)\). Repeatedly choose an elementary invertible row operation \(E\) for which \(\operatorname{nnz}(E\bar A)<\operatorname{nnz}(\bar A)\), and update \((\bar A,\bar b)\leftarrow(E\bar A,E\bar b)\). Stop when no operation in the prescribed candidate set decreases the nonzero count, and output \((\bar A,\bar b)\) together with the product \(U\) of all accepted operations. Since \(U\) is invertible, \(Ax=b\) and \(UAx=Ub\) have identical solution sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply invertible row operations to an equality subsystem whenever they reduce nonzeros; the resulting subsystem has the same solutions.
assumptions_latex: All transformed rows are equalities.
Every accepted row-operation matrix \(E\) is invertible.
Arithmetic is exact, or numerical acceptance safeguards certify equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \((\bar A,\bar b)=(UA,Ub)\) with \(U\) invertible and an unchanged equality-feasible set.

notation.meaning: number of structurally nonzero entries in A

children.title: Fill Growth Control
children.top_down_role: Limits on new nonzeros introduced by substitution, aggregation, or reformulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Fill Growth Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance condition for substitution-based presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For elimination of \(x_j\) with pivot support \(S_p\), define the predicted fill \[\widehat\Delta_j=\sum_{i\ne p:\,j\in S_i}\left|(S_p\setminus\{j\})\setminus S_iight|.\] Given an absolute fill budget \(B\ge0\) and relative budget \(\rho\ge0\), accept the elimination only if \[\widehat\Delta_j\le B+\rho\sum_{i:\,j\in S_i}|S_i|.\] This condition bounds predicted structural growth; it does not itself establish that the substitution preserves feasibility, integrality, or numerical stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an elimination only when its predicted new nonzeros fit a chosen absolute-plus-relative fill budget.
assumptions_latex: The pivot row and all rows incident to \(x_j\) are known.
\(B\ge0\) and \(\rho\ge0\) are fixed presolve parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies the predicted fill satisfies the configured absolute-plus-relative budget.

notation.meaning: predicted fill from eliminating variable j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally consistent and explicitly distinguished from an equivalence guarantee, but the absolute-plus-relative budget is a solver policy requiring a specific source.

children.title: Density-Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Effects of matrix density on memory, factorization, propagation, and later solver work.

knowledge_statements.title: Density-Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse-work proxies for row-wise and pair-generating presolve operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let row \(i\) contain \(d_i\) nonzeros and let \(N=\sum_i d_i\). A full row-wise scan costs \(O(N)\) arithmetic or inspection operations. A transformation that considers every unordered pair of nonzeros within each row costs \[O\!\left(\sum_i d_i^2\right),\] which is at most \(O(d_{\max}N)\). Consequently, fill that raises row densities can change a nominally linear sparse scan into substantially more expensive pair-generating work, even when the row count and column count decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense rows make pair-generating presolve work quadratic in row support, so reducing dimensions can still increase computational cost.
assumptions_latex: Sparse rows are stored with iteration cost proportional to their support size.
Each candidate pair is processed in constant amortized time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pair-generating work is \(O(\sum_i d_i^2)\subseteq O(d_{\max}N)\), while a row scan is \(O(N)\).

notation.meaning: number of nonzeros in row i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sparse-work bounds follow from the stated storage and constant-amortized-processing assumptions and fit a complexity-bound container, but no source supports their presolve interpretation.

children.title: Objective-Dual Reduction Calculus
children.top_down_role: Presolve reductions using objective direction, dominance, and dual-side information.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Presolvers: dominated columns, dual aggregation, dual compensation, and dual inference

children.title: Dual-Side Variable Inference
children.top_down_role: Variable reductions obtained from objective and constraint-direction information.

children.title: Dual Fixing
children.top_down_role: Variable fixing justified by objective direction plus constraint-side information.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Fixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost fixing for an integer variable at its lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization MIP with incumbent value \(U\). Suppose a valid dual certificate for its LP relaxation gives lower bound \(L\) and, for every original feasible point, \[c^{\mathsf T}x\ge L+r_j(x_j-\ell_j),\] where \(r_j>0\), \(x_j\ge\ell_j\), and every admissible value above \(\ell_j\) satisfies \(x_j-\ell_j\ge\delta_j>0\). If \(L+r_j\delta_j\ge U\), then no solution with objective strictly below \(U\) can have \(x_j>\ell_j\); hence \(x_j=\ell_j\) is a valid fixing for an improving-solution search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive certified reduced-cost penalty fixes an integer variable at its lower bound when any increase reaches the incumbent cutoff.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
The displayed dual inequality is valid for every original MIP-feasible point.
\(\delta_j\) is a valid minimum positive step above \(\ell_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L+r_j\delta_j\ge U\) certifies \(x_j=\ell_j\) for the search region \(c^{\mathsf T}x<U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate correctly concerns only solutions strictly improving the incumbent and states a minimum positive domain step, but reduced-cost fixing requires an authoritative source.

children.title: Dual Inference
children.top_down_role: Broader domain or structural deductions derived from dual-side reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain reduction from dual lower bounds conditioned on variable values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization MIP with incumbent value \(U\), let \(D_j\) be the domain of variable \(x_j\). If a dual or relaxation argument supplies a valid conditional lower bound \(L_j(v)\) satisfying \[L_j(v)\le\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in F,\ x_j=v\}\] for every \(v\in D_j\), then every value with \(L_j(v)\ge U\) may be removed when searching for a solution strictly improving \(U\). If all values are removed, no improving solution exists; if one value remains, the variable may be fixed to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable value can be removed when a valid dual bound conditioned on that value reaches the incumbent objective.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the original MIP-feasible set.
\(U\) is attained by a feasible incumbent.
Each \(L_j(v)\) is valid for the corresponding conditional feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_j\leftarrow\{v\in D_j:L_j(v)<U\}\) preserves every solution strictly improving the incumbent.

notation.meaning: conditional dual lower bound at value v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-bound exclusion principle is mathematically coherent and preserves strictly improving solutions, but it has no supporting citation.

children.title: Objective-Direction Dependence
children.top_down_role: Dependence of dual reductions on optimization sense, objective coefficients, and cutoff context.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Direction Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-sensitive form of objective-based dual reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual inference depends on the optimization direction. For minimization, a conditional lower bound \(L_j(v)\) excludes value \(v\) from a strictly improving search when \(L_j(v)\ge U\), where \(U\) is an incumbent upper bound. For maximization, a conditional upper bound \(H_j(v)\) excludes \(v\) when \(H_j(v)\le L\), where \(L\) is an incumbent lower bound. Negating the objective interchanges these rules and reverses the sign interpretation of reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimization uses lower bounds against an incumbent upper bound; maximization uses upper bounds against an incumbent lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Conditional bounds are valid on the original feasible set.
The incumbent cutoff corresponds to the stated optimization direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective negation swaps lower-bound and upper-bound exclusion tests and reverses reduced-cost signs.

notation.meaning: minimization upper cutoff and maximization lower cutoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization and maximization cutoff directions are consistent and fit the property container, but the objective-direction and reduced-cost sign claims lack evidence.

children.title: Dual-Inference Safety Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where feasibility preservation, solution enumeration, or later model changes restrict dual reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Inference Safety Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity limits for objective-dependent domain reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual inference is safe only when its bound is valid for every original feasible point covered by the inferred domain restriction, its cutoff is supplied by a feasible incumbent, and objective direction is handled correctly. Direction errors can destroy optimality: in \(\min\{-x:x\in\{0,1\}\}\), applying the positive-cost lower-fixing rule as though the coefficient were \(+1\) fixes \(x=0\), although the unique optimum is \(x=1\) with value \(-1\). Uncertified multipliers, stale transformations, or unsupported numerical comparisons likewise provide no valid fixing certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual fixing becomes unsafe if the bound, incumbent, transformed model, numerical comparison, or optimization direction is invalid.
assumptions_latex: The counterexample uses exact arithmetic.
The erroneous rule treats the minimization coefficient as having the opposite sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a valid direction-consistent bound and feasible cutoff, dual inference need not preserve an optimum.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direction-error counterexample is correct and the failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but the broader claims about multipliers, stale transformations, and numerical comparisons require sources.

children.title: Dominated-Column Reductions
children.top_down_role: Column comparisons supporting fixing, aggregation, or removal.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominated-Column Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient transfer-dominance test for fixing a variable at its lower bound in a minimization MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set of \(\min\{c^\top x:x\in F\}\), and suppose \(x_j\geq \ell_j\) on \(F\). Column \(j\) is lower-bound dominated by column \(k\) if, for every \(x\in F\), the point \(y=x-(x_j-\ell_j)e_j+(x_j-\ell_j)e_k\) belongs to \(F\), respects all variable domains, and satisfies \(c^\top y\leq c^\top x\). If the problem has an optimal solution, then it has an optimal solution with \(x_j=\ell_j\); hence fixing \(x_j\) at \(\ell_j\) preserves the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every amount of one column can be transferred to another without losing feasibility or worsening cost, the dominated variable may be fixed at its lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\) and the minimum is attained.
The stated transfer preserves continuous and discrete variable domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in F}c^\top x=\min\{c^\top x:x\in F,\ x_j=\ell_j\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sufficient transfer condition is mathematically sound, matches the dominated-column leaf, and uses an appropriate condition container. No inspectable source is supplied for this presolve reduction.

children.title: Objective Normalization-Integrality System
children.top_down_role: Objective transformations and recognized objective-value structure.

children.title: Objective Scaling
children.top_down_role: Rescaling of objective coefficients or values for representation or numerical handling.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive scaling of a minimization objective and the associated value conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\), choose a finite scalar \(s>0\) and define \(\widetilde f(x)=f(x)/s\). Then \(f(x)\leq f(y)\) if and only if \(\widetilde f(x)\leq\widetilde f(y)\). Consequently, the original and scaled problems have identical minimizers. Their infima satisfy \(v=s\widetilde v\), with the equality interpreted in the extended-real sense when appropriate. A negative scale reverses the optimization sense, while a zero scale generally destroys objective information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing an objective by a positive constant preserves its minimizers, and the original optimal value is the scaled value multiplied by that constant.
assumptions_latex: Both problems use the same feasible set \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\widetilde f(x)\) and \(v=s\widetilde v\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-scaling property, minimizer preservation, and affine value recovery are correct and aligned with Objective Scaling, but the record has no cited source.

children.title: Objective Shifting
children.top_down_role: Constant offsets introduced or removed while preserving solution ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Shifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Addition of a decision-independent constant to a minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible set \(F\), objective \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\), and constant \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), define \(\widetilde f(x)=f(x)-\beta\). For all \(x,y\in F\), \(f(x)\leq f(y)\) if and only if \(\widetilde f(x)\leq\widetilde f(y)\). Thus shifting preserves the complete ordering of feasible solutions and the set of minimizers. If \(v=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(\widetilde v=\inf_{x\in F}\widetilde f(x)\), then \(v=\widetilde v+\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a constant from every objective value preserves all solution rankings and shifts the optimal value by the same constant.
assumptions_latex: \(\beta\) is independent of the decision vector.
Both objectives are evaluated on the same feasible set \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\widetilde f(x)\) and \(v=\widetilde v+\beta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constant-shift property is precise, correctly quantified, and suitable for this leaf, but no inspectable source is provided.

children.title: Objective Integrality
children.top_down_role: Discrete objective-value structure available for bounds, gaps, or termination interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lattice structure of objective values over integer-feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), \(c\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), and \(f(x)=\alpha+c^\top x\), where \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\). With \(g=\gcd(|c_i|:c_i\neq0)\), every feasible objective value belongs to \(\alpha+g\mathbb{Z}\); if \(c=0\), the value is constantly \(\alpha\). Therefore any valid lower bound \(L\) for a minimization problem may be strengthened to the smallest point of \(\alpha+g\mathbb{Z}\) not below \(L\), namely \(\alpha+g\lceil(L-\alpha)/g\rceil\), when \(g>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer linear objective over integer variables lies on a known lattice, allowing lower bounds to be rounded upward to the next attainable lattice value.
assumptions_latex: All variables contributing nonzero objective coefficients are integer-valued.
\(c\in\mathbb{Z}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\in\alpha+g\mathbb{Z}\) and \(L\) strengthens to \(\alpha+g\lceil(L-\alpha)/g\rceil\) for \(g>0\).

notation.meaning: greatest common divisor of nonzero objective coefficients

children.title: Objective Value Recovery
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between transformed objective values and values reported for the submitted model.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Value Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery after a recorded positive scaling and constant shift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a transformed objective value \(\widetilde z\), a stored scale \(s>0\), and a stored shift \(\beta\) satisfying \(\widetilde f(x)=(f(x)-\beta)/s\) for every feasible \(x\). Compute \(z=s\widetilde z+\beta\) and output \(z\) as the corresponding original objective value. Apply the same affine map to finite primal bounds, dual bounds, and incumbent values. For minimization, multiplying by \(s>0\) preserves bound direction; infinite bounds retain their signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover the original objective value by multiplying the transformed value by the stored positive scale and adding the stored shift.
assumptions_latex: The transformation record satisfies \(\widetilde f=(f-\beta)/s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z=f(x)=s\widetilde f(x)+\beta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine recovery algorithm is correct, including preservation of bound direction for a positive scale, and algorithm is the proper content kind. It lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Dual-Reduction Safety Regimes
children.top_down_role: Restrictions arising from solution enumeration, reoptimization, and certificate requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Reduction Safety Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety criteria distinguishing optimal-value preservation from preservation required by richer solver tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a reduction map an original feasible set \(F\) to \(F'\), with reconstruction relation \(R\subseteq F'\times F\). It is optimality-safe if the optimal values agree and every optimal \(y\in F'\) has some optimal reconstruction \(x\in F\). It is enumeration-safe only if \(R\) reconstructs every requested original solution without loss or duplication. It is reoptimization-safe only if its validity assumptions remain true under every permitted model modification. It is certificate-safe only if reduced certificates can be checked directly or transformed into certificates valid for the original model. Optimality safety alone implies none of the latter three conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduction preserving one optimum may still be unsafe for enumerating solutions, modifying the model, or producing independently checkable original-model certificates.
assumptions_latex: The intended solver task and permitted model modifications are specified.
A reconstruction relation \(R\) is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{optimality-safe}\not\Rightarrow\text{enumeration-safe, reoptimization-safe, or certificate-safe}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinctions fit the safety-regimes container, but the proposed enumeration, reoptimization, and certificate criteria constitute a solver-safety taxonomy whose exact meanings and non-implications require authoritative support.

children.title: Constraint-Data Strengthening Pair

children.title: Coefficient Reduction
children.top_down_role: Modification of constraint coefficients to improve representation or discrete strength.

assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i a_i x_i\geq b\}=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i\min(a_i,b)x_i\geq b\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient capping for a nonnegative binary covering inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the binary covering inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\geq b\), where \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), \(a_i\geq0\), and \(b>0\). Define \(a_i'=\min\{a_i,b\}\). Over \(\{0,1\}^n\), the inequalities \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\geq b\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i'x_i\geq b\) have exactly the same satisfying assignments. Thus capping coefficients at the right-hand side is an equivalence-preserving reduction under the stated assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonnegative binary covering row, every coefficient exceeding the positive right-hand side can be capped at that right-hand side without changing feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Reduction

children.title: Constraint-Side Tightening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening of lower or upper constraint sides using domain information.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Side Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rounding a row bound when its left-hand side is integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)\in\mathbb{Z}\) for every point \(x\) in the variable domain. For any \(b\in\mathbb{R}\), the inequality \(h(x)\leq b\) is equivalent on that domain to \(h(x)\leq\lfloor b\rfloor\), and \(h(x)\geq b\) is equivalent to \(h(x)\geq\lceil b\rceil\). In particular, if \(h(x)=a^\top x\) with \(a\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) and \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), the right-hand side can be rounded inward without removing or adding integer-feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a row's left side is always integral, an upper bound may be floored and a lower bound ceiled without changing discrete feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(h(x)\in\mathbb{Z}\) throughout the relevant variable domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h(x)\leq b\iff h(x)\leq\lfloor b\rfloor\) and \(h(x)\geq b\iff h(x)\geq\lceil b\rceil\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inward-rounding equivalences are correct under the explicitly stated integer-valued activity hypothesis and fit Constraint-Side Tightening. No source is supplied.

children.title: Strengthening Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which modified constraint data preserves the intended feasible solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Strengthening Equivalence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality is essential for inward rounding of a constraint side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equivalence \(h(x)\leq b\iff h(x)\leq\lfloor b\rfloor\) fails if \(h\) is not integer-valued. For example, on \(D=[0,2]\), the constraint \(x\leq1.7\) admits every \(x\in[0,1.7]\), whereas the rounded constraint \(x\leq1\) removes all \(x\in(1,1.7]\). On the integer domain \(D\cap\mathbb{Z}\), the two constraints are equivalent. Hence side tightening must be justified relative to the actual domain; validity only for integer points does not imply preservation of the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding a row bound inward is equivalent on an integer domain but can cut feasible points from the continuous relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The proposed strengthening replaces \(x\leq1.7\) by \(x\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in[0,2]:x\leq1.7\}\neq\{x\in[0,2]:x\leq1\}\), but equality holds after intersecting both sets with \(\mathbb{Z}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly identifies the continuous-relaxation boundary of inward rounding, and failure_boundary is the proper content kind. It lacks an inspectable source.

\(b,a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\mathbb{Z}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of a continuous variable forced to be integral by an integer equality.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\) be declared continuous, and suppose every feasible point satisfies \(z=b-\sum_{i=1}^m a_i x_i\), where \(b,a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(z\in\mathbb{Z}\) at every feasible point. Consequently, replacing the continuous declaration of \(z\) by an integer declaration does not change the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous variable is implied integer when an equality expresses it as an integer constant minus an integer combination of integer variables.

children.title: Binary Domain Conversion
children.top_down_role: Normalization of eligible integral variables to binary-domain representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Domain Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conversion of a bounded integer domain containing only zero and one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be integer-valued and satisfy \(0\leq x\leq1\). Then its domain is exactly \(\{0,1\}\), so replacing the integer declaration and bounds by the binary declaration \(x\in\{0,1\}\) preserves every feasible solution and every objective value. Conversely, a binary declaration implies integrality and these bounds. The conversion is not valid from the bounds alone when \(x\) is continuous, because then every value in \([0,1]\) is permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer variable bounded between zero and one is exactly binary; a continuous variable with the same bounds is not.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{Z}\).
\(0\leq x\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{Z},\ 0\leq x\leq1\iff x\in\{0,1\}\).

children.title: Discrete-Domain Validity
children.top_down_role: Scope and persistence of inferred discrete domains under reductions or model changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Domain Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection criterion for validity of a discrete-domain normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) and \(D'\) be original and normalized discrete domains. A domain conversion \(T:D\to D'\) is validity-preserving if \(T\) is bijective, its inverse is retained, and every transformed constraint and objective satisfies \(g_r'(T(x))=g_r(x)\) and \(f'(T(x))=f(x)\) for all \(x\in D\). Under these conditions, feasibility, infeasibility, objective values, and optimal solutions correspond exactly through \(T\). If injectivity, surjectivity, or exact reconstruction fails, the conversion may merge solutions, introduce spurious solutions, or prevent recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete-domain normalization is exact when it is bijective and preserves every constraint and objective value under the variable mapping.
assumptions_latex: \(T:D\to D'\) is bijective with a retained inverse.
Constraints and objective are transformed by exact substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is feasible and optimal in \(D\) if and only if \(T(x)\) is feasible and optimal in \(D'\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bijective exact-substitution criterion is a sufficient condition for preservation of feasibility, objective values, and optima and fits the validity leaf. No authoritative source is supplied for the general transformation criterion.

children.title: Constraint-Semantics Upgrade Interface
children.top_down_role: Recovery of specialized constraint semantics from generic algebraic input.

children.title: Constraint-Type Recognition
children.top_down_role: Identification of specialized constraint structure within generic algebraic input.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Type Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recognition of a semantic constraint from algebraic rows and current variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j\) be the current variable domain, let \(R\) be a set of algebraic constraints, and let \(P_\theta(x)\) be a candidate semantic predicate with parameters \(\theta\) computed from \(R\). The pair \((R,D)\) is recognized as type \(P\) precisely when parameter extraction is unambiguous and \[\{x\in D:x\text{ satisfies }R\}=\{x\in D:P_\theta(x)\}.\] Recognition must include every integrality, bound, coefficient-sign, and literal-complement condition used by the equivalence; syntactic resemblance alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row set receives a semantic type only when its feasible points on the current domains equal exactly those satisfying the extracted semantic predicate.
assumptions_latex: \(D_j\subseteq\mathbb R\) is the current domain of variable \(x_j\).
All parameters \(\theta\) used by the recognized type are uniquely determined from \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) and \(P_\theta\) define identical feasible subsets of \(D\).
review_flags: solver-specific recognition criteria require later source certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence criterion is precise and the condition kind fits the leaf, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not establish solver-side recognition criteria, parameter uniqueness, or the listed eligibility checks.

children.title: Constraint Representation Upgrading
children.top_down_role: Replacement or augmentation of generic rows with specialized solver representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Representation Upgrading
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving replacement of recognized rows by a solver-native semantic constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a domain \(D\), recognized rows \(R\), and a supported semantic constraint \(C_\theta\). Verify \(\{x\in D:x\models R\}=\{x\in D:x\models C_\theta\}\), construct \(C_\theta\), and retain a mapping from \(C_\theta\) to every replaced row. Deactivate \(R\) only after the semantic constraint passes consistency checks and enters the active model. The upgraded model uses \(C_\theta\) for propagation, separation, and branching, while solution checking and postsolve reconstruction use the retained mapping. If any verification or construction step fails, output the original active rows unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified equivalent rows are replaced by a native semantic constraint, with a reconstruction map retained; any failed check leaves the algebraic rows active.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) has been recognized as \(C_\theta\) on the current domain \(D\).
The solver supports construction and checking of \(C_\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The upgraded and original models have the same feasible points in \(D\).
review_flags: postsolve mapping requirement needs solver-specific corroboration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the citations do not support native-constraint construction, row deactivation, reconstruction mapping, or the claim that the upgraded representation is used for propagation, separation, and branching.

children.title: Upgrade Eligibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural, numerical, and semantic conditions governing safe representation upgrades.

knowledge_statements.title: Upgrade Eligibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions beyond which semantic replacement cannot safely deactivate the original algebraic rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the original rows, let \(C_\theta\) be a proposed semantic replacement, and let \(D\) be their common validity domain. Deactivation of \(R\) is eligible only if \[\{x\in D:x\models R\}=\{x\in D:x\models C_\theta\},\] every domain and integrality assumption required by this equality is enforced, the solver's construction and feasibility checks preserve the certified interpretation, and postsolve reconstruction is defined. If any requirement is not certified, \(R\) must remain active, although a separately valid redundant annotation or inference structure may be retained. A one-way implication alone does not justify replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Original rows may be deactivated only after feasible-set equivalence, required domains, implementation consistency, and reconstruction have all been certified; one-way implication permits inference but not replacement.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) and \(C_\theta\) are interpreted on the same validity domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deactivation of \(R\) requires exact feasible-set equivalence on \(D\) together with certified implementation and reconstruction conditions.
review_flags: dedicated solver source required for implementation eligibility checks

children.title: Fallback Algebraic Representation
children.top_down_role: Retention or restoration of generic algebraic forms when specialized handling is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Fallback Algebraic Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe retained-row representation when a semantic upgrade is unavailable or uncertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\{r_k(x)\le 0:k\in K_\le\}\cup\{r_k(x)=0:k\in K_=\}\) be the original algebraic representation on domain \(D\). If semantic recognition or upgrade eligibility fails, the fallback model retains every member of \(R\) with its original sense, coefficients, variable domains, and integrality restrictions. Optional extracted metadata may guide propagation or separation, but it cannot replace a row unless exact equivalence has subsequently been certified. Thus the fallback feasible set is \[F_R=\{x\in D:r_k(x)\le0\ (k\in K_\le),\ r_k(x)=0\ (k\in K_=)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When upgrading is uncertified, all original rows and domains remain authoritative; extracted metadata may assist the solver but cannot alter the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: Every original row has a well-defined algebraic evaluation on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fallback representation defines exactly the original feasible set \(F_R\).
review_flags: solver fallback semantics require later source certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and feasible-set formula fit the leaf, but the cited modeling discussion does not substantiate solver fallback behavior, retained-row authority, or restrictions on extracted metadata.

children.title: Logical-Structure Extraction Taxonomy
