children.title: Clique Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of mutual-exclusion structure from algebraic or logical input.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction of pairwise-incompatible Boolean literals from algebraic or logical constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form literals \(L\), where each literal is \(x_i\) or \(1-x_i\) for a binary variable \(x_i\). Add an edge \(\{p,q\}\) to the conflict graph when the active constraints imply \(p+q\le1\). Enumerate or heuristically find cliques \(Q\subseteq L\), and output the valid clique inequality \[\sum_{p\in Q}p\le1.\] A candidate \(Q\) is accepted only after every pairwise conflict is certified under the validity domain of the originating constraints. Record whether the clique is globally valid or conditional on a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a conflict graph of Boolean literals and convert certified cliques into at-most-one inequalities, retaining each clique's global or local validity scope.
assumptions_latex: Each \(x_i\) appearing in a literal is binary.
Every inserted conflict is implied by active constraints in its recorded validity domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each output clique \(Q\) satisfies \(\sum_{p\in Q}p\le1\) throughout its validity domain.
review_flags: clique-extraction algorithm needs a dedicated MIP presolve source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conflict-graph construction is mathematically coherent and algorithm is the correct kind, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not support the extraction procedure, certification policy, or global-versus-local validity handling.

children.title: Implication Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of directed logical consequences among variable states or domain restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Implication Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivation of directed implications between Boolean literals from valid constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) and \(q\) be literals of binary variables and let \(F\) be the feasible set of the active constraints in a recorded validity domain. Insert the directed arc \(p\to q\) exactly when infeasibility of \[F\cap\{x:p=1,\ q=0\}\] is certified. Store the contrapositive arc \((1-q)\to(1-p)\) simultaneously. Implications may be detected by bound propagation, a recognized logical row, or a certified infeasibility test; the extraction procedure outputs only arcs justified by one such check and labels each arc as globally or locally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implication arc is stored only after certifying that its antecedent true and consequent false is infeasible; its contrapositive and validity scope are also recorded.
assumptions_latex: The literals \(p\) and \(q\) take values in \(\{0,1\}\).
The feasibility test uses constraints valid throughout the recorded domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every extracted arc satisfies \(x\in F\land p=1\Rightarrow q=1\).

notation.meaning: feasible set in the recorded validity domain

review_flags: implication-graph extraction needs a dedicated solver reference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The infeasibility characterization and contrapositive are correct for Boolean literals, but the citation does not establish implication-graph extraction methods or validity-scope handling in MIP presolve.

children.title: Gate Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of Boolean gate structure from generic constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Gate Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of exact Boolean gate relations represented by algebraic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given binary variables and a row set \(R\), enumerate supported gate templates and test equality of their Boolean feasible assignments. For example, accept \(z=x\wedge y\) only if the projection of \(R\) onto \((x,y,z)\) equals the solutions of \[z\le x,\qquad z\le y,\qquad z\ge x+y-1.\] Accept \(z=x\vee y\) analogously using \(z\ge x\), \(z\ge y\), and \(z\le x+y\). Output the gate and its defining rows only after exact truth-table equivalence is certified; otherwise retain the rows without a gate label.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary rows are labeled as logical gates only when their projected feasible assignments exactly match a supported gate's truth table.
assumptions_latex: All rows used in a gate template share the same validity domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each extracted gate has exactly the Boolean assignments of its stated logical relation.

notation.meaning: rows tested for a gate pattern

review_flags: gate-extraction implementation requires a dedicated presolve source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The AND and OR formulations are correct for binary variables and the algorithm kind fits, but the supplied section does not support gate-template extraction or exact projected-assignment certification.

children.title: Cardinality Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of counting structure over binary or logical literals.

knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of exact lower, upper, or equality bounds on sums of Boolean literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Normalize complemented binary variables into literals \(p_i\in\{x_i,1-x_i\}\). From an algebraic row set \(R\), extract a cardinality constraint only when its feasible Boolean assignments coincide with one of \[\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\le k,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m p_i\ge k,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m p_i=k,\] for an integer \(k\). Normalization must account exactly for constants introduced by complementation and for any common nonzero coefficient scaling. Output the literal list, relation, threshold, defining rows, and validity scope; otherwise retain the algebraic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal-weight binary rows are normalized into literal counts and accepted as cardinality constraints only after exact adjustment of complements, scaling, and thresholds.
assumptions_latex: Every \(x_i\) underlying a literal is binary.
The normalized nonzero literal coefficients have one common magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extracted cardinality constraint and its defining rows have identical Boolean solutions in their validity domain.
review_flags: cardinality-recognition details need a dedicated presolve source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized cardinality forms are precise, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not support the recognition algorithm, coefficient normalization, or validity-scope claims.

children.title: Extracted-Structure Reuse
children.top_down_role: Persistence and consumption of recovered logical structures across propagation, conflicts, and search.

knowledge_statements.title: Extracted-Structure Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-scoped reuse of extracted logical structure across solver mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be an extracted clique, implication, gate, or cardinality relation, and let \(\mathcal V(S)\) denote its certified validity scope, including any required domain restrictions, assumptions, or search-tree scope. Propagation, separation, branching, or conflict deductions may use \(S\) only at search states belonging to \(\mathcal V(S)\). A globally valid structure may be cached throughout the search. A locally valid structure must retain its dependencies and node scope and must be discarded or revalidated when those conditions no longer hold. Reuse alone does not authorize deletion of defining rows; deletion requires a separately certified exact-representation upgrade.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extracted structures may be reused only where all recorded domain, dependency, and search-scope conditions hold; reuse by itself never authorizes deletion of their defining rows.
assumptions_latex: Each extracted structure \(S\) has a recorded certified validity scope \(\mathcal V(S)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inference using \(S\) is restricted to search states in \(\mathcal V(S)\).

children.title: Activity-Based Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction from row activities and current variable domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Based Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-row domain contraction using minimum and maximum residual activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a row \(\ell\le\sum_i a_i x_i\le u\) with intervals \(x_i\in[L_i,U_i]\), define residual activities \(m_{-j}=\sum_{i\ne j}\min\{a_iL_i,a_iU_i\}\) and \(M_{-j}=\sum_{i\ne j}\max\{a_iL_i,a_iU_i\}\). For \(a_j>0\), intersect the domain of \(x_j\) with \([(\ell-M_{-j})/a_j,(u-m_{-j})/a_j]\); for \(a_j<0\), intersect it with \([(u-m_{-j})/a_j,(\ell-M_{-j})/a_j]\). Ignore an absent row side, round inward for integral \(x_j\), and repeat until no bound changes or a prescribed pass limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual minimum and maximum row activities yield valid new variable bounds; integer bounds are rounded inward and passes repeat until stable or limited.
assumptions_latex: \(L_i\le x_i\le U_i\) and the required residual activities are finite.
The row is valid throughout the domain being tightened.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained feasible point satisfies the tightened variable intervals.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval arithmetic on a valid linear row directly yields the displayed residual-activity bounds
dedicated authoritative presolve locator not supplied

children.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening

children.title: Full Optimization-Based Tightening
children.top_down_role: High-effort auxiliary optimization across selected variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Optimization-Based Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-effort auxiliary optimization across selected variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a relaxation containing every feasible solution of the current MIP, let \(F\subseteq R\) denote the current MIP feasible set, and let \(J\) be the variables selected for full tightening. For every \(j\in J\), solve the auxiliary problems \[\underline v_j=\inf\{x_j:x\in R\},\qquad \overline v_j=\sup\{x_j:x\in R\}.\] If certified finite extrema are obtained, intersect \([L_j,U_j]\) with \([\underline v_j,\overline v_j]\); for integral \(x_j\), use \([\lceil\underline v_j\rceil,\lfloor\overline v_j\rfloor]\). If \(R\) is certified infeasible, then \(F\) is empty. An unbounded or unresolved auxiliary problem yields no new bound on the affected side. Output every certified bound change and auxiliary-solve status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize both directions for every selected variable over a valid relaxation, apply only certified finite bounds, round integral bounds inward, and infer infeasibility only from certified relaxation infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The current MIP feasible set \(F\) satisfies \(F\subseteq R\).
Every accepted auxiliary conclusion is certified to the required solver tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every tightened interval contains the corresponding coordinate of every point in \(F\).

notation.meaning: relaxation infimum and supremum for variable j

children.title: Selective Optimization-Based Tightening
children.top_down_role: Selective auxiliary optimization guided by expected impact.

children.title: Filtered Optimization-Based Tightening
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary optimization restricted to variables selected by expected tightening value.

knowledge_statements.title: Filtered Optimization-Based Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based tightening restricted by a deterministic candidate filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a valid relaxation \(R\), candidate variables \(J\), and a deterministic filter \(\phi_j\in\{0,1\}\) computed from valid statistics such as bound width, fractionality, row incidence, or estimated impact, form \(J_\phi=\{j\in J:\phi_j=1\}\). For each \(j\in J_\phi\), solve the minimization and maximization of \(x_j\) over \(R\), intersect the current interval with the certified extrema, and round inward for integral variables. Leave variables in \(J\setminus J_\phi\) unchanged. The filter controls computational effort only; validity of every accepted bound follows from \(F\subseteq R\), not from the score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic filter selects promising variables for auxiliary minimization and maximization; certified relaxation extrema tighten selected bounds, while rejected candidates remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The current feasible set \(F\) satisfies \(F\subseteq R\).
The filter uses information available without assuming unproved bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All accepted bounds remain valid for \(F\), independently of the filter's selection quality.
review_flags: filtering criteria and partial-solve policy need a dedicated optimization-based tightening source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity argument is mathematically sound and the algorithm kind fits, but the general relaxation-based branch-and-bound locator does not support the filtered candidate-selection mechanism, listed statistics, or selective auxiliary-solve policy.

children.title: Partial Optimization-Based Tightening
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary optimization performed with deliberately incomplete search or restricted effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Optimization-Based Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe tightening from incomplete optimization-based bound subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq [l,u]\) be the current feasible region and let \(J\) be selected variable indices. For each \(j\in J\), start the subproblems \(L_j^*=\min\{x_j:x\in F\}\) and \(U_j^*=\max\{x_j:x\in F\}\). If an interrupted minimization supplies a certified lower bound \(\underline d_j\le L_j^*\), set \(l_j\leftarrow\max\{l_j,\underline d_j\}\). If an interrupted maximization supplies a certified upper bound \(\overline d_j\ge U_j^*\), set \(u_j\leftarrow\min\{u_j,\overline d_j\}\). Round inward when \(x_j\) is integral. Uncertified primal or heuristic values do not justify bound changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interrupted bound subproblems may tighten variables using certified dual bounds; heuristic or merely feasible values are insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible region whose variable bounds are being tightened.
Each accepted subproblem bound is globally valid for its stated optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated box still contains \(F\).

notation.meaning: Exact minimum and maximum of variable j over F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certified-bound directions are mathematically sound and the algorithm fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the interrupted-solve mechanism or its certificate requirements.

children.title: Candidate Selection Criteria
children.top_down_role: Impact, cost, domain, or structural signals used to prioritize tightening candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate Selection Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted selection of variables for optimization-based tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given candidate variables \(J\), a computational budget \(B>0\), estimated costs \(\kappa_j>0\), and nonnegative predicted benefits \(\beta_j\), assign each candidate the score \(s_j=\beta_j/\kappa_j\). Choose a subset \(S\subseteq J\) satisfying \(\sum_{j\in S}\kappa_j\le B\), either by solving \(\max\{\sum_{j\in S}\beta_j:\sum_{j\in S}\kappa_j\le B\}\) or by descending score with a deterministic tie rule. Run bound subproblems only for \(S\). Selection affects effort but not validity: every resulting change must independently possess a valid bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select bound-tightening subproblems by predicted benefit under a cost budget, while certifying every eventual bound change independently.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite.
\(\beta_j\ge0\), \(\kappa_j>0\), and \(B>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected set respects the budget, and selection scores alone certify no bound change.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a plausible budgeted selection algorithm, but the ratio score and knapsack formulation are implementation choices with no cited support.

children.title: Partial-Result Reuse
children.top_down_role: Valid bound information retained from incomplete auxiliary optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Result Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for retaining information from unfinished tightening subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a bound subproblem over \(F\) is interrupted after producing a certified lower bound \(d\le\min_{x\in F}q(x)\), or a certified upper bound \(e\ge\max_{x\in F}q(x)\). For every later feasible region \(F'\subseteq F\), the same inequalities remain valid: \(d\le\min_{x\in F'}q(x)\) and \(e\ge\max_{x\in F'}q(x)\). Stored feasible witnesses, bases, or search states may be reused computationally, but a witness must be checked against \(F'\), and certificates must be recomputed if the objective, relaxation, or assumptions underlying them change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified bounds remain valid after feasible-region restriction; feasible witnesses and solver states require compatibility checks before reuse.
assumptions_latex: \(F'\subseteq F\).
The function \(q\) and the meaning of each retained certificate are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified extremum bounds transfer from \(F\) to \(F'\) in the stated directions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extremum-bound monotonicity under restriction is correct and the property fits the leaf, but the broader claims about reusing bases and search states require an inspectable solver-mechanism source.

children.title: Objective-Relaxation Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain deductions combining incumbent and relaxation-side objective information.

children.title: Objective-Based Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction using incumbent-relative objective limits or cutoff information.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Based Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-objective propagation using a valid incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(x,c,l,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and consider a minimization problem with objective \(c^	op x\), bounds \(l\le x\le u\), and feasible incumbent value \(U\in\mathbb{R}\). Every improving solution satisfies \(c^	op x<U\). For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define \(m_i=\min\{c_i l_i,c_i u_i\}\). For each \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(c_j>0\), every improving solution satisfies \(x_j<(U-\sum_{i
e j}m_i)/c_j\); if \(x_j\) is integral, update \(u_j\leftarrow\min\{u_j,\lceil (U-\sum_{i
e j}m_i)/c_jceil-1\}\). For \(c_j<0\), every improving solution satisfies \(x_j>(U-\sum_{i
e j}m_i)/c_j\); if \(x_j\) is integral, update \(l_j\leftarrow\max\{l_j,\lfloor (U-\sum_{i
e j}m_i)/c_jfloor+1\}\). These restrictions preserve improving solutions, not necessarily every feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded linear minimization objective, a valid incumbent cutoff restricts each variable after the smallest possible contributions of all other variables are subtracted; integral restrictions use the corresponding strict lattice bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(x,c,l,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and every bound used to define \(m_i\) is finite.
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent for the same minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every solution satisfying \(c^\top x<U\) obeys the displayed coordinate restrictions.

notation.meaning: Smallest possible objective contribution of coordinate i over its bounds

children.title: Reduced-Cost Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction using relaxation reduced costs plus available objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP reduced-cost fixing and tightening under an incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an LP relaxation of a minimization problem have optimum \(z_L\), and let \(x_j=l_j\) at an optimal solution with reduced cost \(r_j>0\). If the associated optimal dual solution yields the valid inequality \(c^Tx\ge z_L+r_j(x_j-l_j)\) for every relaxation-feasible \(x\), then every solution satisfying the incumbent cutoff \(c^Tx\le U\) obeys \(x_j\le l_j+(U-z_L)/r_j\). If \(x_j\) is integral, the upper bound can be floored. The symmetric statement applies to a variable at its upper bound with reduced cost of the opposite sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gap between an incumbent and the LP bound, divided by a valid reduced cost, limits movement away from an active bound.
assumptions_latex: \(U\ge z_L\) is a valid incumbent cutoff.
The reduced-cost inequality is valid throughout the relaxation region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j\le l_j+(U-z_L)/r_j\) holds for every relaxation-feasible point satisfying the cutoff.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost at the active lower bound

children.title: Incumbent Dependence
children.top_down_role: Effects of incumbent availability and quality on objective-driven deductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic dependence of objective-derived bounds on the incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(U_1\) and \(U_2\) be valid incumbent values with \(U_2\le U_1\). Then the cutoff regions satisfy \(\{x:c^Tx\le U_2\}\subseteq\{x:c^Tx\le U_1\}\). Consequently, any bound obtained solely by projecting the stronger cutoff region with \(U_2\) is at least as tight as the analogous bound obtained with \(U_1\). Before any incumbent exists, such cutoff-based tightening is unavailable. If an incumbent is invalidated or the objective changes, bounds justified only by its cutoff must be withdrawn or independently recertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A better minimization incumbent creates a smaller cutoff region and cannot weaken correctly derived objective-based bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(U_1\) and \(U_2\) are objective values of feasible solutions to the same minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cutoff region and all exact projected variable intervals shrink monotonically as the incumbent value decreases.

children.title: Relaxation Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Locality, numerical, and model-change conditions affecting reduced-cost deductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-relaxation and cutoff conditions required for safe tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the target feasible set, \(R\) a proposed relaxation in the same variable space, and \(C\) the objective-cutoff region defining the target solutions to preserve. If \(F\cap C\subseteq R\cap C\), every coordinate bound valid for \(R\cap C\) is valid for \(F\cap C\); in particular, \(F\subseteq R\) is sufficient when the same valid cutoff is used. Without this containment, bounds projected from \(R\cap C\) are not guaranteed to be safe. Specifically, if some \(x^*\in F\cap C\) is excluded from \(R\cap C\) and violates an inferred bound, that bound is invalid for the target problem. A cutoff derived from a nonfeasible incumbent can exclude the true optimum and cannot support valid projection or reduced-cost deductions for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected relaxation bounds are guaranteed safe when the relaxed cutoff region contains every target solution that must be preserved; absent that containment, safety requires separate justification.
assumptions_latex: \(F\), \(R\), and \(C\) are subsets of the same variable space.
\(C\) represents the cutoff condition for the target solutions that must be preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The containment \(F\cap C\subseteq R\cap C\) is sufficient for every bound valid on \(R\cap C\) to remain valid on \(F\cap C\); without it, such validity is not guaranteed.

children.title: Expression-Domain Tightening Family
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction for nonlinear expressions and factorable structures.

children.title: Nonlinear Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction exploiting nonlinear constraint structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or certified optimization of variable ranges over nonlinear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in[l,u]:g_k(x)\le0,\ k=1,\ldots,m\}\), possibly with integrality restrictions. For each selected coordinate \(j\), compute certified bounds \(d_j^L\le\inf_{x\in F}x_j\) and \(d_j^U\ge\sup_{x\in F}x_j\) using globally valid nonlinear relaxations or globally solved subproblems. Update \(l_j\leftarrow\max\{l_j,d_j^L\}\) and \(u_j\leftarrow\min\{u_j,d_j^U\}\), with inward integer rounding when applicable. Iterate after material domain reductions. A merely local optimum cannot certify either global extremum and therefore cannot alone justify the corresponding bound change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally certified extrema or relaxation bounds of each variable safely contract a nonlinear feasible box; local optima alone do not.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted extremum bound is globally valid for \(F\).
All nonlinear expressions are defined on the domains used by the certifying relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tightened box contains every point of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper bounds on coordinate extrema

children.title: Interval Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction based on interval enclosures of variable or subexpression ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward and inverse interval propagation through nonlinear expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each constraint by an expression tree whose leaves have intervals \(X_i=[l_i,u_i]\). Evaluate every internal node with an inclusion-isotonic interval extension to obtain forward ranges. Intersect the root range with the constraint's admissible interval, then apply sound inverse interval operators from root to leaves. Replace each node interval by its intersection with every inferred preimage and repeat until no interval changes or a prescribed stopping tolerance is reached. If any intersection is empty, certify infeasibility of the current box. Because every operator is inclusion preserving, no feasible assignment in the original box is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound forward interval evaluation and backward inverse propagation repeatedly contract expression domains without deleting feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: Each interval extension encloses the exact range of its operator on the supplied argument intervals.
Each inverse operator returns an enclosure of every compatible argument value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The contracted intervals contain all feasible assignments from the original box.

notation.meaning: Current interval of variable or expression node i

children.title: Expression Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction propagated through expression trees or factorable representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain propagation on a directed acyclic expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a directed acyclic graph encode auxiliary relations \(v=f_v(v_1,\ldots,v_p)\), with an interval \(X_v\) attached to every node. In a forward sweep, replace \(X_v\) by \(X_v\cap F_v(X_{v_1},\ldots,X_{v_p})\), where \(F_v\) encloses the range of \(f_v\). In a backward sweep, contract each parent interval using sound preimage enclosures induced by \(X_v\) and the other parents. Iterate both sweeps to a fixed point or stopping tolerance. Shared subexpressions must reference the same node interval; duplicating them may lose dependency information and weaken contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward range evaluation and backward preimage propagation contract every node of an expression graph while preserving feasible evaluations.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is acyclic for each sweep.
All forward and inverse enclosures are sound on their current domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible evaluation represented before propagation remains represented after propagation.

notation.meaning: Current interval attached to expression node v
Inclusion-preserving interval extension of node operation

children.title: Expression Dependency Limits
children.top_down_role: Dependency, enclosure, and numerical effects limiting contraction strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression Dependency Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical loss of sharpness from repeated dependent occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(M>0\), let \(x\in[0,1]\) and consider \(f_M(x)=Mx-Mx\). The exact range of \(f_M\) is \(\{0\}\), whereas natural interval evaluation treats the two occurrences independently and returns \(M[0,1]-M[0,1]=[-M,M]\). Thus natural interval arithmetic is inclusion preserving but need not be sharp when one variable occurs repeatedly or correlated subexpressions are evaluated independently. Because \(M\) is arbitrary, the width of the interval overestimation can be arbitrarily large. Symbolic cancellation, suitable shared-dependency reasoning, or stronger relaxations can recover information unavailable to ordinary natural interval evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For x in [0,1], the exact range of Mx−Mx is {0}, while natural interval evaluation gives [−M,M]; increasing positive M makes the dependency overestimation arbitrarily wide.
assumptions_latex: Natural interval subtraction is used without symbolic cancellation or correlation tracking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated-variable dependency can produce a sound interval enclosure whose excess width is arbitrarily large.

notation.meaning: Scaled repeated-variable expression whose interval range is evaluated

children.title: Bound-Change Validity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Validity and persistence regimes for tightened domains.

children.title: Global Bound Changes
children.top_down_role: Domain changes valid throughout the active problem state or search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Bound Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound reductions valid throughout the entire search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of the original model and let variable \(x_j\) initially satisfy \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\). A global bound change is a replacement by \(l'_j\le x_j\le u'_j\), where \(l_j\le l'_j\le u'_j\le u_j\), such that every \(x\in F\) satisfies the new bounds. The change may therefore be installed at the root and inherited by every search node. A deduction conditional on a branch decision, probing assumption, local cutoff, or node-specific constraint is not global unless that condition is discharged by a globally valid implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global bound change is entailed by the original model and is therefore valid at every search-tree node.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) denotes the original model's complete feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global validity is equivalent to \(F\subseteq\{x:l'_j\le x_j\le u'_j\}\).

children.title: Local Bound Changes
children.top_down_role: Domain changes valid only within a search node or descendant subtree.

assumptions_latex: The current search node is represented by a domain box \(D^v=\{x:\ell^v\le x\le u^v\}\) contained in its parent domain.
Propagation is sound: every derived bound contains all feasible points satisfying the node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^v\subseteq D^{v'}\subseteq D^v\), while no validity outside the subtree rooted at \(v\) is asserted.

notation.meaning: feasible set under the restrictions of node v
variable domain box stored at node v

review_flags: Exact solver-level treatment of local bound validity is not supported by the supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local domain tightening in branch-and-bound, excluding globally valid presolve reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local bound change at search node \(v\) replaces \(D^v\) by \(D^{v'}=\{x:\ell^{v'}\le x\le u^{v'}\}\), where \(\ell^v\le\ell^{v'}\le u^{v'}\le u^v\), and is justified using assumptions or deductions valid under the path restrictions defining \(v\). Soundness requires \(F^v\subseteq D^{v'}\). The changed bounds may be inherited by descendants of \(v\), because their feasible sets are subsets of \(F^v\), but they must not be imposed on nodes outside that subtree unless independently established there or promoted to global validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local bound tightening preserves every feasible solution below one search node and may be inherited by descendants, but it is not valid elsewhere without separate justification.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Bound Changes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Local Bound Changes leaf and is mathematically plausible, with consistent plain-text and LaTeX formulations. However, the record cites no source, and the inventory's general branch-and-bound sections do not specifically support the asserted subtree-validity and inheritance semantics. A solver-level source with a precise section or page locator is required.

children.title: Probing Bound Changes
children.top_down_role: Tentative domain changes active within a probing context.

assumptions_latex: A temporary probing restriction \(H\) is imposed on the current domain \(D\).
The propagation operator \(P\) is sound for the restricted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap H\subseteq P(D\cap H)\subseteq D\cap H\), and bounds depending on \(H\) remain conditional on \(H\).
review_flags: The supplied source locators do not specifically document probing-state bound validity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary conditional bounds created while probing a discrete assignment or restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A probing bound change is a bound tightening obtained after temporarily replacing the current domain \(D\) by \(D\cap H\), where \(H\) fixes or restricts selected discrete variables. Sound propagation produces \(P(D\cap H)\) satisfying \(F\cap H\subseteq P(D\cap H)\subseteq D\cap H\). Every bound whose derivation uses \(H\) is conditional on \(H\): it may support implications, conflicts, or deductions valid after discharge of the probing cases, but it cannot directly replace the unconditional bounds of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A probing bound is derived under a temporary discrete restriction and remains conditional until a valid case argument removes that restriction.
knowledge_statements.title: Probing Bound Changes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Probing Bound Changes leaf, but the feasible set F is used without being introduced in the assumptions, statement, or notation. More importantly, no citation supports the conditional validity and discharge semantics. A probing or solver-presolve source with a specific locator is required before the mathematical formulation can be settled.

children.title: Bound-Change Promotion
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which tentative or local deductions become more broadly valid.

assumptions_latex: The current feasible set is \(F\subseteq D\).
A candidate bound \(x_j\ge\beta\) was derived under temporary probe cases \(H_1,\ldots,H_k\).
The cases cover the current feasible set: \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{r=1}^k H_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(F\cap H_r\subseteq\{x:x_j\ge\beta\}\) for every \(r\), then \(F\subseteq\{x:x_j\ge\beta\}\), so the bound may be promoted.
review_flags: Promotion criterion is a standard exhaustive-case argument, but no supplied locator addresses solver probing promotion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Promotion of a conditional probing bound to the current unconditional validity regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A probing-derived bound \(x_j\ge\beta\) is promotable to the current unconditional domain exactly when its derivation can be discharged over a valid cover of the current feasible set. Concretely, if \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{r=1}^k H_r\) and \(F\cap H_r\subseteq\{x:x_j\ge\beta\}\) for every \(r\), then \(F\subseteq\{x:x_j\ge\beta\}\). Promotion to global validity additionally requires the same implication for the original feasible set, not merely for the feasible set of the current search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional bound can be promoted when it holds in every case of a valid cover; global promotion requires validity for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Change Promotion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected condition role fits Bound-Change Promotion, and the finite-cover implication is mathematically correct. The distinction between current-node and original-problem validity is also appropriate. Nevertheless, the record contains no citation supporting its interpretation as a solver promotion criterion; a specific probing or bound-validity source is required.

children.title: Bound-Change Rollback
children.top_down_role: Restoration boundaries for temporary or context-specific domain changes.

assumptions_latex: Each temporary bound update records the previous bound and its decision level.
All deductions depending on a temporary restriction are assigned that restriction's level or a deeper level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After rollback to level \(q\), the restored domain equals the domain produced by exactly the updates whose levels do not exceed \(q\).
review_flags: The supplied locators do not specify reversible bound-stack semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reversible restoration of bounds after leaving a node or temporary probing context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a stack \(S\) of bound updates. Before changing a bound, push a record \(e=(j,b_{\mathrm{old}},b_{\mathrm{new}},\lambda(e))\), where \(\lambda(e)\) is the active decision or probing level. To roll back to level \(q\), repeatedly pop the newest record while \(\lambda(e)>q\) and restore \(b_{\mathrm{old}}\). Invalidate every queued deduction whose justification contains a popped update. Stop when \(S\) is empty or its top record has level at most \(q\); the remaining bounds are precisely those supported at level \(q\) or earlier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rollback pops temporary bound updates in reverse order, restores prior bounds, and invalidates deductions that depended on removed updates.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Change Rollback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is appropriate for the Bound-Change Rollback leaf. The stack discipline is plausible, but the exact update record, dependency invalidation rule, and claim that surviving bounds are precisely those supported at level q are implementation-sensitive and uncited. A solver implementation or authoritative algorithm description with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Probing-Inference Discovery Calculus
children.top_down_role: Tentative domain restrictions used to discover fixings, implications, conflicts, and stronger structure.

children.title: Single-Variable Probing
children.top_down_role: Probing organized around temporary restrictions of one discrete variable.

assumptions_latex: A discrete variable \(x_j\) has finite current domain \(V_j\).
For each tested value, propagation is sound and either returns a reduced domain or detects infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure deletes infeasible values and may retain only deductions valid in every surviving probe case.

notation.meaning: current finite domain of the probed variable
set of values whose probes remain feasible

review_flags: Single-variable probing is standard solver practice, but the supplied locators do not identify this algorithm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive temporary assignment of one finite-domain variable followed by propagation and case aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current domain \(D\) and a discrete variable \(x_j\) with finite domain \(V_j\), for each \(v\in V_j\) temporarily impose \(x_j=v\), propagate to a fixpoint, and record either infeasibility or the resulting domain \(D_v\). Roll back before testing the next value. Delete every \(v\) whose probe is infeasible. Let \(W_j\) be the surviving values. A bound or logical consequence may be retained unconditionally only if it holds for every \(D_v\) with \(v\in W_j\); output the reduced domain and any such common consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probe each value of one discrete variable, remove infeasible values, and retain only consequences shared by all feasible probe cases.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Variable Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role matches Single-Variable Probing and the case-aggregation idea is sound under an exhaustive finite domain. No cited source, however, establishes this exact value-enumeration, fixpoint-propagation, rollback, and common-consequence algorithm. The general branch-and-bound inventory entries are insufficiently specific.

children.title: Concurrent Higher-Order Probing
children.top_down_role: Higher-order and concurrent extensions of basic probing.

children.title: Multi-Variable Probing
children.top_down_role: Tentative restrictions involving combinations or sequences of multiple variables.

assumptions_latex: A finite family \(\mathcal H\) of joint restrictions covers the current feasible set.
Propagation is sound in every restricted case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Infeasible joint cases may be removed, while an unconditional deduction must hold in every surviving case of the cover.
review_flags: Several higher-order probing variants exist, and the supplied locators do not select one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint probing of assignments or restrictions involving more than one discrete variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a finite family \(\mathcal H\) of restrictions, each fixing or restricting at least two discrete variables, such that \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}H\). For each \(H\), impose \(H\), propagate to a fixpoint, record the resulting domain \(D_H\) or infeasibility, and then roll back. Remove infeasible joint cases. A deduction \(C\) is returned as unconditional only when \(D_H\subseteq C\) for every surviving \(H\); deductions holding in only some cases remain conditional implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-variable probing propagates joint temporary restrictions, rejects infeasible combinations, and keeps unconditional consequences only when every surviving case supports them.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Variable Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Multi-Variable Probing, and the cover condition makes the common-consequence rule plausible. Higher-order probing has multiple formulations, and no citation identifies or supports this particular joint-restriction algorithm or its case-removal semantics. A specific authoritative source is required.

children.title: Parallel Probing
children.top_down_role: Concurrent probing tasks over separate candidates or probing contexts.

assumptions_latex: Probe tasks start from the same immutable domain snapshot \(D^0\).
Each worker uses sound propagation and private reversible state.
Reported deductions carry enough assumptions to check their validity against \(D^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After validation, the merge contains only deductions valid for \(F^0\); worker-local state is never merged directly.

notation.meaning: feasible set represented by the snapshot
validated deduction set from worker r

review_flags: Parallel probing protocol is implementation-dependent and unsupported by the supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent evaluation of independent probe cases from a common domain snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the probe cases among workers. Each worker starts from the same immutable snapshot \(D^0\), performs temporary restrictions and propagation using private state, rolls back locally, and emits deductions with their probe assumptions. After all assigned tasks finish, validate each emitted deduction against its stated case and \(D^0\). Merge only case infeasibilities and consequences whose case cover proves validity for \(F^0\). Apply accepted unconditional changes at a synchronization point, then begin any further probing from the resulting new snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel probing runs cases from one snapshot in private states, validates their deductions, and merges only consequences justified for that snapshot.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Parallel Probing, but the immutable-snapshot protocol, private-state requirement, validation phase, synchronization boundary, and admissible merge operations are implementation-dependent. None is supported by a cited source, so the exact algorithm cannot be accepted from the supplied general MIP inventory.

children.title: Cross-Probe Interaction
children.top_down_role: Shared deductions, conflicts, duplication, and consistency across multiple probing contexts.

assumptions_latex: Two probe deductions have antecedents \(H_1,H_2\) and consequences \(C_1,C_2\).
Each implication \(F\cap H_r\subseteq C_r\) is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cross-probe composition is valid only when its antecedent is retained or discharged by a verified cover or implication relation.
review_flags: Cross-probe composition rules require a dedicated solver or constraint-programming source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of deductions composed from distinct probing contexts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Probe results interact through their explicit antecedents. From \(F\cap H_1\subseteq C_1\) and \(F\cap H_2\subseteq C_2\), one may infer \(F\cap H_1\cap H_2\subseteq C_1\cap C_2\), but not generally \(F\subseteq C_1\cap C_2\). A consequence from one probe may strengthen another only after establishing that the second context implies the first antecedent, or after retaining the combined antecedent. An antecedent may be removed only by an exhaustive-case, conflict, or implication argument valid for the current feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consequences from different probes can be combined only with their assumptions, unless a sound cover or implication argument discharges those assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Probe Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A principle is an appropriate role for Cross-Probe Interaction. The displayed intersection inference is correct, and the warning against dropping antecedents is well aligned with the leaf. The broader list of permitted discharge mechanisms and solver interpretation remains uncited; a dedicated probing, implication, or constraint-propagation source is required.

children.title: Parallel Merge Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity and synchronization limits for combining concurrently discovered artifacts.

assumptions_latex: Every parallel probe is evaluated from snapshot \(D^0\).
Each reported artifact identifies its antecedent and derivation snapshot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An artifact may cross the merge boundary only if it is valid for \(F^0\), or is stored with an antecedent that preserves its conditional validity.

notation.meaning: feasible set represented by the snapshot

review_flags: Merge-boundary semantics are solver-specific and absent from the supplied sources.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility criterion for transferring artifacts from private probe states into shared solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parallel probe artifact \((C,H)\) may enter shared state only if either \(F^0\subseteq C\), establishing unconditional snapshot validity, or \(F^0\cap H\subseteq C\) and the antecedent \(H\) is retained with the artifact. A bound update requires the first condition. A conditional implication or conflict may use the second. Artifacts derived after a worker-local update not present in \(D^0\) must include that update among their antecedents. If the shared domain changes before merging, the artifact must be revalidated or discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker result may be merged only when it is valid for the common snapshot or retains every assumption needed for conditional validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Merge Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Parallel Merge Boundaries. The unconditional-versus-conditional validity distinction is plausible, but the claim that changed shared state requires revalidation or discard is protocol-specific and may depend on whether domain strengthening preserves the artifact. A cited parallel-solver protocol is needed to determine the exact admissibility rule.

children.title: Logical-Structure Probing
children.top_down_role: Probing over previously recognized logical relationships.

children.title: Clique Probing
children.top_down_role: Probing guided by mutual-exclusion relationships among literals.

assumptions_latex: Binary literals form a clique \(Q\), meaning at most one literal in \(Q\) can be true.
Propagation under a temporary literal assignment is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A failed true probe fixes its literal false; a surviving probe yields implications conditional on that literal.

notation.meaning: set of pairwise incompatible binary literals

review_flags: The supplied textbook locators do not specifically support clique probing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probing binary literals using an at-most-one clique as logical propagation structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a clique \(Q\) of binary literals satisfying \(\sum_{p\in Q}p\le1\), select \(p\in Q\), temporarily impose \(p=1\), set every \(q\in Q\setminus\{p\}\) to \(0\), and propagate to a fixpoint. If infeasibility results, permanently infer \(p=0\). Otherwise record every derived consequence as conditional on \(p=1\), then roll back. Repeating this operation over selected clique literals can strengthen implications, detect fixed literals, and reveal smaller infeasible literal combinations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique probing sets one binary literal true, forces the other clique literals false, propagates, and records either a fixing or conditional implications.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role matches Clique Probing, and infeasibility under p=1 correctly implies p=0. The exact procedure and its claimed ability to reveal smaller infeasible literal combinations are not supported by any cited locator. A source specifically covering clique-based probing in MIP or constraint programming is required.

children.title: Implication Probing
children.top_down_role: Probing guided by directed consequences among variable states.

assumptions_latex: The current implication graph contains sound arcs between binary literals.
Propagation under a temporarily asserted literal is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reached literal is a valid consequence of the probe literal, and reaching complementary literals proves that the probe literal is false.
review_flags: Implication probing is not specifically documented by the supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary assertion of a binary literal followed by implication-graph and domain propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a directed implication graph \(G\) and a binary literal \(p\), temporarily assert \(p\), traverse all reachable implication arcs, and interleave the traversal with sound domain propagation until no new literal or bound is obtained. If both \(r\) and \(\bar r\) are derived for some literal \(r\), record the conflict and infer \(\bar p\). Otherwise add sound arcs \(p\to q\) for newly derived literals \(q\), record any conditional bound consequences, and roll back the temporary state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assert one literal temporarily, close its implications with propagation, fix it false on conflict, or store the resulting conditional implications.
knowledge_statements.title: Implication Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Implication Probing. Reaching complementary literals under the temporary assertion p correctly refutes p, but the interleaved graph/domain propagation algorithm and insertion of new arcs are not documented by a cited source. A precise implication-probing or solver-presolve reference is required.

children.title: Logical Closure Discovery
children.top_down_role: Additional logical consequences exposed by probing over retained relationships.

assumptions_latex: A finite set \(L\) of binary literals and a sound initial implication relation \(R_0\subseteq L\times L\) are given.
New implications are inserted only after sound probing or transitive composition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(R^*\) is transitively closed, and every pair \((p,q)\in R^*\) satisfies \(F\cap\{p=1\}\subseteq\{q=1\}\).
review_flags: Logical closure discovery requires a source covering implication-graph closure in MIP presolve or probing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixpoint discovery of binary implications generated by probing and transitive closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R:=R_0\). Repeatedly select a literal \(p\in L\), propagate the temporary assertion \(p=1\), and insert \((p,q)\) into \(R\) for every soundly derived literal \(q\). Also insert \((p,r)\) whenever \((p,q)\in R\) and \((q,r)\in R\). If probing \(p\) yields a contradiction, fix \(p=0\). Continue until a complete pass adds no implication or fixing. Output the resulting relation \(R^*\), with every arc interpreted as a valid implication over the current feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly probe literals and compose implications until no new arc or fixing appears, producing a sound transitive implication closure.
knowledge_statements.title: Logical Closure Discovery

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Logical Closure Discovery, and finiteness makes a closure computation plausible. However, fixing literals during the procedure can change the current domain and feasible-set representation, while the statement does not specify whether subsequent implication validity and R* refer to the initial or updated feasible set. No citation resolves this semantic issue or supports the exact closure algorithm.

children.title: Logical Artifact Validity
children.top_down_role: Global, local, or temporary scope of logical deductions discovered through probing.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical Artifact Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity certificate for implications learned by probing a MIP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the current feasible set and let \(B\) be the probing assumptions. A logical artifact \(B\Rightarrow C\) is valid if propagation, relaxation infeasibility, or another sound inference establishes \(F\cap B\subseteq C\). It is globally valid when \(B\) and every inference used are valid for the original feasible set; it is locally valid at a search node when they are valid only for that node's subproblem. The recorded derivation, together with the scopes of its premises, certifies the corresponding inclusion and determines the artifact's admissible scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A probing implication is valid when sound deductions show every feasible point satisfying its probe assumptions also satisfies its conclusion; premise scopes determine whether validity is global or local.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible set represented by the solver at the artifact's claimed scope.
Every propagation or relaxation inference in the recorded derivation is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap B\subseteq C\).

notation.meaning: feasible set at the claimed scope

review_flags: Exact solver-level validity and scope treatment requires a probing or conflict-analysis source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and inclusion-based validity criterion fit the leaf, but the global/local scope and derivation rules lack an inspectable probing or conflict-analysis source.

children.title: Relaxation-Assisted Probing
children.top_down_role: Probing augmented by LP, NLP, or other relaxation information.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Assisted Probing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary probing strengthened by a valid continuous or convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a mixed-integer feasible set \(F\), a relaxation \(R\supseteq F\), and a binary variable \(x_j\), solve or propagate separately over \(R_0=R\cap\{x_j=0\}\) and \(R_1=R\cap\{x_j=1\}\). If \(R_v=\varnothing\), delete branch \(x_j=v\) and fix \(x_j=1-v\). If a bound \(\ell_k^{v}\le x_k\le u_k^{v}\) is valid on each nonempty branch, retain the branch implication and infer the unconditional bound \(\min_v\ell_k^{v}\le x_k\le\max_v u_k^{v}\). Stop after the selected probes and output all scope-valid fixings, bounds, implications, and conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probe each binary value inside a valid relaxation; relaxation infeasibility yields a fixing, while bounds valid in both surviving branches yield unconditional bounds and branch implications.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\).
\(x_j\in\{0,1\}\) for every point of \(F\).
Each reported relaxation bound or infeasibility conclusion is certified sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output artifacts are valid for \(F\) at the scope where \(R\) is valid.

notation.meaning: valid branch-specific bounds on variable k

review_flags: The cited relaxation sections provisionally support relaxation validity; the probing combination needs source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is mathematically plausible, but the cited relaxation sections do not specifically support the probing procedure, persistence of branch implications, or combined-branch bound rule.

children.title: Probing Artifact Persistence System
children.top_down_role: Persistence of implications, fixings, aggregations, and conflicts discovered during probing.

children.title: Probing Implications
children.top_down_role: Logical consequences retained from tentative domain restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Probing Implications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent conditional bounds obtained from a sound probe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set at the probe's scope, and impose a probe literal \(L\). If sound propagation under \(L\) derives \(x_k\le u\), then \(F\cap L\subseteq\{x:x_k\le u\}\), so the implication \(L\Rightarrow x_k\le u\) may be stored. The analogous statement holds for a derived lower bound or literal. The implication may be reused only in subproblems whose feasible sets are contained in the scope where both \(L\) and the derivation are valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound or literal soundly derived under a probe can be stored as an implication and reused only within the derivation's validity scope.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a valid probe literal at the current scope.
The propagation procedure is sound for \(F\cap L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap L\subseteq\{x:x_k\le u\}\).

notation.meaning: feasible set at the probe scope

review_flags: A source explicitly covering persistent MIP probing implications is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches probing implications and is internally coherent, but no source supports storing and reusing such implications under the stated scope rule.

children.title: Probing Fixings
children.top_down_role: Variable fixings established through probing outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Probing Fixings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable fixing certified by infeasibility of one probe branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set at the current scope and let \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\). If a sound probing procedure certifies \(F\,\cap\,\{x_j=v\}=\varnothing\) for some \(v\in\{0,1\}\), then every point in \(F\) satisfies \(x_j=1-v\). The branch-infeasibility certificate therefore certifies the fixing. The fixing is global only when the infeasibility certificate uses exclusively globally valid constraints and assumptions; otherwise it inherits the local scope of the strongest local premise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If probing certifies one value of a binary variable infeasible, the opposite value is fixed; the fixing inherits the scope of its premises.
assumptions_latex: Infeasibility of the probed branch is established by a sound certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\{x:x_j=1-v\}\).

notation.meaning: feasible set at the fixing's scope

review_flags: The elementary disjunction argument is clear, but a solver-probing source is absent from the supplied inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branch-infeasibility certificate correctly implies the opposite binary fixing, but the solver-level certificate and inherited-scope claims are uncited.

children.title: Probing Aggregations
children.top_down_role: Recoverable variable relationships discovered during probing.

knowledge_statements.title: Probing Aggregations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear equality discovered from complementary probe branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set, let \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\), and suppose sound probing proves \(x_k=a_0\) on \(F\cap\{x_j=0\}\) and \(x_k=a_1\) on \(F\cap\{x_j=1\}\). Since these two branches partition \(F\), every feasible point satisfies the aggregation \(x_k=a_0+(a_1-a_0)x_j\). The two branch derivations certify the equality. Its persistence scope is the intersection of their scopes, and substitution is permitted only where the equality remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If complementary binary probes fix another variable to two branch values, those results certify an affine aggregation linking the variables.
assumptions_latex: Both branch fixings are derived soundly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k=a_0+(a_1-a_0)x_j\) for every \(x\in F\).

notation.meaning: feasible set at the common scope

review_flags: A source for probing-derived aggregations and their persistence rules is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine aggregation follows from the two complementary binary branches and the certificate kind fits, but no source supports probing-derived aggregation persistence and substitution.

children.title: Probing Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Conflict information derived from infeasible probing branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Probing Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict clause certified by infeasibility under probe assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set and let \(L_1,\ldots,L_r\) be Boolean probe literals. If sound propagation or a valid relaxation certifies \(F\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^{r}L_i=\varnothing\), then the conflict constraint \(\bigvee_{i=1}^{r}\neg L_i\) is valid for \(F\). The infeasibility derivation certifies the conflict. The learned constraint may be stored globally exactly when all premises used by the derivation are global; otherwise it is valid only below a search node containing every local premise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasibility under a conjunction of probe literals certifies the clause stating that at least one of those literals must be false.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_i\) is a Boolean literal defined on \(F\).
The joint infeasibility conclusion is derived soundly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}\neg L_i\).

notation.meaning: feasible set at the conflict's scope

review_flags: A conflict-analysis source tying probing infeasibility to learned-clause scope is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conflict clause follows from joint infeasibility and fits the certificate container, but the conflict-learning and global-versus-local scope rules require a source.

children.title: Artifact Persistence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Storage, validity scope, invalidation, and later consumption of probing artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Artifact Persistence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scope rule for retaining artifacts learned during probing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate every probing artifact \(A\) with a validity region \(S_A\) containing exactly the subproblems for which its derivation premises remain valid. An artifact is globally persistent when \(S_A\) contains every search subproblem, subtree-persistent when it contains all descendants of one node, and probe-temporary when it is valid only while the probe assumptions are active. Reusing \(A\) in a subproblem with feasible set \(F_N\) is sound only if \(F_N\subseteq S_A\); otherwise the artifact must be discarded or revalidated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store each probing artifact with a global, subtree, or temporary scope, and reuse it only when the current subproblem lies inside that validity region.
assumptions_latex: Each artifact has a sound derivation whose premise scopes are recorded.
Search descendants preserve the local constraints of their ancestors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Artifact reuse at node \(N\) is sound only if \(F_N\subseteq S_A\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of search node N

review_flags: Solver-specific artifact lifetime and revalidation regimes require an authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed persistence regimes. Moreover, S_A is introduced as a set of subproblems but later treated as a point set in F_N subseteq S_A; the validity object and containment relation must be typed consistently.

children.title: Domain Propagation
children.top_down_role: Iterated inference from constraints, objectives, implications, and relaxations during presolve and search.

children.title: Constraint-Objective Propagation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Inference from semantic constraints and incumbent-relative objective information.

children.title: Constraint Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference driven by active semantic or algebraic constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterated domain reduction using individual constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\) and a current domain box \(D=\prod_j D_j\), apply a sound contractor \(T_i\) satisfying \(F\cap D\subseteq T_i(D)\subseteq D\), where \(F=\{x:g_i(x)\le0\text{ for all }i\}\). Whenever a contractor tightens a component domain, enqueue every constraint incident to that variable. Continue until the queue is empty, a prescribed resource limit is reached, or some component domain becomes empty. Output the final box; an empty component certifies infeasibility of the current subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply sound constraint contractors, revisiting affected constraints after every bound change, until stable, limited, or infeasible.
assumptions_latex: Every contractor \(T_i\) preserves all points satisfying constraint \(i\) within its input box.
Variable domains admit intersection and emptiness tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(D'\) satisfies \(F\cap D\subseteq D'\subseteq D\), or \(F\cap D=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: current Cartesian product of variable domains

review_flags: The precise contractor formulation requires confirmation against the cited section.

children.title: Objective Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference driven by objective limits, incumbent cutoffs, or objective structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain tightening from an incumbent objective cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with objective \(f(x)\), current domain \(D\), and incumbent cutoff \(U\), treat \(f(x)\le U\) as an additional constraint. Apply a sound objective contractor \(T_f\) such that \(\{x\in D:f(x)\le U\}\subseteq T_f(D)\subseteq D\), and propagate every resulting bound change through the ordinary constraints. Repeat objective and constraint propagation until no retained bound changes, infeasibility is detected, or a resource limit is reached. Output the reduced domain, or prune if it becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, propagate the valid cutoff inequality like a constraint, alternate it with ordinary propagation, and prune if the reduced domain becomes empty.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent or another valid strict-search cutoff.
\(T_f\) preserves every point in \(D\) satisfying the cutoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every improving feasible point in \(D\) remains in the output domain, or none exists if the output is empty.
review_flags: A source explicitly describing objective-based domain propagation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-cutoff contractor algorithm is coherent and fits the leaf, but no source specifically supports objective-based domain propagation or its alternation with constraint propagation.

children.title: Propagation Source Coordination
children.top_down_role: Exchange and prioritization of deductions produced by constraint-side or objective-side sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Source Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair fixed-point scheduling across constraint, logical, and objective propagators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D^0\) be an initial domain, let \(X\subseteq D^0\) be the set of points satisfying every enabled constraint, logical relation, and valid objective cutoff, and let \(T_1,\ldots,T_m\) be domain operators such that \(X\cap D\subseteq T_i(D)\subseteq D\) for every reachable domain \(D\). Initialize a queue with all enabled operators. When \(T_i\) is removed, replace the current domain \(D^t\) by \(D^{t+1}=T_i(D^t)\); if any component changes, enqueue every enabled operator that depends on that component. Stop on an empty domain, a declared resource limit, or an empty queue. Under a finite-height domain order and fair scheduling, empty-queue termination produces a domain \(D^*\) satisfying \(T_i(D^*)=D^*\) for every enabled operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate all sound propagation sources with a dependency queue. Reschedule every operator affected by any domain change; on finite-height domains, fair unrestricted execution terminates at a common fixed point while preserving all jointly feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(X\cap D\subseteq T_i(D)\subseteq D\) for every enabled \(i\) and every reachable domain \(D\).
The dependency relation enqueues every operator whose result can be affected by a changed component.
The scheduler is fair and the domain order has finite descending height.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At empty-queue termination, \(X\subseteq D^*\subseteq D^0\) and \(T_i(D^*)=D^*\) for every enabled \(i\).

notation.meaning: points satisfying all enabled propagation sources within the initial domain

review_flags: A propagation-specific source should confirm the exact fixed-point scheduling formulation.

children.title: Objective-Cutoff Validity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of objective propagation on incumbent state, optimization context, and cutoff scope.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Cutoff Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which an incumbent cutoff safely supports minimization propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\), an objective cutoff \(U\) is valid for improvement search if every solution that the algorithm must still retain belongs to \(F_U=\{x\in F:f(x)<U\}\) or, when ties must be retained, to \(\{x\in F:f(x)\le U\}\). A feasible incumbent \(\bar x\in F\) supplies \(U=f(\bar x)\). Pruning a region \(Q\) by the cutoff is valid when a sound lower bound \(L(Q)\) satisfies \(L(Q)\ge U\) for strict improvement search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent gives a valid minimization cutoff; a region is safely pruned when its sound lower bound cannot beat that cutoff.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(L(Q)\le\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap Q\}\), with the infimum conventionally infinite when \(F\cap Q\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L(Q)\ge U\), then no \(x\in F\cap Q\) satisfies \(f(x)<U\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound over region Q

children.title: Logical-Relation Propagation
children.top_down_role: Inference over stored logical relationships.

children.title: Implication-Graph Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference through stored directed implications.

knowledge_statements.title: Implication-Graph Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward propagation of active literals through valid implication arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a directed graph whose vertices are Boolean literals and whose arc \((p,q)\) represents the valid implication \(p\Rightarrow q\). Initialize a queue with the currently true literals. Repeatedly remove \(p\), and for each outgoing arc activate \(q\) if it is not already true, recording \(p\) as a reason and enqueueing \(q\). If both \(q\) and \(\neg q\) become active, return a conflict; otherwise stop when the queue is empty and output the reachability closure of the initial literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from active literals, traverse valid implication arcs, activating every reachable consequence and reporting conflict if a literal and its negation are both reached.
assumptions_latex: Every arc in \(E\) is a valid implication at the current search scope.
Initial active literals are valid assumptions of the current subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every activated literal follows from the initial literals, and simultaneous activation of \(q\) and \(\neg q\) certifies inconsistency.
review_flags: A source for implication-graph propagation in MIP presolve or search is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward-reachability algorithm is internally consistent and fits implication-graph propagation, but no source supports its use and scope semantics in MIP presolve or search.

children.title: Clique Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference through mutual-exclusion structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain filtering for an at-most-one relation among binary literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given binary literals \(\ell_i\in\{x_i,1-x_i\}\) satisfying the clique inequality \(\sum_{i\in C}\ell_i\le 1\), maintain current literal domains. If some \(\ell_k\) is fixed to \(1\), set \(\ell_i:=0\) for every \(i\in C\setminus\{k\}\). If two distinct literals are fixed to \(1\), report infeasibility. Otherwise make no clique deduction. Repeat affected cliques until a complete pass produces no domain change; output the resulting domains or the infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an at-most-one clique, a true literal forces every other literal false; two true literals certify infeasibility. Process affected cliques to a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(i\in C\).
\(\sum_{i\in C}\ell_i\le 1\) is valid for the current subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output domains preserve every feasible assignment satisfying the clique inequality.

notation.meaning: Index set of mutually conflicting binary literals.
Binary literal equal to either a variable or its complement.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports clique propagation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches clique propagation and is mathematically sound for a valid at-most-one inequality, but no inspectable source or locator supports the fixed-point processing and certificate formulation.

children.title: Cross-Structure Inference
children.top_down_role: Inference transferred between implication graphs, cliques, or equivalent logical stores.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Structure Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound propagation obtained by combining interacting constraint representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the current variable domain and let \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) be valid structures, such as linear rows, cliques, implications, or variable-bound relations. A cross-structure inference replaces \(D\) by \(D'\subseteq D\) only when every point in \(D\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^m S_j\) belongs to \(D'\). Thus deductions may use facts transferred between representations, but they must not remove any assignment feasible for all participating structures. Iterating finitely many contracting, sound inference operators to stability yields a sound common fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information may pass among rows, cliques, implications, and bounds, provided every domain reduction preserves all assignments satisfying the participating structures.
assumptions_latex: Each participating structure \(S_j\) is valid for the current subproblem.
Every applied inference operator is contracting and feasibility preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^m S_j=D'\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^m S_j\).

notation.meaning: Current Cartesian product of variable domains.
Feasible set represented by the j-th recognized structure.

review_flags: No supplied locator identifies a formal cross-structure propagation calculus.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility-preservation principle fits the leaf, but the cross-representation terminology and common-fixed-point formulation have no cited source. A source should also state the conditions under which iteration reaches stability.

children.title: Relaxation-Guided Propagation
children.top_down_role: Inference informed by relaxation solutions and dual artifacts.
