knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Guided Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe domain deductions using relaxation bounds, solutions, or dual certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set of a minimization subproblem with objective vector \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(U\in\mathbb R\) be the value of a feasible incumbent, and let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(F\subseteq R\). For a candidate restriction \(H\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), suppose a valid relaxation certificate supplies \(L(H)\in\mathbb R\) such that \(L(H)\leq\inf\{c^\top x:x\in R\cap H\}\). If \(L(H)\geq U\), then no feasible point in \(H\) has objective value strictly below \(U\), so \(H\) may be excluded when searching for a strictly improving solution. Relaxation solutions may prioritize candidate restrictions, but any permanent domain reduction must be justified by a valid bound, infeasibility certificate, or implication for the original subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a minimization problem, a restriction may be excluded from the search for a solution better than the incumbent when a certified relaxation lower bound over that restriction is at least the incumbent value. Relaxation artifacts may guide candidate selection, but permanent pruning requires a valid certificate for the original subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and \(H\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
\(L(H)\leq\inf\{c^\top x:x\in R\cap H\}\).
The search seeks a feasible point with objective value strictly below \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap H\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^n:c^\top x<U\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Decision vector and linear objective vector in the real n-dimensional space.
Original feasible set and a relaxation containing it.
Candidate branch, domain slice, or restriction.
Certified lower bound under the restriction and incumbent upper bound.

review_flags: propagation-specific formulation should be checked against solver literature

children.title: Propagation Lifecycle Regimes
children.top_down_role: Lifecycle placements for domain inference.

children.title: Presolve Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference performed before tree search.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-level fixed-point domain reduction before branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(D:=D^0\), the original variable domain. Apply enabled sound presolve propagators \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\), where each \(P_i(D)\subseteq D\) preserves the feasible set represented within \(D\). Whenever a propagator changes a domain, enqueue every propagator depending on that domain. Stop when the queue is empty, infeasibility is certified, or an implementation effort limit is reached. Output the reduced root domain together with reversible transformation data sufficient to reconstruct solutions in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before search, repeatedly apply sound domain reductions, rescheduling affected propagators, and retain transformation data needed to recover original solutions.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_i\) preserves all feasible points in its input domain.
Presolve transformations are recorded when they alter the model representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced model is infeasible exactly when certified so; otherwise its solutions reconstruct to solutions of the original model.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the presolve propagation lifecycle.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifecycle fits presolve propagation, but no cited source supports the queue semantics or reconstruction requirement. Merely recording transformations does not by itself guarantee that reduced-model solutions reconstruct; an explicit equivalence or reconstruction hypothesis is needed.

children.title: Node Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference under local search-tree domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local domain propagation after branch decisions at a search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node \(v\), initialize \(D_v\) by intersecting the inherited parent domain with the branching restrictions on the path to \(v\). Enqueue propagators affected by these new restrictions and repeatedly apply sound contracting operators. If a variable domain becomes empty or a constraint supplies a contradiction certificate, prune \(v\). Otherwise stop at queue exhaustion or the configured effort limit and pass the resulting domain to relaxation solution, separation, or branching. On backtracking, restore the parent state without retaining node-local deductions outside their valid subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each search node, propagate inherited bounds and branch decisions; prune contradictions, otherwise pass tightened domains onward and undo local deductions when backtracking.
assumptions_latex: Branching restrictions are valid throughout the subtree rooted at \(v\).
Every invoked propagator preserves feasible points of the node subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned domain contains exactly all node-feasible points not excluded by sound deductions.

notation.meaning: Current variable domain at the node.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports node propagation and backtracking semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits node propagation, but the backtracking and effort-limit semantics lack a source. The conclusion's phrase 'exactly all node-feasible points not excluded' is ambiguous because a propagated domain may also contain infeasible points.

children.title: Probing Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference within temporary hypothetical domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Probing Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tentative fixing with propagation, conflict detection, and common-consequence extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an unfixed binary variable \(x\in\{0,1\}\). Temporarily impose \(x=0\), propagate soundly to obtain \(D^0\) or a contradiction, restore the initial state, and repeat with \(x=1\) to obtain \(D^1\) or a contradiction. If exactly one tentative branch yields a contradiction, fix \(x\) to the value of the other branch; if both yield contradictions, certify infeasibility. If neither yields a contradiction, retain only deductions valid for every point in \(D^0\cup D^1\). Restore all other temporary changes and output the permanent deductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test both values of an unfixed binary variable and propagate each value temporarily. If one case is contradictory, fix the other value; if both are contradictory, certify infeasibility; otherwise retain only consequences valid in both cases.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}\) is currently unfixed.
Propagation within each tentative branch is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every permanent deduction is valid for the subproblem that existed before probing.

notation.meaning: Propagated domains under the tentative fixings zero and one, when those branches are consistent.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports probing propagation.
common-consequence extraction requires a solver-specific source

children.title: Propagation Scheduling-Explanation System
children.top_down_role: Coordination of repeated inference and retention of reasons for later learning.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Propagator properties, presolving timing, and conflict analysis

children.title: Propagation Activation Policies
children.top_down_role: Ordering and activation of inference components.

children.title: Propagation Priority Policies
children.top_down_role: Ordering policies for competing inference components.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Priority Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queue ordering of eligible propagators without changing deductive validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be the set of currently eligible propagator invocations. Assign each \(q\in Q\) a priority score \(\pi(q)\) computed from fixed policy data and current solver state, and execute an element of \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{q\in Q}\pi(q)\), resolving ties deterministically or by a declared rule. After execution, update eligibility and scores of affected invocations. Priority changes execution order only: every emitted deduction must remain independently sound, and termination occurs at queue exhaustion or a separate effort limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank eligible propagators by a policy score, execute a highest-ranked one, and update the queue; ordering never substitutes for deduction validity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) contains only eligible propagator invocations.
Each invocation is sound independently of its priority.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scheduling by \(\pi\) changes order and cost but does not invalidate emitted deductions.
review_flags: No supplied locator defines propagation priority policies.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Priority-based queue ordering fits the leaf and does not overstate deductive validity, but the scoring, tie-breaking, and update semantics are implementation-dependent and have no cited locator.

children.title: Propagation Delay Policies
children.top_down_role: Activation deferral based on expected utility or current solver state.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Delay Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional postponement of eligible propagators until specified activation events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each eligible propagator \(p\), evaluate a declared delay predicate \(\delta_p(s)\) on solver state \(s\). If \(\delta_p(s)=1\), keep \(p\) dormant until a specified wake event occurs, such as a relevant domain change, exhaustion of higher-priority propagators, or entry into a later propagation round. If \(\delta_p(s)=0\), enqueue \(p\). A delayed propagator may be omitted only under an explicit effort policy; delay itself changes timing, not the soundness requirements on deductions eventually produced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delay predicate postpones eligible propagators until declared wake events; postponement affects timing, while all eventual deductions must remain sound.
assumptions_latex: Each delayed propagator has a declared wake condition.
Every produced deduction is sound for the state in which it is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Delay affects activation time but does not justify any otherwise invalid domain reduction.

notation.meaning: Predicate indicating whether p is delayed in state s.

review_flags: No supplied locator defines propagation delay policies.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The delay-policy algorithm fits the container, but its delay predicate and wake-event semantics are an uncited implementation formalization.

children.title: Propagation Frequency Policies
children.top_down_role: Invocation cadence across rounds, nodes, or lifecycle phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Frequency Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-dependent limits on how often a propagator is activated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each propagator \(p\), maintain an invocation counter \(n_p\) and evaluate an activation predicate \(f_p(n_p,s)\) in solver state \(s\). Invoke \(p\) only when it is eligible and \(f_p(n_p,s)=1\); after invocation, increment \(n_p\) and update any state-dependent schedule. Examples include every propagation round, every \(k\)-th node, root only, or only after a relevant domain event. Frequency controls computational effort but cannot make an unsound deduction valid; skipped invocations may weaken propagation without changing feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activation predicate controls how often an eligible propagator runs. Skipping runs may reduce inference strength but cannot remove feasible solutions.
assumptions_latex: Invocation eligibility is determined separately from frequency.
Every invoked propagator is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Changing \(f_p\) may alter runtime and attained closure but preserves feasibility of retained domains.
review_flags: No supplied locator defines propagation frequency policies.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The frequency-policy formulation fits the leaf, but the activation predicate, counter semantics, and listed schedules require solver documentation or propagation-scheduling literature.

children.title: Propagation Effort Regimes
children.top_down_role: Effort classes for presolve and propagation participation.

children.title: Fast Propagation Regime
children.top_down_role: Low-cost inference participation for latency-sensitive processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Fast Propagation Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Low-effort propagation using a restricted operator set or strict budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a domain \(D\), a set of sound propagators \(\mathcal P\), and a small effort budget \(B_f\), select a designated inexpensive subset \(\mathcal P_f\subseteq\mathcal P\). Process eligible members of \(\mathcal P_f\) until infeasibility is certified, no selected propagator remains eligible, or measured work reaches \(B_f\). Return the current domain immediately at the budget limit. The result need not be a common fixed point of \(\mathcal P\), but every performed reduction must preserve all feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run only inexpensive propagators under a strict budget. The returned domain is sound but need not be fully propagation-closed.
assumptions_latex: Every propagator in \(\mathcal P_f\) is sound and contracting.
Work is measured by a declared implementation cost metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output domain is sound, though it may not be a fixed point of \(\mathcal P\).
review_flags: No supplied locator defines a fast propagation regime.
budget and inexpensive-operator classifications are implementation dependent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded low-effort algorithm is internally sound and fits a fast regime, but neither the regime nor its inexpensive-operator and budget classification has cited support.

children.title: Medium Propagation Regime
children.top_down_role: Balanced inference participation with moderate resource use.

knowledge_statements.title: Medium Propagation Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balanced propagation with broader operators and a moderate effort budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given domain \(D\), sound propagators \(\mathcal P\), and budget \(B_m\), choose \(\mathcal P_f\subseteq\mathcal P_m\subseteq\mathcal P\), where \(\mathcal P_m\) includes the fast-regime operators and designated additional or more expensive propagators. Schedule eligible members of \(\mathcal P_m\) until contradiction, queue exhaustion, or exhaustion of \(B_m\). Output the current domain. With identical initial state and deterministic monotone operators, running the same fast phase followed by additional sound work cannot reintroduce values removed by that fast phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a broader propagator set and moderate budget than the fast regime; additional sound work can tighten, but never enlarge, the propagated domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_f\subseteq\mathcal P_m\) and all selected propagators are sound and contracting.
The medium run starts from the fast phase's resulting state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The medium-regime output is contained in the preceding fast-regime output.
review_flags: No supplied locator defines a medium propagation regime.
nesting relative to the fast regime is a selected formalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additional contracting work cannot enlarge the fast-phase output when the medium run begins from that output, but the nested propagator sets and medium-budget regime are an uncited selected formalization.

children.title: Exhaustive Propagation Regime
children.top_down_role: High-investment inference participation seeking deeper domain reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Propagation Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation to common stability over all enabled operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D^0\) be a finite product of finite variable domains and let \(\mathcal P=\{P_1,\ldots,P_m\}\) be enabled sound, contracting propagators. Starting from \(D:=D^0\), apply propagators under a fair schedule, reactivating every operator affected by a domain change. Stop on contradiction or when \(P_i(D)=D\) for every \(i\). Because each strict update removes at least one domain value, the process terminates after finitely many strict reductions and returns a sound common fixed point; different noncommuting propagators may yield different fixed points unless additional closure conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fairly apply every enabled propagator until none changes the finite domains. This terminates at a sound common fixed point, though order independence needs extra conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(D^0\) is a finite product of finite domains.
Every \(P_i\) is sound and contracting.
The schedule is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates with contradiction or a domain \(D\) satisfying \(P_i(D)=D\) for all \(i\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the exhaustive fixed-point propagation formulation.
order-independence boundary needs a propagation-theory source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain fair-scheduling algorithm correctly reaches a sound common fixed point under the stated assumptions and fits the exhaustive regime. A propagation-theory source is still required for the fixed-point and order-dependence claims.

children.title: Propagation Stopping Calculus
children.top_down_role: Stopping and repetition controls for inference rounds.

children.title: Propagation Fixed Points
children.top_down_role: Termination after inference rounds cease producing material domain changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Fixed Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines quiescence for monotone bound propagation over a finite-domain MIP state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) be the current variable domain, ordered by componentwise inclusion, and let \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\) be sound contracting propagators. Define one complete propagation sweep by \(P=P_m\circ\cdots\circ P_1\). The domain \(D^*\) is a propagation fixed point when \(P_j(D^*)=D^*\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), equivalently when no scheduled propagator can remove a value or tighten a bound. If each \(P_j\) is monotone and contracting and the domain lattice has finite height, repeated fair application terminates at such a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation fixed point is a domain on which every propagator makes no further reduction; finite-height domains and fair monotone propagation guarantee termination at one.
assumptions_latex: \(P_j(D)\subseteq D\) for every propagator \(P_j\).
Each \(P_j\) is monotone under componentwise set inclusion.
The domain lattice has finite height.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^*\) is quiescent exactly when \(P_j(D^*)=D^*\) for all \(j\).

notation.meaning: Current Cartesian product of variable domains.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-domain propagation fixed-point formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point definition is standard, but the record also asserts finite-height fair-scheduling termination. No cited source with an inspectable locator supports that theorem or its precise fairness assumptions.

children.title: Propagation Round Limits
children.top_down_role: Hard caps on repeated inference passes.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Round Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies a deterministic cap on complete propagation sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial domain \(D^0\), an ordered propagator family \((P_1,\ldots,P_m)\), and an integer limit \(R\geq 0\), set \(r=0\). While \(r<R\), execute one complete scheduled sweep to obtain \(D^{r+1}=P_m\circ\cdots\circ P_1(D^r)\). Stop early if \(D^{r+1}=D^r\) or if some component domain is empty; otherwise increment \(r\). Return the last domain together with status fixed-point, infeasible, or round-limit. Round-limit status does not assert propagation closure, because an unexecuted sweep may still tighten the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run at most a prescribed number of propagation sweeps, stopping earlier at quiescence or domain infeasibility; hitting the cap does not certify a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(R\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\).
Every applied propagator is sound and contracting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is sound, but status round-limit need not imply \(P_j(D)=D\) for every \(j\).

notation.meaning: Maximum number of complete propagation sweeps.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the round-limit leaf and correctly distinguishes a cap from closure, but no cited source supports the chosen complete-sweep semantics or status contract.

children.title: Diminishing-Return Stopping
children.top_down_role: Early termination when additional inference yields insufficient benefit.

knowledge_statements.title: Diminishing-Return Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines heuristic stopping from measured propagation gain relative to computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D^r\) be the domain after propagation round \(r\), let \(g_r\geq 0\) measure that round's reduction, and let \(c_r>0\) measure its computational cost. Given a threshold \(\tau\geq 0\) and patience \(q\geq 1\), continue propagation unless infeasibility or a fixed point is detected, but stop with status diminishing-return when \(g_s/c_s\leq\tau\) for every \(s\in\{r-q+1,\ldots,r\}\). The returned domain remains a sound relaxation reduction, although diminishing-return status is heuristic and does not certify propagation closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop after several consecutive rounds have insufficient gain per unit cost. The reduced domain stays sound, but this heuristic does not certify quiescence.
assumptions_latex: \(g_r\geq 0\) and \(c_r>0\) are consistently measured across rounds.
\(\tau\geq 0\) and \(q\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}\).
Every accepted domain reduction is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Diminishing-return stopping preserves soundness but does not imply \(P_j(D^r)=D^r\) for all \(j\).

notation.meaning: Measured domain reduction during round r.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits diminishing-return stopping, but the gain-to-cost rule, patience window, and stopping semantics are an uncited policy rather than a standard uniquely determined formulation.

children.title: Inference-Reason Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Reason-retention regimes supporting conflict analysis.

children.title: Stored Inference Reasons
children.top_down_role: Explicitly retained justification artifacts for later conflict analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Stored Inference Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes an eagerly recorded explanation for a propagated bound or literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose propagation derives a literal \(\ell\) from the current constraint system and active literals \(A\). A stored inference reason is a finite set \(R\subseteq A\), recorded when \(\ell\) is derived, such that the relevant constraint semantics entail \(R\Rightarrow\ell\). The stored object certifies the inference when a checker can verify that every member of \(R\) was active at derivation time and that \(R\wedge\neg\ell\) is inconsistent with the cited constraint or propagator rule. The reason may subsequently be used for conflict analysis while its referenced literals and constraint remain identifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stored reason records active antecedents that entail a propagated literal and can later be checked against the responsible constraint or propagation rule.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq A\) at the inference time.
The cited constraint or propagation rule has checkable semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Verification of \(R\Rightarrow\ell\) certifies that the inference \(\ell\) was logically justified.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, but the implication-based reason object, historical-activity requirement, and permitted later use require a direct source on MIP propagation explanations.

children.title: Reconstructed Inference Reasons
children.top_down_role: Justification artifacts recovered on demand from retained solver state.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstructed Inference Reasons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recreates a propagation explanation on demand from retained inference context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a previously derived literal \(\ell\), retain an identifier for its propagator or constraint and sufficient snapshot data \(S\) describing the relevant inference state. On request, invoke a deterministic explanation routine \(E\) and compute \(R=E(\ell,S)\). Accept \(R\) only if each antecedent was active in the represented state and an independent check establishes \(R\Rightarrow\ell\) under the cited constraint semantics. Otherwise report reason-unavailable. Reconstruction may return a reason different from one that could have been stored originally, but it must justify the same inferred literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruct a reason on demand from retained context, then independently verify that its active antecedents entail the original inference; otherwise report unavailability.
assumptions_latex: The retained state \(S\) identifies the responsible constraint and relevant inference context.
The explanation routine \(E\) terminates and returns either antecedents or failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted reconstructed set \(R\) satisfies \(R\Rightarrow\ell\); reconstruction failure yields no certificate.

notation.meaning: Retained inference snapshot or sufficient context.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches on-demand reason reconstruction, but no source supports the asserted retained snapshot, deterministic explanation routine, independent verification interface, or failure semantics.

children.title: Reason Availability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where retention loss or reconstruction limits restrict conflict analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Reason Availability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when a past propagation inference lacks a recoverable explanation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a derived literal \(\ell\), a usable reason is available only if either an antecedent set \(R\) was stored or retained data determine a checkable set satisfying \(R\Rightarrow\ell\). If the responsible constraint was deleted without an equivalent retained representation, referenced antecedents lost their historical truth state, or reconstruction data identify multiple incompatible inference states without resolving the actual one, then the original inference context is not certifiably recoverable. In that case the solver must mark the reason unavailable and must not use an unverified surrogate reason in proof-producing conflict analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reason is unavailable when neither stored antecedents nor retained context can yield a checkable implication for the inference; unverified substitutes cannot support certified conflict analysis.
assumptions_latex: Conflict analysis requires independently checkable implication reasons.
No external proof object supplies the missing inference context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absent stored or reconstructible \(R\) with \(R\Rightarrow\ell\), the inference has no available reason certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificate availability requires retained checkable context

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the listed loss conditions and prohibition on surrogate reasons in proof-producing conflict analysis need direct authoritative support.

children.title: Reversible Presolve Safety System
children.top_down_role: Structural obligations and failure boundaries connecting reduced models to original-space outcomes.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Certifying MIP-Based Presolve Reductions for 0–1 Integer Linear Programs
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Certifying MIP-Based Presolve Reductions for 0–1 Integer Linear Programs

children.title: Original-Space Solution Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-space solutions from reduced-space solutions.

children.title: Reduced-Space Solution Lifting
children.top_down_role: Transfer of reduced-model solution values through recorded transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Solution Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies a reversible presolve log backward to lift a reduced feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0\) be the original feasible set and let presolve transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) produce the reduced set \(F_k\). Each log entry supplies a partial inverse \(L_i\) satisfying \(L_i(y)\in F_{i-1}\) whenever \(y\in F_i\). Given \(y^k\in F_k\), set \(y^{i-1}=L_i(y^i)\) for \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), checking the entry's side conditions at each step. Output \(x=y^0\) only after verifying original bounds, integrality, and constraints. Under the inverse-validity assumptions, \(x\in F_0\), and an objective-preserving log also gives \(c^\top x=\bar c^\top y^k+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse the presolve log to lift a reduced feasible point, validate every inverse step, and accept only a point satisfying the original model.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_i\) is valid on every reduced state reachable at step \(i\).
The reduced point satisfies \(y^k\in F_k\).
All transformation side data required by the inverse maps are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reverse composition yields \(x=L_1\circ\cdots\circ L_k(y^k)\in F_0\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set after i presolve transformations.
Logged partial inverse for transformation i.
Feasible solution of the reduced model.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reverse-composition model of reversible presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reverse-log lifting algorithm is plausible and locally appropriate, but no cited source supports the partial-inverse abstraction, side-condition protocol, or objective-adjustment formula.

children.title: Original-Variable Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of eliminated or substituted variables in original model space.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Variable Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers eliminated variables from logged defining relations and admissible domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Process eliminated variables in reverse dependency order. For each original variable \(x_j\), use its logged recovery relation \(x_j=\phi_j(z)\), or choose \(x_j\) from a logged nonempty admissible set \(I_j(z)\), where \(z\) contains already recovered and surviving variables. Require \(x_j\in\mathbb Z\) for every original integer variable and enforce its original bounds. If no admissible value exists, return recovery-failure. After all variables are assigned, return \(x\) only if the complete original constraint system accepts it; otherwise return recovery-failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover eliminated variables in reverse dependency order using logged equations or admissible sets, enforcing original bounds, integrality, and final feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The recovery dependency graph is acyclic after reversing the presolve order.
Each recovery relation or admissible set is retained with its side conditions.
Surviving reduced variables have already been assigned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful recovery returns a complete vector \(x\) satisfying all original domains and constraints.

notation.meaning: Logged admissible set for nondeterministic recovery.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reverse dependency recovery from presolve substitutions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits original-variable recovery, but the reverse dependency order, admissible-set recovery model, and stated acyclicity assumption require a specific presolve/postsolve source.

children.title: Reconstruction Failure Handling
children.top_down_role: Postsolve cases affected by missing records, inconsistent values, or numerical loss.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Failure Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines safe handling when postsolve cannot validate a lifted original-space solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) be a reduced-space solution and let the postsolve procedure return either a candidate \(x\) or a failure witness \(w\). Reconstruction fails if an inverse-map precondition is false, required log data are absent, no recovered value satisfies its original domain, or final validation finds \(x\notin F_0\). On failure, the solver must not report \(x\) as an original-model feasible solution. It must preserve \(w\), invalidate the affected solution claim, and either retry with a sound alternative reconstruction, resolve an unreduced model, or terminate with an explicit postsolve-failure status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If inverse data, domains, or final feasibility checks fail, reject the lifted point and retry safely or report explicit postsolve failure.
assumptions_latex: Original-model feasibility can be checked independently.
A reconstruction attempt records enough context to identify its failing step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If validation does not establish \(x\in F_0\), no original-space feasibility claim may be issued for \(x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound postsolve requires rejection of unvalidated lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification is appropriate, but the required witness preservation, retry alternatives, unreduced resolve, and explicit failure status are uncited solver-policy claims.

children.title: Relaxation-Artifact Postsolve Family
children.top_down_role: Recovery of relaxation artifacts needed for reuse, diagnosis, or certification.

children.title: Dual-Value Postsolve
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-space dual information after reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Value Postsolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maps reduced LP dual multipliers backward through dual-valid presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an original linear relaxation and a reduced relaxation obtained by logged transformations. Given reduced primal-dual values \((\bar x,\bar y)\), traverse the log backward. At each step apply its dual recovery map to restore multipliers for removed rows, translate multipliers under row scaling or aggregation, and update reduced costs for restored columns. Accept the reconstructed pair \((x,y)\) only if primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness hold for the original relaxation within declared tolerances. When every logged map preserves the primal-dual correspondence, an optimal reduced pair is mapped to an optimal original pair with the corresponding objective adjustment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse dual-valid presolve transformations to restore row multipliers and reduced costs, accepting them only after original primal-dual optimality checks.
assumptions_latex: The reduced pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is primal-dual optimal for the reduced relaxation.
Every presolve entry retains a valid dual recovery map.
Numerical acceptance tolerances are fixed before validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful validation yields an original pair \((x,y)\) satisfying primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness.

notation.meaning: Reconstructed original primal and dual solution.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reverse dual mapping with KKT validation for LP presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits dual-value postsolve, but dual recovery under deletion, scaling, and aggregation is transformation-specific; no source establishes the stated maps or optimality-preservation claim.

children.title: Basis Postsolve
children.top_down_role: Recovery or transfer of basis state for reuse or diagnosis.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Postsolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstructs an original LP basis from a reduced basis and presolve history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonsingular reduced LP basis \(\bar B\), traverse the presolve log backward. For each restored row or column, apply the entry's basis extension or pivot rule, assign a compatible basic or nonbasic status, and pivot when necessary to maintain a square nonsingular basis. Let \(B\) denote the resulting original-space basis. Accept it only if \(B\) has the original row dimension, is nonsingular, and its associated primal and dual basic solutions satisfy the declared feasibility tolerances. Degeneracy permits multiple valid reconstructed bases; postsolve need return only one valid basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse the presolve log, extending or pivoting the reduced basis until a nonsingular, dimensionally correct, primal-dual valid original basis is obtained.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar B\) is a valid nonsingular basis of the reduced relaxation.
Every basis-affecting presolve transformation records a valid inverse status or pivot rule.
Original rows and columns have identifiable postsolve positions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful postsolve returns a nonsingular original basis \(B\) with valid associated primal-dual basic solutions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reverse basis extension across LP presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits basis postsolve, but basis extension, status assignment, pivot rules, and guaranteed recovery of a valid original basis depend on transformation-specific results that are not cited.

children.title: Ray Postsolve
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-space infeasibility or unboundedness rays.

knowledge_statements.title: Ray Postsolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifts reduced unboundedness or infeasibility rays through reversible LP presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the reduced relaxation possess either a primal recession ray \(\bar d\) or a dual infeasibility ray \(\bar y\). Traverse the presolve log backward using homogeneous recovery maps for directions and the corresponding transpose maps for dual multipliers. A lifted primal ray \(d\) is accepted only if it satisfies the original recession constraints, variable-sign restrictions, and \(c^\top d<0\) for minimization. A lifted dual ray \(y\) is accepted only if it satisfies the original dual homogeneous constraints and the strict separating inequality required by the chosen Farkas convention. These checks certify the corresponding original-space conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift reduced primal or dual rays backward and validate the original homogeneous constraints and strict objective or separation inequality before certification.
assumptions_latex: Every ray-affecting presolve transformation retains a valid homogeneous recovery map.
The reduced ray satisfies its reduced-space certificate conditions.
The original primal or dual sign convention is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A validated \(d\) certifies original primal unboundedness, while a validated \(y\) certifies original primal infeasibility under the stated Farkas convention.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: homogeneous lifting and direct validation of LP rays

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf concerns ray postsolve, but the record combines two distinct lifting procedures and certificates—primal recession rays and dual Farkas rays—without fixing the primal-dual model or Farkas convention. Direct sources are needed to determine the valid maps, hypotheses, and whether algorithm rather than certificate is the proper role.

children.title: Presolve Audit Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Auditable evidence connecting transformations to recovered outcomes.

children.title: Reduction Logs
children.top_down_role: Recorded transformation histories supporting replay, recovery, or diagnosis.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Logs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational log for reversible presolve transformations of a mixed-integer optimization instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\) be a mixed-integer optimization instance. A reduction log is an ordered sequence \(L=((R_k,w_k,U_k))_{k=1}^{m}\), where \(R_k\) transforms \(P_{k-1}\) into \(P_k\), \(w_k\) records the data and predicates used to justify that transformation, and \(U_k\) reconstructs an admissible solution of \(P_{k-1}\) from any admissible solution of \(P_k\). The log is reversible when every \(U_k\) preserves feasibility and objective value, or records the exact objective offset introduced by \(R_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduction log records presolve transformations, their justification data, and reverse maps sufficient to reconstruct solutions while accounting exactly for objective changes.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0\) is a finite mixed-integer optimization instance.
Each logged transformation has a specified reconstruction convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=((R_k,w_k,U_k))_{k=1}^{m}\) is a reversible reduction log for \(P_0\).

notation.meaning: instance after the first k reductions
justification witness and numerical data for reduction k
solution reconstruction map for reduction k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operational definition synthesized from reversible-presolve practice

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Reduction Logs leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source is supplied for this particular reversible-log specification, including its witness fields and objective-offset semantics.

children.title: Presolve Certificates
children.top_down_role: Auditable evidence supporting presolve outcomes or transformation validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable evidence that presolve preserves feasibility and objective information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a reduction chain \(P_0\to P_1\to\cdots\to P_m\), a presolve certificate consists of witnesses \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\) and reconstruction maps \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\). A checker must verify from \((P_{k-1},P_k,c_k)\) that every feasible point retained in \(P_k\) corresponds under \(U_k\) to a feasible point of \(P_{k-1}\), with the recorded objective offset, and that every discarded point cannot improve the reduced optimum. If all checks succeed, the certificate attests that the chain preserves the optimum and supports postsolve reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve certificate supplies locally checkable witnesses and reconstruction maps establishing optimum preservation and valid postsolve recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0,\ldots,P_m\) use an exact, explicitly stated arithmetic or tolerance semantics.
Every reduction exposes a checker for its witness type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{opt}(P_0)=\operatorname{opt}(P_m)+\sum_{k=1}^{m}\delta_k\), with feasible solutions reconstructible by \(U_1\circ\cdots\circ U_m\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificate specification follows reversible transformation semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind fits the leaf, but the proposed local checking obligations and the resulting optimum-preservation claim require an authoritative certificate or presolve-verification source. The status of discarded points and the precise objective-offset convention cannot be validated from the supplied evidence.

children.title: Certificate-to-Log Traceability
children.top_down_role: Links between certified claims, recorded reductions, and recovered outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-to-Log Traceability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Traceability condition linking every certificate claim to concrete reduction-log entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m)\) be a reduction log and \(C=(c_1,\ldots,c_q)\) a presolve certificate. Certificate-to-log traceability holds when there is a total map \(\tau:\{1,\ldots,q\}\to 2^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}\) such that every datum used by checker claim \(c_j\) is either contained in the referenced entries \(\{\ell_i:i\in\tau(j)\}\) or deterministically derived from them, and every solution-affecting log entry is covered by at least one certificate claim. Dependencies between claims must respect the chronological dependency order of the referenced reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traceability requires every certificate claim to reference sufficient log entries and every solution-affecting reduction to be covered by a claim.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) and \(C\) have stable entry identifiers.
Derived certificate data have deterministic derivation rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\) provides complete, dependency-consistent traceability between \(C\) and \(L\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: audit-traceability predicate specialized to presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits Certificate-to-Log Traceability, but the total-map, coverage, derivation, and chronological-dependency requirements are a synthesized audit model without cited support. A formal solver-certificate or presolve-logging source is needed.

children.title: Reduction Reliability-Structure Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Reductions that jeopardize reliability or obscure exploitable structure.

children.title: Numerically Fragile Reductions
children.top_down_role: Transformations vulnerable to scaling, cancellation, tolerance, or conditioning effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerically Fragile Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision boundary for reductions justified by small residuals or divisors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a reduction whose validity is decided from a computed scalar \(\widehat r\) and threshold \(\tau\), while the exact decision depends on \(r\). If an error bound \(|\widehat r-r|\leq\varepsilon\) is known, the decision is numerically certified only when \(|\widehat r-\tau|>\varepsilon\). When \(|\widehat r-\tau|\leq\varepsilon\), either decision may disagree with exact arithmetic; elimination, fixing, or infeasibility declarations based on that comparison are numerically fragile and require exact checking, directed rounding, or deferral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A threshold-based reduction is fragile when its computed decision margin does not exceed the certified numerical error.
assumptions_latex: \(|\widehat r-r|\leq\varepsilon\) is a valid absolute error bound.
The reduction decision changes when \(r\) crosses \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widehat r-\tau|\leq\varepsilon\) is the unresolved numerical boundary; \(|\widehat r-\tau|>\varepsilon\) certifies the comparison's sign.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval-error test for threshold decisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval-error comparison is mathematically coherent and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but no source connects this generic threshold test to the claimed presolve failure boundary or prescribed remedies.

children.title: Structure-Destructive Reductions
children.top_down_role: Transformations that obscure exploitable combinatorial or algebraic structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Destructive Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where an equivalent reduction destroys exploitable block, network, or sparsity structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(P)\) be the variable-constraint incidence graph of an instance \(P\), and let \(s(P)\) be a declared structural measure such as maximum row support, separator size, or matrix bandwidth. An equivalent reduction \(R\) is structure-destructive relative to budget \(B\) when \(R(P)\) preserves the feasible optimum but \(s(R(P))>B\) while \(s(P)\leq B\). Substitution is a canonical mechanism: eliminating a variable adjacent to several constraints can connect all of its neighboring variables, creating fill-in despite reducing dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equivalent reduction is structure-destructive when induced fill-in pushes a chosen sparsity or decomposition measure beyond its usable budget.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) preserves the feasible optimum of \(P\).
\(s\) and the admissible budget \(B\) are fixed before applying \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(P)\leq B<s(R(P))\) marks loss of the declared exploitable structure.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_refs.locator: 5.6.1 Block structure p. 66; 5.6.2 Network structure p. 67

review_flags: locator supports structural context; exact failure-boundary formulation requires review

They do not yet support the budget-based definition, the asserted fill-in mechanism, or its application to equivalent presolve reductions.

children.title: Fragility–Structure Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Reduction choices balancing numerical reliability against structural simplification.

knowledge_statements.title: Fragility–Structure Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule balancing numerical safety, structural preservation, and reduction benefit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each admissible reduction \(R\), let \(g(R)\) denote predicted downstream work saved, \(f(R)\) its certified numerical-risk penalty, and \(d(R)\) its structural-damage penalty. Given nonnegative weights \(\lambda_f,\lambda_d\), select reductions only when \(g(R)-\lambda_f f(R)-\lambda_d d(R)>0\), subject to mandatory correctness checks. Consequently, a reduction with larger dimensional benefit need not be preferred when it has a small numerical decision margin or creates fill-in that impairs decomposition, sparsity, or relaxation solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a reduction only when predicted savings exceed its weighted numerical-risk and structural-damage penalties, after mandatory correctness checks.
assumptions_latex: \(g(R),f(R),d(R)\) are evaluated under one fixed cost scale.
\(\lambda_f,\lambda_d\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accept \(R\) only if \(g(R)>\lambda_f f(R)+\lambda_d d(R)\) and its correctness conditions are certified.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit decision model for competing presolve costs
empirical or theoretical calibration source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the tradeoff leaf, but the weighted selection rule is a proposed heuristic rather than a sourced presolve principle. Sources are needed for the meanings and calibration of the gain, numerical-risk, and structural-damage terms.

children.title: Presolve Cost-Reuse Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Reduction costs and state-reuse losses that can outweigh later savings.

children.title: Presolve Runtime Overhead
children.top_down_role: Time or memory costs incurred while discovering and applying reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Runtime Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work bound for repeated sparse presolve passes and their audit records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose presolve performs \(p\) passes over a representation containing \(N\) active nonzeros, each pass scans every active nonzero at most \(c\) times and performs \(O(1)\) amortized work per visit. If \(u\) accepted reductions each append \(O(1)\) log records, then presolve uses \(O(pN+u)\) time and \(O(N+u)\) storage. This bound excludes reduction routines requiring global factorizations, sorting, or closure computations; their separately accounted costs must be added.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under bounded sparse scans, p presolve passes cost O(pN+u) time and O(N+u) storage, excluding global subroutines.
assumptions_latex: Each pass visits an active nonzero at most \(c=O(1)\) times.
Each accepted reduction creates \(O(1)\) audit records.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{m pre}=O(pN+u)\) and \(M_{m pre}=O(N+u)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct accounting under the stated sparse-scan model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind correctly distinguishes this statement from a generic definition, and the accounting follows from its assumptions. However, no solver-presolve source supports the bounded-scan and constant-size logging model as a meaningful presolve runtime bound.

children.title: Reoptimization State Invalidation
children.top_down_role: Loss of reusable solver state after model transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reoptimization State Invalidation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity test for cached solver artifacts after model changes or renewed presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a cached artifact \(z\) carry a dependency set \(D(z)\) of model rows, columns, bounds, coefficients, and reduction identifiers, together with their versions. After an edit set \(E\), the artifact remains reusable exactly when \(D(z)\cap E=
othing\) and every transformation on which its interpretation depends retains the same identifier and version. Otherwise \(z\) is invalidated and must be recomputed or transported through a certified update map. Typical artifacts include bases, factorizations, primal starts, dual multipliers, cuts, and propagation states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached reoptimization artifact is invalid when an edit intersects its dependencies or changes a transformation needed to interpret it.
assumptions_latex: Every cached artifact exposes complete dependency and version metadata.
\(E\) contains all model and transformation changes since caching.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(z\) is reusable if and only if \(D(z)\cap E=
othing\) and all dependent transformation versions agree.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dependency-based cache invalidation specialized to solver state

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the exact if-and-only-if reuse criterion depends on a complete semantic dependency model, not merely version metadata. No authoritative source establishes that model for bases, factorizations, starts, multipliers, cuts, and propagation state collectively.

children.title: Reduction Break-Even Regimes
children.top_down_role: Workload regimes where downstream savings do or do not offset reduction costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Break-Even Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost condition under which presolve investment decreases total expected solution time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{m pre}\) be presolve cost, \(C_{m post}\) postsolve and audit cost, \(T_0\) expected solution time without a proposed reduction set, and \(T_R\) expected solution time for the reduced instance. The reduction set is in a single-solve break-even regime precisely when \(C_{m pre}+T_R+C_{m post}<T_0\). For \(q\) compatible reoptimizations sharing the same valid reduced state, the regime becomes \(C_{m pre}+\sum_{i=1}^{q}(T_{R,i}+C_{{m post},i})<\sum_{i=1}^{q}T_{0,i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve breaks even when its setup and recovery costs are smaller than the downstream solution time it saves, across all valid reuse episodes.
assumptions_latex: All compared costs use the same computational environment and stopping criteria.
Shared reduced state remains valid across the counted reoptimizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accept the reduction investment when total reduced-work cost is strictly below total unreduced-work cost.
review_flags: empirical presolve and reoptimization cost source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the break-even leaf and the inequalities are direct cost comparisons, but no source supports their use as a presolve and reoptimization regime. The relationship between expected solve times and the displayed summed costs also requires sourced probabilistic or empirical semantics.

children.title: Node Relaxation Processing

children.title: LP Relaxation State

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(c,\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\ell\leq u\).
All integrality restrictions are omitted from the node relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusable mathematical and algorithmic state of a node's linear-programming relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node with local bounds \(\ell\leq x\leq u\), an LP relaxation state is a tuple \(S_{\rm LP}=(A,b,c,\ell,u,\mathcal B,x,\pi,r,\beta)\). The data \((A,b,c,\ell,u)\) specify the relaxation \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax\geq b,\ \ell\leq x\leq u\}\); \(\mathcal B\) is an optional basis or factorization, \(x\) and \(\pi\) are primal and dual iterates, \(r\) contains reduced costs or residuals, and \(\beta\) is a certified bound when the applicable termination or dual-feasibility conditions hold.

children.title: NLP Relaxation States

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node relaxation \(\min\{f(x):g(x)\leq 0,\ \ell\leq x\leq u\}\), an NLP relaxation state is \(S_{\rm NLP}=(f,g,\ell,u,x,\lambda,H,\rho,\beta)\). children.title: Conic Relaxation States

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*\). For the conic relaxation \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax-b\in K\}\), a conic relaxation state is \(S_K=(A,b,c,K,x,y,s,\rho,\beta)\), where \(s=Ax-b\in K\), \(y\in K^*\), \(\rho\) records primal, dual, and complementarity residuals, and \(\beta=b^\top y\) is a valid lower bound for minimization whenever \(A^\top y=c\).

children.title: Alternative Relaxation States

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Relaxation States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver state for relaxations other than direct NLP or conic formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node problem with feasible set \(F_v\) and objective \(f\), an alternative relaxation state is a tuple \(S_v=(\mathcal R_v,s_v,L_v)\), where \(\mathcal R_v\) is a relaxation mechanism such as a Lagrangian, decomposed, or extended formulation, \(s_v\) contains its current multipliers, generated objects, and solver status, and \(L_v\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) satisfies \(L_v\leq \inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)\) whenever the state is certified. The state is complete only if the asserted bound has a verifiable relaxation certificate; otherwise its bound status is incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alternative relaxation state stores a non-NLP, non-conic relaxation, its computational data, and any certified lower bound for the node problem.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\neq\varnothing\) unless infeasibility is itself certified.
The original problem is posed as minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certified state supplies a valid node lower bound \(L_v\leq\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)\).

children.title: Incomplete Relaxation State Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Node states where a complete relaxation solution is absent or deferred.

children.title: Pseudo-Solution States
children.top_down_role: Provisional node states used without a complete relaxation solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Solution States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational state produced before a node relaxation has been certified solved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node relaxation \(R_v\), a pseudo-solution state is a tuple \(P_v=(\hat x_v,\hat z_v,r_v,\sigma_v)\) returned by an incomplete relaxation procedure, where \(\hat x_v\) is a candidate point, \(\hat z_v=f(\hat x_v)\) when defined, \(r_v\) records primal, dual, and integrality residuals, and \(\sigma_v\) explicitly indicates that optimality is uncertified. Neither \(\hat z_v\) nor a solver estimate derived from it is a valid node bound unless an independent certificate establishes the required bound inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pseudo-solution is an incomplete relaxation iterate with residuals and uncertified status; its objective value cannot by itself justify pruning.
assumptions_latex: \(R_v\) is the relaxation associated with search node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state alone certifies neither relaxation optimality nor a valid pruning bound.
review_flags: needs authoritative source for pseudo-solution terminology
boundary between candidate iterate and certified state requires validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between an incomplete iterate and a certified pruning bound is plausible, but “pseudo-solution state” and its exact tuple are not standard enough to accept without an authoritative, specifically located source.

children.title: Unresolved Relaxation States
children.top_down_role: Node states awaiting completion, interpretation, or additional relaxation work.

knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved Relaxation States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incomplete node state with no certified terminal classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unresolved relaxation state at node \(v\) is a state \(U_v=(D_v,\sigma_v)\) for which the available data \(D_v\) establish none of the terminal predicates: certified infeasibility, certified unboundedness, or a certified optimum with value \(L_v\). A time limit, numerical failure, interrupted oracle, or missing dual certificate may produce such a state. Its search status must remain distinct from feasible, infeasible, optimal, and unbounded, even if it contains incumbent candidates or provisional objective estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unresolved state lacks a certificate of optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness and must remain explicitly distinct from every terminal solver status.
assumptions_latex: Node \(v\) has a well-defined relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No terminal relaxation classification follows from \(U_v\) alone.
review_flags: listed failure mechanisms require source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed nonterminal status is coherent, but the exact terminal-predicate taxonomy and listed failure mechanisms have no cited support.

children.title: Incomplete-State Search Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Limits on pruning, branching, heuristics, or bound use under incomplete relaxation information.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete-State Search Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe branch-and-bound actions when node-relaxation processing is incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization branch-and-bound with incumbent value \(U\). If node \(v\) has only an incomplete relaxation state, then bound pruning is valid only when that state includes a certificate of some \(L_v\) satisfying \(L_v\leq z_v^*\) and \(L_v\geq U\), where \(z_v^*\) is the node optimum. Infeasibility pruning likewise requires an infeasibility certificate. Without either certificate, the solver may continue processing, postpone, branch using rules independent of the uncertified bound, or conservatively retain the node, but it must not discard the node on the incomplete state alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incompletely solved node may be pruned only through an independently valid bound or infeasibility certificate; otherwise it must remain searchable.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uncertified relaxation information alone cannot justify pruning node \(v\).

children.title: Relaxation State-Reuse Calculus
children.top_down_role: Reuse of parent-node or previous-iteration relaxation information.

children.title: Simplex Basis Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of basis information across related node relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Basis Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of a parent LP basis after a local node-model change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a child LP obtained from a parent LP and a nonsingular parent basis matrix \(B\), map surviving basic rows and columns into the child model, augment or delete basis positions to obtain a square candidate basis \(B'\), and factorize \(B'\). Compute the associated basic primal and dual values. If the basis is dual feasible but primal infeasible, apply dual-simplex pivots; if primal feasible but dual infeasible, apply primal-simplex pivots; otherwise repair feasibility or refactorize. Stop at a certified optimum, infeasibility certificate, unboundedness certificate, or an explicit unresolved status, and return the final basis and solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map the parent basis into the child LP, repair it if necessary, and resume simplex iterations until a certified or explicitly unresolved outcome.
assumptions_latex: The child relaxation is linear.
The mapped candidate basis can be repaired or replaced if singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a child relaxation state together with its final reusable basis when available.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the basis-mapping, repair, pivot-selection, and terminal-status procedure is an implementation-sensitive algorithm with no cited source.

children.title: Non-Simplex Warm-Start Family
children.top_down_role: State reuse outside a simplex-basis regime.

children.title: Barrier Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of interior-point state across related relaxation solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization of a related primal-dual barrier solve from a prior interior state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a modified convex relaxation and a previous primal-dual interior-point state \((x,s,y)\), map the surviving variables and constraints into the new model, initialize new components, and choose corrections producing \(x'>0\) and \(s'>0\). Select \(\mu'>0\), form primal and dual residuals for the modified model, and apply damped primal-dual Newton steps that preserve strict positivity while reducing residuals and complementarity. Stop when the prescribed feasibility and complementarity tolerances hold, or return a numerical-failure or iteration-limit status; output the resulting primal-dual state for possible further reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer and interiorize the prior primal-dual point, then continue barrier iterations on the modified relaxation until tolerances or a failure limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: The modified relaxation admits the selected primal-dual barrier formulation.
Mapped variables and slacks can be initialized strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a barrier state for the modified relaxation and an explicit completion status.

notation.meaning: previous primal, slack, and dual state

review_flags: interiorization and mapping rules vary by solver

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Barrier warm starts are method-sensitive, and the asserted mapping, interiorization, barrier-parameter selection, and stopping procedure lacks an authoritative source.

children.title: Crossover Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of state supporting transition from interior solutions to basic solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Crossover Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of primal-dual information to initialize a basic solution recovery phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a related LP and a transferred primal-dual point \((x,y,s)\), first repair or project it to the new rows, columns, and bounds within chosen tolerances. Rank variables by proximity to bounds and reduced-cost information, select a linearly independent candidate basis, and compute its basic primal and dual values. Repair singularity or infeasibility by basis exchanges, then run simplex pivots until a certified basic optimum or an explicit failure status is obtained. Return the resulting basis and basic solution; no optimality claim is made unless simplex feasibility and reduced-cost conditions are certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a transferred primal-dual point to construct and repair a candidate basis, then finish with simplex and certify the resulting basic optimum.
assumptions_latex: The target relaxation is linear.
A crossover procedure has access to primal and dual estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful crossover returns a certified optimal basic solution and reusable basis.

notation.meaning: transferred primal, dual, and reduced-cost or slack information

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The candidate-basis ranking and repair steps describe one possible crossover strategy rather than a source-independent algorithm. A specific crossover reference and variant are required.

children.title: NLP Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of nonlinear solver state across related node problems.

knowledge_statements.title: NLP Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of primal-dual nonlinear-programming state between related node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a modified nonlinear relaxation, map the previous state \((x,\lambda,z,H)\) to surviving variables and constraints, initialize new components, project or restore \(x\) toward the new bounds and constraints, and regularize the Hessian approximation \(H\) if required. Resume the chosen local NLP method using the transferred multipliers \((\lambda,z)\). Stop when its prescribed stationarity, primal-feasibility, dual-feasibility, and complementarity tolerances hold, or return an explicit local-failure status. The output certifies at most the guarantees of the underlying NLP method and does not by itself establish global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map and repair the prior NLP primal-dual state, resume a local NLP solver, and retain only the guarantees certified by that solver.
assumptions_latex: Parent and child relaxations have an explicit variable-and-constraint correspondence.
The underlying NLP method accepts the transferred state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a locally certified or explicitly unresolved child NLP state, not automatically a global node bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transfer and repair operations, stopping conditions, and meaning of local certification vary across NLP methods. No source identifies the intended method or supports the stated algorithm.

children.title: Local Model-Change Reuse
children.top_down_role: Relaxation-state retention after local model changes.

children.title: Row Modification Reuse
children.top_down_role: Retention of relaxation state after constraint-row changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Row Modification Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State transfer after adding, deleting, or changing relaxation constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a solved relaxation state and a child model formed by row modifications, retain state components belonging to unchanged rows. For an added linear row, append its slack and dual component, initialize the slack from the transferred primal point, and extend a simplex basis with the slack column when nonsingular; for a deleted row, remove its dual and repair any affected basis position. Recompute primal and dual residuals under every changed row, invalidate certificates depending on removed or altered rows, and resume the relaxation solver until it returns a new certificate or explicit unresolved status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserve unchanged row data, initialize or delete affected components, invalidate stale certificates, and reoptimize the modified relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The parent and child models identify corresponding unchanged rows.
All changed rows are explicitly supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only certificates recomputed or validated for the modified row system may be reported.
review_flags: needs source for row-state update rules
details depend on relaxation solver representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record blends generic relaxation-state reuse with simplex-specific slack and basis updates. The exact row-update algorithm and its applicability require a specifically located source.

children.title: Column Modification Reuse
children.top_down_role: Retention of relaxation state after variable-column changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Modification Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State transfer after adding, deleting, or changing relaxation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a solved relaxation state and a child model formed by column modifications, retain components corresponding to unchanged columns. Initialize each added variable at a permitted value, create its bound and reduced-cost data, and price it against the transferred dual vector; before deleting a variable, remove or pivot out any associated basic position and delete its primal and dual-bound components. Recompute residuals and reduced costs for every changed column, invalidate any certificate using obsolete column data, and resume the relaxation solver until a new certificate or an explicit unresolved status is obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserve unchanged column data, initialize additions, safely remove deletions, reprice changed columns, and reoptimize before asserting a certificate.
assumptions_latex: The parent and child models identify corresponding unchanged columns.
Added variables have specified domains and objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned state is valid only after residuals and certificates are checked against the modified columns.

notation.meaning: transferred constraint-dual vector used for pricing
