children.title: Bound Modification Reuse
children.top_down_role: Retention of relaxation state after local or global bound changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Modification Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State transfer after tightening or relaxing variable bounds at a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a parent relaxation state and child bounds \(l'\leq x\leq u'\), retain the parent state for unchanged variables and replace its bound data by \((l',u')\). If the transferred point violates a new bound, move it to the bound or let the selected reoptimization method restore feasibility; update bound slacks, active-set labels, and bound multipliers accordingly. Recompute feasibility and dual residuals, invalidate the parent optimality certificate unless it satisfies the child conditions, and reoptimize until a child certificate or explicit unresolved status is returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update bound data and affected state components, restore feasibility, and reoptimize because the parent certificate need not remain valid.
assumptions_latex: The child bounds satisfy \(l'_i\leq u'_i\) for every variable \(i\).
Variables retain their parent-to-child correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only a certificate validated under \(l'\leq x\leq u'\) is valid for the child node.
review_flags: state updates differ across simplex, barrier, and NLP solvers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record combines simplex, active-set, barrier, and NLP-style state components into one algorithm. Solver-specific conditions and update rules need authoritative sourcing or explicit delimitation.

children.title: Search-Stage Processing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Differences in effort, available information, and persistence between root and later nodes.

children.title: Root Processing Regime
children.top_down_role: High-investment processing before extensive tree search.

children.title: Root Relaxation Processing
children.top_down_role: High-investment solution of the initial node relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Root Relaxation Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified construction and strengthening of the initial search relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization MIP with feasible set \(F\), form a root relaxation with feasible region \(R_0\supseteq F\) and solve it to obtain a certified lower bound \(L_0\). At each permitted root round, generate inequalities valid for every point of \(F\), add selected inequalities to obtain \(R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\), and reoptimize or explicitly mark the state unresolved. Optionally pass relaxation solutions to primal heuristics, accepting only solutions verified feasible for \(F\). Stop by the configured round, progress, or resource rule; return the strengthened model, certified bound, incumbent if any, and reusable solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve and iteratively strengthen the root relaxation with valid cuts, verify heuristic incumbents, and retain the certified bound and reusable state.
assumptions_latex: The problem is posed as minimization.
Every added inequality is valid for the original feasible set \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For certified rounds, \(L_0\leq L_1\leq\cdots\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: root relaxation after strengthening round k
certified lower bound from round k

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

review_flags: cut-round and heuristic details require solver-mechanism source

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited branch-and-bound sections do not clearly support the full cut-round, heuristic, persistence, and stopping algorithm. Moreover, nested strengthened regions alone do not make arbitrary certified lower bounds monotone; the conclusion needs exact relaxation optima or an explicit monotone bound-update rule.

children.title: Root Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Root-level effort devoted to improving the relaxation or domain.

assumptions_latex: The root relaxation feasible region is a polyhedron \(P_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The integer-feasible set \(X\) satisfies \(X\subseteq P_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned relaxation \(P_r\) satisfies \(X\subseteq P_r\subseteq P_0\).
review_flags: solver-specific cut acceptance and stopping rules intentionally abstracted
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite root-cut strengthening for a minimization MIP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(P_0\) and \(X\), initialize \(r=0\). At round \(r\), solve or reoptimize the relaxation over \(P_r\), generate finitely many inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) valid for every \(x\in X\), and retain an accepted subset \(I_r\). Set \(P_{r+1}=P_r\cap\bigcap_{i\in I_r}\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\}\). Stop when \(I_r=\varnothing\), a prescribed round or resource limit is reached, or another root-processing termination test holds; output the last relaxation. Every update preserves \(X\subseteq P_{r+1}\subseteq P_r\), so the root lower bound for minimization cannot decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the root relaxation, add accepted valid inequalities, and stop by convergence or resource limits; the resulting relaxation contains all integer-feasible solutions and is no weaker.
knowledge_statements.title: Root Strengthening

children.title: Root-State Persistence
children.top_down_role: Retention of root-derived information for later tree processing.

assumptions_latex: A branch-and-bound search begins from a completed root-processing state \(S_0\).
Every persisted object records a validity domain covering each node where it is reused.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every node \(v\), each inherited object in \(S_v\) is valid on the node region \(P_v\).

notation.meaning: processing state available at node v

review_flags: source support is indirect and does not specify root-state persistence semantics
REQUEST_SOURCES: authoritative solver reference for persistence and validity domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving reuse of root artifacts during descendant processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_0\) contain root-derived global bounds, globally valid constraints, incumbent information, and reusable relaxation data. For a node \(v\) with region \(P_v\), construct \(S_v\) by inheriting only objects whose recorded validity domains include \(P_v\), then adjoining node-local objects separately. An inherited inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) may constrain the node relaxation only if it is valid for every integer-feasible \(x\in P_v\); an inherited bound may prune \(v\) only under the same objective convention and certified validity scope. Thus persistence may change computational state but must not exclude a feasible integer solution belonging to \(P_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root information may be reused at descendants only within its recorded validity domain; local artifacts remain distinguished so persistence cannot remove feasible integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-State Persistence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity-scoped persistence property is plausible, but no citation supports the asserted lifecycle, inheritance, and pruning semantics.

children.title: Local Node Processing
children.top_down_role: Processing under inherited and node-local restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization MIP with incumbent value \(U\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
Node \(v\) inherits a relaxation region \(P_v\) and valid global information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node is pruned only by certified infeasibility, bound dominance \(L_v\ge U\), or completion by an integral feasible solution.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at node v

review_flags: processing order and optional solver operations intentionally abstracted
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic local processing step in minimization branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), intersect inherited restrictions with the branching restrictions defining \(P_v\), apply validity-preserving propagation or local strengthening, and solve the resulting relaxation. If it is infeasible, prune \(v\). Otherwise obtain a valid lower bound \(L_v\). Prune when \(L_v\ge U\). If the relaxation solution is integer-feasible, update \(U\) when its objective is smaller and close \(v\). Otherwise optionally invoke separation, pricing, or primal heuristics, repeating relaxation solution after accepted changes. If no closing test holds, select a valid search disjunction, create children whose integer-feasible regions cover that of \(v\), and output those children with their inherited state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process a node under inherited and local restrictions, prune it by infeasibility or bound, accept integral solutions, or branch into children covering its remaining feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Node Processing

children.title: Deferred Node-Processing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Deferral caused by limits, incomplete pricing, or unresolved relaxation work.

children.title: Delayed Node Processing
children.top_down_role: Node work postponed before full relaxation processing begins.

assumptions_latex: Node \(v\) is open and has not yet begun its designated relaxation-processing phase.
Its inherited state remains recoverable while it waits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Delay changes the processing time of \(v\), not its feasible region or logical status.

notation.meaning: search time at which v becomes eligible

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distinguishes pre-processing deferral from interruption after processing begins
REQUEST_SOURCES: solver terminology for delayed-node lifecycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deferral before the designated local processing phase starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node \(v\) is delayed until search time \(\tau_v\) when it remains an open node but is excluded from processing selections at every time \(t<\tau_v\), unless an earlier explicit release event occurs. Its branching restrictions, inherited validity-scoped state, and parent relation are retained. Delay alone neither declares \(v\) infeasible nor supplies an objective bound sufficient for pruning. At release, \(v\) reenters the eligible open-node set and begins local node processing from its retained state, subject to any globally valid information accumulated while it waited.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delayed node remains open but temporarily ineligible before local processing starts; its state is retained, and delay alone neither prunes nor modifies its feasible region.
knowledge_statements.title: Delayed Node Processing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally coherent and distinguishes pre-processing delay from suspension, but its precise node-lifecycle semantics have no cited support.

children.title: Suspended Node Processing
children.top_down_role: Partially completed node work retained for possible resumption.

assumptions_latex: Processing of node \(v\) has begun but has not produced a terminal node decision.
A resumable checkpoint \(C_v\) can be stored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Suspension preserves an unfinished node together with sufficient state for a validity-preserving continuation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distinguishes interruption of active processing from delay before processing
REQUEST_SOURCES: authoritative checkpoint and suspension semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interruption after node processing has started but before closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Processing of \(v\) is suspended when execution stops after at least one local processing operation but before pruning, completion, or branching closes the node, and a checkpoint \(C_v\) is recorded. The checkpoint identifies the node restrictions, accepted validity-scoped bounds and constraints, incumbent-dependent tests already performed, and the relaxation status needed to continue or safely recompute. While suspended, \(v\) is open but not selectable for ordinary processing. Resumption restores \(C_v\), incorporates subsequently obtained globally valid information, invalidates stale incumbent-dependent conclusions when necessary, and continues without treating incomplete computations as certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A suspended node is an interrupted, unfinished node with a checkpoint; resumption restores or safely recomputes state and never treats incomplete work as a certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Suspended Node Processing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed suspension and checkpoint semantics are plausible but include implementation-specific state, invalidation, and resumption requirements without authoritative support.

children.title: Node Resumption Eligibility
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing return to deferred or incomplete node work.

assumptions_latex: Node \(v\) is delayed or suspended and remains logically open.
The current global state is \(G_t\) at search time \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Node \(v\) may resume exactly when \(E(v,G_t)=1\); terminal tests are applied before further relaxation work.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: eligibility is modeled as an explicit scheduler predicate plus mandatory validity checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract eligibility predicate for delayed or suspended nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E(v,G_t)=1\) precisely when \(v\) is open, its release condition is satisfied, required inherited or checkpoint state is available or safely reconstructible, and the scheduler admits \(v\) under current resource and priority rules. Before executing resumed relaxation work, incorporate globally valid updates from \(G_t\) and test whether they certify infeasibility or a node bound at least the incumbent value. Such a certificate closes \(v\) instead of resuming it. Otherwise, a delayed node starts local processing and a suspended node continues from a validated checkpoint or a reconstructed equivalent state. If any required state cannot be validated or reconstructed, \(E(v,G_t)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deferred node resumes only after release, state validation, and scheduler admission; new global information is first used to close it when already infeasible or dominated.
knowledge_statements.title: Node Resumption Eligibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scheduler predicate is a reasonable abstraction, but the claimed exact eligibility and mandatory resumption protocol are unsupported by a cited solver or algorithmic reference.

children.title: Node-Processing Coordination
children.top_down_role: Interfaces among inference, relaxations, separation, pricing, branching, and primal search.

children.title: Propagation–Relaxation Coordination
children.top_down_role: Exchange of local bounds, infeasibility information, and relaxation state.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation is \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\).
Every propagation rule and relaxation-derived inference used is validity preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns infeasibility or bounds \([\ell',u']\subseteq[\ell,u]\) containing every feasible point of \(P\).

notation.meaning: current lower and upper variable bounds
updated lower and upper variable bounds

review_flags: source support is indirect for the coordination loop
REQUEST_SOURCES: propagation and LP-relaxation coordination reference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point exchange between valid bound propagation and relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((\ell',u')=(\ell,u)\). Apply valid propagation rules to \(Ax\le b\) and the current bounds. If a contradiction is certified, return infeasible. Otherwise solve or reoptimize the relaxation with the tightened bounds. Convert only certified relaxation information, such as valid reduced-cost implications under a stated incumbent cutoff, into additional bound changes or infeasibility conclusions. Repeat whenever either phase changes a bound relevant to the other. Stop when neither phase yields an accepted change or a prescribed resource limit is reached. Return infeasible only with a valid certificate; otherwise return \((\ell',u')\), which must contain every feasible point of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate valid propagation and relaxation solution, exchanging certified bounds or infeasibility information until no accepted change remains or a resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation–Relaxation Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity-preserving coordination loop is mathematically plausible, but the reduced-cost implications, fixed-point exchange, and certificate handling require an authoritative propagation–relaxation source.

children.title: Cut-Generation Integration Interface
children.top_down_role: Node-level interfaces to externally owned cut-generation mechanisms.

children.title: Separation Entry Points
children.top_down_role: Node-processing hooks for invoking externally owned cut generation.

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation region is \(P\) and its solution is \(\bar x\in P\).
The target integer-feasible set is \(X\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted separator output is valid for \(X\) and violated by \(\bar x\) beyond the prescribed tolerance.
review_flags: callback timing and separator scheduling are solver-specific
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invocation contract for separating a fractional relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a relaxation solution \(\bar x\) is available and before a decision that requires the relaxation to be final, a separation entry point supplies \(\bar x\), the node restrictions, and the validity scope to one or more separation routines. A routine may return inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) only with a declared scope for which they are valid for every relevant \(x\in X\). An inequality is eligible for immediate integration when \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b_i+\varepsilon_i\), where \(\varepsilon_i\ge0\) is its acceptance tolerance. Accepted cuts modify \(P\), invalidate the current relaxation solution, and require reoptimization before bound-based conclusions use the strengthened relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a separation entry point, routines inspect a relaxation solution and return scoped valid inequalities; violated accepted cuts trigger relaxation reoptimization before bound decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Entry Points

children.title: Cut-Pool Entry Points
children.top_down_role: Node-processing hooks for retrieving, filtering, or returning pooled cuts.

assumptions_latex: A cut pool contains inequalities with recorded validity scopes and activity metadata.
The current node has region \(P_v\) and relaxation solution \(\bar x_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A retrieved cut may enter node \(v\)'s relaxation only if its validity scope covers \(P_v\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pool retrieval requires explicit validity filtering before numerical selection
REQUEST_SOURCES: authoritative cut-pool lifecycle and entry-point reference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-filtered retrieval and insertion of previously generated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a cut-pool entry point, form the eligible set \(\mathcal C_v=\{c\in\mathcal C:\operatorname{scope}(c)\text{ covers }P_v\}\). Evaluate eligible cuts at \(\bar x_v\), then select a finite subset using declared numerical tests such as violation, efficacy, conditioning, duplication, and resource limits. Add only selected members of \(\mathcal C_v\) to the current relaxation. Cuts generated with merely local validity remain unavailable outside their recorded subtree or region. If at least one cut is added, mark \(\bar x_v\) and relaxation-dependent certificates stale and reoptimize before using a new node bound. Pool aging or deletion may remove stored cuts but cannot remove their logical validity from cuts already required by an active relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut-pool entry point filters stored cuts by validity scope and numerical acceptance, inserts a finite subset, and forces reoptimization when the active relaxation changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Entry Points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Validity filtering is necessary, but the detailed selection, staleness, aging, deletion, and active-relaxation lifecycle claims have no cited support.

children.title: Cut Integration Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ownership boundaries between node processing, separation, and relaxation modification.

assumptions_latex: Each candidate inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) has a certified validity scope.
The active node relaxation has feasible region \(P_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integration is admissible only when validity, numerical acceptance, and lifecycle requirements all hold.

notation.meaning: candidate cut coefficients and right-hand side

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical and numerical boundary for adding a cut to an active relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A candidate cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) with validity domain \(D\) may be integrated at node \(v\) only if every integer-feasible point in \(P_v\) lies in \(D\) or otherwise satisfies the inequality, its coefficients pass the solver's finite-arithmetic acceptance tests, and its insertion respects declared local or global scope. A globally valid cut may be shared across nodes; a locally valid cut may be used only where its validity domain applies. Once integrated, the cut becomes part of the active relaxation until explicitly removed by a relaxation-management operation, and any solution or bound depending on the previous relaxation must be recomputed or independently revalidated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut crosses the integration boundary only with certified scope, acceptable numerics, and correct lifecycle handling; changing the relaxation invalidates dependent solutions and bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Integration Boundaries

children.title: Dynamic-Column Integration Interface
children.top_down_role: Node-level interfaces to dynamically generated variables.

children.title: Pricing Entry Points
children.top_down_role: Node-processing hooks for invoking dynamic variable generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Entry Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced-cost pricing for a standard-form linear minimization master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the restricted master over columns in \(J_R\) and obtain an optimal primal solution and dual vector \(\pi\). At the pricing entry point, evaluate reduced costs \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\) for admissible omitted columns \(j\in J\setminus J_R\). If exact pricing certifies \(\bar c_j\ge 0\) for every \(j\in J\setminus J_R\), then \(\pi\) is feasible for the dual of the full master and the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master. Otherwise, add one or more admissible columns satisfying \(\bar c_j<0\) and reoptimize. A practical threshold \(\bar c_j< -\varepsilon\), with \(\varepsilon>0\), may govern insertion, but failure to find such a column is not an exact optimality certificate unless pricing supplies a valid nonnegative lower bound for every omitted reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the restricted master, price all admissible omitted columns under its dual solution, add negative-reduced-cost columns, and declare full-master optimality only when exact pricing certifies that every omitted reduced cost is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: The full master is \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda_j\ge0\text{ for every }j\in J\}\).
The restricted set satisfies \(J_R\subseteq J\), and the restricted master is feasible and has an optimal primal-dual solution.
Pricing is exact or returns a valid lower bound on \(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\) over every omitted column \(j\in J\setminus J_R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in J\setminus J_R\), the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full linear master.

children.title: Column-Pool Entry Points
children.top_down_role: Node-processing hooks for retrieving, filtering, or returning pooled columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Pool Entry Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost screening of previously generated columns for a standard-form linear minimization master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a column-pool entry point, retain only objects \(j\in\mathcal J\) that are admissible columns for the current master and are not already represented in \(J_R\). For each retained column, compute \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\) using the current dual vector \(\pi\). Select a finite subset satisfying the insertion tolerance and declared duplication, compatibility, and resource tests, and add it to \(J_R\). After any insertion, reoptimize the restricted master or independently revalidate its previous primal solution, dual vector, and reduced costs before using them for subsequent conclusions. Failure to find an improving pooled column does not certify full-master optimality unless \(\mathcal J\) contains every admissible omitted column or a separate exact pricing oracle certifies nonnegative reduced cost for every omitted column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter the column pool for admissible omitted columns, screen them using current reduced costs, insert an accepted finite subset, and then reoptimize or revalidate the restricted master; an unproductive pool search alone does not certify full-master optimality.
assumptions_latex: The full master is \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda_j\ge0\text{ for every }j\in J\}\), with current restricted column set \(J_R\subseteq J\).
The pool \(\mathcal J\) stores candidate columns together with their vectors \(a_j\), costs \(c_j\), and admissibility metadata.
The current restricted master has been solved and has dual vector \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only admissible omitted columns may enter \(J_R\), and after an insertion the previous master solution, dual vector, and reduced costs must be recomputed or independently revalidated.

children.title: Column Integration Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ownership boundaries between node processing, pricing, and relaxation modification.

assumptions_latex: \(P_N\) is solved to optimality as a restricted linear master relaxation for a minimization problem at node \(N\).

The corresponding full master is a valid relaxation of the mixed-integer node problem and admits every column in the original column domain that satisfies the branching restrictions inherited by \(N\).
Reduced costs are computed from a dual-optimal solution of \(P_N\), and the pricing oracle searches the complete admissible omitted-column domain exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted-master value is not by itself a certified lower bound for the mixed-integer node problem. If exact pricing establishes \(\bar c_j\ge 0\) for every admissible omitted column \(j\), then the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master relaxation and its value is a valid node lower bound.

notation.meaning: Restricted linear master relaxation at the node
Reduced cost of an admissible omitted column

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundaries for column admission and exact lower-bound certification in linear branch-and-price.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N\), an admitted column must belong to the original column domain and satisfy every branching restriction inherited by \(N\). After insertion, the restricted master \(P_N\) is reoptimized. For a minimization problem, its value alone is not a certified lower bound for the full mixed-integer node problem. If reduced costs are computed from a dual-optimal solution of \(P_N\) and exact pricing over the complete admissible omitted-column domain establishes \(\bar c_j\ge 0\) for every omitted column \(j\), then the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master relaxation. Because that full master is assumed to be a valid node relaxation, its optimal value is then a certified node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admitted columns must satisfy the original column domain and inherited branching restrictions. In linear branch-and-price, a restricted-master value becomes a certified node lower bound only after exact pricing over all admissible omitted columns finds no negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Column Integration Boundaries

children.title: Search-Decision Integration Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces to externally owned search-decision mechanisms.

children.title: Branching Entry Points
children.top_down_role: Node-processing hooks supplying state to branch-candidate selection.

assumptions_latex: The current node relaxation has a solution \(x^N\) that violates integrality.
The chosen child disjunction is valid for every integer-feasible point remaining at node \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated children cover all integer-feasible descendants of \(N\), so replacing \(N\) by those children preserves completeness of the search.

notation.meaning: Current node and its relaxation solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard variable-branching entry after a fractional node-relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a solved node \(N\) with fractional relaxation solution \(x^N\), select an integer-constrained component \(k\) with \(x_k^N\notin\mathbb Z\). Create children \(N^-\) and \(N^+\) by appending, respectively, \(x_k\le\lfloor x_k^N\rfloor\) and \(x_k\ge\lceil x_k^N\rceil\). More generally, any finite valid disjunction may be used if its terms cover every integer-feasible descendant of \(N\). Initialize each child with the inherited domain, local constraints, and valid local solver state, then return the children to the open-node store.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fractional relaxation point, branching creates children from a valid disjunction that covers every remaining integer-feasible descendant.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Entry Points

children.title: Node-Selection Entry Points
children.top_down_role: Node-processing hooks supplying status or priority information to tree scheduling.

assumptions_latex: The open-node set \(\mathcal O\) is finite and contains all created, unfathomed nodes.
Each open node has a deterministic priority key \(\pi(N)\), including any tie-breaking data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected node is an unfathomed member of \(\mathcal O\) minimizing the declared priority key; returning no node is valid exactly when \(\mathcal O=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract entry contract encompassing best-bound, depth-first, and hybrid node selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an open-node set \(\mathcal O\). Whenever search requests another node, discard entries already marked fathomed, compute or update the declared priority key \(\pi(N)\) for each remaining \(N\in\mathcal O\), and choose \(N^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{N\in\mathcal O}\pi(N)\), using the declared deterministic tie-breaker. Remove \(N^*\) from \(\mathcal O\), activate its inherited bounds and local constraints, and pass it to node processing. If \(\mathcal O=\varnothing\), return the empty-search signal rather than a node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node selection chooses an unfathomed open node according to an explicit priority and tie-break rule, or reports that no open node remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Selection Entry Points

children.title: Search-Decision Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of processed-node information to externally owned search decisions.

assumptions_latex: All node-processing updates are complete before the handoff is committed.
The handed-off state identifies a single search node \(N\) and a single incumbent version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A search decision made from the committed state is consistent with the node conclusion, incumbent, bounds, and generated children represented by that same state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for transferring completed node results to global search control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A valid search-decision handoff commits one state tuple \(S_N=(N,s_N,L_N,U,\mathcal C_N)\), where \(s_N\) is the final node status, \(L_N\) is any certified node bound, \(U\) is the incumbent value or \(+\infty\), and \(\mathcal C_N\) is the set of created children. The tuple is admissible only after all bound, incumbent, pruning, and child-creation updates for \(N\) have completed. Global search must base node insertion, deletion, and selection on this committed tuple, not on a mixture of earlier state versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node processing hands global search one consistent snapshot containing the final node status, certified bound, incumbent version, and created children.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Decision Handoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The consistency condition matches the leaf concept, but the cited general branch-and-bound section does not inspectably support the specific committed tuple, atomic-update requirement, or prohibition on mixed state versions. A source addressing solver search-state handoff or callback/interface consistency is required.

children.title: Primal-Heuristic Entry Points
children.top_down_role: Node states at which feasible-solution search consumes solver information.

assumptions_latex: A node \(N\) has a current domain and locally valid solver state.
A heuristic returns only points that can be checked against the original mixed-integer constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted heuristic point is a certified feasible incumbent candidate; failure to find a point changes neither node feasibility nor the validity of node bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-solution searches invoked at defined node-processing states.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a declared entry state, such as node creation, completion of propagation, availability of a relaxation solution, or discovery of a new incumbent, invoke a primal heuristic using only solver information valid for node \(N\). If it returns \(\hat x\), independently verify all original constraints, integrality requirements, and objective value \(f(\hat x)\). For minimization, accept \(\hat x\) and set \(U\leftarrow f(\hat x)\) only when it is feasible and \(f(\hat x)<U\). A null or rejected return has no implication for node feasibility or pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal heuristics may consume valid node information at declared states, but only independently verified feasible improvements may update the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Heuristic Entry Points

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Node-Processing Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Operational conclusion families produced by local processing.

children.title: Subtree Exclusion Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Local conclusions excluding a node or subtree.

children.title: Node Infeasibility Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Local relaxation outcomes excluding a node through infeasibility.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation feasible set \(R_N\) contains every mixed-integer feasible point satisfying the node restrictions.
Relaxation infeasibility is established exactly or by a valid infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_N=\varnothing\) implies \(F_N=\varnothing\); hence node \(N\) and every descendant inheriting its restrictions may be fathomed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fathoming certificate obtained from infeasibility of a valid node relaxation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) be the original mixed-integer feasible set restricted by the decisions defining node \(N\), and let \(R_N\) be a valid relaxation with \(F_N\subseteq R_N\). If the relaxation solver returns a valid certificate that \(R_N=\varnothing\), then necessarily \(F_N=\varnothing\). Because every descendant \(D\) adds restrictions and therefore satisfies \(F_D\subseteq F_N\), the certificate permits fathoming \(N\) without branching and excludes every descendant of \(N\) from further search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified infeasibility of a relaxation containing the node's integer-feasible set proves the node and all its descendants infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Node Infeasibility Conclusions

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

children.title: Bound-Cutoff Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Local bound outcomes excluding a node relative to the incumbent cutoff.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with incumbent value \(U\).
\(L_N\) is a certified lower bound on every feasible objective value in the subtree rooted at \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_N\ge U\), or \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon\) under absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), no descendant can improve the incumbent beyond the chosen tolerance.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound for the node subtree

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-based fathoming for a minimization branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, suppose \(L_N\) satisfies \(f(x)\ge L_N\) for every feasible point \(x\) in the subtree rooted at node \(N\), and suppose the incumbent has value \(U\). If \(L_N\ge U\), then no point in that subtree can strictly improve the incumbent, so \(N\) may be fathomed. With declared absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the analogous cutoff test is \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon\); this certifies only the corresponding tolerance-based conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization node is cut off when its certified lower bound cannot improve the incumbent, subject to the declared optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Cutoff Conclusions

children.title: Subtree Exclusion Scope
children.top_down_role: Extent to which local exclusion evidence applies to descendants.

assumptions_latex: A fathoming certificate is valid under the restrictions defining node \(N\).
Every descendant \(D\) inherits those restrictions and may add further restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate excludes the entire subtree rooted at \(N\), but it does not exclude siblings or other nodes whose feasible sets are not contained in \(F_N\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical reach of certificates established under node-local restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) denote the feasible set under the restrictions defining node \(N\). Every descendant \(D\) inherits these restrictions, so \(F_D\subseteq F_N\). Consequently, a certificate proving \(F_N=\varnothing\), or proving that no point of \(F_N\) can improve the incumbent, applies to \(N\) and every descendant \(D\). It does not generally apply to a node \(M\) outside this subtree unless a separate containment \(F_M\subseteq F_N\) or an independently valid global certificate has been established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-local exclusion certificate covers that node and descendants inheriting its restrictions, but not unrelated nodes unless a separate containment argument applies.
knowledge_statements.title: Subtree Exclusion Scope

children.title: Integer-Feasible Relaxation Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Node conclusions associated with feasible integral relaxation points.

assumptions_latex: The problem at node \(N\) is a minimization problem with mixed-integer feasible set \(F_N\).
The relaxation feasible set \(R_N\) satisfies \(F_N\subseteq R_N\).
The point \(x^N\in R_N\) is a globally optimal relaxation solution and also satisfies \(x^N\in F_N\).
The current incumbent value is \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \(x^N\) is globally optimal over \(F_N\). If \(f(x^N)<U\), it may replace the incumbent, and node \(N\) may be fathomed without branching.

notation.meaning: Mixed-integer feasible set at the node
Relaxation feasible set at the node
Globally optimal relaxation solution that is mixed-integer feasible

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality and fathoming conclusion for a globally solved node relaxation whose optimizer is feasible for the mixed-integer node problem.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) be the mixed-integer feasible set at node \(N\), and let \(R_N\) be a relaxation satisfying \(F_N\subseteq R_N\). If \(x^N\) is a globally optimal solution of \(\min\{f(x):x\in R_N\}\) and \(x^N\in F_N\), then \(f(x^N)=\min\{f(x):x\in F_N\}\). If \(f(x^N)<U\), the incumbent may be updated to \(x^N\). In all cases, node \(N\) may be fathomed without branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally optimal relaxation solution that is feasible for the mixed-integer node problem is node-optimal, may improve the incumbent, and permits fathoming without branching.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Feasible Relaxation Conclusions

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

children.title: Indeterminate Relaxation Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Relaxation outcomes requiring additional interpretation before search action.

children.title: Unbounded Relaxation Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Node outcomes indicating an unbounded relaxation direction.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation of a minimization problem is valid and has value \(-\infty\).
No independently verified mixed-integer feasible recession construction has yet been supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation unboundedness alone neither proves that the mixed-integer node problem is unbounded nor justifies fathoming the node.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of inference from an unbounded continuous node relaxation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the valid node relaxation satisfies \(\inf_{x\in R_N}f(x)=-\infty\), then it supplies no finite node lower bound. This fact alone does not imply \(\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)=-\infty\), because the unbounded relaxation sequence may contain no mixed-integer feasible sequence. Declaring the node problem unbounded requires an independent certificate, for example a point \(\bar x\in F_N\) and a direction \(d\) preserving feasibility and integrality along an unbounded sequence while driving the objective to \(-\infty\). Without such a certificate, pruning is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded continuous relaxation gives no finite bound but does not by itself prove that the mixed-integer node problem is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Relaxation Conclusions

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

children.title: Ambiguous Relaxation Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Node outcomes lacking a reliable status interpretation.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation solver reports a nondefinitive status caused by limits, numerical uncertainty, or unresolved feasibility.
No independent valid bound, infeasibility certificate, or feasible integral point resolves the node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported status supports no mathematical conclusion of node infeasibility, optimality, or cutoff and therefore cannot alone justify fathoming.

notation.meaning: Certified node lower bound, when available

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconclusive solver statuses and their prohibited search inferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A status \(s_N\) such as iteration limit, time limit, numerical failure, interrupted solve, or unresolved infeasible-or-unbounded does not constitute a certificate of relaxation optimality or infeasibility. Unless separate verified information supplies a valid lower bound \(L_N\), an infeasibility certificate, or a feasible integral point, the status permits no conclusion that node \(N\) is infeasible, cutoff, or solved. In particular, an ambiguous status must not be silently mapped to infeasible or unbounded, and it cannot alone authorize subtree exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical or limit-induced ambiguous relaxation status proves neither infeasibility nor optimality and cannot by itself authorize pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Relaxation Conclusions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed failure boundary is plausible, but the citation is an indirect general branch-and-bound section and does not inspectably establish the semantics of iteration limits, numerical failure, interruption, or an infeasible-or-unbounded status. A solver-status or numerical-optimization source is needed before accepting the full list and its exact implications.

children.title: Search-Action Deferral
children.top_down_role: Delayed pruning or branching while relaxation status remains unresolved.

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation result is insufficient for a certified branch, cutoff, infeasibility, or unboundedness conclusion.
The node state can be preserved or reconstructed without losing inherited restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deferral preserves search correctness provided \(N\) remains unresolved and is eventually reconsidered or explicitly covered by a later valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct treatment of nodes whose relaxation outcome does not support a certified search action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When node \(N\) has no certified conclusion supporting fathoming or branching, preserve its state \(S_N\), mark it unresolved, and return it to an open or suspended store \(\mathcal O\). A subsequent attempt may change tolerances, algorithms, resources, or relaxation formulation, but must retain all inherited node restrictions and distinguish newly certified information from heuristic estimates. Deferral is correct only if \(N\) is not treated as excluded and termination is not declared while \(N\) remains unresolved, unless a later valid global certificate covers its feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inconclusive node may be deferred with preserved state, but it remains unresolved and cannot be omitted from correctness or termination accounting.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Action Deferral

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deferral principle is coherent and matches the leaf, but the cited general branch-and-bound section does not inspectably support the prescribed suspended-store protocol, reconstruction requirement, or termination accounting for unresolved nodes. A source explicitly addressing incomplete node solves or search deferral is required.

children.top_down_role: Mechanisms for constructing, importing, repairing, improving, retaining, and scheduling feasible solutions.

children.title: Candidate Construction-Repair Family
children.top_down_role: Primal methods that assemble candidates or restore feasibility.

children.title: Fractional-Lock Construction Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction guided by fractional values and constraint locks.

children.title: Value-Rounding Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction driven by fractional relaxation values.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation point satisfies \(\bar x\in P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\).
The integer index set is \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with integral bounds on variables in \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\hat x\) is integral on \(I\), but feasibility requires separate checking or repair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise value rounding for constructing an integral candidate from a relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\bar x\in P\), define \(\hat x_j=\bar x_j\) for \(j\notin I\). For each \(j\in I\), choose \(\hat x_j\in\mathbb Z\cap[\ell_j,u_j]\), commonly by \(\hat x_j\in\{\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor,\lceil\bar x_j\rceil\}\), minimizing a prescribed score such as \(|\hat x_j-\bar x_j|\) or an objective-weighted displacement. Ties are resolved deterministically. After all integer coordinates are assigned, return \(\hat x\) as a candidate; integrality is guaranteed on \(I\), whereas \(A\hat x\le b\) is not guaranteed and must be tested before acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round each integer variable near its relaxation value using a chosen score. The result is integral but may violate constraints and therefore needs feasibility checking or repair.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Rounding Heuristics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the Value-Rounding Heuristics leaf, and the statement clearly distinguishes integrality from feasibility. However, no citation supports the particular scoring, tie-breaking, and candidate-construction procedure, so the record requires a direct heuristic source.

children.title: Lock-Based Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction guided by constraint-lock exposure.

assumptions_latex: The linear constraints are \(Ax\le b\), and \(I\) indexes bounded integer variables.
A current partial assignment and relaxation point \(\bar x\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns an integral candidate whose rounding directions are selected to limit adverse constraint movement.

notation.meaning: number of constraints made harder by rounding variable j downward or upward

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rounding directions selected from up-lock and down-lock counts in a linear MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each unfixed \(j\in I\), compute the down-lock count \(L_j^-\) and up-lock count \(L_j^+\), where a lock counts a row whose activity can move toward violation when \(x_j\) is respectively decreased or increased. Select an unfixed variable by a prescribed priority rule. If \(L_j^-<L_j^+\), set \(x_j=\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor\); if \(L_j^+<L_j^-\), set \(x_j=\lceil\bar x_j\rceil\); resolve equality using displacement or objective score. Propagate bounds, repeat until all variables in \(I\) are fixed, and accept only if every constraint is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count constraints endangered by rounding each variable up or down, prefer the direction with fewer locks, propagate bounds, and retain the completed assignment only if feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Lock-Based Heuristics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and lock-based rounding content match the terminal container. The definitions of up-lock and down-lock direction, the selection rule, propagation step, and termination behavior have no cited support; a solver or MIP-heuristics source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Rounding Conflict Repair
children.top_down_role: Handling of infeasibilities created by tentative rounding choices.

assumptions_latex: A rounded vector \(x\) satisfies all variable bounds and is integral on \(I\), but may violate \(Ax\le b\).
Each repair move preserves bounds and integrality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a feasible integral candidate or reports failure when no admissible improving move exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy repair of row conflicts created by rounding an LP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(v_i(x)=\max\{0,a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\}\) and \(V(x)=\sum_i w_i v_i(x)\) for fixed weights \(w_i>0\). While \(V(x)>0\), form admissible integer moves \(x_j\leftarrow x_j+d\), where \(j\in I\), \(d\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\), and \(\ell_j\le x_j+d\le u_j\). Choose a move with \(V(x+d e_j)<V(x)\), using objective degradation as a tie-breaker, and apply bound propagation. Stop successfully when \(V(x)=0\); stop unsuccessfully if no improving admissible move exists or a prescribed iteration limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly change bounded integer values to reduce weighted row violations. Stop with a feasible candidate, or fail when no improving move or iteration budget remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Conflict Repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted-violation repair algorithm fits Rounding Conflict Repair and does not overclaim successful recovery. Its move set, merit function, tie-breaking rule, and stopping conditions are nevertheless uncited and are not uniquely determined by standard terminology.

children.title: Feasibility-Restoration Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Feasibility restoration through value changes and propagation.

children.title: Candidate Repair Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Feasibility restoration through targeted changes to an infeasible candidate.

assumptions_latex: The candidate \(x\) obeys variable domains but may violate constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\).
An admissible neighborhood \(N(x)\) and positive violation weights are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a feasible domain-respecting candidate or an explicit repair failure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic local repair of a domain-valid but constraint-infeasible MIP candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(V(x)=\sum_i w_i\max\{0,g_i(x)\}\) with \(w_i>0\). For \(k=0,\ldots,K-1\), return \(x\) if \(V(x)=0\). Otherwise generate \(N(x)\), discard moves that violate bounds or integrality, and select \(y\in N(x)\) minimizing a prescribed merit \(V(y)+\rho\max\{0,c^{\mathsf T}y-c^{\mathsf T}x\}\), with \(\rho\ge0\). Apply \(x\leftarrow y\) only under the method's acceptance rule, then propagate implied bounds. Report failure if no acceptable neighbor exists or if \(K\) iterations elapse without \(V(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search a domain-preserving neighborhood for moves that reduce constraint violation while controlling objective loss. Return a feasible candidate or report that the repair attempt failed.
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate Repair Heuristics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected algorithm kind fits Candidate Repair Heuristics, but the record specifies a particular merit function and acceptance framework without evidence. Because these choices define the mathematical algorithm rather than merely notation, a direct source is needed.

children.title: Value-Shifting Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Feasibility restoration through coordinated variable-value shifts.

assumptions_latex: The current candidate \(x\) respects variable domains, and violated constraints are identifiable.
Allowed shifts preserve bounds and integrality of integer variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted shift decreases the selected repair merit; termination yields feasibility or declared failure.

notation.meaning: admissible shift set for coordinate j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate shifts chosen to restore feasibility while retaining variable-domain validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At candidate \(x\), define \(V(x)=\sum_i w_i\max\{0,g_i(x)\}\). For each eligible coordinate \(j\), construct \(D_j(x)\) from shifts \(d\) satisfying \(\ell_j\le x_j+d\le u_j\), with \(d\in\mathbb Z\) when \(j\in I\). Evaluate \(\Delta_{j,d}=V(x+d e_j)-V(x)\) and choose an admissible pair with \(\Delta_{j,d}<0\), breaking ties by objective change. Set \(x\leftarrow x+d e_j\), propagate consequences, and repeat. Return \(x\) when \(V(x)=0\); otherwise report failure when no decreasing shift exists or a limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift one bounded variable at a time, preserving integrality where required, to reduce weighted infeasibility. Continue until constraints are satisfied or no improving shift exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Shifting Heuristics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-shifting algorithm is locally appropriate and its feasibility limitation is stated correctly. No source supports the exact violation measure, admissible-shift construction, move rule, propagation step, or stopping conditions.

children.title: Repair Propagation Feedback
children.top_down_role: Interaction between tentative repairs and resulting domain inference.

assumptions_latex: A repair procedure maintains current bounds \([\ell,u]\) and a partial assignment.
A propagation oracle either tightens bounds consistently or detects infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted repair move is evaluated after propagation, so implied violations influence subsequent move selection.

notation.meaning: propagation operator applied after a tentative move

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback loop coupling tentative repair moves with constraint and bound propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every tentative domain-valid repair move \(m\), compute \((x^m,\ell^m,u^m)=\mathcal P(m(x),\ell,u)\). Reject \(m\) if propagation proves \(\ell_j^m>u_j^m\) for some \(j\) or contradicts a fixed integer value. Otherwise score \(m\) using a merit \(M(x^m,\ell^m,u^m)\) that includes residual row violations and newly forced assignments. Accept a move satisfying the prescribed improvement rule, replace \((x,\ell,u)\) by its propagated state, and regenerate the repair neighborhood. Stop when the propagated candidate is feasible, or report failure if every tentative move is rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate each tentative repair before accepting it. Newly tightened bounds, forced values, or contradictions feed back into move scoring and the next repair neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: Repair Propagation Feedback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role matches Repair Propagation Feedback, and the statement consistently evaluates tentative moves after propagation. The propagation-and-merit feedback rule is a substantive algorithmic specification with no cited evidence, so it cannot be accepted as candidate-review knowledge yet.

children.title: Staged-Integrality Construction Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Construction through staged enforcement of integrality.

children.title: Integrality Staging
children.top_down_role: Partitioning discrete variables across successive enforcement stages.

assumptions_latex: The MIP has integer index set \(I\) and continuous relaxation feasible region \(P\).
An ordered partition \(I=I_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_T\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After stage \(T\), every variable indexed by \(I\) is integral unless a stage has reported failure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential enforcement of integrality on prescribed blocks of integer variables.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(F_0=\varnothing\). For stages \(t=1,\ldots,T\), solve a residual relaxation over \(P\) with variables in \(F_{t-1}\) fixed and integrality enforced, or explicitly rounded and repaired, on \(I_t\). If no acceptable stage solution \(x^{(t)}\) is found, invoke recovery or report failure. Otherwise set \(F_t=F_{t-1}\cup I_t\), fix each \(j\in I_t\) at the accepted integer value \(x_j^{(t)}\), propagate bounds, and continue. Return the final candidate only after feasibility and integrality checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition integer variables into ordered stages. Enforce and fix one block at a time, solving the remaining relaxation after each stage and checking the final candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality Staging

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Integrality Staging, but the cited subsection on integrality constraints does not, from the supplied locator, support ordered block staging, repeated fixing, propagation, or recovery. A source specifically describing staged integrality construction is required.

children.title: Stagewise Variable Fixing
children.top_down_role: Retention of selected discrete values between construction stages.

assumptions_latex: An ordered staging \(I_1,\ldots,I_T\) of integer variables is given.
At stage \(t\), a feasible residual solution \(x^{(t)}\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed set grows monotonically, \(F_{t-1}\subseteq F_t\), and fixed variables retain integral values.

notation.meaning: integer variables selected at stage t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permanent or tolerance-controlled fixing of variables accepted at each integrality stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(t\), select \(S_t\subseteq I_t\setminus F_{t-1}\) using a prescribed reliability rule, such as small distance to an integer and acceptable lock or feasibility score. For each \(j\in S_t\), choose \(z_j^{(t)}\in\mathbb Z\cap[\ell_j,u_j]\), add the equality \(x_j=z_j^{(t)}\), and set \(F_t=F_{t-1}\cup S_t\). Propagate the new equalities and solve the resulting residual subproblem. If propagation or solution proves infeasibility, invoke the specified backtracking or recovery policy; otherwise retain all fixings and proceed to the next stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select reliable integer variables at each stage, fix them to accepted values, propagate the equalities, and solve the residual problem, with recovery if the fixings cause infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Variable Fixing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record is correctly classified as an algorithm and matches Stagewise Variable Fixing. Its reliability selection, permanent fixing, propagation, and backtracking policy are uncited substantive choices and require direct source support.

children.title: Residual Subproblem Recovery
children.top_down_role: Handling of infeasible, weak, or stalled residual construction problems.

assumptions_latex: A staged construction has fixed variables \(F\) at integer values \(z_F\).
The residual subproblem is infeasible or fails to produce an acceptable completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recovery either produces a feasible completion consistent with retained fixings or returns failure after exhausting its budget.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery from infeasible or unproductive residual subproblems by selectively relaxing earlier fixings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the subproblem with \(x_F=z_F\) has no acceptable solution, rank fixings by a prescribed conflict, age, or reliability score. Select a nonempty release set \(R\subseteq F\), replace the equalities for \(R\) by their original domains, and retain \(x_j=z_j\) for \(j\in F\setminus R\). Propagate and re-solve the enlarged residual subproblem, optionally imposing a neighborhood bound on released variables. If a feasible completion is found, return it; otherwise enlarge \(R\) or change retained values according to the recovery schedule, terminating with failure when the recovery budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When staged fixings block completion, release selected low-reliability or conflicting fixings and re-solve the enlarged residual problem until a completion is found or recovery is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Subproblem Recovery

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The release-and-resolve procedure fits Residual Subproblem Recovery and states success and failure outcomes conservatively. The ranking criteria, release schedule, optional neighborhood restriction, and recovery budget have no supporting citation.

children.title: Decomposition-Based Primal Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction from solutions of decomposed model components.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set has block variables \(x=(x^1,\ldots,x^K)\) with local constraints \(x^k\in X_k\).
Coupling constraints are the only constraints linking different blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The heuristic returns a globally feasible assembled point or reports failure of reconciliation.

notation.meaning: block-feasible sets, possibly containing integrality restrictions
coupling residual of the assembled point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal candidate construction from block solutions followed by coupling-constraint reconciliation.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve or approximately solve each block problem over \(X_k\) under current master decisions, prices, or targets, obtaining \(x^k\). Assemble \(x=(x^1,\ldots,x^K)\) and evaluate the coupling residual \(r(x)\). If \(r(x)=0\) and all global inequalities hold, return \(x\). Otherwise solve a reconciliation problem that changes selected block decisions while preserving \(x^k\in X_k\), minimizing a specified combination of coupling violation, displacement, and objective degradation. Re-solve affected blocks as needed and return the assembled point only after global feasibility and integrality checks; otherwise report failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine solutions of nearly independent blocks, then solve a reconciliation problem for coupling constraints. Accept the assembled point only after global feasibility and integrality checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Based Primal Heuristics

children.title: Lagrangian Primal Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction from Lagrangian relaxation information.

assumptions_latex: The MIP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ Hx=h\}\), where \(X\) contains local constraints and integrality.
A multiplier vector \(\lambda\) is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a feasible primal candidate or reports that repair failed; the Lagrangian minimizer alone need not be feasible for \(Hx=h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal recovery from solutions of a Lagrangian relaxation of coupling equalities.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(x(\lambda)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Hx-h)\}\), exploiting any block separability of \(X\). If \(Hx(\lambda)=h\), return \(x(\lambda)\). Otherwise use its integer block decisions as a candidate and solve a primal recovery problem over \(X\) that enforces \(Hx=h\), minimizing a prescribed combination of distance from \(x(\lambda)\) and original objective value. Optionally update \(\lambda\) and repeat. Return only a point satisfying all original constraints and integrality requirements; report failure when the recovery or iteration budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the Lagrangian relaxation at chosen multipliers, then repair its possibly inconsistent block decisions under the original coupling constraints. Return only a globally feasible integral point.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Primal Heuristics

children.title: Component-Solution Reconciliation
children.top_down_role: Assembly of globally usable candidates from partial or inconsistent component solutions.

assumptions_latex: Local solutions \(x^k\in X_k\) assign possibly inconsistent values to shared or coupled quantities.
A reconciliation model specifies admissible changes to component solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted reconciled vector is locally feasible in every component and satisfies all enforced consistency constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconciliation of locally feasible component solutions that disagree on shared or coupling quantities.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Lagrangian Decomposition via Copying Constraints p. 88

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given component solutions \(x^k\in X_k\), solve a reconciliation problem over \(y^k\in X_k\) that enforces the required consistency equations, for example \(B_k y^k=B_\ell y^\ell\) for designated component pairs \((k,\ell)\). Minimize \(\sum_k d_k(y^k,x^k)+\rho\Phi(y)\), where each \(d_k\) is a prescribed displacement measure, \(\Phi\) measures objective degradation, and \(\rho\ge0\). If the reconciliation problem is infeasible, selectively release component decisions or regenerate local solutions. Assemble and return \(y\) only after checking every local domain, integrality condition, and global coupling constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Modify locally feasible component solutions as little as possible so shared quantities agree and coupling constraints hold. If reconciliation is infeasible, release decisions or regenerate components.
knowledge_statements.title: Component-Solution Reconciliation
