children.title: Diving Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Temporary search paths formed by progressively restricting relaxation variables.

children.title: Geometry-Integrality Diving Signal Family
children.top_down_role: Diving variants guided by discrete infeasibility and relaxation geometry.

children.title: Fractionality-Guided Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving choices ranked by discrete infeasibility in the relaxation solution.

assumptions_latex: The current node relaxation has an optimal solution \(x^*\), and \(I\) indexes integer variables not fixed by their bounds.
At least one \(i\in I\) satisfies \(x_i^*\notin\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns an integral feasible incumbent if repair succeeds; otherwise it terminates without an incumbent.

notation.meaning: fractionality score of integer variable i
current set of unfixed fractional integer variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical most-fractional diving template; production solvers may reverse priorities or use different rounding directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(F=\{i\in I:x_i^*\notin\mathbb Z\}\). While \(F\neq\varnothing\), choose \(i\in\arg\max_{j\in F} f_j\), select \(r_i\in\{\lfloor x_i^*\rfloor,\lceil x_i^*\rceil\}\) by a fixed tie-breaking rule, impose \(x_i=r_i\), propagate bounds, and reoptimize the relaxation. Stop when propagation proves infeasibility, a prescribed depth or iteration limit is reached, or all integer variables are integral. In the last case, retain the point only if every original constraint is satisfied, optionally after a feasibility-repair procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly fix a maximally fractional integer variable, propagate, and reoptimize; accept the resulting point only after integrality and original-model feasibility checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractionality-Guided Diving

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the diving leaf, but no citation supports the most-fractional priority, rounding convention, or optional repair guarantee. These choices are variant-dependent, so the mathematical version cannot be validated from the supplied evidence.

children.title: Vector-Length-Guided Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving choices ranked by relaxation-geometry displacement measures.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation solution is \(x^*\), and each eligible integer variable \(i\) has column vector \(a_i\) in the active linearized constraints.
At least one eligible integer variable is fractional and has a defined positive scaling factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure either produces a validated feasible incumbent or terminates at infeasibility or a resource limit.

notation.meaning: active constraint column of variable i
Euclidean displacement caused by rounding i to r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A column-displacement interpretation is stated; the title admits solver-specific vector-length definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(D=\{(i,r):i\in I,\ x_i^*\notin\mathbb Z,\ r\in\{\lfloor x_i^*\rfloor,\lceil x_i^*\rceil\}\}\). At each dive step, choose a pair \((i,r)\) minimizing \(L_i(r)=|r-x_i^*|\|a_i\|_2\), fix \(x_i=r\), perform domain propagation, and reoptimize the relaxation. Remove fixed variables from consideration and repeat until integrality, detected infeasibility, or a depth or work limit. An integral relaxation point is returned only after checking all original constraints and applying any permitted repair procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the rounding whose scaled constraint-space displacement is smallest, then fix, propagate, and reoptimize until feasibility, failure, or a work limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Vector-Length-Guided Diving

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but “vector length” is not established as the proposed column-displacement score. A solver-specific or scholarly diving reference is required to validate the formula and minimization rule.

children.title: Geometry–Integrality Signal Selection
children.top_down_role: Regimes favoring discrete infeasibility signals or geometric signals.

assumptions_latex: Every eligible variable-direction pair has a geometry score \(g_{ir}\) and an integrality score \(q_{ir}\).
Scores are normalized over the current candidate set before aggregation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected pair maximizes the declared normalized geometry-integrality score among currently eligible moves.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic selector combining geometric displacement and distance-to-integrality signals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \((i,r)\in D\), compute \(S_{ir}=\lambda N_D(g)_{ir}+(1-\lambda)N_D(q)_{ir}\), where larger normalized values denote preferred moves and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\) is fixed before the dive. Select \((i^*,r^*)\in\arg\max_{(i,r)\in D}S_{ir}\) using a deterministic tie breaker, impose \(x_{i^*}=r^*\), propagate, and reoptimize. Recompute both score families after each successful relaxation solve. Stop at integrality, infeasibility, or a resource limit, and validate original-model feasibility before returning an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize geometry and integrality scores, combine them with a fixed weight, and repeatedly execute the highest-scoring valid rounding move.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry–Integrality Signal Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is a reasonable role for this selection leaf, but the normalization operator and convex aggregation rule are neither fully defined nor sourced. Evidence is needed that this is an established geometry–integrality selector rather than an invented generic template.

children.title: Model-Structure Diving Signal Family
children.top_down_role: Diving variants guided by model coefficients, locks, or objective impact.

children.title: Coefficient-Guided Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving choices guided by model coefficient structure.

assumptions_latex: The active linear relaxation is \(Ax\le b\), with relaxation solution \(x^*\) and integer index set \(I\).
Each fractional integer variable admits at least one bound-feasible adjacent integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns only a point satisfying integrality and every original constraint; otherwise it reports heuristic failure.

notation.meaning: constraint coefficient of variable i in row k
weighted row displacement caused by rounding i to r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic coefficient-magnitude diving rule, not a claim about one solver's implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each feasible adjacent rounding \((i,r)\), compute \(C_i(r)=|r-x_i^*|\sum_k w_k|a_{ki}|\), with fixed nonnegative row weights \(w_k\). Choose a pair minimizing \(C_i(r)\), fix \(x_i=r\), propagate the resulting domains, and reoptimize the relaxation. Recompute scores after reoptimization and continue until all integer variables are integral, propagation or relaxation proves infeasibility, or a prescribed work limit is reached. Return an integral point only after checking it against the original, unscaled model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round the fractional variable producing the smallest coefficient-weighted row displacement, then propagate and reoptimize until success or termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Guided Diving

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the diving leaf, but no source supports this coefficient-weighted displacement formula or the choice to minimize it. Coefficient-guided variants can use materially different scores and directions.

children.title: Lock-Guided Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving choices guided by constraint-lock exposure.

assumptions_latex: For every eligible integer variable, propagation can count the active constraints that may be violated by rounding down or up.
At least one bound-feasible rounding direction exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each chosen move minimizes the declared lock count among eligible adjacent roundings at that dive step.

notation.meaning: number of active constraints opposing rounding i downward
number of active constraints opposing rounding i upward

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard fewer-locks template; lock definitions and tie breakers vary across solver implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every fractional \(i\), associate \(L_i(\lfloor x_i^*\rfloor)=\ell_i^-\) and \(L_i(\lceil x_i^*\rceil)=\ell_i^+\), discarding bound-infeasible moves. Select an eligible pair \((i,r)\) with minimum \(L_i(r)\), break ties by a fixed secondary score, impose \(x_i=r\), and run domain propagation followed by relaxation reoptimization. Repeat until integrality, detected infeasibility, or a work limit. If all integer variables become integral, accept the candidate only after verifying every original constraint or completing an allowed feasibility repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefer a rounding direction opposed by the fewest active constraints, then fix, propagate, reoptimize, and validate any integral candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Lock-Guided Diving

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate and the fewer-locks idea is plausible, but the direction-specific lock convention and global minimization rule require a precise source locator.

children.title: Objective-Guided Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving choices guided by estimated objective impact.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation minimizes \(c^Tx\), has solution \(x^*\), and \(I\) indexes its integer variables.
At least one fractional integer variable has a bound-feasible adjacent rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every step, the selected adjacent rounding has minimum predicted linear objective change among eligible moves.

notation.meaning: linear objective coefficient of variable i
predicted objective change from rounding i to r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-objective rounding template for a minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct \(D\) from all bound-feasible adjacent roundings of fractional integer variables. Choose \((i,r)\in\arg\min_{(j,s)\in D}\Delta_j(s)\), where \(\Delta_i(r)=c_i(r-x_i^*)\), impose \(x_i=r\), propagate, and reoptimize the relaxation. Recompute \(D\) and the objective-change scores at the new solution. Stop when integrality is attained, infeasibility is detected, or a resource limit is reached. Return a candidate only after verification against all original constraints; objective preference does not itself certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the adjacent integer rounding with the best predicted linear objective change, then propagate and reoptimize while separately enforcing feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Guided Diving

children.title: Search-Evidence Diving Signal Family

children.title: Dual-Guided Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving choices guided by dual relaxation artifacts.

assumptions_latex: The current LP relaxation has primal solution \(x^*\) and reduced costs \(\bar c_i\) under a fixed minimization sign convention.
At least one fractional integer variable admits a bound-feasible adjacent rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chosen move minimizes the reduced-cost estimate among eligible adjacent rounding moves.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost-guided diving template under a minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each relaxation solution, form \(E\) from bound-feasible adjacent roundings of fractional integer variables and compute \(D_i(r)=\max\{0,\bar c_i(r-x_i^*)\}\). Select a pair minimizing \(D_i(r)\), with deterministic tie breaking, fix \(x_i=r\), perform propagation, and reoptimize to obtain updated primal and dual information. Stop at integrality, infeasibility, or a resource limit. Any integral candidate is returned only after original-model feasibility is checked; the reduced-cost value is a selection signal, not a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use reduced costs to estimate objective damage, take the least damaging rounding, and refresh dual information after propagation and reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Guided Diving

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the truncated reduced-cost expression is not a generally valid direction-independent degradation estimate without additional basis, bound-status, and sign hypotheses. A source is required for the exact dual-guided rule.

children.title: Inference-Guided Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving choices guided by expected propagation consequences.

assumptions_latex: Historical search data provide nonnegative inference estimates for each eligible variable and rounding direction.
The estimates are updated only from completed propagation events under a fixed counting convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each dive step chooses an eligible rounding with maximal estimated propagation inference.

notation.meaning: observed number of domain reductions after rounding i to r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Historical-propagation interpretation of inference-guided diving.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize each \(H_{ir}\) from available search observations, for example as the mean of recorded values \(n_{ir}^{(t)}\). At a dive step, select \((i,r)\in\arg\max_{(j,s)\in E}H_{js}\), fix \(x_i=r\), and run propagation. Record the resulting domain reductions, update \(H_{ir}\), and reoptimize if propagation remains feasible. Repeat until an integral candidate, infeasibility, or a work limit is reached. Validate every original constraint before returning an incumbent, and use a declared fallback score when no observation exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefer roundings that historically triggered many domain reductions, update the inference statistics after propagation, and validate any resulting candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Inference-Guided Diving

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate, but the historical mean, observation unit, update policy, and maximization convention are implementation-dependent and unsupported. A solver-specific or scholarly reference is needed.

children.title: Conflict-Guided Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving choices guided by learned conflict information.

assumptions_latex: Conflict analysis supplies nonnegative direction-specific scores from previously learned conflicts.
Scores are computed using a fixed aging and aggregation policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each dive step selects a currently eligible move maximizing the declared conflict-derived score.

notation.meaning: learned conflicts containing the bound change associated with (i,r)
nonnegative weight of learned conflict C
conflict score of a rounding move

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic learned-conflict scoring rule; implementations may prefer or avoid conflict-associated directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every eligible adjacent rounding \((i,r)\), compute \(K_{ir}=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C_{ir}}w_C\). Under the declared preference convention, select a pair maximizing \(K_{ir}\), fix \(x_i=r\), propagate using the current learned constraints, and reoptimize when feasible. Update conflict scores after any newly analyzed infeasibility. Stop at an integral point, detected infeasibility, or a work limit. An integral point becomes an incumbent only after original-model validation; if the implementation interprets conflict evidence as risk, it must reverse the score order explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score rounding directions from learned conflicts, follow the declared preference order, update scores after conflict analysis, and validate any candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Guided Diving

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but conflict evidence may indicate either a promising direction or a risky one. The candidate explicitly leaves that central interpretation variant-dependent, so the maximization rule requires a source.

notation.meaning: solution of the current NLP relaxation

children.title: Constraint-Specific Diving
children.top_down_role: Diving adapted to specialized constraint-handler semantics.

assumptions_latex: Each active constraint handler can recognize its constraint class and propose sound domain reductions or candidate assignments.
All proposed moves are checked against current variable domains before application.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure accepts only a domain-consistent, integral candidate satisfying all original constraints.

notation.meaning: moves proposed by handler h at state x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract handler-driven diving protocol for constraints with exploitable semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the current relaxation state \(x\), request from each \(h\in\mathcal H\) a finite set \(M_h(x)\) of domain-valid fixing or rounding moves and scores \(p_h(m)\). Select the highest-priority compatible move, apply it, invoke all affected handlers for propagation, and reoptimize the relaxation if no contradiction is found. Recompute proposals after every state change. Stop when no move exists, infeasibility is detected, a resource limit is reached, or all integer variables are integral. In the last case, validate the candidate with every original constraint handler before returning it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let constraint handlers propose and score semantically valid fixing moves, propagate after each choice, and require unanimous original-constraint validation of candidates.

children.title: Semantic Feasibility Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Restrictions protecting specialized or nonlinear feasibility during diving.

assumptions_latex: Every variable has a current domain, and each semantic constraint handler implements a sound feasibility and propagation test.
Numerical comparisons use declared absolute and relative tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dive candidate is returned only if it passes domain, integrality, numerical, and original semantic-constraint checks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance and early-abort safeguards for semantics-aware diving.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After every tentative move, require \(x_i\in D_i\) for each fixed variable and invoke sound propagation for every affected \(g\in\mathcal G\); abort the dive if any domain becomes empty or a handler proves infeasibility. Before incumbent acceptance, require \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every integer variable, finite evaluability of every original expression, satisfaction of discrete semantics such as indicators or disjunctions, and residual violation at most \(\varepsilon_g\) for each \(g\). Relaxation feasibility or feasibility of a surrogate formulation alone is insufficient for acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Abort on semantic or domain contradiction, and accept only finite, integral candidates satisfying every original constraint and discrete semantic rule within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Feasibility Safeguards

children.title: Linear Feasibility Pumps
children.top_down_role: Feasibility-pump processing for linear integer-model settings.

assumptions_latex: The linear relaxation \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\) is nonempty.
The index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) identifies bounded integer variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a mixed-integer feasible point when an iterate satisfies all linear constraints and integrality requirements; otherwise it terminates without such a certificate.

notation.meaning: Rounded integer target at iteration k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The alternating rounding and distance-minimizing LP formulation is the standard linear feasibility-pump template.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic linear feasibility pump for bounded MILP feasibility; cycling controls are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x^0\in P\). At iteration \(k\), form \(z^k_i=\operatorname{round}(x^k_i)\) for \(i\in I\), retaining the continuous coordinates only as auxiliary values. If some \(x\in P\) satisfies \(x_i=z^k_i\) for every \(i\in I\), return such an \(x\). Otherwise compute a projection by solving \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\sum_{i\in I}|x_i-z^k_i|.\] Linearize each absolute value with nonnegative deviation variables. Continue until feasibility is obtained, a prescribed iteration limit is reached, or a repeated state triggers a separately specified perturbation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate componentwise integer rounding with an LP minimizing distance to the rounded target, stopping when the target extends to a feasible mixed-integer point.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Feasibility Pumps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits this leaf and the linear alternating-rounding/LP-projection description is plausible, but the record has no citation with an inspectable locator. The supplied inventory does not identify a section supporting this feasibility-pump template, stopping rule, or perturbation interface.

children.title: Mixed-Binary Feasibility Pumps
children.top_down_role: Feasibility-pump processing specialized to binary-plus-continuous models.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation \(P\subseteq[0,1]^B\times\mathbb R^{n-|B|}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
Exactly the variables indexed by \(B\) are binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any returned point belongs to \(P\) and has binary coordinates on \(B\), hence is feasible for the mixed-binary model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Binary feasibility pumps use componentwise rounding and the linear Hamming-distance projection objective.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical mixed-binary feasibility pump with continuous variables handled by the LP projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with \(x^0\in P\). For each iteration, set \(z^k_i=1\) when \(x^k_i\ge \tfrac12\) and \(z^k_i=0\) otherwise, for every \(i\in B\). Test whether the face \(\{x\in P:x_i=z^k_i\ \text{for all }i\in B\}\) is nonempty and return a point on it when it is. Otherwise solve \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\left(\sum_{i\in B:z^k_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in B:z^k_i=1}(1-x_i)\right).\] Stop at feasibility, an iteration limit, or invocation of a stagnation control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round binary relaxation values and repeatedly solve an LP minimizing Hamming distance to the rounded vector until a feasible mixed-binary point is found.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Binary Feasibility Pumps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the mixed-binary leaf, and the displayed objective is the standard linear expression for Hamming distance on binary coordinates. No cited source supports the precise rounding threshold, face-feasibility test, projection step, and stopping behavior.

children.title: General-Integer Extension Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits encountered when binary-oriented pump behavior is extended to broader integer domains.

assumptions_latex: At least one integer variable has a domain containing three distinct integers.
A binary feasibility-pump distance formula is applied without a general-integer reformulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Binary Hamming-distance projections do not directly define a valid magnitude-sensitive general-integer pump; general-integer extensions require absolute-deviation modeling, scaling, or another explicit distance convention.

notation.meaning: A rounded target value for y.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The binary linearization of Hamming distance relies essentially on variables taking only zero and one.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the binary Hamming-distance formula, not impossibility of general-integer feasibility pumps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary variable, disagreement with \(\bar y\in\{0,1\}\) equals \(y\) when \(\bar y=0\) and \(1-y\) when \(\bar y=1\). This identity fails for a general-integer variable. For example, if \(y\in\{0,1,2\}\) and \(\bar y=2\), the expression \(1-y\) is negative at \(y=2\), while the valid absolute deviation is \(|y-2|=0\). Moreover, unit Hamming disagreement assigns the same distance to \(y=0\) and \(y=1\), although their absolute deviations from \(2\) differ. Thus the binary projection objective cannot be transferred unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The binary Hamming-distance formula fails for variables with more than two integer values; a general-integer pump must choose and model another distance.
knowledge_statements.title: General-Integer Extension Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the exact leaf, and the record correctly limits its claim to transferring the binary Hamming formula unchanged. A targeted source is still required for the asserted extension boundary and the stated general-integer alternatives; none of the inventory locators specifically addresses feasibility pumps.

children.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Pumps
children.top_down_role: Projection and repair regimes adapted to nonlinear feasibility.

assumptions_latex: The continuous relaxation is \(R=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\).
The index set \(I\) identifies integer coordinates, and each projection subproblem is solved to a declared local or global standard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned iterate is feasible for the nonlinear mixed-integer model; failure of a projection subproblem or exhaustion of the budget yields no feasibility certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Nonlinear feasibility-pump variants alternate discrete rounding with nonlinear projection or restoration subproblems.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic nonlinear projection-and-repair regime; projection may be local and therefore heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select \(x^0\in R\). At iteration \(k\), round the coordinates \(x^k_I\) to an admissible integer vector \(z^k\). Attempt nonlinear restoration with those coordinates fixed by solving a feasibility problem over \(\{x\in R:x_I=z^k\}\); return any feasible solution. If restoration fails, compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}d_I(x_I,z^k),\] where \(d_I\) is a declared nonnegative distance that vanishes exactly at equality. Apply a declared perturbation when targets repeat. Stop upon mixed-integer feasibility, projection failure, or exhaustion of the iteration or time budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate integer rounding with nonlinear feasibility restoration and distance projection, acknowledging that nonconvex projection may return only a local solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Pumps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the nonlinear-feasibility-pump topic, but the proposed restoration/projection regime is source-sensitive. In particular, the meaning of restoration failure and membership in an argmin depends on whether subproblems are solved locally or globally. The general MINLP inventory entries do not specifically support this algorithm.

children.title: Objective-Aware Feasibility Pumps
children.top_down_role: Feasibility-pump variants balancing feasibility and incumbent quality.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation region \(P\) is nonempty and the original objective is \(c^Tx\).
The integer indices are \(I\), and finite objective scaling constants are fixed before iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameter \(\alpha_k\) explicitly trades objective quality against agreement with the integer target; any returned feasible iterate remains valid for the original model.

notation.meaning: Objective-weight parameter in the unit interval.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Objective-aware pumps use a weighted projection objective combining integrality distance and normalized original objective value.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-sum objective-aware feasibility pump with explicitly normalized objective and distance terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation point \(x^k\), round \(x^k_I\) to \(z^k\) and first test feasibility with \(x_I=z^k\). If the test fails, compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\left((1-\alpha_k)\widehat d_I(x_I,z^k)+\alpha_k\widehat f(x)\right),\qquad 0\le\alpha_k\le1,\] where \(\widehat d_I\) is a nonnegative normalized integrality distance and \(\widehat f\) is an affine normalization of \(c^Tx\) consistent with minimization. Update \(\alpha_k\) by a declared schedule, usually reducing objective emphasis as feasibility search proceeds. Return only an iterate satisfying the original constraints and integrality conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project using a weighted combination of distance to the rounded target and normalized original objective value, with a declared weight schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Aware Feasibility Pumps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the objective-aware leaf, but the precise weighted objective, affine normalization, and claim that objective emphasis is usually reduced require a source. No supplied locator addresses objective-aware feasibility pumps or establishes this schedule.

children.title: Feasibility-Pump Stagnation Controls
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms addressing stagnation and repeated projection patterns.

children.title: Projection Perturbation
children.top_down_role: Controlled displacement of repeated projection states.

assumptions_latex: A feasibility-pump state \((x^k,z^k)\) has stagnated or repeated.
Each integer variable has a finite admissible set or bounded perturbation neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perturbed target differs from the stagnant target on the selected coordinates and is admissible; it does not by itself certify feasibility or eventual convergence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Feasibility-pump perturbations modify selected rounded coordinates before repeating the projection step.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract admissible perturbation used after detected stagnation; selection rules remain implementation-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Upon stagnation, select a nonempty set \(S_k\subseteq I\) using a declared deterministic or randomized rule. Construct an admissible integer vector \(\widetilde z^k\) such that \(\widetilde z^k_i=z^k_i\) for \(i\notin S_k\) and \(\widetilde z^k_i\ne z^k_i\) for at least one \(i\in S_k\). For binary coordinates, an admissible choice is \(\widetilde z^k_i=1-z^k_i\) on selected indices. Replace the next distance projection toward \(z^k\) by a projection toward \(\widetilde z^k\), then resume rounding and feasibility tests. Reject perturbations violating variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When projection stagnates, alter selected integer target coordinates within their domains and project toward the perturbed target before resuming alternation.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Perturbation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits projection perturbation, but the selection and admissibility policy is intentionally abstract and has no supporting citation. Moreover, the statement uses the integer index set I without introducing it in the assumptions. A sourced perturbation policy is needed before selecting a definitive replacement formulation.

children.title: Cycle-Avoidance Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Detection or suppression of recurring projection patterns.

assumptions_latex: Each generated rounded target is an element of a discrete set \(Z\).
A finite history of recent targets is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted next target is absent from the retained history; this prevents immediate repetition but does not exclude longer cycles after history expiration.

notation.meaning: Rounded target proposed at iteration k.
Retained set of previously accepted targets.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Tabu histories and target perturbations are standard feasibility-pump cycle-avoidance mechanisms.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory target-level cycle avoidance for feasibility-pump iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain \(H_k\subseteq Z\) containing at most the last \(h\ge1\) accepted rounded targets. After rounding produces \(z^k\), accept it if \(z^k\notin H_k\). If \(z^k\in H_k\), generate admissible perturbations in a declared order until finding \(\widetilde z^k\in Z\setminus H_k\); if none is found within the perturbation budget, signal restart. Project toward the accepted target and update the history by inserting it and deleting the oldest entry when necessary. Feasibility is tested before projection so a repeated target that extends to a feasible point is not discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store recent rounded targets; when rounding repeats one, perturb to an admissible target outside the history or request a restart.
knowledge_statements.title: Cycle-Avoidance Mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits cycle avoidance, and the finite-history conclusion is appropriately limited to retained targets. The specific tabu-history mechanism, perturbation ordering, feasibility-test ordering, and restart behavior are uncited and are not supported by a relevant inventory locator.

children.title: Feasibility-Pump Restarts
children.top_down_role: Reinitialization regimes following persistent cycling or stagnation.

assumptions_latex: The current feasibility-pump run has met a declared restart trigger without finding feasibility.
A relaxation point or relaxation-solving procedure is available for reinitialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A restart begins a new trajectory while preserving the validity of any incumbent; it provides diversification but no finite-time feasibility guarantee.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Restart mechanisms reinitialize feasibility-pump trajectories after cycling, stagnation, or budget exhaustion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diversification restart after stagnation, cycling, or an exhausted per-run budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the trigger fires, increment \(r\), retain every feasible incumbent already found, and choose \(x^{0,r}\) by a declared rule, such as a new relaxation optimum, an alternative optimum, or an admissibly perturbed relaxation point. Clear or age the history \(H\) according to a declared memory policy, reset per-run counters, and start rounding and projection from \(x^{0,r}\). Terminate globally when feasibility is obtained or the total restart, time, or node budget is exhausted. The initialization rule must keep \(x^{0,r}\) in the continuous relaxation unless the subsequent step explicitly performs feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a declared stagnation trigger, preserve incumbents, reinitialize the relaxation trajectory, reset selected memory, and resume the feasibility pump under a global budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Pump Restarts

children.title: Single-Neighborhood Local Branching
children.top_down_role: Search within one incumbent-centered neighborhood.

assumptions_latex: The MILP has binary variables indexed by \(B\) and a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\).
A positive integer neighborhood radius \(k\) and a subproblem resource limit are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every subproblem solution differs from the incumbent in at most \(k\) binary positions; an improving feasible solution becomes the new incumbent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Classical local branching adds one incumbent-centered Hamming-ball inequality and solves the resulting restricted MILP.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One binary Hamming-ball subproblem centered at a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(B_1=\{i\in B:\bar x_i=1\}\) and \(B_0=B\setminus B_1\). Add the local-branching inequality \[\sum_{i\in B_0}x_i+\sum_{i\in B_1}(1-x_i)\le k\] to the original MILP and solve the restricted subproblem under the specified resource limit, optionally adding an objective cutoff requiring strict improvement over \(\bar x\). If the solver returns a feasible point \(x'\) with a better objective value, replace \(\bar x\) by \(x'\); otherwise retain \(\bar x\). The procedure performs no search outside this single neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add one Hamming-ball constraint around a binary incumbent, solve the restricted MILP, and accept any improving feasible solution found within the resource limit.

children.title: Variable-Neighborhood Local Branching
children.top_down_role: Search across neighborhoods with changing size or composition.

assumptions_latex: The MILP has binary index set \(B\) and an initial feasible incumbent \(\bar x^0\).
A finite sequence of radii, centers, and subproblem budgets is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted solution is feasible for the original MILP; changing radii or centers explores a sequence of distinct incumbent-related neighborhoods.

notation.meaning: Incumbent used as the neighborhood center at stage t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Variable-neighborhood local branching repeatedly changes the Hamming radius, center, or excluded region around incumbents.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential local-branching neighborhoods with declared radius and center updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(t\), solve the original MILP restricted by \[\sum_{i\in B:\bar x^t_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in B:\bar x^t_i=1}(1-x_i)\le k_t.\] Impose any objective cutoff and exclusions of previously completed neighborhoods explicitly. Choose \(k_{t+1}\) and the next center by the declared expansion, contraction, or recentering policy. Stop after the neighborhood sequence or global resource budget is exhausted, returning the best feasible incumbent encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a sequence of local-branching subproblems while changing the Hamming radius or center, retaining the best feasible incumbent found.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Neighborhood Local Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits variable-neighborhood local branching, and the record clearly distinguishes a sequence of neighborhoods from a single Hamming ball. No citation supports the expansion, contraction, recentering, or exclusion framework, and the objective sense governing improvement is not declared.

children.title: Relaxation-Induced Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Neighborhoods derived from agreement or proximity between incumbents and relaxation points.

children.title: RINS
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood restriction based on incumbent–relaxation agreement.

assumptions_latex: A feasible incumbent \(\bar x\) and a relaxation solution \(x^{LP}\) are available at a search node.
The set \(I\) indexes integer-constrained variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible solution of the RINS subproblem agrees with both reference solutions on all fixed coordinates; any improving subproblem solution is feasible for the original model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: RINS fixes integer variables on which an incumbent and relaxation solution agree, then solves the remaining restricted MIP.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical relaxation-induced neighborhood search based on exact incumbent-relaxation agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(F=\{i\in I:x^{LP}_i=\bar x_i\}\), where equality implies that the relaxation value is integral. Create a restricted subproblem from the original model by imposing \(x_i=\bar x_i\) for every \(i\in F\). Optionally impose an objective cutoff requiring improvement over \(\bar x\), and solve the subproblem under a prescribed node or time limit. If an improving feasible solution is found, install it as the incumbent; otherwise retain \(\bar x\). Variables in \(I\setminus F\) remain integer-constrained but unfixed, and continuous variables retain their original domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix integer variables where the incumbent and LP relaxation agree, solve the remaining restricted MIP, and accept an improving feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: RINS

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits RINS, and the fixing rule based on exact incumbent-relaxation agreement is mathematically coherent. The record supplies no primary or textbook citation with a locator for RINS, and none of the listed inventory sections specifically supports this neighborhood construction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: RINS neighborhood induced by agreement between a feasible incumbent and an optimal LP-relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible solution $x^*\in X$ and an optimal LP-relaxation solution $x^{\mathrm{LP}}$, let $F=\{j\in N:x_j^*=x_j^{\mathrm{LP}}\}$. Solve $\max\{c^Tx:x\in X,\ x_j=x_j^*\ \text{for all }j\in F\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix each indexed variable on which the feasible incumbent and optimal LP-relaxation solution agree, then optimize the resulting restricted integer program.
assumptions_latex: x^*\in X\text{ is feasible.}
x^{\mathrm{LP}}\text{ is an optimal solution of the LP relaxation.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The RINS subproblem optimizes over }X\cap\{x:x_j=x_j^*\ \forall j\in F\},\quad F=\{j\in N:x_j^*=x_j^{\mathrm{LP}}\}.

children.title: RENS Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Relaxation-enforced neighborhoods based on agreement with a relaxation solution.

assumptions_latex: A relaxation solution \(x^{LP}\) is available for a mixed-integer model.
All integer variables indexed by \(I\) have valid original bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The RENS neighborhood contains every integer vector obtained by independently rounding each fractional relaxation coordinate up or down, subject to the original constraints.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Classical RENS fixes integral relaxation coordinates and confines fractional integer coordinates between floor and ceiling.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical floor-ceiling relaxation-enforced neighborhood for bounded integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the neighborhood by retaining all original constraints and imposing, for every \(i\in I\), \[x_i=x^{LP}_i\quad\text{if }x^{LP}_i\in\mathbb Z,\qquad \lfloor x^{LP}_i\rfloor\le x_i\le\lceil x^{LP}_i\rceil\quad\text{otherwise}.\] Intersect these restrictions with the original variable bounds and integrality requirements to obtain \(N_{RENS}(x^{LP})\). Solve the resulting restricted mixed-integer subproblem under a declared resource limit, optionally with an incumbent-improvement cutoff. Return an improving feasible solution when one is found; otherwise report no neighborhood improvement without asserting global infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix integer variables already integral in the relaxation and restrict each fractional integer variable to its floor or ceiling before solving the subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: RENS Neighborhoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits RENS neighborhoods, and the floor-ceiling restrictions are internally consistent with the plain statement and conclusion. A targeted source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is required; the supplied inventory contains no locator specifically addressing RENS.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation-enforced neighborhood search specialized to a mixed-integer quadratically constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an optimal LP-relaxation solution \(\widetilde x\) at a branch-and-bound node, construct a sub-MIQCP by fixing each integer variable \(x_j\) with \(\widetilde x_j\in\mathbb Z\) to \(\widetilde x_j\), and restricting each integer variable with \(\widetilde x_j\notin\mathbb Z\) by \[\lfloor\widetilde x_j\rfloor\le x_j\le\lceil\widetilde x_j\rceil.\] Partially solve this sub-MIQCP as a primal heuristic. Every feasible solution of the sub-MIQCP is feasible for the original MIQCP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the optimal LP solution at a search node to define a RENS subproblem: fix integer variables that are integral in the relaxation and restrict each fractional integer variable to its two nearest integer values. Partially solve the resulting sub-MIQCP; every feasible subproblem solution is feasible for the original MIQCP.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde x\text{ is an optimal LP-relaxation solution at a branch-and-bound node}
x_j\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every integer-designated variable }j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname{Feas}(\operatorname{subMIQCP}(\widetilde x))\implies x^*\in\operatorname{Feas}(\operatorname{MIQCP}).

children.title: DINS Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Distance-induced neighborhoods combining incumbent information with relaxation proximity.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the feasible region of a mixed-integer program with integer index set \(I\).
\(\bar x\in X\) is an incumbent and \(x^{LP}\) is a current relaxation solution.
\(\varepsilon\ge 0\), \(k\ge 0\), and \(w_i>0\) are prescribed neighborhood parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{DINS}}(\bar x,x^{LP};\varepsilon,k)\) is a restricted feasible neighborhood containing \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Integer coordinates on which the incumbent and relaxation solution agree within tolerance.
Distance budget for unfixed integer coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a parameterized agreement-fixing and incumbent-distance formulation; exact published DINS conventions require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(A_\varepsilon=\{i\in I:|\bar x_i-x_i^{LP}|\le\varepsilon\}\). A parameterized distance-induced neighborhood is \[N_{\mathrm{DINS}}(\bar x,x^{LP};\varepsilon,k)=\left\{x\in X:x_i=\bar x_i\ \text{for all }i\in A_\varepsilon,\ \sum_{i\in I\setminus A_\varepsilon}w_i|x_i-\bar x_i|\le k\right\}.\] Since \(\bar x\in X\) satisfies the fixing equations and has zero distance, \(\bar x\in N_{\mathrm{DINS}}\). Solving the original objective over this set defines the associated restricted sub-MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DINS fixes integer coordinates where the incumbent and relaxation point agree, then searches within a bounded weighted distance of the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: DINS Neighborhoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied for this named DINS formulation. The agreement set, weighted incumbent-distance constraint, and claim that this parameterization represents DINS are version-sensitive and cannot be validated from standard-field rationale alone.

children.title: Relaxation-Support Neighborhood Variants
children.top_down_role: Related neighborhoods organized by relaxation support or enforced variable agreement.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a mixed-integer feasible region with integer index set \(I\).
\(\bar x\in X\) and a relaxation point \(x^{LP}\) are available.
A fixing rule, a center-selection rule, and a nonnegative distance function are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Different choices of \(F\), \(q\), \(D\), and \(\rho\) generate a common family of relaxation-support neighborhoods.

notation.meaning: Integer coordinates fixed by the variant.
Coordinatewise fixing values derived from the incumbent and relaxation point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract representation covering fixing, rounding, and distance-bounded relaxation-support variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F\subseteq I\), fixing values \(q_i(\bar x,x^{LP})\in\mathbb{Z}\), a function \(D:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\), and \(\rho\ge0\), define \[N(F,q,D,\rho)=\{x\in X:x_i=q_i(\bar x,x^{LP})\ \text{for all }i\in F,\ D(x;\bar x,x^{LP})\le\rho\}.\] Agreement-based fixing, relaxation-rounding fixing, and incumbent-distance restrictions are obtained by changing \(F\), \(q\), and \(D\). The resulting subproblem remains valid because every member of \(N(F,q,D,\rho)\) belongs to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation-support variants share one template: fix selected integer coordinates using incumbent-relaxation information and optionally impose a distance radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Support Neighborhood Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is internally coherent, and representation is an appropriate kind for a variants container, but no inspectable source establishes that the proposed template accurately covers the intended relaxation-support neighborhood family.

children.title: Multi-Solution Recombination Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Neighborhoods derived from multiple stored solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A primal MIP polishing heuristic that constructs a restricted subproblem by fixing variables on which selected stored solutions agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a list of at most \(k\) best feasible solutions. Select \(r\ge 2\) solutions \(x^1,\ldots,x^r\), define \(F=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:x_j^1=x_j^t\text{ for every }t=1,\ldots,r\}\), and denote the common value for \(j\in F\) by \(x_j^*\). Solve \(\max\{c^\top x:x\in X,\ x_j=x_j^*\text{ for every }j\in F\}\). For two-parent selection, choose the first solution randomly and the second randomly from better solutions in the list. A mutation variant fixes only a randomly selected subset of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep a list of at most k best feasible solutions, select two or more of them, fix variables on which all selected solutions agree, and solve the resulting restricted integer program. For a pair, the first solution is selected randomly and the second randomly from better listed solutions. Mutation consists of fixing only a random subset of the agreement variables.
assumptions_latex: k\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}
r\ge 2
x^1,\ldots,x^r\in X\text{ are stored feasible solutions}
F=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:x_j^1=x_j^t\ \forall t=1,\ldots,r\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Solve }\max\{c^\top x:x\in X,\ x_j=x_j^*\ \forall j\in F\},\text{ optionally fixing only a random subset of }F\text{ for mutation.}

children.title: Incumbent Crossover Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Neighborhoods formed from differing assignments among stored feasible solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a mixed-integer feasible region with integer index set \(I\).
\(P=\{x^1,\ldots,x^m\}\subseteq X\) is a set of feasible parent solutions with \(m\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{cross}}(P)\) preserves every integer allele shared by all parents and leaves every discordant integer coordinate available for recombination.

notation.meaning: Integer coordinates having the same value in every parent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-fixing sub-MIP crossover for two or more feasible parent solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the consensus set \[C(P)=\{i\in I:x_i^1=x_i^2=\cdots=x_i^m\}.\] The incumbent crossover neighborhood generated by \(P\) is \[N_{\mathrm{cross}}(P)=\{x\in X:x_i=x_i^1\ \text{for every }i\in C(P)\}.\] Each parent belongs to this neighborhood. Integer coordinates outside \(C(P)\) are not fixed by the crossover construction, although the original constraints in \(X\) continue to restrict them. Minimizing the original objective over \(N_{\mathrm{cross}}(P)\) may therefore combine parent assignments while preserving their common coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A crossover neighborhood fixes integer coordinates shared by all selected parents and lets a sub-MIP recombine their differing coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Crossover Neighborhoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The consensus-fixing neighborhood is mathematically coherent and definition is an appropriate kind, but no cited source confirms that this construction is the intended incumbent crossover neighborhood rather than one particular recombination variant.

children.title: Multi-Solution Recombination
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction from compatible components of several stored solutions.

assumptions_latex: The mixed-integer problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in X\}\).
A pool \(S\subseteq X\) of feasible solutions and an integer parent count \(m\ge2\) are available.
A finite sub-MIP resource limit and improvement tolerance \(\delta\ge0\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure either returns a feasible offspring improving the reference incumbent by at least \(\delta\), or leaves the incumbent unchanged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic restricted-sub-MIP recombination with explicit feasibility and acceptance rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(P\subseteq S\) with \(|P|=m\), construct a restricted recombination region \(N(P)\subseteq X\) containing the parents, and solve \[\min\{f(x):x\in N(P),\ f(x)\le f(\bar x)-\delta\}\] subject to the prescribed resource limit. If the sub-MIP returns a feasible point \(x^+\) satisfying \(f(x^+)\le f(\bar x)-\delta\), insert \(x^+\) into \(S\) and replace \(\bar x\) when \(f(x^+)<f(\bar x)\). If no such point is found before the limit, output the unchanged incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select feasible parents, solve a restricted recombination sub-MIP, and accept only an offspring meeting the stated improvement threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Solution Recombination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate kind for this procedural leaf, but the construction of the recombination region is delegated to an unspecified rule and no source supports the proposed acceptance procedure as a recognized multi-solution recombination method.

children.title: Parent-Solution Selection
children.top_down_role: Criteria governing which stored solutions supply neighborhood information.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq X\) is a finite pool of feasible solutions with \(|S|\ge m\ge2\).
The objective \(f\), a distance \(d\) on integer projections, and a weight \(\lambda\ge0\) are given.
Positive scaling constants \(s_f\) and \(s_d\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimizing set \(P^*\) balances parent quality against pairwise integer diversity under the declared score.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One explicit quality-diversity parent-selection rule; solver implementations may use different scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(P\subseteq S\) with \(|P|=m\), define \[\Phi(P)=\frac{1}{m s_f}\sum_{x\in P}f(x)-\frac{2\lambda}{m(m-1)s_d}\sum_{\{x,y\}\subseteq P}d(x_I,y_I).\] Select any \[P^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\subseteq S,\ |P|=m}\Phi(P),\] with deterministic tie-breaking if reproducibility is required. The first term favors lower-objective parents, while the second rewards separation of their integer projections. The selected set \(P^*\) is then passed to the recombination-neighborhood constructor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a fixed-size parent set by minimizing an explicit score that rewards objective quality and pairwise diversity.
knowledge_statements.title: Parent-Solution Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite argmin rule is well-defined and algorithm is an appropriate kind, but the quality-diversity score is explicitly only one formalized variant. An authoritative source is required before storing this particular score under the general parent-selection leaf.

children.title: Recombination Diversity Loss
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes caused by overly similar parents or excessively restrictive agreement.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) has integer index set \(I\).
A crossover neighborhood fixes every integer coordinate on which all selected parents agree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the parents have identical integer projections, recombination cannot produce a new integer assignment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp degeneracy boundary for consensus-fixing crossover neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(P=\{x^1,\ldots,x^m\}\subseteq X\) satisfies \(x_I^1=\cdots=x_I^m=z\). Then every integer coordinate is a consensus coordinate, so the crossover neighborhood is \[N_{\mathrm{cross}}(P)=\{x\in X:x_I=z\}.\] Consequently, every feasible offspring \(y\in N_{\mathrm{cross}}(P)\) satisfies \(y_I=z\). Recombination may still change continuous coordinates, but it cannot generate an integer assignment absent from the parents. Thus identical parent integer projections constitute complete integer-diversity loss for this crossover rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all parents have the same integer projection, consensus-fixing crossover cannot generate any new integer assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Recombination Diversity Loss

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conclusion follows for the stated consensus-fixing crossover rule, and failure_boundary is the correct kind for this leaf. However, the underlying crossover rule and the interpretation as recombination diversity loss have no cited support.

children.title: Restricted Incumbent Improvement Family
children.top_down_role: Restricted improvement focused on selected variable blocks or late-stage incumbent quality.

children.title: Fix-Optimize Block Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of variable blocks released for restricted incumbent improvement.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in X\}\) with integer index set \(I\).
\(\bar x\in X\) is the incumbent and \(\mathcal B\subseteq2^I\) is a nonempty family of candidate blocks.
A block score and a finite sub-MIP budget are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration changes integer variables only in the selected block and preserves feasibility of every accepted incumbent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic score-based fix-and-optimize block-selection procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\bar x^0=\bar x\). At iteration \(t\), choose an eligible block \[B_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B}\operatorname{score}_t(B),\] then solve, within the resource budget, \[\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ x_i=\bar x_i^t\ \text{for all }i\in I\setminus B_t\}.\] If a feasible solution \(x^t\) with \(f(x^t)<f(\bar x^t)\) is found, set \(\bar x^{t+1}=x^t\); otherwise set \(\bar x^{t+1}=\bar x^t\). Stop after the declared block schedule, stagnation limit, or global resource limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an integer-variable block, fix all other integer variables to the incumbent, solve the sub-MIP, and retain only an improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Fix-Optimize Block Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The procedure is internally coherent and algorithm fits the block-selection leaf, but the score-based selection and scheduling rules are generic constructions with no source establishing them as the intended fix-and-optimize mechanism.

children.title: Overlapping Block Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Restricted searches using overlapping or rotating variable groups.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) has integer index set \(I\), and \(\bar x\in X\).

\(B_1,
\ldots,B_q\subseteq I\) cover \(I\) and at least two blocks intersect.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family \(\{N_k(\bar x)\}_{k=1}^q\) is an overlapping collection of incumbent-centered restricted neighborhoods.

notation.meaning: Neighborhood obtained by freeing block k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines overlap through shared free-variable blocks in incumbent-centered sub-MIPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(k\in\{1,
\ldots,q\}\), define \[N_k(\bar x)=\{x\in X:x_i=\bar x_i\ \text{for all }i\in I\setminus B_k\}.\] The collection is covering when \(\bigcup_{k=1}^qB_k=I\), and it is overlapping when \(B_k\cap B_\ell\ne\varnothing\) for at least one pair \(k\ne\ell\). A variable in \(B_k\cap B_\ell\) can be reoptimized in both corresponding sub-MIPs, while variables outside the active block remain fixed at the current incumbent values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping block neighborhoods free intersecting subsets of integer variables while fixing all remaining integer coordinates to the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Block Neighborhoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The neighborhood definition and overlap condition are mathematically precise, and definition is suitable for this leaf. No citation supports this exact free-block formulation or its placement as the intended overlapping-block neighborhood concept.

children.title: Incumbent Solution Polishing
children.top_down_role: Late-stage improvement focused on incumbent quality within limited search regions.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in X\}\), and \(\bar x^0\in X\) is an incumbent.

A finite ordered neighborhood family \(N_1,
\ldots,N_q\) and a strict improvement tolerance \(\delta>0\) are given.
Each restricted solve has a finite resource budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is feasible, and its objective value never exceeds \(f(\bar x^0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone incumbent polishing by repeated budgeted restricted-subproblem solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(t=0\). For neighborhoods \(N_k(\bar x^t)\) in the prescribed order, solve \[\min\{f(x):x\in N_k(\bar x^t),\ f(x)\le f(\bar x^t)-\delta\}\] within its resource budget. When a feasible \(x^+\) is found, set \(\bar x^{t+1}=x^+\), increment \(t\), and restart or continue according to the declared schedule. Otherwise leave the incumbent unchanged. Stop when a full pass yields no accepted point or a global budget is exhausted, and output the current incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve restricted incumbent neighborhoods and accept only sufficiently improving feasible solutions until a pass stagnates or resources expire.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Solution Polishing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotone acceptance procedure is coherent and algorithm is the appropriate role, but no source supports this particular neighborhood schedule and improvement-cutoff formulation as incumbent solution polishing.

children.title: Restricted-Improvement Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Cases where fixed variables or weak block choices prevent further improvement.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in X\}\), with incumbent \(\bar x\in X\).

\(N_1(\bar x),
\ldots,N_q(\bar x)\subseteq X\) are the fully searched restricted neighborhoods.
Each restricted subproblem is solved to proven optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is locally optimal over \(\bigcup_{k=1}^qN_k(\bar x)\), but need not be globally optimal over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact local-optimality certificate; budget termination alone does not provide this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U(\bar x)=\bigcup_{k=1}^qN_k(\bar x)\). If every restricted solve proves \[\min_{x\in N_k(\bar x)}f(x)\ge f(\bar x)\qquad\text{for all }k\in\{1,
\ldots,q\},\] then \(f(x)\ge f(\bar x)\) for every \(x\in U(\bar x)\). Hence \(\bar x\) is locally optimal relative to the searched neighborhood union. This certificate says nothing about points in \(X\setminus U(\bar x)\); therefore restricted-improvement stagnation does not certify global optimality unless \(U(\bar x)=X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proven failure to improve in every restricted neighborhood certifies local optimality over their union, not global optimality over the full feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Improvement Stagnation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed implication is mathematically correct under exact optimal solves, but certificate does not fit the failure-oriented terminal title as well as failure_boundary. It also treats only proven exhaustive stagnation, whereas practical budget-induced stagnation is explicitly excluded. A source is needed to determine the intended scope before revising the kind or statement.

children.title: Sub-MIP Resource-State Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-solver budgets, copying, and information transfer.

children.title: Sub-MIP Resource Budgets
children.top_down_role: Time, node, memory, or iteration limits assigned to auxiliary searches.

assumptions_latex: A sub-MIP solver exposes nondecreasing counters for nodes, elapsed time, and accepted feasible solutions.
Finite nonnegative limits \(B_N\), \(B_T\), and \(B_S\) are declared before the run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sub-MIP remains admissible exactly while every monitored counter is within its corresponding budget.

notation.meaning: Consumed node, time, and solution resources.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise resource condition for a budgeted auxiliary MIP solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For resource state \(r=(r_N,r_T,r_S)\in\mathbb{R}_+^3\) and budget \(B=(B_N,B_T,B_S)\in\mathbb{R}_+^3\), define admissibility by \[r\preceq B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r_N\le B_N,\quad r_T\le B_T,\quad r_S\le B_S.\] The auxiliary solve may continue only while \(r\preceq B\). It must terminate or return control when any monitored counter first exceeds its limit, or earlier when another declared stopping condition holds. Any incumbent returned at termination must separately satisfy the original feasibility and acceptance tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sub-MIP may run only while each monitored resource counter remains within its declared node, time, and solution budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Sub-MIP Resource Budgets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is a suitable kind, but the proposed counter tuple and componentwise policy are implementation-dependent. The statement also allows continuation at equality yet specifies return only after a counter first exceeds its limit, creating an off-by-one ambiguity that must be resolved from authoritative solver semantics.

children.title: Auxiliary Solver State Copying
children.top_down_role: Transfer of model state into isolated or reusable subsolver instances.

assumptions_latex: The main solver state is a tuple \(S=(M,P,C,L,H,R)\).
A declared copy map \(\Pi\) identifies transferable model, parameter, cutoff, limit, hint, and random-state components.
Mutable search state not selected by \(\Pi\) is excluded from the auxiliary solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The auxiliary solver starts from \(S_{\mathrm{sub}}^0=\Pi(S)\) and subsequent auxiliary mutations do not alter \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract copy-by-projection model for initializing an isolated auxiliary solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the main state as \(S=(M,P,C,L,H,R)\), where the components denote the model, parameters, objective cutoff, resource limits, transferable hints, and random state. For a declared projection \(\Pi\), initialize the auxiliary solver by \[S_{\mathrm{sub}}^0=\Pi(S).\] The projection must preserve the restricted model's variable and constraint semantics and copy every parameter required for deterministic interpretation. Components outside the range of \(\Pi\), including active search-tree state unless explicitly transferable, are initialized independently. After initialization, updates to \(S_{\mathrm{sub}}\) do not mutate \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize an auxiliary solver by an explicit projection of transferable main-solver state, then keep subsequent auxiliary mutations isolated.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Solver State Copying

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the abstract state-copying formulation, but the tuple components, deterministic-copy requirements, and mutation-isolation guarantees are solver-architecture claims without an inspectable source. The cited inventory does not address this mechanism.

children.title: Sub-MIP Information Transfer
children.top_down_role: Movement of incumbents, bounds, cuts, or statistics between search contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Sub-MIP Information Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility rule for transferring results from a restricted sub-MIP to its parent solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the parent MIP have feasible set \(F\), and let a sub-MIP have feasible set \(F'\subseteq F\). A subsolver output may update the parent incumbent only when it supplies \(x'\in F'\) whose feasibility is verified in the parent model. A lower bound computed solely over \(F'\) is not a valid lower bound over \(F\). Cuts, domain reductions, or infeasibility conclusions may be transferred only when independently valid for every \(x\in F\); otherwise they remain local to the subsolver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sub-MIP solutions may become parent incumbents after validation, but local bounds, cuts, reductions, and infeasibility conclusions require global validity before transfer.
assumptions_latex: \(F'\subseteq F\).
Parent and subsolver objective values use the same objective convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x'\in F'\) is transferable as a feasible incumbent, whereas a sub-MIP inference is globally transferable only if it is valid on \(F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports the solver-dependent rules governing transfer of incumbents, bounds, cuts, reductions, or infeasibility conclusions.

children.title: Subsolver Isolation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on which main-search state may be shared with auxiliary solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsolver Isolation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-separation condition preventing local sub-MIP deductions from corrupting the parent search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_P\) and \(S_Q\) denote parent and subsolver states. Isolation holds when the subsolver reads only an explicitly copied state \(C(S_P)\), writes only to \(S_Q\), and modifies \(S_P\) solely through a validation map \(V\). For every proposed update \(u\), \(V(u,S_P)\) must either reject \(u\) or return a parent state preserving the parent model, global-validity invariants, and incumbent feasibility. Terminating or exhausting the subsolver must leave \(S_P\) unchanged except for updates already accepted by \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subsolver is isolated when it uses copied state and can affect the parent only through validated, invariant-preserving updates.
assumptions_latex: The parent state has specified model-validity and incumbent-feasibility invariants.
State copying and accepted-update interfaces are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_P^{+}=S_P\) for rejected or absent updates, and \(S_P^{+}=V(u,S_P)\) only for an accepted invariant-preserving update.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the isolation-boundary leaf, but the copying and validation-map contract is an abstract implementation specification without authoritative supporting documentation.

children.title: MIP Start Transfer Interface
children.top_down_role: User- or solver-supplied candidates and their adaptation to current solver state.

children.title: MIP Start Coverage-Multiplicity Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Starts distinguished by variable coverage and candidate multiplicity.

children.title: Complete MIP Starts
children.top_down_role: Imported candidates supplying assignments across the required model variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete MIP Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete assignment supplied for every original decision variable of a MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a MIP with variables indexed by \(N\), a complete MIP start is a vector \(s\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\) assigning one finite value \(s_i\) to every \(i\in N\). Completeness concerns coverage, not validity: \(s\) is an admissible incumbent only if it satisfies all variable bounds, integrality restrictions, and model constraints. Thus a complete start can be infeasible and may require repair or rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete MIP start assigns every model variable; it becomes an incumbent only after satisfying bounds, integrality, and constraints.
assumptions_latex: The MIP has a finite variable index set \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}(s)=N\); feasibility is a separate predicate \(s\in F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent and distinguishes coverage from feasibility, but the exact meaning of a complete MIP start is an interface convention requiring a specifically located solver or standard reference.

children.title: Partial MIP Starts
children.top_down_role: Imported candidates whose missing assignments require solver completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial MIP Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Start assignment covering a proper subset of the MIP variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variables indexed by \(N\), a partial MIP start is a pair \((S,s_S)\) with \(S\subsetneq N\) and \(s_S\in\mathbb{R}^{S}\). Its feasible completions are \(C(S,s_S)=\{x\in F:x_i=s_i\text{ for every }i\in S\}\). The start is completable precisely when \(C(S,s_S)\neq\varnothing\). Values of unassigned variables are determined by a completion procedure rather than implicitly fixed to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial start fixes only selected variables and is usable when those values admit at least one feasible completion.
assumptions_latex: The MIP feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((S,s_S)\) is completable if and only if \(C(S,s_S)\neq\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical formalization is consistent, but the claims about partial-start semantics and treatment of omitted coordinates require an inspectable solver-interface source.

children.title: Multiple MIP Starts
children.top_down_role: Collections of alternative candidates submitted for validation or completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple MIP Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite collection of independently submitted complete or partial start assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiple-start submission is a finite indexed family \(\mathcal{S}=\{(S_k,s^k_{S_k}):k=1,\ldots,K\}\), where \(K\geq2\), \(S_k\subseteq N\), and each member is interpreted independently as a complete start when \(S_k=N\) or a partial start otherwise. The family is successful if at least one member has a feasible completion. Multiplicity does not imply that submitted assignments are combined coordinatewise or that every member is processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple MIP starts form a finite family of independent candidates; success requires a feasible completion of at least one candidate.
assumptions_latex: All starts refer to the same model-variable index set \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{S}\) is potentially incumbent-producing exactly when \(\bigcup_{k=1}^{K}C(S_k,s^k_{S_k})\neq\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but independence, processing, and success semantics for multiple starts vary by solver and are unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Start Coverage Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Operational consequences of differing assignment coverage across submitted starts.

knowledge_statements.title: Start Coverage Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete binary example showing that greater start coverage need not improve usability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{2}:x_1+x_2=1\}\). The complete start \((0,0)\) has full coverage but is infeasible. The partial start fixing only \(x_1=0\) has the feasible completion \((0,1)\). Conversely, the feasible complete start \((0,1)\) directly supplies an incumbent, while the partial start still requires completion. Hence neither maximal coverage nor minimal coverage uniformly dominates: coverage can reduce completion work while also removing degrees of freedom needed to restore feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: More coverage can eliminate completion work but can also lock in infeasibility; a two-variable binary equality demonstrates both effects.
assumptions_latex: Starts are interpreted as exact assignments on their submitted coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coverage alone determines neither whether a start is feasible nor whether completion is required.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the example MIP.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: MIP Start Adaptation Pipeline
children.top_down_role: Acceptance and adaptation of imported candidates.

children.title: MIP Start Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks governing whether an imported candidate is acceptable to the current model.

knowledge_statements.title: MIP Start Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct validation of a complete candidate against the original MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a complete candidate \(s\), feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon_f\geq0\), and integrality tolerance \(\varepsilon_I\geq0\), first verify finite values and variable bounds. For every integer index \(i\), require \(\lvert s_i-\operatorname{round}(s_i)\rvert\leq\varepsilon_I\). Evaluate every original constraint using its prescribed feasibility residual and require residual at most \(\varepsilon_f\). Accept \(s\) as a start-derived incumbent only if all checks pass; otherwise reject it or send it to an explicitly enabled completion or repair stage.
