knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validation checks finiteness, bounds, integrality, and original constraints within declared tolerances before accepting a start as an incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The candidate assigns every original variable.
Constraint residuals and tolerances are specified consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\) is accepted only if all bound, integrality, and constraint residual tests pass.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but bound tolerances, residual definitions, integrality tests, and routing to repair or completion are solver-dependent and lack authoritative documentation.

children.title: Partial Start Completion
children.top_down_role: Solver processing used to fill assignments absent from a partial candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Start Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion by solving the original MIP with submitted coordinates fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a partial start \((S,s_S)\), form the completion subproblem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in F,\ x_i=s_i\text{ for all }i\in S\}\), or its feasibility version with zero objective. Solve it subject to a declared resource limit. If a feasible \(x\) is found, validate \(x\) in the original model and return it as a complete candidate. If infeasibility is proved, declare the start noncompletable; if the resource limit is reached, return an unresolved status rather than infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix submitted coordinates, solve for the missing values, validate any completion, and distinguish proven infeasibility from resource exhaustion.
assumptions_latex: The submitted values can be imposed as exact fixings.
The completion subproblem preserves the original constraints and integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned completion \(x\) satisfies \(x\in F\) and \(x_S=s_S\).

notation.meaning: Partial start and its assigned values.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-coordinate completion formulation is mathematically sound as one method, but no source establishes it as the intended MIP-start completion mechanism for this solver-oriented container.

children.title: Infeasible Start Repair
children.top_down_role: Adaptation of imported candidates that violate current model requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Start Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repair formulated as minimum weighted deviation from a submitted assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a start \((S,s_S)\), positive weights \(w_i\), and feasible set \(F\), solve \(\min\{\sum_{i\in S}w_i d_i:x\in F,\ d_i\geq x_i-s_i,\ d_i\geq s_i-x_i,\ d_i\geq0\}\). Under a resource limit, validate and return any feasible solution \(x\), preferably an optimal minimum-deviation solution. If the repair model is proved infeasible, report that no feasible repair exists under its retained constraints; resource exhaustion yields unresolved status. Coordinates declared immutable may instead be fixed exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair seeks a feasible solution minimizing weighted deviation from submitted values, while distinguishing infeasibility from an interrupted search.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i>0\) for every submitted coordinate.
The repair model retains the original feasibility and integrality requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any returned \(x\) lies in \(F\), and an optimal return minimizes \(\sum_{i\in S}w_i\lvert x_i-s_i\rvert\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted absolute-deviation model is a valid generic repair formulation, but the leaf concerns solver mechanisms and no source supports this particular repair objective or immutable-coordinate policy.

children.title: Start Rejection Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Reasons and signals reported when candidate adaptation does not succeed.

knowledge_statements.title: Start Rejection Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally checkable witnesses explaining why a submitted start was rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rejected complete start \(s\), a rejection diagnostic is a witness of at least one failed validation predicate: an index \(i\) with a nonfinite or out-of-bound value, an integer index \(i\) with \(\lvert s_i-\operatorname{round}(s_i)\rvert>\varepsilon_I\), or a constraint index \(j\) whose residual exceeds \(\varepsilon_f\). For a partial start, a valid terminal diagnostic may instead be a certificate that the fixed completion subproblem is infeasible. Resource exhaustion or unsupported mapping is a status explanation, not an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rejection certificate identifies a violated bound, integrality condition, constraint, or certified-infeasible completion problem; timeout alone proves none of these.
assumptions_latex: Validation predicates and tolerances are recorded.
Any claimed completion infeasibility has a solver-verifiable certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The witness is independently checkable and implies failure of the stated start-acceptance condition.

notation.meaning: Variable index witnessing a failed value test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is an appropriate content kind, and the witness distinctions are coherent, but actual rejection diagnostics and infeasibility certificates are solver-dependent and unsupported here.

children.title: Cross-Space Start Mapping
children.top_down_role: Translation of candidates between original and transformed spaces.

children.title: Original-Space Start Mapping
children.top_down_role: Translation of submitted assignments into the solver's active representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Start Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relational image of an original-variable start under presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{M}\) be the consistency relation between original variables \(x\) and presolved variables \(y\). For an original-space start \((S,s_S)\), its presolved-space image is \(Y(S,s_S)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{M}:\exists x\in\mathbb{R}^{N},\ (x,y)\in R,\ x_S=s_S\}\). Mapping succeeds when this set is nonempty and the interface can produce a member or a representable partial restriction on \(y\). Eliminated variables are handled through \(R\), not by assuming that original and presolved coordinates coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An original-space start maps to presolved assignments consistent with both the submitted values and the recorded presolve transformations.
assumptions_latex: Presolve records a consistency relation \(R\) between original and presolved variables.
Submitted variable identifiers refer unambiguously to original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(S,s_S)\) is exactly the set of presolved assignments consistent with the original-space start.

notation.meaning: Presolved image of the submitted start.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relational representation fits the mapping leaf, but the assumed consistency relation and production of representable presolved restrictions require an authoritative presolve or solver-interface source.

children.title: Presolved-Space Candidate Mapping
children.top_down_role: Candidate translation across eliminated, substituted, or aggregated model entities.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolved-Space Candidate Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifting a presolved candidate through the recorded presolve relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}^{M}\) encode valid original-to-presolved transformations. For a presolved candidate \(\hat y\), define its original-space fiber by \(X(\hat y)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{N}:(x,\hat y)\in R\}\). A candidate is liftable when \(X(\hat y)\neq\varnothing\). A mapping procedure selects \(\hat x\in X(\hat y)\), reconstructs eliminated variables in reverse presolve order, and validates \(\hat x\) against the original MIP before incumbent acceptance. Membership in the presolved feasible set alone does not replace original-space validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolved candidate maps back through recorded transformations; reconstructed original values must then pass original-model validation.
assumptions_latex: The presolve transformation history defines \(R\).
The candidate \(\hat y\) uses the active presolved-variable indexing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successfully mapped candidate satisfies \(\hat x\in X(\hat y)\), and incumbent acceptance additionally requires \(\hat x\in F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fiber representation is coherent, but reverse-order reconstruction and mandatory original-space validation are implementation-sensitive claims without an inspectable presolve source.

children.title: Postsolve Assignment Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-space assignments from transformed candidate solutions.

assumptions_latex: The original MIP has feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
Presolve records an ordered sequence of reversible reductions and any required auxiliary data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned assignment \(x\) is an original-space candidate; it is accepted only if \(x\in F\) under the solver's feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic reconstruction after presolve, including mandatory original-space validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a complete presolved assignment \(y\), initialize the current assignment with \(y\). Apply the recorded inverse reductions in reverse presolve order. For each eliminated variable, recover its value from its stored substitution, fixed value, or aggregation relation; restore removed rows and auxiliary variables when required. Denote the resulting original-space vector by \(x=R(y)\). Check original bounds, integrality restrictions, and constraints using the solver's stated tolerances. Return \(x\) as a reconstructed candidate if every check passes; otherwise report reconstruction failure rather than treating \(y\) as an original-space feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse every recorded presolve reduction, reconstruct eliminated variables, and validate the resulting assignment against all original bounds, integrality restrictions, and constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Assignment Reconstruction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content and content_kind fit the postsolve-reconstruction leaf, and the notation is internally consistent. However, no citation supports the claimed reconstruction sequence, treatment of reductions, or solver-tolerance validation semantics. An inspectable presolve/postsolve implementation or solver manual section is required.

children.title: Mapping Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where transformations prevent reliable transfer of candidate assignments.

assumptions_latex: A start or candidate is represented in one model space and must be transferred to another.
The transfer uses recorded variable correspondences and presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Outside the stated domain of \(T\), successful cross-space mapping is not guaranteed and the candidate must be rejected, repaired, or completed by another procedure.

notation.meaning: domain of assignments supported by the mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp operational boundary for transferring assignments between original and presolved model spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:D\to Y\) be the implemented cross-space assignment map. Mapping is undefined or unsuccessful when \(s\notin D\), including cases where a required variable correspondence is absent, an eliminated variable cannot be inferred consistently, a supplied value violates a fixed-value or aggregation equation beyond tolerance, or the transformation record is stale. Even when \(T(s)\) exists, the mapped assignment is not certified feasible until all target-space bounds, integrality conditions, and constraints are checked. Thus a syntactically complete source assignment need not yield a valid target-space candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mapping can fail through missing correspondences, inconsistent eliminated-variable values, stale transformations, or target-space infeasibility; successful translation alone does not certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Mapping Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the distinction between successful translation and feasibility certification is mathematically coherent. The listed mapping failures and tolerance behavior are implementation-dependent and have no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Related-Model Incumbent Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of solutions across related models and reoptimization runs.

children.title: Repeated-Run Incumbent Reuse
children.top_down_role: Transfer of feasible solutions between successive solves of a model lineage.

assumptions_latex: Two runs use the same variable identities and the same MIP formulation.
The earlier run produced an original-space incumbent \(x^{old}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted reuse candidate is a feasible incumbent for the new run, but its objective value must be recomputed under the new run's data.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the new run

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start reuse when repeated runs preserve the model's variable semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store the previous original-space incumbent \(x^{old}\) with stable variable identifiers. Before the next solve, map its components to the new model, discard values for removed variables, and leave newly introduced variables unspecified unless valid completion values are available. Submit the resulting partial or complete assignment as a MIP start. Accept it as an incumbent only after completion, if needed, and verification that \(x^{old}\in F^{new}\) under current tolerances. Recompute \(f^{new}(x^{old})\); never reuse the old objective value as the new incumbent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer the prior incumbent by stable variable identity, complete missing values, recheck new-run feasibility, and recompute its objective before accepting it.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Run Incumbent Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits repeated-run incumbent reuse and correctly separates start submission from incumbent acceptance. Source support is absent for partial-start handling, variable removal, completion, current-tolerance validation, and objective recomputation behavior.

children.title: Scenario-to-Scenario Solution Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of candidate assignments across related parameter or data scenarios.

assumptions_latex: Scenarios share a set of variables with stable semantics.
A source scenario provides a feasible assignment \(x^s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred vector is merely a target-scenario start until it is completed and verified to belong to \(F^t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent transfer between related scenario models with shared variable semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each shared variable \(j\in J\), assign the target start value \(x_j^t:=x_j^s\). Do not transfer source-only components, and leave target-only components unspecified or initialize them by a declared completion rule. Project transferred values onto neither changed bounds nor integrality domains silently; instead, reject or explicitly repair incompatible components. Submit the resulting assignment to the target model, complete any missing components, and test all target constraints. Accept it as a target incumbent exactly when the completed vector satisfies \(x^t\in F^t\) under the target solver's tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Copy values only for semantically shared variables, handle unmatched variables explicitly, and accept the target candidate only after completion and target-scenario feasibility checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-to-Scenario Solution Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches scenario-to-scenario transfer, and all principal symbols are introduced. The correspondence, repair, partial-start, completion, and target-tolerance policies are solver- or application-specific and unsupported by an inspectable citation.

children.title: Model-Change Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing whether an earlier incumbent remains meaningful after model changes.

assumptions_latex: An old model and a new model have identified common variables.
The stored assignment \(x^{old}\) is feasible for the old model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility permits submission as a start; it does not imply that the transferred assignment is feasible for the new model.

notation.meaning: new bound interval for variable j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic and domain compatibility required before a stored incumbent can become a new-model start.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stored assignment is transfer-compatible with the new model if there exists an identity-preserving map on the common variables \(J\) such that \(z_j=x_j^{old}\) is representable in the new variable domain for every supplied \(j\in J\): \(\ell_j^{new}\le z_j\le u_j^{new}\), and \(z_j\in\mathbb{Z}\) whenever the new variable is integral. Every new variable needed by the start interface must either receive a valid value or be permitted to remain unspecified. Changed constraints and objective coefficients do not destroy syntactic compatibility, but they require fresh feasibility and objective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stored solution is compatible when shared variables retain identity and valid domains, while required new variables can be supplied or left unspecified by the interface.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Change Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate for this leaf, and the statement clearly distinguishes transfer compatibility from new-model feasibility. No source establishes the proposed compatibility criterion or the claim about which new variables may remain unspecified under a start interface.

children.title: Stale Incumbent Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Invalidity or poor guidance caused by obsolete transferred solutions.

assumptions_latex: A stored incumbent was feasible for an earlier model with feasible set \(F^{old}\).
The current model has feasible set \(F^{new}\) or objective \(f^{new}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An old incumbent cannot serve as a current incumbent bound unless current-model validation and objective recomputation succeed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalidation mechanisms for incumbents retained across model or data changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The stored incumbent is stale whenever its variable identities no longer map consistently, a changed domain excludes a supplied value, or \(x^{old}\notin F^{new}\). It is also value-stale when feasibility remains valid but the objective changed, because the previous value need not equal \(f^{new}(x^{old})\). Deleted variables, newly required variables, tightened bounds, modified integrality types, and added or altered constraints can trigger these failures. Therefore neither old feasibility nor an old objective value may be used for current pruning without remapping, completion where necessary, current-model feasibility checking, and objective recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model changes can invalidate variable mappings, feasibility, or objective values, so an old incumbent cannot support pruning until fully revalidated and revalued.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Incumbent Failure Modes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the container, and the distinction among mapping staleness, feasibility staleness, and objective-value staleness is coherent. The operational consequences for pruning, completion, tolerances, and model changes require authoritative solver or algorithmic documentation.

children.title: Solution Pool Selection System
children.top_down_role: Storage and selection of feasible solutions beyond the active incumbent.

children.title: Quality-Ranked Solution Storage
children.top_down_role: Pool organization by objective quality and dominance.

assumptions_latex: The MIP is a minimization problem with objective \(f\).
Each admitted pool member is a distinct feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained pool contains at most \(K\) solutions and, among all admitted solutions, consists of those selected by the declared quality order and tie rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded pool maintenance ordered by objective quality for a minimization MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P:=\varnothing\). When a feasible solution \(x\) is admitted, discard it if it duplicates an existing member under the declared equality tolerance. Otherwise insert \(x\), order all members by nondecreasing \(f(x)\), and resolve equal objective values by a fixed deterministic tie rule. If \(|P|>K\), delete the last-ranked member. For a vector-valued quality measure, replace scalar ordering by the declared dominance relation and retain only nondominated solutions before applying the capacity and tie rules. Query rank \(r\) returns the \(r\)-th retained member only when \(1\le r\le |P|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Insert distinct feasible solutions, rank them by objective quality or declared dominance, apply deterministic ties, and evict the worst member when capacity is exceeded.
knowledge_statements.title: Quality-Ranked Solution Storage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits quality-ranked storage, but the record combines scalar objective ranking with a vector-valued nondominance policy whose retention and capacity semantics are materially different. Because neither policy is cited, source inspection is needed to determine whether both belong to the intended pool system and to validate duplicate and tie behavior.

children.title: Diversity-Aware Solution Storage
children.top_down_role: Pool organization preserving structurally distinct solutions.

assumptions_latex: Every admitted member is feasible and represented on a common set of comparison variables.
A nonnegative dissimilarity function \(d\) and pool capacity \(K\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted insertion preserves the declared separation threshold, and the pool size never exceeds \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pool maintenance that enforces structural separation under a fixed capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P:=\varnothing\). For each feasible candidate \(x\), compute \(d(x,y)\) for all \(y\in P\). Reject \(x\) when \(d(x,y)<\delta\) for some retained member, unless a declared replacement rule prefers \(x\) to every conflicting member. Otherwise insert \(x\). If insertion makes \(|P|>K\), remove a member minimizing a declared diversity contribution, with objective quality and a deterministic tie rule used secondarily. For binary variables, one admissible choice is normalized Hamming distance \(d(x,y)=|J|^{-1}\sum_{j\in J}|x_j-y_j|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admit solutions only when sufficiently separated under a chosen metric, then enforce capacity by removing the least diversity-contributing member under a declared tie rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Diversity-Aware Solution Storage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches diversity-aware storage, and the normalized Hamming example is well-formed when the declared comparison set J is nonempty. The metric, conflict-replacement rule, diversity contribution, and eviction policy are design choices without cited support, so the exact intended algorithm cannot be verified.

children.title: Solution-Pool Consumption Interface
children.top_down_role: Use of stored solutions by heuristics and applications requesting alternatives.

children.title: Heuristic Pool Reuse
children.top_down_role: Use of stored feasible solutions as inputs to subsequent primal heuristics.

assumptions_latex: The pool contains feasible solutions for the current model.
A primal heuristic accepts one or more seed assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A heuristic output may become an incumbent only after current-model feasibility verification; pool membership alone does not validate a modified candidate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Using retained feasible solutions as seeds for subsequent primal heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a seed \(x^s\in P\) by a declared rule based on quality, diversity, recency, or search context. Initialize the heuristic state from \(x^s\), construct a neighborhood or fixing pattern around it, and run \(H(x^s)\) subject to its resource limit. For every candidate \(z\) returned by \(H\), restore any fixed or omitted components and check all current bounds, integrality restrictions, and constraints. Insert each verified feasible \(z\) into the incumbent mechanism and, when permitted, back into \(P\) under the pool's duplicate, ranking, and capacity policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a stored solution as a heuristic seed, search or perturb around it, and validate every resulting candidate before incumbent or pool insertion.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Pool Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is locally appropriate for heuristic pool reuse and correctly requires validation of modified candidates. The seed-selection interface, neighborhood construction, resource handling, and reinsertion behavior are solver-specific and unsupported by any source reference.

children.title: Alternative-Solution Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Application access to multiple feasible solutions beyond the active incumbent.

assumptions_latex: The MIP has a finite set of feasible integer assignments of interest.
A deterministic total order \(\prec\) or an objective-ranking rule is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each returned solution is distinct and feasible; exhaustive completion is certified only when the residual model is proved infeasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite enumeration by repeated solution and exclusion of prior integer assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(E:=\varnothing\). At iteration \(k\), solve the MIP with constraints excluding every integer assignment represented in \(E\), using the declared order or objective rule to select \(x^k\). If a feasible solution is found, output it, set \(E:=E\cup\{x^k\}\), and add a valid exclusion constraint that forbids the same assignment on \(I\) without excluding any distinct assignment. Stop upon reaching a user limit, a resource limit, or proven infeasibility of the residual model. Only the last condition certifies that all eligible solutions have been enumerated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve, return a distinct feasible solution, exclude its integer assignment, and continue; only residual infeasibility certifies complete enumeration.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternative-Solution Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits alternative-solution enumeration, and the statement appropriately reserves exhaustive certification for residual infeasibility. A source is required to specify a valid exclusion construction, the exact notion of distinctness, and whether solutions differing only in continuous components are eligible as distinct alternatives.

children.title: Pool Query Semantics
children.top_down_role: Selection, ordering, filtering, or retrieval behavior exposed to pool consumers.

assumptions_latex: A pool snapshot contains \(m\) retained solutions.
The snapshot has a declared ordering, equality tolerance, and indexing convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pool query is well-defined only relative to one snapshot and its declared order; an invalid rank returns no solution.

notation.meaning: objective value of the r-th member

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal meaning of ranked retrieval from a fixed solution-pool snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pool snapshot is an ordered tuple \(P=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(m)})\) of distinct retained feasible solutions, ordered by the pool's declared ranking and tie rules. The count query returns \(m\). A rank query with \(r\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) returns the assignment \(x^{(r)}\) and its recomputed metadata, including \(v_r=f(x^{(r)})\); for any other \(r\), it returns an out-of-range result. Queries refer to the same immutable snapshot. If solving or pool mutation occurs, a new snapshot and possibly new ranks are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pool query addresses a fixed ordered snapshot: count returns its size, valid ranks return the corresponding solution, and invalid ranks return no solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Pool Query Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits pool query semantics, and the fixed-snapshot formulation is internally consistent. Snapshot immutability, one-based indexing, metadata recomputation, equality tolerance, and out-of-range behavior are interface-specific claims with no cited manual or API locator.

children.title: Pool Exhaustion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on completeness, distinctness, or availability of enumerated alternatives.

assumptions_latex: Enumeration or pool filling is performed under declared eligibility, distinctness, and tolerance rules.
The solver may terminate either by proof or by an external limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pool exhaustion is certified exactly by proof that \(S\setminus E=\varnothing\), not by failure to find another solution within finite resources.

notation.meaning: solutions already enumerated or retained as relevant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between proved absence of further solutions and resource-limited non-discovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pool is exhaustively complete only when the solver proves that no eligible distinct solution remains, equivalently \(S\setminus E=\varnothing\). Reaching capacity, a solution count limit, a time or node limit, numerical failure, interruption, or heuristic non-discovery does not establish this equality. Moreover, a bounded pool may be full while many eligible solutions remain outside it, and an empty pool may reflect failure to find a solution rather than infeasibility. Consequently, query exhaustion means only that the current snapshot has no further stored member unless accompanied by a separate residual-infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No further stored member is not proof that no further feasible solution exists; exhaustive completion requires a residual-infeasibility proof under the declared eligibility rules.
knowledge_statements.title: Pool Exhaustion Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind is correct, and the distinction between snapshot exhaustion and proved exhaustive enumeration is mathematically sound. An authoritative source is still required for the solver-status distinctions, eligibility rules, and residual-infeasibility certificate semantics asserted here.

children.title: Heuristic Portfolio Control Regimes
children.top_down_role: Allocation of heuristic effort and conditions under which primal search becomes ineffective.

children.title: Heuristic Invocation Control System
children.top_down_role: Placement and resource limits of heuristic calls.

children.title: Heuristic Call Timing
children.top_down_role: Search phases or solver events at which primal heuristics are invoked.

assumptions_latex: A branch-and-bound MIP solver processes nodes at event times \(t\in\mathcal T\).
Each primal heuristic \(h\in\mathcal H\) has an eligibility predicate \(E_h(s_t)\) depending on solver state \(s_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h\) is called exactly at the eligible events selected by \(T_h\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: event-triggered scheduling is the standard operational abstraction for heuristic call timing
needs_source: supplied locators do not specifically document primal-heuristic timing policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-triggered timing within a branch-and-bound run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the current state \(s_t\), compute eligibility \(E_h(s_t)\in\{0,1\}\). The timing policy \(T_h\) selects a call when \(E_h(s_t)=1\) and a prescribed trigger occurs, such as root completion, incumbent improvement, bound improvement, restart, or elapsed-work threshold. Initialize trigger histories as empty, update them after every event, invoke \(h\) on selection, and record its cost and outcome before processing the next event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A timing policy calls an eligible heuristic when designated solver events occur and updates its trigger history after every call.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Call Timing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits call timing, but no cited source supports the proposed triggers or update protocol, and the selection rule T_h is not formally defined.

children.title: Heuristic Invocation Frequency
children.top_down_role: Policies controlling repetition rates for heuristic calls.

assumptions_latex: Solver progress is indexed by processed-node count \(k\in\mathbb N_0\).
A heuristic call is permitted only when its eligibility predicate is true.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The schedule enforces at most one periodic call in every \(q_h\) processed-node opportunities, subject to eligibility.

notation.meaning: last processed-node count at which h was called

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: node-period schedules are a standard formalization of heuristic invocation frequency
needs_source: supplied locators do not specify invocation-frequency controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic node-period control, excluding adaptive frequency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an integer period \(q_h\ge 1\) and initialize \(\ell_h=-q_h\). At processed-node count \(k\), call heuristic \(h\) if it is eligible and \(k-\ell_h\ge q_h\); after a call set \(\ell_h\leftarrow k\). If the test fails, continue branch-and-bound without calling \(h\). Terminate this schedule when the solver terminates, and return the incumbents generated by its calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-period schedule invokes an eligible heuristic only after at least a prescribed number of processed nodes since its previous call.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Invocation Frequency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The node-period algorithm fits invocation frequency, but it lacks supporting evidence and the phrase “every q_h processed-node opportunities” should be defined precisely relative to the processed-node index.

children.title: Search-Depth Placement
children.top_down_role: Node-depth regimes governing where heuristic effort is applied.

assumptions_latex: Each search node \(v\) has depth \(d(v)\in\mathbb N_0\).
Heuristic \(h\) is otherwise eligible at \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The depth placement predicate is \(D_h(v)=1\) exactly for the selected depth set \(S_h\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: depth predicates are the direct mathematical representation of search-depth placement
needs_source: supplied locators do not document depth-dependent primal-heuristic placement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth eligibility independent of timing and budget tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a prescribed set \(S_h\subseteq\mathbb N_0\), define \(D_h(v)=\mathbf 1\{d(v)\in S_h\}\). Root-only placement uses \(S_h=\{0\}\); a depth interval uses \(S_h=\{d_{min},\ldots,d_{max}\}\); periodic placement uses \(S_h=\{d:d\bmod q=r\}\). A call at node \(v\) passes the depth-placement condition if and only if \(D_h(v)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search-depth placement permits a heuristic only at a specified set of branch-and-bound depths, such as the root, an interval, or periodic levels.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Depth Placement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits search-depth placement, but no source is cited and d_min, d_max, q, and r are not introduced with their domains and required bounds.

children.title: Heuristic Resource Budgets
children.top_down_role: Limits on time, nodes, iterations, or memory consumed by heuristic work.

assumptions_latex: Every call of heuristic \(h\) consumes a nonnegative measurable amount of work.
The solver maintains cumulative heuristic work over the run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A proposed call is admissible only when its predicted consumption fits both remaining call and global budgets.

notation.meaning: cumulative work already consumed by h

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive work accounting gives a checkable heuristic-budget condition
needs_source: supplied locators do not specifically support primal-heuristic resource accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic per-call and run-wide work limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix finite budgets \(0\le b_h\le B_h\). If a proposed call has predicted work \(\widehat w_h\ge0\), it is budget-admissible precisely when \(\widehat w_h\le b_h\) and \(W_h+\widehat w_h\le B_h\). During execution, stop the call when its realized work reaches \(b_h\) or the remaining global allowance \(B_h-W_h\), then increase \(W_h\) by the realized work. No later call is admissible once \(W_h=B_h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic call must fit its per-call allowance and the heuristic's remaining run-wide work budget; execution stops at either limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Resource Budgets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits heuristic resource budgets, but the predicted-work admission rule and realized-work stopping protocol have no supporting citation.

children.title: Adaptive Success-Based Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Effort allocation informed by observed cost and solution yield.

assumptions_latex: Each heuristic call has observed cost \(c_{h,t}>0\) and nonnegative solution yield \(y_{h,t}\).
Scheduling epochs are indexed by \(t\in\mathbb N_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At each epoch the policy allocates the next call to an eligible heuristic maximizing its estimated yield per unit cost, while preserving exploration.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cost-normalized empirical reward with exploration is a standard adaptive allocation rule
needs_source: no supplied locator supports this particular adaptive heuristic-scheduling formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online allocation by empirical solution yield per work unit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(Y_{h,0}\ge0\), \(C_{h,0}>0\), and call counts \(n_{h,0}=0\). At epoch \(t\), choose an eligible, budget-admissible heuristic maximizing \(Y_{h,t}/C_{h,t}+u_{h,t}\), where \(u_{h,t}>0\) favors insufficiently sampled heuristics. After observing \((y_{h,t},c_{h,t})\), update \(Y_{h,t+1}=(1-\alpha)Y_{h,t}+\alpha y_{h,t}\) and \(C_{h,t+1}=(1-\alpha)C_{h,t}+\alpha c_{h,t}\), with \(0<\alpha\le1\). Stop when the solver or heuristic budget terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scheduler estimates each heuristic's solution yield per unit cost, favors the best eligible estimate, and retains an exploration bonus for under-sampled heuristics.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Success-Based Scheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches adaptive success-based scheduling, but no source supports this formulation. Merely requiring u_{h,t}>0 does not guarantee persistent exploration, and updates for heuristics not selected at epoch t are unspecified.

children.title: Weak-Guidance Feasibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Model regimes that frustrate construction and projection heuristics.

children.title: Sparse Feasible Regions
children.top_down_role: Model regimes where feasible assignments occupy a very limited search region.

assumptions_latex: A bounded mixed-integer search region is \(X=P\cap(\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p})\), with bounded polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
A finite reference measure \(\mu\) is fixed on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible region is \(\varepsilon\)-sparse exactly when its feasible neighborhood occupies at most an \(\varepsilon\) fraction of \(P\).

notation.meaning: radius-d neighborhood of X within P

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: neighborhood-volume ratio makes informal feasible-set sparsity mathematically checkable
needs_source: sparse feasible regions have no single canonical quantitative definition and supplied locators do not resolve the intended version
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quantitative neighborhood-volume notion for bounded MIP regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta\ge0\), let \(N_\delta(X)=\{z\in P:\operatorname{dist}(z,X)\le\delta\}\). Given \(0le\varepsilon\le1\), call \(X\) \((\delta,\varepsilon)\)-sparse in \(P\) when \(\mu(P)>0\) and \(\mu(N_\delta(X))/\mu(P)\le\varepsilon\). The case \(\delta=0\) measures the feasible set itself; positive \(\delta\) measures the proportion from which a repair of radius at most \(\delta\) can reach feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded MIP feasible region is sparse when even a prescribed neighborhood around it occupies only a small fraction of the relaxation region.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Feasible Regions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed neighborhood-volume definition is noncanonical and unsupported, so the intended meaning of sparse feasible regions remains uncertain. The statement also contains “0le\varepsilon” instead of “0\le\varepsilon”.

children.title: Weak Relaxation Guidance
children.top_down_role: Relaxations whose solutions provide poor direction for primal construction.

assumptions_latex: At search node \(v\), the continuous relaxation has solution \(x_v^{LP}\).
A primal heuristic maps \(x_v^{LP}\) and node data to a candidate or failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation guidance is weak at \(v\) when the heuristic's conditional success or quality is no better than the stated reference level.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: predictive success relative to a baseline operationalizes weak heuristic guidance
needs_source: the intended empirical or deterministic notion of weak guidance is not fixed by supplied sources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational weakness relative to a declared baseline policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_v\) contain only information derived from \(x_v^{LP}\), and let \(S_v\) denote production of an accepted feasible solution within a fixed work budget. For a declared baseline probability \(p_0\), relaxation guidance is weak on node class \(\mathcal V\) when \(\mathbb P(S_v\mid G_v)\le p_0\) for almost every \(v\in\mathcal V\). An objective-quality version replaces \(S_v\) by a declared bounded reward and compares its conditional expectation with the baseline expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation guidance is weak when relaxation-derived information does not improve a heuristic's success probability or declared solution-quality reward beyond a baseline.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Relaxation Guidance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is an unsupported operationalization rather than an established definition. No probability law over nodes is introduced, making the conditional-probability and almost-everywhere assertions ill-defined, and the baseline comparison is underspecified.

children.title: Misleading Fractional Structure
children.top_down_role: Fractional patterns that direct projection or rounding toward unproductive candidates.

assumptions_latex: Binary variables satisfy \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
A rounding heuristic maps each relaxation component below \(1/2\) to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Componentwise proximity of the relaxation point to zero does not imply that rounding preserves feasibility.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed binary covering family directly demonstrates misleading componentwise fractional structure
needs_source: no supplied locator specifically supports this counterexample's heuristic interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary covering family defeating componentwise nearest-integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(m\ge3\), consider \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^m x_i\ge1\) and objective \(\min\sum_{i=1}^m x_i\). The continuous relaxation has the optimal point \(x^{LP}=(1/m,\ldots,1/m)\). Every component is closer to zero than to one, so componentwise nearest-integer rounding returns \(\widehat x=0\), which violates \(\sum_i x_i\ge1\). Nevertheless, each binary optimum has exactly one component equal to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a binary covering model, a symmetric optimal relaxation point rounds entirely to zero and becomes infeasible, although every integer optimum selects one variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Misleading Fractional Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically coherent and fits misleading fractional structure, but no cited source supports its placement or heuristic interpretation.

children.title: Repair-Dominated Search
children.top_down_role: Search behavior where most heuristic effort is consumed by candidate repair.

assumptions_latex: A candidate generator produces \(z\) in an ambient set \(P\).
A repair operator \(R\) attempts to map \(z\) into the feasible set \(X\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Search is repair-dominated when expected repair work exceeds expected generation work by the prescribed factor.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a cost-ratio predicate formalizes the operational phrase repair-dominated search
needs_source: repair-dominated search lacks a canonical threshold and supplied locators do not specify one
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-based definition for generate-and-repair primal heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a candidate distribution \(Q\) and factor \(\kappa>1\). A generate-and-repair heuristic is \(\kappa\)-repair-dominated on \(Q\) if \(0<\mathbb E_Q[C_G(z)]<\infty\) and \(\mathbb E_Q[C_R(z)]\ge\kappa\mathbb E_Q[C_G(z)]\), where \(C_R(z)\) includes all feasibility-restoration work whether repair succeeds or fails. If calls are truncated, both costs are measured under the same stopping rule and budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate-and-repair search is repair-dominated when expected feasibility-restoration work exceeds expected candidate-generation work by a declared factor under the same budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Repair-Dominated Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cost-ratio definition fits the title operationally, but the threshold and cost model are noncanonical and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Heuristic Search-Interference Failures
children.top_down_role: Repeated candidates, ineffective neighborhoods, and excessive competition with dual search.

children.title: Repeated-Candidate Cycling
children.top_down_role: Recurring generation of identical or equivalent candidate solutions.

assumptions_latex: A deterministic heuristic has finite internal state space \(\Sigma\).
Its update map is \(F:\Sigma\to\Sigma\), and state \(s\) emits candidate \(g(s)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Revisiting a state without external diversification forces a periodic state and candidate sequence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: repetition under a deterministic finite-state map is an elementary finite-state dynamical property
needs_source: no supplied locator connects this property specifically to MIP heuristic cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-state cycling without diversification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_{k+1}=F(s_k)\). If \(s_i=s_j\) for some \(0\le i<j\), then \(s_{i+r}=s_{j+r}\) and \(g(s_{i+r})=g(s_{j+r})\) for every \(r\ge0\). Thus the trajectory is periodic from iteration \(i\), with period dividing \(j-i\). Candidate cycling can be broken only by changing the state, update map, accepted-history information, or random input used by the heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic finite-state heuristic cycles forever after revisiting a state unless diversification changes its state, update rule, history, or random input.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Candidate Cycling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-state periodicity statement is mathematically sound and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no source connects it to MIP heuristic cycling. The claim that cycling can be broken “only” by the listed changes requires a more precise model boundary.

children.title: Neighborhood Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Persistent failure of restricted neighborhoods to improve the incumbent.

assumptions_latex: An incumbent \(x^k\in X\) is searched over a neighborhood \(N(x^k)\subseteq X\).
The next incumbent must have strictly smaller objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the current neighborhood contains no strict improvement and the neighborhood rule is unchanged, repeated local searches cannot improve the incumbent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: absence of a strict improvement in an unchanged neighborhood is the standard local-search stagnation boundary
needs_source: no supplied locator specifically documents MIP neighborhood stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-neighborhood local search with strict-improvement acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization objective \(f\), define the improving set \(I(x)=\{y\in N(x):f(y)<f(x)\}\). If \(I(x^k)=\varnothing\), then no exact search of \(N(x^k)\) can produce an accepted successor. Repeating the same neighborhood with unchanged incumbent and data leaves \(I(x^k)\) empty, so the sequence remains \(x^{k+r}=x^k\) for all \(r\ge1\). Escaping requires enlarging or changing the neighborhood, accepting a nonimproving move, or altering solver information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a fixed neighborhood contains no strict improvement, repeatedly searching it cannot change the incumbent; escape requires diversification or relaxed acceptance.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Stagnation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-neighborhood stagnation boundary is mathematically coherent and fits the terminal container, but it has no cited support specific to MIP neighborhood search.

children.title: Dual-Search Interference
children.top_down_role: Competition between primal heuristic effort and progress in bounding or tree search.

assumptions_latex: A solver has total work budget \(B>0\).
Primal-heuristic work consumes \(H\in[0,B]\), leaving \(B-H\) for dual-bound search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Heuristic work interferes with dual search whenever its primal benefit does not offset the lost dual progress under the solver's declared merit function.

notation.meaning: dual-bound progress from w units of dual-search work
primal benefit from h units of heuristic work
relative weight assigned to primal benefit

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: opportunity-cost comparison formalizes competition between primal heuristics and dual-bound search
needs_source: supplied dual-search locators do not establish this solver-level interference criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-budget opportunity cost between primal and dual progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(w)\) and \(P(h)\) be nondecreasing progress measures with \(D(0)=P(0)=0\), and score an allocation by \(M(h)=D(B-h)+\lambda P(h)\) for \(\lambda\ge0\). Relative to pure dual search, heuristic allocation \(H>0\) causes dual-search interference when \(M(H)<M(0)\), equivalently \(D(B)-D(B-H)>\lambda P(H)\). The boundary is equality; beyond it, the heuristic's weighted primal gain fails to compensate for displaced dual work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fixed work budget, heuristic effort interferes with dual search when its weighted primal gain is smaller than the dual progress sacrificed.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Search Interference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits dual-search interference, but the scalar merit function, weighting parameter, and resulting interference criterion are an unsupported modeling choice rather than a sourced solver principle.

children.title: Heuristic Portfolio Contention
children.top_down_role: Overlapping heuristic calls competing for shared solver resources.

assumptions_latex: A finite family of primal heuristics \(H_1,\ldots,H_m\) shares a time budget \(T>0\), solver state \(S\), and candidate-processing capacity \(C>0\).
Each invocation of \(H_i\) consumes time \(t_i\) and submits \(q_i\) candidates, of which \(u_i\) are distinct and admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Contention occurs whenever the selected invocation set \(I\) satisfies \(\sum_{i\in I}t_i>T\) or \(\sum_{i\in I}q_i>C\), or whenever shared-state interference makes \(\sum_{i\in I}u_i<\sum_{i\in I}u_i^{\mathrm{iso}}\), where \(u_i^{\mathrm{iso}}\) is the distinct admissible yield of \(H_i\) in isolation.

notation.meaning: Isolated distinct admissible yield of heuristic \(H_i\).

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this formal contention criterion.
Operational quantities depend on solver instrumentation and require a dedicated source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure criterion for simultaneous or interleaved primal heuristics under shared solver resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a portfolio \(H_1,\ldots,H_m\), let an invocation of \(H_i\) consume \(t_i\) time units, submit \(q_i\) candidates, and yield \(u_i\) distinct admissible candidates. Given a time budget \(T\), processing capacity \(C\), isolated yields \(u_i^{\mathrm{iso}}\), and a selected invocation set \(I\), heuristic portfolio contention occurs if
\[
\sum_{i\in I}t_i>T,\qquad \sum_{i\in I}q_i>C,\qquad\text{or}\qquad \sum_{i\in I}u_i<\sum_{i\in I}u_i^{\mathrm{iso}}.
\]
The first two conditions express resource oversubscription; the third expresses destructive interference through duplicated candidates or adverse shared-state changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic portfolio contends when its selected invocations exceed shared time or candidate-processing capacity, or interference reduces their combined distinct admissible yield below isolated performance.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Portfolio Contention

children.title: Solver Assurance Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms for learning from local infeasibility, explaining submitted-model failures, controlling numerical risk, and validating final outcomes.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Computational Aspects of Infeasibility Analysis in Mixed Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Computational Aspects of Infeasibility Analysis in Mixed Integer Programming

children.title: Local Conflict Analysis
children.top_down_role: Extraction, representation, and reuse of explanations for infeasible or cutoff local states.

children.title: Propagation-Graph Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Conflict learning reconstructed from domain-inference reasons.

assumptions_latex: Domain propagation derives bound literals from antecedent bound literals, and every derivation stores a valid reason implication.
A conflict literal \(\bot\) is reached because the current bounds make some constraint infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resolving the conflict backward through recorded reasons yields a bound clause \(\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\) valid for every feasible solution of the original MIP.

notation.meaning: Directed implication graph of bound inferences.
Antecedent set recorded as the reason for literal \(v\).

review_flags: No supplied locator directly documents propagation-graph conflict analysis.
A solver-conflict-analysis reference is required to certify the resolution and stopping conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reason-graph reconstruction for conflicts caused solely by bound propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Construct a directed graph \(G\) whose vertices are asserted or inferred bound literals. For every inferred literal \(v\) with recorded reason \(R(v)\), add arcs from each \(u\in R(v)\) to \(v\). Add a conflict vertex \(\bot\) with its recorded infeasibility reason. Initialize the frontier with the predecessors of \(\bot\). Repeatedly replace a chosen inferred frontier literal \(v\) by the literals in \(R(v)\), removing duplicates, until the prescribed stopping frontier \(C\) is reached. Output the learned bound clause
\[
\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell.
\]
The required terminal condition is \(\bigwedge_{\ell\in C}\ell\Rightarrow\bot\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace an infeasible propagation backward through recorded valid reasons, resolve away inferred bounds until a prescribed frontier is reached, and negate that frontier to obtain a learned bound clause.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Graph Conflicts

children.title: Relaxation-Proof Conflict Family
children.top_down_role: Conflict learning from infeasible linear relaxations and dual proof information.

children.title: LP-Infeasibility Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Learned conflict information derived from infeasible node relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation is \(Ax\le b\), \(L\le x\le U\), and is infeasible.
Nonnegative Farkas multipliers exist for the row, upper-bound, and negated lower-bound inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The supported local bounds form an LP-infeasibility conflict, and a reduced support remains valid only if its retained multipliers satisfy both the zero aggregate left-hand-side condition and the strict negative right-hand-side condition.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative Farkas multipliers for rows, upper bounds, and negated lower bounds.

review_flags: The cited section supports LP-based branch-and-bound generally; its support for conflict extraction remains provisional.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for infeasibility of a node LP with local bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the node LP as \(Ax\le b\), \(x\le U\), and \(-x\le-L\). Its infeasibility is certified by nonnegative multipliers \(y,p,q\) satisfying
\[
y^{\top}A+p^{\top}-q^{\top}=0,\qquad y^{\top}b+p^{\top}U-q^{\top}L<0.
\]
The local bound rows corresponding to positive components of \(p\) or \(q\), together with the supported global rows, form an LP-infeasibility conflict. A reduced set of local bound rows is also valid when there exist nonnegative multipliers supported on the retained rows that satisfy both displayed certificate conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas certificate identifies local bounds whose conjunction with supported global rows makes the node LP infeasible; removing bounds is valid only when a certificate satisfying both Farkas conditions remains.
knowledge_statements.title: LP-Infeasibility Conflicts

children.title: Dual-Proof Conflict Extraction
children.top_down_role: Conflict information obtained from dual evidence associated with relaxation infeasibility.

assumptions_latex: The infeasible node LP is expressed as \(Mx\le d\).
An LP solver returns a nonzero ray \(\lambda\ge0\) with \(\lambda^{\top}M=0\) and \(\lambda^{\top}d<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The positive support of \(\lambda\) indexes an infeasible subsystem, and when its nonglobal rows are local bounds, negating their conjunction gives a valid conflict disjunction relative to the supported global rows.
review_flags: The cited section is provisional for dual-ray conflict extraction and does not clearly document support minimization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction of a conflict explanation from an LP dual infeasibility ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an infeasible node LP \(Mx\le d\), obtain a nonzero dual ray \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(\lambda^{\top}M=0\) and \(\lambda^{\top}d<0\). Set \(S=\{j:\lambda_j>0\}\). An optional deletion step may remove \(j\in S\) only when another nonnegative ray supported on \(S\setminus\{j\}\) satisfies both certificate conditions. Output the subsystem indexed by the final set \(S\). If every supported nonglobal row is a local-bound row, also output the disjunction that negates the conjunction of those local bounds, relative to the supported global rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extract the positive support of a dual infeasibility ray, optionally remove a row only when another valid ray remains, and negate the retained local bounds to obtain a conflict relative to the supported global constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Proof Conflict Extraction

children.title: Relaxation Conflict Localization
children.top_down_role: Scope of LP-derived conflicts within local or global search contexts.

assumptions_latex: A Farkas certificate for one node relaxation has positive support \(S\).
Every supported local-bound row was introduced at a node on the current root-to-node path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conflict is valid beginning at the deepest introduction node among all retained local bounds; changing the certificate support can move that validity point to an earlier ancestor.

notation.meaning: Positive support of a Farkas certificate.
Deepest introduction depth among retained local bounds.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports tree-local relaxation-conflict localization.
The localization and certificate-support modification policy require a conflict-analysis source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-tree localization of an LP-derived conflict by certificate support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\) be the local-bound rows retained in a Farkas certificate for a node relaxation. Assume each row \(j\in B\) was introduced at depth \(d_j\) on the current root-to-node path, and define
\[
d(B)=\max_{j\in B}d_j.
\]
The resulting relaxation conflict is valid at the ancestor of depth \(d(B)\) and its descendants, where every retained local bound is active. Localization seeks another valid certificate with a smaller value of \(d(B)\), for example by deleting or replacing supported local-bound rows while retaining nonnegative multipliers, a zero aggregate left-hand side, and a strictly negative aggregate right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For bounds introduced along the current search path, an LP-derived conflict becomes valid at the deepest node that introduced any retained bound; changing certificate support can move that validity point upward.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Conflict Localization

children.title: Objective-Exclusion Conflict Family
children.top_down_role: Conflict learning from objective-based exclusion of local subproblems.

children.title: Cutoff-Bound Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Conflicts arising when a local subproblem cannot beat the active cutoff.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization MIP with feasible set \(X\), objective \(c^{\top}x\), incumbent value \(\bar z\), and improvement margin \(\epsilon\ge0\).
The node relaxation includes the cutoff inequality \(c^{\top}x\le\bar z-\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid infeasibility certificate involving the cutoff proves that the retained node bounds exclude every feasible solution satisfying that cutoff; it does not by itself prove ordinary infeasibility without the cutoff.

notation.meaning: Objective vector and incumbent objective value.

review_flags: The branch-and-bound locator supports incumbent cutoffs generally; explicit objective-conflict semantics remain provisional.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-exclusion certificate for a minimization node pruned by the incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be the original feasible set, let \(B(x)\) denote a conjunction of retained node bounds, and let \(\epsilon\ge0\) specify the required improvement margin. If a valid infeasibility certificate establishes
\[
X\cap\{x:B(x)\}\cap\{x:c^{\top}x\le\bar z-\epsilon\}=\varnothing,
\]
then \(B\) is a cutoff-bound conflict at incumbent value \(\bar z\). Equivalently,
\[
x\in X\ \text{and}\ B(x)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c^{\top}x>\bar z-\epsilon.
\]
The negation of \(B\) may therefore be used for the search subject to that cutoff, but the certificate does not imply \(X\cap\{x:B(x)\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cutoff conflict proves that certain node bounds admit no feasible solution meeting the incumbent-improvement cutoff, not necessarily that those bounds admit no feasible solution at all.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutoff-Bound Conflicts

children.title: Objective-Domain Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Learned exclusions based on objective restrictions within a search region.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(X\), and the minimization objective is \(c^{\top}x\).
A conjunction \(B(x)\) of variable-bound literals has a certified objective lower bound \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(B(x)\Rightarrow c^{\top}x\ge\beta\), restricted to \(x\in X\), is an objective-domain conflict and excludes \(B\) whenever the active improving-solution cutoff requires \(c^{\top}x<\beta\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports objective-domain conflict objects.
A source is needed for the intended solver representation and update semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional objective lower bound represented as a domain-based learned conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization problem with feasible set \(X\), an objective-domain conflict is a valid implication
\[
x\in X\ \text{and}\ B(x)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c^{\top}x\ge\beta,
\]
where \(B(x)\) is a conjunction of variable-bound literals and \(\beta\) is a certified lower bound. It may equivalently be stored, relative to \(X\), as
\[
\neg B(x)\quad\vee\quad c^{\top}x\ge\beta.
\]
Under an active improving-solution cutoff requiring \(c^{\top}x<\beta\), the objective literal is false and the object reduces to the bound exclusion \(\neg B(x)\). Retaining the objective literal makes the implication independent of the current incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain-conditioned objective lower bound can be stored as a disjunction between leaving the domain and satisfying that lower bound; an incompatible cutoff reduces it to a bound exclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Domain Conflicts

children.title: Incumbent-Dependent Conflict Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity limits for conflicts tied to a changing incumbent cutoff.

assumptions_latex: A minimization conflict was derived using cutoff \(c^{\top}x\le\bar z-\epsilon\), where \(\epsilon\ge0\).
The conflict asserts that domain condition \(B(x)\) admits no feasible solution satisfying that cutoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bound-only exclusion remains usable when the current cutoff is no weaker than the derivation cutoff; the objective-conditional implication remains valid independently of subsequent incumbent changes.

notation.meaning: Domain conjunction in the learned object.

review_flags: The cited branch-and-bound section is provisional for incumbent monotonicity and does not clearly document learned-conflict lifecycle rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for minimization conflicts learned from an incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose derivation at incumbent \(\bar z\) establishes
\[
x\in X\ \text{and}\ B(x)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c^{\top}x>\bar z-\epsilon.
\]
If the current incumbent is \(\bar z'\), then the bound-only exclusion \(\neg B(x)\) is valid for the improving-solution search whenever
\[
\bar z'-\epsilon\le\bar z-\epsilon,
\]
so the current cutoff is no weaker than the derivation cutoff. If the cutoff is relaxed, the bound-only exclusion must be disabled or separately revalidated. The conditional implication retaining its objective conclusion remains valid independently of later incumbent changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-only objective conflict survives cutoff tightening but not cutoff relaxation; retaining its objective conclusion makes the learned implication incumbent-independent.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Dependent Conflict Validity

children.title: Cut-Based Conflict Analysis
children.top_down_role: Learned infeasibility information represented through valid inequalities.

assumptions_latex: The relevant feasible set is \(X\), and a local bound conjunction \(B(x)\) satisfies \(X\cap\{x:B(x)\}=\varnothing\).
An inequality is available that is valid for \(X\) and violated by every point satisfying \(B(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Such an inequality \(\pi^{\top}x\le\pi_0\) is a cut-based representation of the conflict and may be used wherever all assumptions establishing its validity hold.

notation.meaning: Relevant feasible set for which the learned inequality is valid.
Coefficients and right-hand side of the learned inequality.

review_flags: The locator supports branch-and-cut systems broadly; explicit conflict-cut construction remains to be checked.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Learned infeasibility information encoded as a valid linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be the relevant feasible set and let \(B(x)\) be a conjunction of local bounds with
\[
X\cap\{x:B(x)\}=\varnothing.
\]
A cut-based conflict representation is an inequality
\[
\pi^{\top}x\le\pi_0
\]
that is valid for every \(x\in X\) and satisfies \(\pi^{\top}x>\pi_0\) for every \(x\) satisfying \(B(x)\). It may be installed wherever all assumptions used to establish its validity hold. It can strengthen an LP relaxation at points beyond those satisfying the entire conflicting conjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut-based conflict is an inequality valid for the relevant feasible set that excludes the entire conflicting local-bound region and may strengthen additional points in the LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Based Conflict Analysis

children.title: Learned Conflict Object Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Solver objects and retention policies used to exploit learned infeasibility information.

children.title: Conflict Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Constraint and disjunctive representations of excluded bound combinations.

children.title: Conflict Constraint Representations
children.top_down_role: Constraint-form storage of learned exclusions from infeasible bound combinations.

assumptions_latex: The conflicting literals are binary assignments \(x_i=1\) for \(i\in P\) and \(x_i=0\) for \(i\in N\), where \(P\cap N=\varnothing\).
Every variable appearing in the conflict satisfies \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conflict clause is represented exactly on the binary domain by \(\sum_{i\in P}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i\in N}x_i\ge1\).

notation.meaning: Indices fixed to one in the forbidden assignment.
Indices fixed to zero in the forbidden assignment.

review_flags: The disjunctive-representation locator is provisional for this standard no-good inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear no-good representation of a forbidden partial binary assignment.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Parsimonious MIP Representation of Disjunctive Sets p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) and \(N\) be disjoint index sets defining the forbidden partial binary assignment \(x_i=1\) for \(i\in P\) and \(x_i=0\) for \(i\in N\). Its conflict clause is
\[
\bigvee_{i\in P}(x_i=0)\quad\vee\quad\bigvee_{i\in N}(x_i=1).
\]
For variables satisfying \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), this clause has the exact conflict-constraint representation
\[
\sum_{i\in P}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i\in N}x_i\ge1.
\]
The inequality holds exactly when at least one assignment in the forbidden conjunction is reversed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forbidden partial binary assignment becomes an exact no-good inequality requiring at least one of its assigned binary values to be reversed.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Constraint Representations

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Parsimonious MIP Representation of Disjunctive Sets p. 59

children.title: Bound Disjunction Representations
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive storage of alternatives that exclude an infeasible assignment pattern.

assumptions_latex: Each literal is a variable-bound statement of the form \(x_i\le a_i\) or \(x_i\ge b_i\).
The conjunction of the complementary bounds has empty intersection with the relevant feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disjunction of the stated bound literals is a valid learned object excluding the simultaneous complementary-bound assignment.
review_flags: The disjunctive-programming locator supports disjunctive sets generally; solver-specific bound-disjunction storage remains to be checked.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical representation of a learned conflict over general variable bounds.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Parsimonious MIP Representation of Disjunctive Sets p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite bound disjunction is a learned constraint
\[
D(x)=\bigvee_{i\in P}(x_i\le a_i)\quad\vee\quad\bigvee_{i\in N}(x_i\ge b_i).
\]
It excludes the complementary bound conjunction
\[
\bigwedge_{i\in P}(x_i>a_i)\quad\wedge\quad\bigwedge_{i\in N}(x_i<b_i).
\]
If that conjunction has empty intersection with the relevant feasible set, then \(D(x)\) is valid on that set. For integral \(x_i\), a strict complementary bound may be normalized using the variable's next admissible integer value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite bound disjunction requires at least one stated upper or lower bound to hold, thereby excluding an infeasible conjunction of all complementary bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Disjunction Representations

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Parsimonious MIP Representation of Disjunctive Sets p. 59

children.title: Representation Conversion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on translating learned information between constraint and disjunctive forms.

assumptions_latex: The learned object is a finite disjunction of variable-bound literals with feasible set \(S=\bigcup_{k=1}^m S_k\).
An exact conversion must preserve \(S\) in the original variable space and under the stated variable domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Binary assignment disjunctions admit an exact no-good inequality on the binary domain, whereas a nonconvex continuous bound disjunction cannot be represented exactly by one linear inequality in the original variables unless its union is itself a halfspace.

notation.meaning: Union of sets defined by the bound literals.
Convex hull of the disjunctive set.

review_flags: The cited section is provisional for exact and extended MIP representations of disjunctive sets.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact clause inequalities and general disjunctive MIP formulations.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Parsimonious MIP Representation of Disjunctive Sets p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S=\bigcup_{k=1}^m S_k,
\]
where each \(S_k\) is defined by a variable-bound literal. If the literals encode a forbidden partial assignment of binary variables, the corresponding disjunction converts exactly on the binary domain to
\[
\sum_{i\in P}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i\in N}x_i\ge1.
\]
For continuous variables, when \(S\) is nonconvex, no single linear inequality in the original variables can represent \(S\) exactly because the feasible set of one linear inequality is a halfspace. Exact conversion then requires an appropriate disjunctive or mixed-integer extended formulation. Linear inequalities valid for \(S\) instead describe outer approximations of \(S\), including descriptions or relaxations of \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary assignment clauses admit an exact no-good inequality on the binary domain; a nonconvex continuous bound disjunction cannot equal one halfspace and generally requires an extended disjunctive or mixed-integer formulation, while linear cuts provide outer approximations.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Conversion Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Parsimonious MIP Representation of Disjunctive Sets p. 59

children.title: Conflict Graph Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Graph representations connecting assignments, deductions, and contradictions.

children.title: Conflict Graph Representations
children.top_down_role: Graph structures recording mutually incompatible assignments or bound states.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Graph Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undirected incompatibility representation for bound literals at a fixed MIP search context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a finite set of bound literals and let \(F_s\) be the feasible set of search context \(s\). The conflict graph is the undirected graph \(G_s=(L,E_s)\) satisfying \[\{\ell_i,\ell_j\}\in E_s\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F_s\cap S(\ell_i)\cap S(\ell_j)=\varnothing,\] where \(S(\ell)\) is the set satisfying literal \(\ell\). Thus every edge certifies pairwise incompatibility in context \(s\). A clique \(C\subseteq L\) yields the valid set-packing relation \(\sum_{\ell\in C}z_\ell\le 1\) whenever each indicator \(z_\ell\) records satisfaction of \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vertices are bound literals; edges certify pairwise incompatibility. Cliques consequently induce valid at-most-one relations within the graph's search context.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is finite.
Every literal \(\ell\in L\) has a well-defined satisfaction set \(S(\ell)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\ell_i,\ell_j\}\in E_s\) exactly when the two literals cannot jointly hold in \(F_s\).

notation.meaning: feasible set in search context s

review_flags: solver-specific meaning of conflict graph requires an authoritative conflict-analysis source
pairwise graph semantics may omit higher-order conflicts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and clique consequence are mathematically coherent, but no citation supports this exact MIP conflict-graph convention or its context-specific semantics.
