children.title: Implication Graph Representations
children.top_down_role: Graph structures recording deductions and their causal predecessors.

knowledge_statements.title: Implication Graph Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed reason graph for propagation and conflict analysis in a MIP search context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a propagation episode, let \(L\) contain the asserted and inferred bound literals. Its implication graph is a directed acyclic graph \(D=(L\cup\{\bot\},A)\). If an inferred literal \(v\) has recorded reason \(R(v)\subseteq L\), include \((u,v)\in A\) for every \(u\in R(v)\). If a violated constraint has falsifying literals \(R(\bot)\), include \((u,\bot)\in A\) for every \(u\in R(\bot)\). A reverse cut separating decision literals from \(\bot\) identifies antecedent literals whose conjunction implies contradiction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed arcs connect each propagated bound to its recorded antecedents; a contradiction sink permits graph-cut extraction of a learned conflict.
assumptions_latex: Every propagated literal has a sound recorded reason.
Vertices are ordered by propagation time, with arcs directed forward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every directed path ending at \(\bot\) records a reason chain contributing to the contradiction.

notation.meaning: recorded antecedent set for vertex v

review_flags: requires a source fixing the MIP implication-graph convention
hypergraph reasons are flattened into ordinary arcs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the stated MIP implication-graph convention. Flattening multi-literal reasons into ordinary arcs also requires an authoritative account showing that the proposed cut interpretation remains sound.

children.title: Contradiction Extraction Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections between implication histories and learned conflict objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Contradiction Extraction Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract interface converting recorded propagation reasons into a verifiable learned conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite reason structure \(D\), a contradiction vertex \(\bot\), and a validity context \(s\). Initialize the frontier with the immediate antecedents of \(\bot\). Repeatedly replace a nondecision frontier literal by the antecedents in its recorded sound reason, optionally stopping according to a prescribed cut rule. Output a set \(C\) and context \(s_C\) only if the checker verifies \[F_{s_C}\cap\bigcap_{\ell\in C}S(\ell)=\varnothing.\] Otherwise output failure. The learned conflict is the clause \(\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\), retained with the verified context label.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface traces sound reasons backward from contradiction and emits a learned clause only after checking its contextual validity.
assumptions_latex: Recorded reasons are available to the extractor.
The checker can test or certify infeasibility under a context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful output \((C,s_C)\) certifies \(F_{s_C}\cap\bigcap_{\ell\in C}S(\ell)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: validity context attached to the conflict

review_flags: abstract solver interface needs authoritative specification
cut and verification mechanisms vary among MIP solvers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the extraction-interface leaf, but its reason-expansion, cut, contextual verification, and retention semantics are unsupported by any inspectable citation.

children.title: Conflict Refinement Calculus
children.top_down_role: Validity scope and reduction of learned conflict objects.

children.title: Conflict Locality
children.top_down_role: Search regions within which a learned conflict remains valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Locality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity scope of conflicts learned under global and node-local MIP assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the global feasible set and let search node \(s\) impose local domain restrictions \(B_s\), so \(F_s=F\cap B_s\). A conflict \(C\) learned from literals is local to \(s\) when \[F_s\cap\bigcap_{\ell\in C}S(\ell)=\varnothing\] but global validity has not been established. It may be used only at nodes \(t\) satisfying \(F_t\subseteq F_s\). If instead \(F\cap\bigcap_{\ell\in C}S(\ell)=\varnothing\), the conflict is globally valid and may be used throughout the search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally derived conflict is reusable only where its derivation context remains valid; a globally valid conflict is reusable everywhere.
assumptions_latex: Node feasible regions are obtained by adding domain restrictions to the global model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local validity propagates from \(s\) to every descendant context \(t\) with \(F_t\subseteq F_s\).
review_flags: requires a MIP conflict-analysis source distinguishing local and global validity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-inclusion argument is coherent, but an authoritative MIP source is needed for the distinction between local and global conflicts and the exact permitted reuse rule.

children.title: Conflict Strength
children.top_down_role: Comparative pruning value or restrictiveness of learned conflict objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic dominance order for learned conflicts over a fixed literal universe and context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a context feasible set \(F_s\). For conflicts \(C_1\) and \(C_2\), define their surviving regions by \[Q_s(C_i)=F_s\setminus\bigcap_{\ell\in C_i}S(\ell).\] Conflict \(C_1\) is at least as strong as \(C_2\) in context \(s\) when \(Q_s(C_1)\subseteq Q_s(C_2)\); it is strictly stronger when the inclusion is strict. For clausal conflicts over the same literal convention, the sufficient syntactic condition \(C_1\subseteq C_2\) implies that the clause from \(C_1\) dominates the clause from \(C_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One conflict is stronger when enforcing it leaves no more admissible points than enforcing another; literal-set inclusion gives a common sufficient test.
assumptions_latex: Both conflicts use the same context and literal semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_1\) dominates \(C_2\) exactly when \(Q_s(C_1)\subseteq Q_s(C_2)\).

notation.meaning: region surviving enforcement of conflict C

review_flags: conflict strength has multiple solver-specific metrics
semantic formulation needs a supporting source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed semantic order is unreliable without a source. Moreover, if C is already a valid conflict for F_s, then F_s intersects the simultaneous satisfaction set trivially, so Q_s(C)=F_s for every such conflict and the claimed strength order becomes degenerate. A source-backed definition over an appropriate assignment or relaxation domain is required.

children.title: Conflict Minimization
children.top_down_role: Reduction of unnecessary literals, bounds, or premises from learned conflicts.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-based minimization of a context-valid set of conflict literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite conflict \(C\), context \(s\), and a sound predicate \(P_s(U)\) that returns true only when \(F_s\cap\bigcap_{\ell\in U}S(\ell)=\varnothing\). Initialize \(M\leftarrow C\). Visit literals \(\ell\in M\) in a prescribed order; if \(P_s(M\setminus\{\ell\})\) is true, set \(M\leftarrow M\setminus\{\ell\}\). Output \(M\). After a complete pass, \(M\) remains a valid conflict and is deletion-minimal relative to the tested predicate: \(P_s(M)\) holds while \(P_s(M\setminus\{\ell\})\) fails for every \(\ell\in M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test each literal for removal, retaining the deletion whenever the remaining literals still certify contradiction; the output is deletion-minimal.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and satisfies \(P_s(C)\).
The predicate \(P_s\) is sound and monotone under adding literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(M\subseteq C\) is valid and deletion-minimal for \(P_s\).

notation.meaning: conflict-validity test for literal set U in context s

review_flags: standard deletion procedure lacks a supplied conflict-analysis source
solver implementations may use recursive reason minimization instead

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deletion procedure is coherent under the stated monotonicity assumption and fits the algorithm leaf, but no source supports it as a MIP conflict-minimization mechanism or fixes the intended validity predicate.

children.title: Minimization Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between smaller conflicts and the effort required to derive them.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimization Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-cost bound and stopping tradeoff for deletion-based conflict minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an initial conflict contain \(m\) literals, and let one validity-oracle call cost at most \(T\). A single deletion pass makes at most \(m\) oracle calls, uses \(O(m)\) additional literal storage, and costs \(O(mT)\) beyond conflict construction. Stopping after \(k<m\) tested deletions costs \(O(kT)\) and preserves validity, but does not certify deletion-minimality for untested literals. Hence a budgeted minimizer may exchange oracle work for a potentially larger, semantically weaker learned conflict without compromising soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deletion pass costs at most one validity test per literal; early stopping saves work and preserves validity but forfeits minimality.
assumptions_latex: The validity oracle is sound.
Removing a literal is committed only after a successful oracle test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full minimization costs \(O(mT)\); a budget of \(k\) tests costs \(O(kT)\) but may leave redundant literals.

notation.meaning: upper bound on one validity-oracle call

review_flags: bound applies to the stated oracle model only
no supplied source supports the solver-level tradeoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asymptotic count follows from the stated oracle model, but no citation supports that model, the storage claim, or its interpretation as a solver-level minimization tradeoff.

children.title: Conflict Database Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Management of learned information over long searches.

children.title: Conflict Aging Policies
children.top_down_role: Activity or relevance tracking for learned conflict objects over time.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Aging Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activity-based aging rule for managing a finite learned-conflict database.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each learned conflict \(c\), maintain nonnegative activity \(a_c\). Initialize \(a_c\leftarrow a_0\) at insertion. Whenever \(c\) participates in propagation or contradiction analysis, update \(a_c\leftarrow a_c+b\), where \(b>0\). At each aging event, update every stored score by \(a_c\leftarrow\rho a_c\), where \(0<\rho<1\). A database-reduction routine may rank removable conflicts by increasing \(a_c\), with protected conflicts excluded. The policy outputs scores and rankings only; deletion requires a separate soundness-preserving lifecycle rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict activity rises when used and decays geometrically at aging events, allowing database reduction to prioritize stale, low-activity objects.
assumptions_latex: The stored conflict set is finite at every aging event.
Protected conflicts are identified independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After \(r\) unused aging events, an unbumped score equals \(\rho^r a_c\).
review_flags: aging formulas and event schedules are solver-specific

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The activity-and-decay policy is internally coherent and appropriately classified as an algorithm, but its scoring formula and aging events are solver-specific and uncited.

children.title: Conflict Deletion Policies
children.top_down_role: Retention limits governing removal of learned conflict information.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Deletion Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted database reduction that preserves locked, protected, and currently necessary conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a learned-conflict database \(D\), target capacity \(B\), removable predicate \(R(c)\), and priority score \(q(c)\). Form \(U=\{c\in D:R(c)\}\), order \(U\) from least to most valuable by \(q\), and delete elements in that order until \(|D|\le B\) or \(U\) is exhausted. The predicate must exclude locked conflicts serving as active propagation reasons, conflicts required by the current certificate state, and objects protected by policy. Deletion removes only redundant learned objects and does not alter the original MIP constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Database reduction deletes lowest-priority removable conflicts until meeting a capacity target, while preserving locked or otherwise protected objects.
assumptions_latex: Learned conflicts are redundant consequences of constraints valid in their recorded contexts.
The removability predicate protects every currently required object.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned database has size at most \(B\) unless fewer than \(|D|-B\) conflicts are removable.
review_flags: protection and deletion criteria vary among solvers
requires a source for MIP conflict-database lifecycle semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The budgeted reduction algorithm is coherent, but no authoritative citation supports the removability, locking, certificate-protection, or contextual-redundancy rules asserted for a MIP solver.

children.title: Restart Conflict Retention
children.top_down_role: Persistence of learned conflict objects across search restarts.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Conflict Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity criterion for carrying learned conflicts across a search restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a restart replace search state \(s\) by \(s'\) without changing the global model. A learned conflict \(c\), with validity region \(V(c)\), may be retained after restart exactly when the new feasible context satisfies \(F_{s'}\subseteq V(c)\). In particular, every globally valid conflict has \(V(c)=F\) and survives any restart of the unchanged model. A node-local conflict may survive only if its recorded local assumptions remain implied by the restarted context; otherwise it must be deactivated or discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarts may retain globally valid conflicts; local conflicts remain usable only when the restarted context still implies their validity assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The restart does not modify the global model.
Every retained conflict carries a checkable validity scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retention is sound when \(F_{s'}\subseteq V(c)\).

notation.meaning: feasible set in the restarted context

review_flags: restart and locality conventions require an authoritative solver source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The retention criterion is plausible, but the meaning of a conflict's validity region and the restart-locality convention require a direct authoritative source before the exact statement can be trusted.

children.title: Conflict Database Saturation
children.top_down_role: Runtime or memory degradation caused by excessive retained conflict information.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Database Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource failure boundary when learned-conflict production persistently exceeds database reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_t\) be the number of stored conflicts after epoch \(t\), with \(g_t\) insertions and \(d_t\) deletions. Then \[N_{t+1}=N_t+g_t-d_t.\] If there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(t_0\) such that \(g_t-d_t\ge\varepsilon\) for every \(t\ge t_0\), then \(N_t\ge N_{t_0}+\varepsilon(t-t_0)\), so an unbounded database saturates any fixed memory budget. With a hard capacity, saturation instead forces deletion, insertion rejection, or replacement; without such control, lookup and propagation workloads may also grow with \(N_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If conflict insertions persistently exceed deletions, database size grows at least linearly and eventually exceeds every fixed memory budget.
assumptions_latex: Conflict counts are measured at consistent lifecycle epochs.
No unmodeled bulk compaction changes the recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A persistent positive net insertion rate makes \(N_t\) unbounded and violates every fixed capacity eventually.

notation.meaning: stored conflict count after epoch t

review_flags: counting argument is standard but solver performance consequences need sourcing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counting recurrence and linear-growth conclusion are correct under the stated assumptions and fit a failure-boundary leaf, but the solver saturation and workload consequences lack supporting evidence.

children.title: Global Status Diagnostic System
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic objects intended to explain infeasibility, unboundedness, or ambiguous status of the submitted model.

children.title: Irreducible Infeasible Subsystems
children.top_down_role: Minimality-oriented subsystem explanations.

children.title: Continuous-Relaxation IIS Family
children.top_down_role: Subsystem diagnostics for continuous relaxations.

children.title: Linear IIS Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Irreducible subsystem diagnostics for linear continuous constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear IIS Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite linear-system certificate identifying an irreducible infeasible subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite linear system indexed by \(I\), with constraints \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\). A subset \(J\subseteq I\) is an irreducible infeasible subsystem when \[\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\text{ for every }i\in J\}=\varnothing\] and, for every \(j\in J\), the subsystem indexed by \(J\setminus\{j\}\) is feasible. A diagnostic certificate consists of \(J\), an infeasibility certificate for its subsystem, and a feasible witness for every single-constraint deletion. These objects jointly verify infeasibility and irreducibility; they do not assert that \(J\) has minimum cardinality among infeasible subsystems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An IIS is infeasible but becomes feasible after deleting any one member; certificates verify both infeasibility and every required deletion test.
assumptions_latex: The linear system has finitely many constraints.
Feasibility is interpreted over \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The supplied witnesses certify that \(J\) is inclusion-minimal infeasible, not necessarily minimum-cardinality infeasible.

notation.meaning: index set of all linear constraints
index set of the reported subsystem

review_flags: supplied locator hints do not identify an IIS definition or diagnostic theorem
needs a direct authoritative source for linear IIS certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The IIS definition and distinction from minimum cardinality are standard, but no direct IIS citation is supplied, and the form of the linear infeasibility certificate is not specified sufficiently to establish a checkable diagnostic certificate.

children.title: Conic IIS Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Irreducible subsystem diagnostics for supported conic constraint systems.

assumptions_latex: The continuous conic system consists of finitely many indexed constraints, including affine equations, bounds, and cone memberships \(F_i(x)\in K_i\).
Each \(K_i\) is a specified closed convex cone, and feasibility is interpreted in the solver's declared numerical tolerance regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned index set \(J\) certifies infeasibility of the selected conic subsystem and irreducibility under deletion of any single selected constraint.

notation.meaning: Finite index set of model constraints
Indices selected for the diagnostic subsystem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional continuous conic subsystems; integrality restrictions are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conic irreducible infeasible subsystem is an index set \(J\subseteq I\) such that \[\{x:F_i(x)\in K_i\text{ for every }i\in J\}=\varnothing,\] while, for every \(j\in J\), \[\{x:F_i(x)\in K_i\text{ for every }i\in J\setminus\{j\}\}\ne\varnothing.\] Affine equations and variable bounds may be represented as cone memberships and included among the indexed constraints. Thus the diagnostic certifies inclusion-minimal infeasibility relative to the chosen constraint granularity, not minimum cardinality and not infeasibility of integer restrictions omitted from the continuous system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic IIS is an infeasible collection of conic constraints that becomes feasible whenever any one selected constraint is removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic IIS Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and inclusion-minimal definition fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports conic IIS availability, constraint granularity, or tolerance semantics.

children.title: Conic Diagnostic Support Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limitations arising from cone types, transformations, or solver capabilities.

assumptions_latex: The diagnostic is computed from a finite-dimensional conic formulation and a specified solver configuration.
Presolve transformations, cone support, and numerical tolerances may differ across solver implementations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reported conic diagnostic is valid only for the supported formulation, transformations, and tolerance semantics; outside them, absence of a diagnostic does not imply feasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between mathematical conic IIS notions and solver-supported diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conic IIS interpretation requires that the solver preserve a traceable correspondence between the original system \(S\) and the analyzed system \(\widehat S\). If unsupported cones are reformulated, nonlinear cone expressions are approximated, presolve aggregation is not invertible, or feasibility is decided only to tolerance, an IIS of \(\widehat S\) need not be an irreducible subsystem of the original named constraints. Moreover, failure to return an IIS may mean unsupported diagnostic machinery or unresolved numerical status rather than \(S\ne\varnothing\). Consequently, conic diagnostic support must state the accepted cone classes, presolve mapping guarantees, atomic constraint granularity, and tolerance convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic IIS results apply only where the solver supports the cones, preserves constraint mappings, and resolves feasibility reliably; unavailable diagnostics do not establish feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Diagnostic Support Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the claims about supported cones, reformulation, presolve mapping, and diagnostic failure require solver-specific authoritative sources.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Conflict Refiners
children.top_down_role: Subsystem diagnostics incorporating integrality and semantic constraints.

assumptions_latex: A mixed-integer model has finitely many constraints, variable bounds, integrality declarations, and optional semantic constraints.
The refiner tests infeasibility under a fixed numerical and logical interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any returned conflict \(C\) certifies that its selected restrictions cannot hold simultaneously; deletion-minimality is an additional property, not automatic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflicts may contain algebraic constraints, bounds, integrality restrictions, and supported semantic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) contain every eligible model restriction, including integrality declarations. A mixed-integer conflict is a subset \(C\subseteq\mathcal R\) satisfying \[\{x:x\text{ satisfies every restriction in }C\}=\varnothing.\] It is deletion-minimal if every \(r\in C\) satisfies \[\{x:x\text{ satisfies every restriction in }C\setminus\{r\}\}\ne\varnothing.\] A conflict refiner returns an infeasible \(C\), possibly guided by user priorities; unless deletion-minimality is explicitly guaranteed, the returned conflict may contain redundant restrictions. Because integrality belongs to \(\mathcal R\), such a conflict can explain infeasibility absent from the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-integer conflict is an infeasible subset of constraints, bounds, domains, and supported semantic restrictions; it need not be irreducible unless explicitly minimized.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Conflict Refiners

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role is plausible, but eligibility and deletion semantics for integrality declarations and semantic constraints vary by refiner and require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Relaxation-Based Explanation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Explanations organized around controlled model relaxation and violation patterns.

children.title: Feasibility-Relaxation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic outputs based on controlled relaxation of model requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Relaxation Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive relaxation of inequality constraints; equalities and bounds require corresponding two-sided slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given weights \(w_i>0\), introduce one slack \(s_i\ge 0\) for each relaxable constraint and solve \[\min_{x\in X,\,s\ge 0}\ \sum_{i\in I}w_i\phi_i(s_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)\le s_i\quad(i\in I).\] Return an optimizer \((x^*,s^*)\). If every \(\phi_i\) is strictly increasing on \(\mathbb R_+\) and satisfies \(\phi_i(0)=0\), then \(s_i^*=\max\{0,g_i(x^*)\}\), so positive components identify constraints relaxed at the returned repair. An optimal value of zero establishes feasibility of \(x^*\) for the original inequalities; a positive value quantifies only the selected relaxation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility relaxation minimizes a strictly increasing, positively weighted penalty on added slacks and returns a minimum-penalty repair whose positive slacks identify the constraints relaxed at that repair.
assumptions_latex: The original model has finitely many constraints \(g_i(x)\le 0\) indexed by \(I\) and a nonempty domain \(X\).
Each weight satisfies \(w_i>0\), and each penalty \(\phi_i:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R_+\) is strictly increasing with \(\phi_i(0)=0\).
The relaxed optimization problem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimizer \((x^*,s^*)\) is a minimum-penalty repair and satisfies \(s_i^*=\max\{0,g_i(x^*)\}\) for every \(i\in I\).

notation.meaning: Finite index set of relaxable constraints
Nonnegative relaxation assigned to constraint i

children.title: Constraint-Violation Profiles
children.top_down_role: Organization of infeasibility evidence by the location or magnitude of violations.

assumptions_latex: A candidate point \(x\) is evaluated against normalized inequalities \(g_i(x)\le 0\).
Any scaling used to compare constraints is fixed and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The profile \(v(x)\) records componentwise violation, while its support identifies the violated constraints at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise violations for normalized scalar inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_i(x)\le 0\) indexed by \(I\), the scaled constraint-violation profile is \[v(x)=\bigl(v_i(x)\bigr)_{i\in I},\qquad v_i(x)=\frac{\max\{0,g_i(x)\}}{\sigma_i},\quad \sigma_i>0.\] Its violated-constraint support is \[\operatorname{supp}v(x)=\{i\in I:v_i(x)>0\}.\] The unscaled convention is recovered by \(\sigma_i=1\). A profile is point-dependent and scaling-dependent: it describes violations at \(x\), but by itself neither proves global infeasibility nor identifies an irreducible infeasible subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violation profile lists each constraint's positive residual, optionally scaled; it describes one point and is not an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Violation Profiles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and fits the leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for the diagnostic-profile convention.

children.title: Weighted Relaxation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic behavior under differing penalties for relaxed model components.

assumptions_latex: Relaxable constraints have slacks \(s_i\ge 0\) and penalties \(w_i\ge 0\).
The relaxed feasible region is nonempty and the selected objective attains its optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Different weights and norms define different diagnostic priorities and can yield different optimal repairs even for the same infeasible model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted cardinality, sum, and maximum relaxation objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Three standard weighted regimes for a slack vector \(s\ge 0\) are \[R_0(s)=\sum_i w_i\mathbf 1_{\{s_i>0\}},\qquad R_1(s)=\sum_i w_i s_i,\qquad R_\infty(s)=\max_i w_i s_i.\] Minimizing \(R_0\) favors few relaxed constraints, minimizing \(R_1\) favors small total weighted violation, and minimizing \(R_\infty\) controls the largest weighted violation. A weight \(w_i=0\) makes violation of constraint \(i\) unpenalized; a nonrelaxable constraint must instead retain zero slack. These regimes are generally nonequivalent and need not select the same repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted zero-, one-, and infinity-type penalties prioritize respectively few violations, small total violation, or small worst violation, and may produce different repairs.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Relaxation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits and the three objectives are coherent, but their naming and diagnostic interpretation require an authoritative feasibility-relaxation source.

children.title: Relaxation Explanation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Cases where low-cost relaxations do not yield a useful model explanation.

assumptions_latex: A diagnostic minimizes a slack penalty over a chosen family of relaxable constraints.
The original model is infeasible, but the relaxed problem has an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal relaxation vector need not certify an IIS, a unique explanation, or the cause of infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of interpreting minimum-penalty repairs as causal infeasibility explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s^*\) minimize a selected feasibility-relaxation objective and let \(J=\{i:s_i^*>0\}\). The set \(J\) depends on penalty weights, scaling, norm, tie-breaking, and which constraints are relaxable. Even when \(s^*\) is optimal, \(J\) need not be an infeasible subsystem of the original model: removing or relaxing the constraints in \(J\) repairs feasibility, but the constraints indexed by \(J\) alone may be mutually feasible. Multiple optimal slack vectors may also have different supports. Hence minimum relaxation is a repair certificate under a chosen metric, not generally an irreducible or unique causal explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-cost repair depends on weights and scaling; its positive slacks need not form an IIS or a unique causal explanation.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Explanation Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and distinction between repair support and IIS support are mathematically plausible, but no source is supplied for these nontrivial diagnostic claims.

children.title: Recession-Status Diagnostic System
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic families for recession behavior and ambiguous relaxation status.

children.title: Unbounded Ray Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Evidence exposing recession directions in supported relaxation spaces.

assumptions_latex: The continuous problem is \(\inf\{c^Tx:Ax\le b\}\) and has a feasible point \(x^0\).
The objective is minimized and arithmetic is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A direction \(d\) with \(Ad\le0\) and \(c^Td<0\) certifies that the objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal rays for continuous linear minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal unbounded-ray diagnostic consists of a feasible point \(x^0\) and a nonzero direction \(d\) satisfying \[Ax^0\le b,\qquad Ad\le0,\qquad c^Td<0.\] For every \(t\ge0\), \(A(x^0+td)\le b\), while \[c^T(x^0+td)=c^Tx^0+t\,c^Td\longrightarrow-\infty.\] Thus \((x^0,d)\) is directly checkable and certifies unboundedness below. For mixed-integer models, the ray additionally requires \(td_j\) to preserve each integer variable's domain along an unbounded sequence; a continuous-relaxation ray alone does not certify mixed-integer unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and improving recession direction certify continuous unboundedness; mixed-integer unboundedness additionally requires preservation of integer domains along an infinite sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Ray Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The continuous linear certificate is precise and fits the leaf, but it lacks a citation, and the mixed-integer extension needs an authoritative formulation of domain-preserving ray conditions.

children.title: Infeasible-or-Unbounded Status
children.top_down_role: Ambiguous solver outcomes where infeasibility cannot yet be separated from unboundedness.

assumptions_latex: A solver has terminated without a primal or dual certificate distinguishing infeasibility from unboundedness.
The reported status refers to a specified original or transformed model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The status \(\mathrm{INF\_OR\_UNBD}\) supports only the disjunction; neither infeasibility nor unboundedness may be asserted separately.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the model under diagnosis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguous global status before certificate-based disambiguation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization model with feasible set \(F\) and value \(p^*=\inf_{x\in F}c^Tx\), an infeasible-or-unbounded status represents only \[F=\varnothing\quad\lor\quad p^*=-\infty.\] It is not a certificate of either disjunct. The ambiguity can arise when presolve or dual reductions establish that no finite optimum exists without retaining enough information to classify the original model. Until a verifiable infeasibility certificate or primal improving ray is obtained, downstream logic must preserve the disjunction and must not treat the model as definitely infeasible or definitely unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasible-or-unbounded means only that no finite optimum was classified; a separate certificate is required to choose either status.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-or-Unbounded Status

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but INF_OR_UNBD is a solver status whose exact meaning and causes must be supported by solver documentation with a specific locator.

children.title: Status Disambiguation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver facilities used to refine ambiguous infeasible-or-unbounded outcomes.

assumptions_latex: The model is initially reported as infeasible-or-unbounded.
The solver permits a rerun with ambiguity-producing reductions disabled or provides certificate queries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns infeasible only with a valid infeasibility certificate, unbounded only with a valid improving ray, and unresolved otherwise.

notation.meaning: Infeasibility certificate returned by the solver
Primal improving ray returned by the solver

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-oriented interface for resolving an ambiguous recession status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an \(\mathrm{INF\_OR\_UNBD}\) result, rerun the model with reductions that merge infeasible and unbounded outcomes disabled, while preserving the original objective and domains. If the rerun returns infeasible, request and validate an infeasibility certificate \(y\) against the declared formulation. If it returns unbounded, request and validate a feasible improving ray \(d\). Return \(\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\) only after successful validation of \(y\), return \(\mathrm{UNBOUNDED}\) only after successful validation of \(d\), and otherwise return \(\mathrm{UNRESOLVED}\). A changed objective or domain would answer a different status question and is therefore excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rerun with ambiguity-producing reductions disabled, validate an infeasibility certificate or improving ray, and retain an unresolved status when neither validates.
knowledge_statements.title: Status Disambiguation Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits, but reduction controls, certificate queries, and validation interfaces are solver-specific and have no cited authoritative support.

children.title: Ray Mapping Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on translating recession evidence back to the submitted model.

knowledge_statements.title: Ray Mapping Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits on lifting reduced-space rays to original variables, constraints, objectives, and domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original minimization model have feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and objective \(c^Tx\). Suppose recorded presolve reconstruction has the affine form \(x=Pz+q\). For a reduced-space ray \(d_z\), define the candidate lift \(d_x=Pd_z\). It is an original-model unbounded ray only if there is an original feasible point \(x^0\in F\) such that \[x^0+t d_x\in F\quad\text{for every }t\ge0,\qquad c^Td_x<0.\] For a mixed-integer model, an unbounded sequence along the lifted direction must also preserve every original variable domain. If these conditions cannot be validated after eliminated variables, substitutions, and objective transformations are reconstructed, the reduced ray cannot be reported as an original-model certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-space ray is an original-model certificate only when its reconstructed direction preserves all original feasibility and domain conditions and strictly improves the original objective.
assumptions_latex: The original problem minimizes \(c^Tx\) over a feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
Presolve records an affine reconstruction \(x=Pz+q\) from reduced variables \(z\) to original variables \(x\).
A reduced-space direction \(d_z\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The candidate lift \(d_x=Pd_z\) certifies original-model unboundedness only after the original recession, objective-improvement, and domain-preservation conditions are validated.

notation.meaning: Original-model feasible set, including declared variable domains

children.title: Presolve-Aware Diagnostic Mapping
children.top_down_role: Translation of reduced-space explanations to original model objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve-Aware Diagnostic Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional reconstruction of conflicts, IIS information, residual profiles, certificates, and rays after presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a recorded transformation log from an original model \(M\) to a reduced model \(\widehat M\), process the transformations in reverse order. At each step, apply the recorded diagnostic-mapping rule when that rule is defined for the diagnostic object's type, producing a candidate object expressed in original model objects. Validate the reconstructed candidate directly against \(M\): check subsystem infeasibility for conflicts or IIS data, original residuals for violation profiles, certificate identities for infeasibility certificates, or recession and improvement conditions for rays. Return an original-model diagnostic only when reconstruction is complete and validation succeeds; otherwise return the reduced-model diagnostic with an explicit partially mapped or unmapped status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse only those presolve transformations having applicable recorded diagnostic mappings, then validate the reconstructed object against the original model before presenting it as an original-model explanation.
assumptions_latex: Presolve transforms an original model \(M\) into a reduced model \(\widehat M\) through a recorded sequence of transformations.
A diagnostic object \(D_{\widehat M}\) is available for the reduced model.
Diagnostic-mapping rules may be unavailable for some transformations or diagnostic-object types.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A candidate diagnostic \(D_M\) is an original-model explanation only when reconstruction is complete and direct validation against \(M\) succeeds.

notation.meaning: Diagnostic object for the reduced model
Candidate diagnostic reconstructed for the original model

children.title: Diagnostic Explanation Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Large, unstable, or incomplete diagnostic outputs.

children.title: Oversized Diagnostic Objects
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic outputs too large for effective inspection or remediation.

assumptions_latex: For each integer \(n\ge 1\), consider a linear feasibility system with variables \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_n\) is inclusion-minimal yet \(|D_n|=n+1\), so minimality does not imply a small diagnostic.

notation.meaning: The diagnostic subsystem consisting of all displayed inequalities.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the diagnostic-size construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete IIS family showing that inclusion-minimal diagnostics can grow with the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_n\) contain the inequalities \(x_i\ge 0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le -1\). The full system is infeasible. Removing the summation inequality leaves a feasible system, while removing \(x_k\ge 0\) permits \(x_k=-1\) and \(x_i=0\) for \(i\ne k\). Hence every proper subsystem obtained by deleting one member is feasible, and \(D_n\) is an irreducible infeasible subsystem with \(|D_n|=n+1\). Therefore an inclusion-minimal infeasibility diagnostic may still be arbitrarily large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An irreducible infeasible subsystem can contain every constraint of an arbitrarily large model; deletion minimality alone does not guarantee a concise explanation.
knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Diagnostic Objects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the IIS construction is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports its use as a solver-diagnostic size limitation. An authoritative IIS or conflict-diagnostics source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Diagnostic Instability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of reported explanations to solver settings or minor model changes.

assumptions_latex: A diagnostic rule maps each model-data vector \(d\) to a nonempty constraint-index set \(D(d)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
A metric \(\rho\) measures perturbations of model data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If such sequences exist, the diagnostic rule is unstable at \(d\).

notation.meaning: Diagnostic constraint-index set returned for data d.

review_flags: No supplied source locator identifies a standard quantitative definition of diagnostic instability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A set-valued discontinuity criterion for solver explanations under vanishing data perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The diagnostic rule is unstable at \(d\) if there exist data vectors \(d_k\) with \(\rho(d_k,d)\to 0\) and a constant \(\eta>0\) such that \[\frac{|D(d_k)\triangle D(d)|}{|D(d_k)\cup D(d)|}\ge \eta\] for every \(k\). Thus arbitrarily small perturbations produce a diagnostic whose normalized symmetric difference from the reference diagnostic remains bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagnostic is unstable when arbitrarily small data perturbations cause a persistently large change in the constraints selected as the explanation.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagnostic Instability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is plausible for this leaf, but the normalized symmetric-difference criterion is a particular formalization rather than an established solver-diagnostic convention. No source supports the chosen metric, threshold, or local instability definition.

children.title: Incomplete Explanatory Coverage
children.top_down_role: Gaps between solver failure status and the components represented in diagnostic output.

assumptions_latex: Let \(\mathcal{M}\) be the family of all inclusion-minimal infeasible subsystems of an infeasible finite constraint system.
A diagnostic procedure returns a subfamily \(\widehat{\mathcal{M}}\subseteq\mathcal{M}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coverage is incomplete exactly when \(\operatorname{cov}(\widehat{\mathcal{M}})<1\).

notation.meaning: Family of all inclusion-minimal infeasible subsystems.
Fraction of all minimal explanations returned.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this coverage formalization.
Enumerating all minimal infeasible subsystems may be computationally prohibitive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage measured against all irreducible infeasibility explanations, not merely one returned subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the explanatory coverage of the returned diagnostics by \[\operatorname{cov}(\widehat{\mathcal{M}})=\frac{|\widehat{\mathcal{M}}|}{|\mathcal{M}|}.\] The explanation has incomplete coverage when there exists \(M\in\mathcal{M}\setminus\widehat{\mathcal{M}}\), equivalently when \(\operatorname{cov}(\widehat{\mathcal{M}})<1\). A single valid diagnostic therefore establishes one minimal source of infeasibility but does not establish that all distinct minimal sources have been identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Returning one valid minimal infeasible subsystem does not cover other distinct minimal explanations; complete coverage requires returning every such subsystem.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Explanatory Coverage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits incomplete coverage, and the finite-system assumptions make the displayed ratio well-defined because the family of minimal infeasible subsystems is finite and nonempty. However, no source supports treating enumeration of all minimal infeasible subsystems as the relevant explanatory-coverage standard.

children.title: Diagnostic Interpretability Limits
children.top_down_role: Cases where technically valid outputs remain difficult to connect to model intent.

assumptions_latex: A diagnostic is computed solely from the algebraic coefficient, bound, and integrality data of a finite MIP.
Two models may differ only in semantic labels, provenance, or business meaning attached to corresponding rows and columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Algebraically identical inputs cannot determine which distinct semantic interpretation is the intended causal explanation.

notation.meaning: Algebraic model data supplied to the solver.
A semantic interpretation attached outside the algebraic model.

review_flags: No supplied source directly formalizes the distinction between algebraic diagnosis and semantic explanation.
Interpretability claim needs a solver-diagnostics source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of inferring domain-level causes from algebraic solver diagnostics alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the diagnostic map be \(D(d)\), where \(d\) contains only algebraic model data. Suppose the same \(d\) admits two distinct semantic annotations \(s_1\ne s_2\) that assign different domain-level causes to the constraints in \(D(d)\). Since the solver receives identical \(d\) in both cases, it returns the same diagnostic. Consequently \(D(d)\) can certify an algebraic conflict, but it cannot, without external metadata, distinguish the causal explanations encoded by \(s_1\) and \(s_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An algebraic conflict certificate cannot by itself identify the business or physical cause when identical coefficients admit different semantic interpretations.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagnostic Interpretability Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role matches the terminal container, and the algebraic-versus-semantic distinction is coherent. A solver-diagnostics or explainability source is still required to support the claimed interpretability boundary.

children.title: Floating-Point Reliability
children.top_down_role: Numerical controls and failure boundaries in finite-precision mixed-integer solving.

children.title: Solver Decision Tolerance System
children.top_down_role: Tolerance regimes governing acceptance and ordering decisions.

children.title: Feasibility Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Numerical acceptance margins for constraint satisfaction.

assumptions_latex: A candidate point is \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) for constraints \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
The solver uses absolute row tolerances \(\varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{feas}}\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point is tolerance-feasible exactly when every row satisfies its relaxed inequality.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly specifies practical solver feasibility-tolerance semantics.
Exact scaling conventions vary by solver.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute row-feasibility convention; production solvers may additionally scale residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the row violation by \(v_i(x)=\max\{0,a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\}\). The candidate \(x\) is feasibility-accepted under the absolute tolerance convention if and only if \[v_i(x)\le \varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{feas}}\quad\text{for every }i=1,\ldots,m.\] Equality rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\) are accepted when \(|a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i|\le\varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{feas}}\). Tolerance acceptance is a numerical decision and need not imply exact mathematical feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver accepts a row when its computed violation is no larger than the configured feasibility tolerance; accepted points need not be exactly feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Tolerances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits feasibility tolerances, but practical solvers differ in residual scaling, bound handling, and absolute-versus-relative tests. With no cited solver manual or numerical-optimization source, the displayed absolute row convention cannot be treated as a general solver rule.

children.title: Integrality Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Numerical acceptance margins for integer-valued variables.

assumptions_latex: The index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) identifies variables required to be integral.
The integrality tolerance is \(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{int}}\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The candidate is integrality-accepted exactly when all designated components lie within tolerance of an integer.

notation.meaning: Distance from a scalar to the nearest integer.

review_flags: The locator supports integrality constraints but may not state solver tolerance conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard nearest-integer acceptance test for integer-designated variables.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), define \(\operatorname{dist}(t,\mathbb{Z})=\min_{z\in\mathbb{Z}}|t-z|\). A candidate \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is integrality-accepted if and only if \[\operatorname{dist}(x_j,\mathbb{Z})\le\varepsilon^{\mathrm{int}}\quad\text{for every }j\in I.\] For a binary variable with bounds \(0\le x_j\le1\), this is equivalent to \(\min\{|x_j|,|1-x_j|\}\le\varepsilon^{\mathrm{int}}\), subject also to the solver's bound-feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer-designated value is accepted when its distance to the nearest integer does not exceed the integrality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality Tolerances

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role and nearest-integer formula are appropriate, but the cited section concerns integrality constraints and is not shown to specify numerical integrality-acceptance tolerances. A solver manual or numerical MIP reference with a locator for the tolerance test is required.

children.title: Comparison Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Numerical margins used when ordering bounds, objectives, or candidate values.

assumptions_latex: The quantities compared are finite real numbers \(u,v\).
Absolute and relative tolerances satisfy \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate equality and order are determined by the displayed absolute-relative threshold.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports a solver comparison-tolerance convention.
Production solvers may use asymmetric or context-specific comparisons.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic combined absolute-relative convention for floating-point solver comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\tau(u,v)=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{|u|,|v|\}\). Declare \(u\approx_{\tau}v\) when \(|u-v|\le\tau(u,v)\), and declare \(u\le_{\tau}v\) when \(u\le v+\tau(u,v)\). These predicates create an indifference band around exact equality or order. They are decision conventions rather than transitive mathematical relations; in particular, \(u\approx_{\tau}v\) and \(v\approx_{\tau}w\) need not imply \(u\approx_{\tau}w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Comparison tolerances create a scale-aware indifference band, but approximate equality may fail transitivity and can depend on solver context.
knowledge_statements.title: Comparison Tolerances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but the symmetric combined absolute-relative threshold is only one possible comparison convention. No source supports its use in practical MIP solver decisions, which may be asymmetric and context dependent.

children.title: Tolerance Interaction Risks
children.top_down_role: Inconsistent conclusions produced by mismatched numerical acceptance regimes.

assumptions_latex: The solver accepts row violations up to \(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{feas}}>0\).
The variable \(x\) is binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tolerance-feasible and integrality-accepted need not imply exact feasibility for the original MIP.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly addresses interaction among solver tolerances.
Concrete construction uses the absolute feasibility convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete mismatch between separate feasibility and integrality acceptance tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the exact constraint \(x\ge\varepsilon^{\mathrm{feas}}/2\) with \(x\in\{0,1\}\). At the candidate \(x=0\), integrality is exact, while the row violation is \(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), so the row is accepted under feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{feas}}\). Nevertheless, \(x=0\) violates the original exact constraint. Thus independently satisfied feasibility and integrality tests can jointly accept a point that is not feasible for the exact MIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate feasibility and integrality tests can jointly accept an exactly integral point that still violates the original constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Interaction Risks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is correct and the example is coherent under the explicitly assumed absolute feasibility convention. A source is nevertheless required to connect this convention and the separate acceptance tests to actual MIP solver tolerance behavior.

children.title: Model Data Reliability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Reliability risks associated with heterogeneous or inaccurate model data.

children.title: Model Scaling Quality
children.top_down_role: Reliability effects of coefficient normalization and row or column scaling.

assumptions_latex: The finite constraint matrix is \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
Positive diagonal row and column scalings \(R\) and \(C\) are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Smaller finite \(Q(RAC)\) indicates more uniform nonzero coefficient magnitudes after scaling.
review_flags: The displayed quality metric is a local formalization, not necessarily the source's exact definition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-uniformity criterion after admissible positive row and column rescaling.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 How to build a good model p. 36

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B=RAC\), define \[Q(B)=\frac{\max\{|B_{ij}|:B_{ij}\ne0\}}{\min\{|B_{ij}|:B_{ij}\ne0\}}.\] Relative to a prescribed threshold \(\Gamma\ge1\), the matrix has acceptable scaling quality if there exist admissible positive diagonal \(R\) and \(C\) such that \(Q(RAC)\le\Gamma\). This criterion concerns coefficient magnitudes only; it does not by itself guarantee good conditioning, accurate data, or numerical reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling quality is acceptable when permitted row and column rescaling keeps nonzero coefficient magnitudes within a prescribed spread; this alone does not ensure conditioning.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Scaling Quality

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 How to build a good model p. 36

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is reasonable, but the cited model-building sections are not shown to define the proposed existential row-and-column scaling criterion or the threshold Gamma. Because this local metric is the mathematical substance of the record, a source directly supporting it is required.

children.title: Coefficient Dynamic Range
children.top_down_role: Numerical risks caused by widely separated coefficient magnitudes.

assumptions_latex: The finite coefficient collection \(S\subset\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\) contains quantities measured in compatible units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dynamic range is the ratio of the largest to the smallest nonzero magnitude in \(S\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of nonzero coefficients under comparison.

review_flags: Compatible units are required for the ratio to be meaningful.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Magnitude spread for a specified, unit-compatible collection of nonzero model coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The coefficient dynamic range of \(S\) is \[\operatorname{dr}(S)=\frac{\max_{s\in S}|s|}{\min_{s\in S}|s|}.\] It satisfies \(\operatorname{dr}(S)\ge1\) and is invariant under multiplication of every member of \(S\) by the same nonzero scalar. Coefficients with incompatible physical units must not be pooled without normalization, because their numerical ratio then depends on the chosen units.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient dynamic range is the largest nonzero magnitude divided by the smallest, computed only among quantities made comparable by consistent units or normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Dynamic Range

children.title: Input Data Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Reliability consequences of rounded, noisy, or imprecisely encoded model data.

assumptions_latex: Nominal data are \(\widehat A,\widehat b\), while the unknown true data satisfy componentwise bounds \(|A_{ij}-\widehat A_{ij}|\le\Delta A_{ij}\) and \(|b_i-\widehat b_i|\le\Delta b_i\).
The uncertainty bounds are nonnegative and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed margin is sufficient for row feasibility for every admissible realization of the data.
review_flags: The robust margin is a conservative formalization of input-data accuracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise bounded-error criterion linking recorded data accuracy to reliable row satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed candidate \(x\), row \(i\) is guaranteed feasible for every admissible realization \((A,b)\) if \[\widehat a_i^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{j=1}^n\Delta A_{ij}|x_j|\le\widehat b_i-\Delta b_i.\] Indeed, the uncertainty terms bound the largest possible increase in the left-hand side and decrease in the right-hand side. Nominal feasibility without this margin need not persist under data errors allowed by \((\Delta A,\Delta b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With bounded coefficient and right-hand-side errors, a candidate is reliably feasible only when its nominal slack covers the worst admissible data perturbation.
knowledge_statements.title: Input Data Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits a data-accuracy criterion, and the displayed componentwise robust margin is mathematically coherent. The cited data-management sections are not shown to support this exact uncertainty model or worst-case formula, so a robust-optimization or verified data-uncertainty source is required.

children.title: Unit Inconsistency Risks
children.top_down_role: Numerical problems caused by incompatible or poorly chosen measurement units.

assumptions_latex: Each physical quantity \(q\) has a dimension vector \(\delta(q)\in\mathbb{Z}^p\).
Products and powers obey \(\delta(qr)=\delta(q)+\delta(r)\) and \(\delta(q^k)=k\delta(q)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A row is dimensionally consistent only when all additive terms and its right-hand side have the same dimension vector.

notation.meaning: Dimension of the j-th term in a row.

review_flags: The supplied locator concerns model quality rather than a formal dimensional-analysis theorem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensional homogeneity as a necessary modeling condition before numerical scaling is assessed.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Ease of detecting errors in the model p. 37
3.5.1 A more natural input format p. 41

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a row \(\sum_{j=1}^n q_j\le r\), and let \(d_j=\delta(q_j)\). Dimensional consistency requires \[d_1=d_2=\cdots=d_n=\delta(r).\] If this condition fails, the numerical sum combines physically incomparable quantities. Changing units can then alter relative coefficients in a way that is not a common rescaling of the row, so solver feasibility and objective comparisons may represent a different physical model rather than an equivalent numerical formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every additive term in a constraint must share the right-hand side's physical dimension; otherwise unit changes can alter the modeled relationship itself.
knowledge_statements.title: Unit Inconsistency Risks

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Ease of detecting errors in the model p. 37
3.5.1 A more natural input format p. 41

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits unit inconsistency risks, and dimensional homogeneity is a standard necessary modeling condition. The cited general model-quality sections are not shown to support the formal dimension-vector framework or the concluding claim about solver comparisons, so a dimensional-analysis or modeling reference with a direct locator is required.

children.title: Relaxation Basis Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relaxation-solver behavior affecting node conclusions and warm starts.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations whose numerical sensitivity undermines reliable solver conclusions.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation is an LP with nonsingular basis matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\).
A norm \(\|\cdot\|\) and reliability threshold \(\tau_{\mathrm{cond}}>1\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis is ill-conditioned precisely when \(\kappa(B)>\tau_{\mathrm{cond}}\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports LP basis conditioning in floating-point MIP computation.
standard_field_rationale: normwise matrix conditioning is the standard local diagnostic for sensitivity of basis solves.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to a nonsingular simplex basis of an LP node relaxation under a fixed norm and threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) be a nonsingular basis matrix of an LP relaxation, and define \(\kappa(B)=\|B\|\,\|B^{-1}\|\) in a fixed subordinate norm. For a prescribed threshold \(\tau_{\mathrm{cond}}>1\), the relaxation basis is ill-conditioned when \[\kappa(B)>\tau_{\mathrm{cond}}.\] In this regime, relative perturbations in the basis data or right-hand side may be amplified by a factor proportional to \(\kappa(B)\) in computed basic solutions, so feasibility and bound conclusions obtained near their tolerances require additional validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation basis is ill-conditioned when its condition number exceeds a fixed threshold, allowing small data or rounding errors to cause much larger errors in computed basic solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition-number diagnostic fits the leaf and the selected kind, but no cited source supports the threshold convention or the floating-point MIP reliability claim. The statement should also distinguish worst-case sensitivity bounded in terms of the condition number from actual error amplification.

children.title: Degenerate Relaxation Bases
children.top_down_role: Basis regimes with extensive degeneracy affecting progress or interpretation.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation is written in standard form \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge 0\), with basis index set \(\mathcal B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis is primal degenerate exactly when some basic component equals zero.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix formed from columns indexed by \(\mathcal B\)

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports simplex degeneracy in practical MIP relaxations.
standard_field_rationale: zero-valued basic variables are the standard definition of primal basis degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses primal degeneracy for a feasible simplex basis in standard-form LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the standard-form LP relaxation \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge 0\), and let \(\mathcal B\) index a nonsingular basis \(B=A_{\mathcal B}\). Its basic solution is \(x_{\mathcal B}=B^{-1}b\), with all nonbasic variables set to zero. A primal-feasible basis is degenerate if and only if \[x_{\mathcal B}\ge 0\quad\text{and}\quad \min_{i\in\mathcal B}(x_i)=0.\] Equivalently, at least one basic variable is at its lower bound, so a simplex pivot can change the basis without changing the represented primal solution or objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible relaxation basis is degenerate when at least one basic variable is zero; pivots may then change the basis without changing the represented solution or objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Relaxation Bases

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit a feasible standard-form LP basis, but the record has no citation. The final pivot consequence also needs qualified support: degeneracy permits a zero-step pivot in appropriate circumstances, but the definition alone does not ensure that a basis-changing pivot with unchanged solution is available.

children.title: Basis Instability
children.top_down_role: Unreliable basis behavior across reoptimization, node transitions, or perturbations.

assumptions_latex: Two nearby relaxation instances have basis matrices \(B\) and \(B+\Delta B\).
Both matrices are nonsingular and use a fixed subordinate norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large \(\|B^{-1}\Delta B\|\), especially near one, makes reuse of the basis numerically unstable.

notation.meaning: Perturbation induced by relaxation changes or numerical error

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports basis-instability thresholds in floating-point LP solves.
Threshold interpretation depends on the norm, factorization, scaling, and solver tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation boundary for reusing a nonsingular LP basis; it is not a solver-independent numerical threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a nonsingular relaxation basis and let \(B+\Delta B\) be the basis matrix after perturbation. Set \(\rho=\|B^{-1}\Delta B\|\). If \(\rho<1\), then the perturbed matrix is nonsingular and its inverse satisfies \[\|(B+\Delta B)^{-1}\|\le \frac{\|B^{-1}\|}{1-\rho}.\] Thus the stability margin vanishes as \(\rho\uparrow 1\); when \(\rho\) is near or above one, this guarantee is lost, and small perturbations may invalidate the former basis or strongly alter its computed primal and dual quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis reuse loses a perturbation guarantee as the relative basis change approaches one; near that boundary, small changes can strongly alter feasibility, dual values, or nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Instability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse perturbation bound is standard and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no source is cited. The condition rho near or above one only removes this sufficient nonsingularity bound; it does not itself establish numerical instability or failure of basis reuse.

children.title: Warm-Start Reliability Loss
children.top_down_role: Degradation of relaxation warm starts caused by unstable basis information.

assumptions_latex: A stored basis \(B\) is supplied to a modified LP relaxation.
The modified relaxation is solved in finite precision using fixed feasibility and optimality tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of residual, conditioning, or status checks makes the warm start unreliable and requires repair or refactorization.

notation.meaning: Computed warm-start primal and dual vectors

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports warm-start reliability criteria for practical MIP solvers.
Exact acceptance checks vary by solver, scaling, and simplex implementation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers numerical acceptance of a basis warm start after changes to a node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a stored basis \(B\) initialize a modified LP relaxation, producing computed vectors \((\widehat x,\widehat y)\). The warm start is numerically admissible only if \(B\) remains nonsingular, its factorization passes the solver's conditioning checks, and the scaled primal and dual residuals and bound violations are at most \(\varepsilon\). If any such condition fails, or if the implied basic/nonbasic statuses are inconsistent with the modified bounds, reliability of the warm start is lost; the basis must be repaired, refactorized, or discarded before its feasibility or bound information is trusted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start becomes unreliable when its basis, residuals, or variable statuses fail validation for the modified relaxation; it must then be repaired, refactorized, or discarded.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Reliability Loss

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the asserted necessary admissibility checks, scaled residuals, conditioning tests, and repair actions are solver-specific and are not defined or sourced. A solver manual or numerical simplex reference with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Numerical Search-Conclusion Failures
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision contamination of consequential search conclusions.

children.title: Unsafe Search Bounds
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision errors that compromise bounds used for search decisions.

assumptions_latex: The MIP is a minimization problem and a node relaxation has exact optimum \(z_R\).
A computed value \(\widehat L\) is used as a lower bound for pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search bound is unsafe exactly when \(\widehat L>z_R\) has not been excluded by certification.

notation.meaning: Exact optimum of the node relaxation
Computed lower bound used by the search

review_flags: Supplied relaxation locators address mathematical bounds but not floating-point certification of computed search bounds.
standard_field_rationale: a valid minimization lower bound cannot exceed the exact relaxation optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention; inequalities reverse for maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization MIP, let \(z_R\) be the exact optimum of a node relaxation and let \(\widehat L\) be the floating-point value used as the node lower bound. The bound is search-safe only if \[\widehat L\le z_R.\] It is unsafe whenever numerical error can make \(\widehat L>z_R\) and no rigorous correction or certificate excludes that event. Using such an overestimated lower bound in comparisons with an incumbent may prune a node containing a feasible solution whose objective is strictly better than the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, a computed node lower bound is unsafe if it can exceed the exact relaxation optimum, because incumbent-based pruning may then discard an improving solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Search Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For minimization, a valid lower bound must not exceed the exact relaxation optimum, and the failure-boundary kind fits. However, no source supports the floating-point search-safety claim, and the referenced rigorous correction or certificate is not formalized sufficiently to establish when the risk has been excluded.

children.title: Erroneous Objective Cutoffs
children.top_down_role: Numerically unreliable cutoff comparisons that exclude viable search regions.

assumptions_latex: The MIP is a minimization problem with incumbent objective \(U\).
A node is cut off using computed lower bound \(\widehat L\) and tolerance \(\delta\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cutoff is erroneous when \(\widehat L\ge U-\delta\) but the node contains a feasible point with objective below \(U\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports floating-point objective-cutoff failure criteria.
The precise cutoff convention and tolerance adjustment are solver dependent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization node cutoff with an incumbent and an explicit absolute cutoff tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be the incumbent objective in a minimization MIP, and suppose a node is discarded when its computed lower bound satisfies \(\widehat L\ge U-\delta\), where \(\delta\ge0\) is the cutoff tolerance. The cutoff is erroneous if \[\widehat L\ge U-\delta\quad\text{but}\quad \inf\{c^Tx:x\text{ is MIP-feasible in the node}\}<U.\] This mismatch can arise from an overstated relaxation bound, an incorrectly rounded incumbent cutoff, or inconsistent scaling and tolerances; it destroys the validity of the resulting optimality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective cutoff is erroneous when the solver discards a node as nonimproving even though that node contains a feasible solution better than the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Erroneous Objective Cutoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes the intended failure phenomenon, but the cutoff rule is implementation-dependent and uncited. With delta greater than zero, pruning a node containing an objective in the interval from U-delta to U may be consistent with a tolerance-based guarantee while invalidating exact optimality, so the claimed error criterion requires an explicit guarantee convention.

children.title: False Conflict Generation
children.top_down_role: Spurious learned conflicts caused by unreliable infeasibility conclusions.

assumptions_latex: A node subproblem has exact feasible set \(F\).
A learned conflict excludes all assignments satisfying a predicate \(C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conflict is false exactly when some \(x\in F\) satisfies \(C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Exact feasible set of the node subproblem
Predicate describing assignments excluded by the learned conflict

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports numerical validation of MIP conflict constraints.
Conflict representations differ across propagation, infeasibility analysis, and solver implementations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic validity test for a learned conflict derived from a numerically declared infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) denote the exact feasible set of the node subproblem. Suppose numerical infeasibility analysis learns a conflict whose effect is to exclude every assignment satisfying \(C(x)\). The conflict is valid precisely when \[F\cap\{x:C(x)\}=\varnothing.\] A witness \(x^\star\in F\) with \(C(x^\star)\) is therefore a verifiable certificate that the conflict is false. Such a false conflict can result when an approximate infeasibility conclusion or an invalid bound propagation is treated as exact and generalized to other search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned conflict is false if it excludes an exactly feasible assignment; that assignment is a direct certificate of invalid conflict generation.
knowledge_statements.title: False Conflict Generation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-theoretic validity test is coherent under the record's stipulated meaning of C, and a feasible excluded point is a countercertificate. Nevertheless, the leaf concerns a failure phenomenon rather than a certificate container, so content_kind certificate is not the best terminal role. Conflict representations and the numerical-generation claim also lack any cited source.

children.title: Incorrect Pruning Consequences
children.top_down_role: Loss of valid solutions or proof reliability following contaminated search conclusions.

assumptions_latex: The search tree partitions the MIP feasible set among active or processed nodes.
At least one node containing an improving feasible solution is pruned by an invalid numerical conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The remaining search no longer certifies global optimality or infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Feasible subset represented by the incorrectly pruned node
