review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports the assurance consequence of numerically incorrect pruning.
standard_field_rationale: branch-and-bound certification requires every pruned region to be validly dominated or infeasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the logical effect of invalid pruning on a minimization branch-and-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\subseteq F\) be the feasible region assigned to a pruned node in a minimization search, and let \(U\) be the objective value ultimately reported. If pruning is incorrect and \[\inf_{x\in F_N}c^Tx<U,\] then the reported incumbent is not certified globally optimal. If the solver instead reports infeasibility while \(F_N\ne\varnothing\), that conclusion is also invalid. More generally, once a region is removed without a sound infeasibility or dominance certificate, exhaustive coverage of the feasible set is lost, irrespective of whether subsequent processing is numerically accurate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorrect pruning breaks exhaustive search coverage: it can hide a better feasible solution or any feasible solution, invalidating reported optimality or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Incorrect Pruning Consequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical consequence fits the leaf and property is a defensible role: invalidly removing a region containing a better or any feasible point defeats the corresponding exact certificate. No source is cited, however, and the exhaustive partition and certification assumptions need support from a branch-and-bound reference.

children.title: Numerical Reliability Indicators
children.top_down_role: Solver-reported indicators used to identify unreliable runs.

children.title: Numerical Quality Metrics
children.top_down_role: Reported measures of residuals, violations, conditioning, or solution reliability.

assumptions_latex: A computed candidate \(\widehat x\) is checked against linear constraints \(Ax\le b\), bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\), and integer index set \(I\).
Scaling denominators are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The metric vector records maximum scaled row, bound, and integrality violations.

notation.meaning: Candidate solution computed in floating point

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly specifies numerical quality metrics for MIP solutions.
Scaling conventions and reported metric sets vary across solvers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A solver-independent core metric vector; implementations may add dual residuals and basis condition estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed candidate \(\widehat x\), define the scaled row violation, bound violation, and integrality violation by \[q_{\mathrm{row}}=\max_i\frac{[a_i^T\widehat x-b_i]_+}{1+|b_i|},\qquad q_{\mathrm{bnd}}=\max_j\left\{\frac{[\ell_j-\widehat x_j]_+}{1+|\ell_j|},\frac{[\widehat x_j-u_j]_+}{1+|u_j|}\right\},\qquad q_{\mathrm{int}}=\max_{j\in I}\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x_j,\mathbb Z).\] The vector \((q_{\mathrm{row}},q_{\mathrm{bnd}},q_{\mathrm{int}})\) is a numerical quality summary; smaller components indicate closer satisfaction of the corresponding exact conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical quality can be summarized by maximum scaled row violation, bound violation, and distance of integer variables from the nearest integers.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Quality Metrics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind, but the proposed metric schema is uncited and not well-defined for infinite variable bounds, an empty integer index set, or potentially empty row and bound index sets. Finite-bound index sets and empty-maximum conventions must be introduced, and the particular scaling must be sourced or explicitly scoped as a chosen convention.

children.title: Solver Numerical Warnings
children.top_down_role: Messages indicating instability, suspicious conclusions, or degraded numerical behavior.

assumptions_latex: A solver has declared a status or accepted a candidate solution.
Warning thresholds for residuals, conditioning, or status consistency are fixed before inspection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A warning is triggered whenever at least one monitored reliability predicate fails.
review_flags: No supplied source locator defines a common warning protocol across MIP solvers.
Warning categories and thresholds are implementation specific.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract predicate covering explicit solver warnings without prescribing vendor-specific messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_k)\) collect monitored quantities such as scaled primal residual, dual residual, integrality violation, basis condition estimate, or bound inconsistency, and let \(\tau\ge0\) contain their warning thresholds. Let \(S\) be the declared solver status and \(V(S)\) its independent validation predicate. A numerical warning is required when \[\left(\exists i:\ q_i>\tau_i\right)\ \lor\ \neg V(S).\] Absence of this predicate is only absence of a detected anomaly; it is not, by itself, a certificate that all search conclusions are exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical warning is warranted when a monitored metric exceeds its threshold or an independent check contradicts the declared solver status; no warning alone does not certify correctness.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver Numerical Warnings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a warning trigger, but the statement invents a universal requirement across solvers without evidence. The monitored quantities, threshold semantics, and independent predicate V(S) are implementation- and conclusion-specific and need a precise source and definition.

children.title: Run-to-Run Quality Comparison
children.top_down_role: Use of numerical indicators to compare alternative settings or repeated solves.

assumptions_latex: Two runs solve the same mathematical MIP instance under possibly different numerical settings.
Both runs report the same predefined vector of quality metrics and status data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The runs are compared componentwise after normalizing direction and scale, with disagreements reported rather than collapsed into runtime alone.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly specifies a run-to-run numerical quality comparison protocol.
Metric availability, normalization, and equivalence tolerances are solver dependent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison procedure for repeated solves of one fixed model using a predefined common metric schema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given runs \(r=1,2\) on the same model, first validate that their objective conventions, scaling, tolerances, and termination criteria are recorded. For each common quality metric with smaller values preferred, choose \(s_i>0\) and compute \[d_i=\frac{q_i^{(2)}-q_i^{(1)}}{s_i}.\] Compare declared feasibility, objective values, best bounds, and termination statuses within predefined tolerances; then output \((d_i)_i\) together with every status or conclusion disagreement. A run is declared uniformly no worse only when all comparable \(d_i\le0\) and no validated status or objective comparison favors the other run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare repeated runs using normalized common quality metrics plus objective, bound, and status checks; report disagreements explicitly and claim dominance only when every comparable criterion agrees.
knowledge_statements.title: Run-to-Run Quality Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the procedural leaf, but the normalization, tolerances, status comparison, and dominance rule are an uncited proposed protocol rather than an established method. The phrase that a status or objective comparison favors a run is not formalized, especially when termination guarantees differ.

children.title: Silent Reliability Failures
children.top_down_role: Unreliable outcomes not clearly exposed by available metrics or warnings.

assumptions_latex: A solver run terminates without emitting a numerical warning.
An independent exact or higher-accuracy check is available for the reported conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A silent reliability failure occurs when the independent check rejects the unwarned conclusion.

notation.meaning: Independent validation predicate for that conclusion
Predicate that an explicit numerical warning was emitted

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports a formal definition of silent numerical failure in MIP solvers.
The independent validation method depends on whether feasibility, optimality, a bound, or infeasibility is reported.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines silence relative to an explicit warning channel and an independently checkable solver conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a reported feasibility, infeasibility, bound, or optimality conclusion; let \(V(S)\) denote acceptance by an independent exact, interval, or sufficiently higher-accuracy validation; and let \(W\) mean that the run emitted an explicit numerical warning relevant to \(S\). A silent reliability failure is the event \[\neg W\ \land\ \neg V(S).\] Thus ordinary residuals lying within internal tolerances and the absence of warning messages do not exclude failure when the search used an unsafe bound, false conflict, incorrect cutoff, or another invalid numerical inference not exposed by the reported indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reliability failure is silent when the solver emits no relevant warning but an independent exact or higher-accuracy check rejects its reported conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Silent Reliability Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The event definition matches the leaf and failure-boundary kind, but no source is supplied. The phrase sufficiently higher-accuracy validation does not by itself ensure an independent check is authoritative, and V(S) must be specialized for feasibility, bounds, optimality, and infeasibility before the claimed failure is reliable.

children.title: Safe Dual-Bound Calculus
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision safeguards for relaxation bounds and pruning decisions.

children.title: Directed Rounding Regimes
children.top_down_role: Controlled finite-precision rounding used to preserve conservative numerical conclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Rounding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward-rounded interval evaluation for certified lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each real input be enclosed by a machine interval \([\underline{x},\overline{x}]\). For every supported arithmetic operation \(\circ\), compute its lower endpoint with rounding toward \(-\infty\) and its upper endpoint with rounding toward \(+\infty\). Thus \([\underline{x},\overline{x}]\circ[\underline{y},\overline{y}]\) encloses \(x\circ y\) for all enclosed operands whenever the operation is defined and exceptional values are handled conservatively. Consequently, evaluating a dual objective downward produces a value no greater than its exact value; evaluating an upper bound upward produces a value no smaller than its exact value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward rounding encloses every exact arithmetic result. Downward evaluation of a valid dual objective therefore remains a safe lower bound.
assumptions_latex: All input intervals contain their exact real values.
The arithmetic implementation honors directed rounding and handles overflow and undefined operations conservatively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline{z}\le z\le\overline{z}\), with downward-rounded dual values safe for minimization.

notation.meaning: Certified interval enclosing the exact value x.

children.title: Safe Dual Bound Construction
children.top_down_role: Protection of relaxation bounds used in pruning or optimality assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Dual Bound Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a certified LP lower bound from a dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the rational relaxation \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), take a proposed multiplier \(y\). Compute \(r=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\) using exact arithmetic or outward-rounded intervals. Accept the proposal only if every certified lower endpoint of \(r\) is nonnegative. Then evaluate \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) with exact arithmetic or rounding toward \(-\infty\), and output the resulting number \(L\). If feasibility of \(r\ge0\) cannot be certified, return no bound. Every accepted output satisfies \(L\le c^{\mathsf T}x\) for each primal-feasible \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verify dual feasibility with exact or outward-rounded arithmetic, then round the dual objective downward to obtain a certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) are represented exactly or by certified enclosing intervals.
The relaxation is a minimization problem in the displayed standard form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned value satisfies \(L\le z_{\mathrm{LP}}\).

children.title: Safe Pruning Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Use of protected bounds in consequential branch-and-bound decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Pruning Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified bound comparison at a minimization branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node \(v\), let \(L_v\) be a certified lower bound on every feasible objective value in the node region, and let \(U\) be the exact objective value of a globally feasible incumbent. The solver may prune \(v\) by bound when \(L_v\ge U\). If either value is interval-valued, the safe test is \(\underline{L}_v\ge\overline{U}\), where \(\underline{L}_v\) is a certified lower endpoint and \(\overline{U}\) is a certified upper endpoint. Equality is safe when only one optimal solution is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization node may be pruned only when its certified lower bound is at least a certified incumbent upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The node bound applies to every feasible point remaining at node \(v\).
The incumbent is globally feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\ge U\) certifies that node \(v\) cannot improve the incumbent.

children.title: Bound-Safety Limitations
children.top_down_role: Model or arithmetic conditions where finite-precision safeguards remain insufficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Safety Limitations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of pruning when a purported lower bound is rounded upward.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:1\le x\le1+\varepsilon\}\) with \(\varepsilon>0\), and suppose the incumbent has value \(U=1+\varepsilon\). The true node optimum is \(1\). If numerical error reports the nonvalid lower bound \(\widehat L=1+2\varepsilon\), the test \(\widehat L\ge U\) prunes the node although it contains the improving point \(x=1\). Hence feasibility tolerances, approximate dual multipliers, or nearest/upward rounding cannot support certified pruning unless their aggregate error is enclosed in the safe direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An overestimated node lower bound can prune a node containing a better solution; numerical tolerances require conservative error enclosure.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
The solver uses the uncertified value \(\widehat L\) as a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uncertified overestimation of a lower bound can invalidate branch-and-bound pruning.

notation.meaning: Numerically reported but invalid lower bound.

children.title: Exact Relaxation Artifact Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery and checking of exact relaxation artifacts from numerical computations.

children.title: Rational Value Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of exact candidate values from numerical relaxation artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational Value Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-denominator reconstruction of an exact rational from an approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), an error bound \(\delta\ge0\), and a denominator limit \(Q\in\mathbb N\), enumerate convergents and required intermediate convergents of the continued fraction of \(\alpha\). Return a reduced fraction \(p/q\) only if \(1\le q\le Q\), \(|\alpha-p/q|\le\delta\), and no other reduced fraction with denominator at most \(Q\) satisfies that interval test. In particular, if an unknown reduced \(p/q\) obeys \(q\le Q\) and \(|\alpha-p/q|<1/(2Q^2)\), it is the unique admissible reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continued fractions recover a bounded-denominator rational when the approximation is sufficiently accurate and the candidate is unique.
assumptions_latex: A certified bound on \(|\alpha-p/q|\) is available.
The denominator cap \(Q\) is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under \(|\alpha-p/q|<1/(2Q^2)\), the admissible reduced rational is unique.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reconstruction rule and uniqueness threshold are mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports the continued-fraction algorithm or the stated bounded-denominator uniqueness guarantee.

children.title: Exact Basis Verification
children.top_down_role: Checking numerical basis information against exact arithmetic requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Basis Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-dual verification of a proposed LP basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(B\) index \(m\) columns with nonsingular rational matrix \(A_B\), and let \(N\) be the remaining indices. Compute exactly \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\), \(x_N=0\), \(y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\), and \(r_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y\). If \(x_B\ge0\) and \(r_N\ge0\), then \(x\) is primal feasible, \(y\) is dual feasible, and their objectives agree. The basis therefore certifies optimality with exact value \(c_B^{\mathsf T}x_B=b^{\mathsf T}y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact nonnegativity of the basic solution and reduced costs certifies that a proposed rational LP basis is optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) are rational.
\(A_B\) is square and nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_B\ge0\) and \(r_N\ge0\) certify LP optimality and exact primal-dual objective equality.

notation.meaning: Basic and nonbasic column index sets.
Exact dual vector induced by the basis.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact primal-dual basis certificate is standard and internally consistent, but the record supplies no source with a section, theorem, or page locator.

children.title: Reconstruction Acceptance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing whether reconstructed exact artifacts are considered reliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Acceptance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance predicate for reconstructed LP artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reconstructed rational basis and associated values are accepted only when all three checks succeed: bounded-denominator reconstruction is unique within the certified approximation intervals; the proposed basis matrix is exactly nonsingular; and exact recomputation yields primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and equal primal-dual objectives. Formally, acceptance requires \(1\le q_i\le Q\) for every reconstructed denominator, \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\). Approximate closeness alone is not an acceptance condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept reconstructed artifacts only after unique bounded-denominator recovery and exact primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and objective equality checks.
assumptions_latex: The original LP data are rational and available exactly.
Certified approximation intervals and a denominator cap are supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies that the reconstructed primal-dual pair is an exact optimality certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The acceptance condition is mathematically sufficient, but no cited source supports this particular reconstruction-and-verification regime.

children.title: Reconstruction Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where numerical artifacts do not support stable exact recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity and invalidity boundaries for rational reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proximity test cannot identify a rational uniquely without a denominator cap and a sufficiently narrow certified interval. For any \(Q\ge2\), take \(\alpha=1/(2Q)\). Both reduced rationals \(0/1\) and \(1/Q\) have denominator at most \(Q\) and satisfy \(|\alpha-r|=1/(2Q)\). Thus tolerance \(\delta\ge1/(2Q)\) admits two reconstructions in this instance. Even a unique nearby rational must be rejected when exact substitution violates feasibility, reduced-cost signs, or objective equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wide intervals can contain multiple bounded-denominator rationals, and a nearby unique candidate can still fail exact LP verification.
assumptions_latex: Acceptance is based on proximity unless the stated exact checks are added.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither proximity without uniqueness nor reconstruction without exact verification certifies an LP artifact.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ambiguity example and exact-verification boundary are correct, but the record has no authoritative source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Fully Exact Rational MILP Solving
children.top_down_role: Exact-arithmetic regimes for principal relaxation and search computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Exact Rational MILP Solving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact branch-and-bound for rational MILPs with bounded variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rational MILP whose variables have finite rational bounds and whose integer-variable index set is \(I\), initialize the root node and no incumbent. At each node, solve its rational LP relaxation exactly. Prune only upon exact infeasibility or when its exact lower bound is no smaller than the exact incumbent value. If an optimal relaxation solution satisfies \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\), update the incumbent exactly. Otherwise choose an index \(j\in I\) with fractional value \(x_j^*\) and create the children \(x_j\le\lfloor x_j^*\rfloor\) and \(x_j\ge\lceil x_j^*\rceil\). Select nodes by an exhaustive policy. Because every integer domain is finite and each split strictly reduces the admissible integer values along its branch, the search tree is finite. When no nodes remain, return the exact incumbent, or exact infeasibility if no incumbent exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact rational branch-and-bound solves every relaxation and correctness-critical comparison exactly and uses standard integer splits over finite domains, yielding a finite exact search.
assumptions_latex: All model data and finite variable bounds are rational.
Every integer variable has a finite domain.
LP relaxations are solved exactly, and node selection is exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates with an exact optimal solution or an exact infeasibility conclusion.

notation.meaning: Fractional value of the selected integer variable in the current exact LP optimum.
Exact relaxation lower bound at node v.

children.title: Hybrid Floating-Point–Exact Solving
children.top_down_role: Numerical search combined with exact correction or verification.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Floating-Point–Exact Solving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point search with exact validation of correctness-critical decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a branch-and-bound search using floating-point relaxations to propose bases, incumbents, cuts, and branching choices. Before accepting an incumbent, verify its feasibility and objective exactly. Before pruning by infeasibility or bound, reconstruct or recompute an exact certificate; if certification fails, retain the node and invoke exact rational resolution or conservative interval bounding. Before applying a cut, verify exactly that it is valid for every relevant feasible solution, so it cannot discard a solution permitted by the original model and the current node constraints. Stop only when every open node has an exact fathoming certificate. Return an exactly verified incumbent when all remaining nodes are exactly fathomed, or report exact infeasibility only when every leaf is certified infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Floating-point computations may propose search actions, but exact certificates must validate incumbents, cuts, pruning decisions, and the final conclusion.
assumptions_latex: The original model data are rational.
Every correctness-critical floating-point decision has an exact or certified fallback.
Cuts are accepted only after their validity for the relevant feasible set is certified exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unverified numerical results may influence search order but cannot determine elimination of feasible solutions or the final answer.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound used for node pruning.

children.title: Exact-Arithmetic Scalability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Runtime, memory, and encoding-size limits of exact regimes.

children.title: Exact Arithmetic Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of integer or rational encoding sizes during exact computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Arithmetic Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Determinant-based bit-length bounds for exact rational basis computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_B\in\mathbb Z^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular with \(|(A_B)_{ij}|<2^L\), and let \(b\in\mathbb Z^m\) satisfy \(|b_i|<2^{L_b}\). Hadamard's inequality gives \(|\det A_B|\le m^{m/2}2^{mL}\), so the binary length of \(\det A_B\) is at most \(mL+(m/2)\log_2 m+1\). By Cramer's rule, each coordinate of \(A_B^{-1}b\) can be represented with a denominator dividing \(\det A_B\); its unreduced numerator is a determinant bounded by \(m^{m/2}2^{(m-1)L+L_b}\). Consequently, reduced denominators have \(O(m(L+\log m))\) bits and reduced numerators have \(O((m-1)L+L_b+m\log m)\) bits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hadamard's inequality and Cramer's rule bound the bit lengths of exact basis-solution numerators and denominators in terms of the basis dimension and input bit lengths.
assumptions_latex: \(A_B\) is a nonsingular integer matrix in \(\mathbb Z^{m\times m}\).
Every entry of \(A_B\) has absolute value below \(2^L\).
The vector \(b\in\mathbb Z^m\) satisfies \(|b_i|<2^{L_b}\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact basis denominators have at most \(O(m(L+\log m))\) bits, with analogous numerator bounds incorporating \(L_b\).

notation.meaning: Bit-length bound for entries of the right-hand side.

children.title: Exact-Solve Runtime Overhead
children.top_down_role: Additional computation time imposed by exact arithmetic regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Solve Runtime Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-operation cost of normalized rational arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an exact solver performs \(k\) normalized rational arithmetic operations and all encountered numerators and denominators have at most \(B\) bits. Under a bit-complexity model in which multiplying two \(B\)-bit integers costs \(M(B)\), rational addition or multiplication followed by greatest-common-divisor reduction costs \(O(M(B)\log B)\) bit operations. Hence these \(k\) operations cost \(O(kM(B)\log B)\), excluding combinatorial search growth. A fixed-precision implementation treats corresponding machine operations as constant time, so coefficient growth creates runtime overhead absent from a unit-cost arithmetic count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact rational operations become more expensive as coefficient bit lengths grow, adding bit-complexity overhead beyond the branch-and-bound search itself.
assumptions_latex: All intermediate rational components have at most \(B\) bits.
Fractions are normalized using greatest-common-divisor computations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The arithmetic runtime is \(O(kM(B)\log B)\) under the stated bit model.

notation.meaning: Cost of multiplying two B-bit integers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated bit-operation estimate is plausible under the declared normalization and multiplication-cost model, but no authoritative source supports the gcd and rational-operation complexity bound.

children.title: Exact-Solve Memory Overhead
children.top_down_role: Additional storage requirements arising from exact numerical representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Solve Memory Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-storage overhead for explicitly represented exact rational solver data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an exact solver simultaneously stores \(q\) reduced rational numbers, each represented by a signed numerator and positive denominator with combined binary encoding length at most \(L\). Their explicit encodings require \(O(qL)\) bits. If every encoding has length at least \(L/2\), they require \(\Theta(qL)\) bits. By comparison, \(q\) fixed-width floating-point values of width \(w\) require \(\Theta(qw)\) bits. Under the lower-length condition, the exact-value storage overhead is therefore \(\Theta(L/w)\), excluding indexing, allocator, and proof-log storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit storage of q exact rationals uses at most order qL bits and uses order qL bits when every encoding has length comparable to L; in that case its overhead relative to w-bit floating-point storage is proportional to L divided by w.
assumptions_latex: \(q\ge 1\) rational values are stored explicitly.
\(L\ge 1\) bounds each value's combined numerator-denominator encoding length.
\(w\ge 1\) is the fixed floating-point width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{exact}}=O(qL)\), and under the lower-length condition \(M_{\mathrm{exact}}=\Theta(qL)\) and \(M_{\mathrm{exact}}/M_{\mathrm{float}}=\Theta(L/w)\).

notation.meaning: number of simultaneously stored rational values
maximum combined bit length per exact rational value

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct bit counting for explicit rational encodings

children.title: Exact-Regime Scalability Limits
children.top_down_role: Problem sizes or structures for which exact solving becomes impractical.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Regime Scalability Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource boundary induced jointly by exact object size and search-tree size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an exact branch-and-bound solve on an input of binary encoding length \(n\). Suppose it processes \(T\) nodes, retains at most \(S\) node records concurrently, and uses \(W_t\) bit operations and \(M_t\) bits of node-local exact data while processing node \(t\). Then the node-processing work is \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}W_t\), and peak node-local memory is at least \(\max_{1\le t\le T}M_t\). If each retained node record occupies at least one bit, peak record storage is also \(\Omega(S)\). Consequently, polynomial per-node arithmetic does not imply polynomial end-to-end resource use when the processed tree, exact encodings, or retained certificate objects have superpolynomial size as functions of \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial work at each exact branch-and-bound node does not ensure polynomial overall scaling when the search tree, exact encodings, or retained certificates grow superpolynomially with input length.
assumptions_latex: \(n\) is the binary encoding length of the input.
\(T\ge1\) nodes are processed and \(W_t\ge1\) for every processed node.
Node records, exact data, and retained proof objects are represented explicitly.

children.title: MIP Certificate Verification System
children.top_down_role: Checkable evidence for solver outcomes and the independent systems that validate it.

children.title: Primal Solution Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable evidence for candidate feasibility and objective value.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Solution Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for feasibility and objective value of a rational MILP candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization MILP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax\le b,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i\in I)\}\), a primal solution certificate is a rational vector \(\bar x\) together with the asserted value \(U\). It is valid exactly when an independent checker verifies \(A\bar x\le b\), verifies \(\bar x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\), and verifies \(U=c^T\bar x\), all in exact arithmetic. A valid certificate proves that the feasible set is nonempty and that the optimal value, when defined, is at most \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational candidate certifies primal feasibility and its objective value when every constraint, integrality condition, and objective evaluation checks exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) and \(\bar x\) are rational data.
The problem is interpreted as a minimization MILP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity implies \(\bar x\) is feasible, \(U=c^T\bar x\), and \(z^*\le U\) whenever \(z^*\) exists.

children.title: Global-Bound Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting global bounds and optimality conclusions.

children.title: Dual-Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable evidence supporting a claimed global objective bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-dual certificate of a global lower bound for a minimization MILP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the minimization MILP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i\in I)\}\). A rational vector \(y\) is a dual-bound certificate for its LP relaxation when \(y\ge0\) and \(A^Ty\le c\). Exact verification of these conditions certifies \(L=b^Ty\) as a lower bound on \(c^Tx\) for every mixed-integer feasible \(x\). The certificate does not assert that \(L\) is the strongest bound obtainable from the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly verified feasible dual vector for the LP relaxation certifies a lower bound on every mixed-integer feasible solution, without necessarily certifying the strongest relaxation bound.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) and \(y\) are rational.
The displayed LP relaxation contains every mixed-integer feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\ge0\) and \(A^Ty\le c\) imply \(c^Tx\ge L=b^Ty\) for every mixed-integer feasible \(x\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

children.title: Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable evidence supporting the conclusion that a feasible solution is globally optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certificate obtained by matching primal and global bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization MILP with optimal value \(z^*\), an optimality certificate consists of a valid primal certificate \((\bar x,U)\) and a valid global lower-bound certificate \(L\). If exact checking establishes \(U=c^T\bar x\), feasibility of \(\bar x\), validity of \(L\le c^Tx\) for every feasible \(x\), and \(L=U\), then \(L\le z^*\le U\) forces \(z^*=U\). Hence \(\bar x\) is globally optimal. With only \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), the objects certify an absolute optimality gap, not exact optimality unless \(\varepsilon=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible solution is exactly optimal when its verified objective equals a verified global lower bound; unequal bounds certify only a gap.
assumptions_latex: The MILP is a minimization problem.
Both component certificates are independently valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=U\) implies \(z^*=U\) and global optimality of \(\bar x\); \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) implies an absolute gap at most \(\varepsilon\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

children.title: Bound-Certificate Composition
children.top_down_role: Organization of local or global evidence contributing to a final bound claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Certificate Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of local relaxation bounds through a certified disjunctive cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of a minimization problem. Suppose a finite family \((R_k)_{k=1}^K\) has a checkable cover certificate \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^K R_k\), and each local certificate proves \(c^Tx\ge L_k\) for every \(x\in R_k\). Then \(L=\min_{1\le k\le K}L_k\) is a valid global lower bound on \(F\). A compositional certificate must therefore contain both the local bound derivations and evidence that the disjunction covers every feasible point; local bounds alone do not certify a global bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified bounds over search regions compose by taking their minimum, provided a separately checked disjunction proves that those regions cover the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite and positive.
The cover and every local lower bound are exactly checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^K R_k\) and \(c^Tx\ge L_k\) on each \(R_k\) imply \(c^Tx\ge\min_k L_k\) on \(F\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on region k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary composition of lower bounds over a finite certified cover

children.title: Optimality Verification Gaps
children.top_down_role: Unsupported solver components that prevent complete checking of an optimality claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Verification Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which reported bounds fail to constitute an exact optimality proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reported minimization incumbent \(\bar x\) and lower bound \(L\) do not certify exact optimality if any required implication is unchecked: primal feasibility or integrality of \(\bar x\), exact evaluation of \(c^T\bar x\), global validity of \(L\), exhaustive coverage of search regions, or equality \(L=c^T\bar x\). In particular, floating-point residual acceptance and a positive termination tolerance establish exact optimality only when accompanied by a sound conversion to exact inequalities. Otherwise the report may support an approximate claim but leaves a verification gap for exact global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality remains uncertified whenever primal checks, bound validity, search coverage, exact arithmetic, or equality of bounds is missing.
assumptions_latex: The intended conclusion is exact global optimality for a minimization MILP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure to verify any link needed for \(L\le z^*\le c^T\bar x=L\) prevents that chain from certifying exact optimality.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: failure follows from a missing premise in the bound-sandwich certificate

children.title: Terminal-Status Certificate Family
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting absence of feasible solutions or finite optima.

children.title: Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable evidence supporting the absence of feasible solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-cover certificate whose leaves carry exact Farkas contradictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{x:Ax\le b,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i\in I)\}\), an infeasibility certificate may consist of a finite branching tree whose valid branching disjunctions exhaust all points of \(F\). At every leaf \(k\), the resulting linear system \(A_kx\le b_k\) carries a rational multiplier \(y_k\ge0\) satisfying \(y_k^TA_k=0\) and \(y_k^Tb_k<0\). Exact verification of every branching disjunction and every leaf multiplier certifies \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MILP infeasibility is certified by an exhaustive finite branch cover when every leaf has an exactly verified Farkas contradiction.
assumptions_latex: All model and certificate data are rational.
Every branching disjunction is valid and exhaustively covers its parent region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid leaf contradictions together with exhaustive branching imply \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative Farkas multiplier at leaf k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Farkas contradictions composed over an exhaustive finite integer-branching tree

children.title: Unboundedness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable evidence supporting the absence of a finite optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-point and recession-direction certificate for mixed-integer unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax\le b,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i\in I)\}\), an unboundedness certificate consists of a feasible rational point \(\bar x\) and a nonzero rational direction \(d\) satisfying \(Ad\le0\), \(d_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\), and \(c^Td<0\). Exact verification of these conditions certifies that \(x^{(k)}=\bar x+kd\) is mixed-integer feasible for every \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) and that the objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and an exactly checked integer-compatible improving recession direction certify an infinite feasible sequence with objective unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c,\bar x,d\) are rational.
\(\bar x\) satisfies all constraints and integrality requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{(k)}=\bar x+kd\) is feasible for every \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\), and \(c^Tx^{(k)}\to-\infty\).

notation.meaning: feasible point generated at integer step k

children.title: Mixed-Integer Status Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate structures addressing discrete search contributions to global status.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Status Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate obligations for principal exact terminal statuses of a rational MILP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational minimization MILP, a terminal-status certificate is valid only when its payload proves the reported predicate: feasible requires an exactly checked mixed-integer point; optimal requires a valid primal point and matching global lower bound; infeasible requires exhaustive elimination of all mixed-integer feasible points; and unbounded requires a feasible sequence whose objective tends to \(-\infty\), for example through an integer-compatible improving recession direction. A status such as time limit, interrupted, or unknown records termination behavior but does not, without an additional payload, certify any of these mathematical predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each mathematical solver status has distinct proof obligations; operational termination statuses alone certify neither feasibility, optimality, infeasibility, nor unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: The model data and checked certificate payloads are rational.
Statuses use exact mathematical rather than tolerance-dependent semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reported status is certified precisely to the extent that its independently checkable payload entails the corresponding mathematical predicate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: status obligations are assembled from the component certificate predicates

children.title: Certificate Coverage Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model features or solver operations not represented in available status evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Coverage Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between checked certificate claims and unsupported solver behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a checker accept only a certificate language \(\mathcal C\) and inference rules \(\mathcal R\). Acceptance certifies a solver status only when every model transformation, relaxation, branch, cut, bound, and terminal argument needed for that status has a representation in \(\mathcal C\) and is validated by \(\mathcal R\). If an unsupported transformation changes the model used by later steps, or if a required phase is omitted without a checked equivalence or implication, acceptance of the remaining fragments does not entail the status of the original model. Certificate coverage is therefore claim-relative and end-to-end.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checker proves only claims covered by its language and rules; one unsupported or disconnected solver phase can break certification of the original model.
assumptions_latex: The checker is sound for the certificate constructs it implements.
The intended claim concerns the original input model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Checked fragments certify the original status only if their validated dependency chain covers every status-critical transformation and inference.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: soundness of a composed proof requires validation of every dependency

children.title: Cross-Phase Solver Proof Logs
children.top_down_role: Records connecting solver transformations and search conclusions.

children.title: Presolve Transformation Proof Logs
children.top_down_role: Records supporting presolve reductions, substitutions, eliminations, and reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Transformation Proof Logs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stepwise certificate connecting a presolved model to the original MILP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolve transformation proof log for an original model \(P_0\) is a finite sequence \((P_j,w_j)_{j=1}^r\), where each witness \(w_j\) lets an independent checker validate the relation between \(P_{j-1}\) and \(P_j\) required by the terminal claim. For optimality, the validated relations must transfer terminal primal witnesses to \(P_0\) and preserve the certified objective-bound relation, or otherwise establish equality of the two models' optimal values. For infeasibility, each step must validate that feasibility of \(P_{j-1}\) implies feasibility of \(P_j\). When every step has the required relation, a valid terminal certificate for \(P_r\) transfers the corresponding certified conclusion to \(P_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve proof log transfers a reduced-model certificate to the original model only when every transformation has a checked relation sufficient for that particular terminal claim, including both witness and bound transfer for optimality.
assumptions_latex: The transformation sequence is finite.
Each witness \(w_j\) is checked under the relation required by the terminal claim.
The terminal certificate for \(P_r\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validated claim-specific step relations transfer the certified terminal status from \(P_r\) to \(P_0\).

children.title: Cut Derivation Proof Logs
children.top_down_role: Records supporting the validity and use of generated cutting planes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Derivation Proof Logs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checkable log certifying every inequality added during branch-and-cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the initial relaxation be \(P_0=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\), with designated integer variables. A cut-derivation proof log is a sequence \((C_t,w_t)_{t=1}^T\), where \(C_t\) is an asserted inequality and \(w_t\) records a derivation accepted by a specified rule from rows of \(A x\le b\), branching assumptions, and earlier cuts \(C_s\) with \(s<t\). The log is valid if a checker verifies each derivation and hence establishes \(P_{t-1}\cap(\mathbb{Z}^I\times\mathbb{R}^{n-|I|})\subseteq C_t\). Therefore adding every logged cut preserves all feasible mixed-integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cut log gives a locally checkable derivation for every added inequality, establishing that no feasible mixed-integer solution is removed.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are represented exactly.
Every derivation rule used by the log has specified checker semantics.
Earlier logged cuts are referenced only after successful verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_0\cap(\mathbb{Z}^I\times\mathbb{R}^{n-|I|})=P_T\cap(\mathbb{Z}^I\times\mathbb{R}^{n-|I|})\).

notation.meaning: Relaxation after accepting the first t logged cuts.
Witness for the derivation of the t-th cut.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports formal MIP cut-proof logging semantics.
Exact supported inference rules remain system-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind fits the leaf, and the statement is internally plausible, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports the claimed proof-log semantics, supported derivation rules, or exact linking of verified cuts to preservation of mixed-integer feasibility. The listed branch-and-cut source does not establish certificate logging semantics.

children.title: Search Exhaustion Proof Logs
children.top_down_role: Records supporting node pruning, domain partitioning, and search completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Exhaustion Proof Logs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite branch-and-bound certificate for infeasibility or an optimal objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization over a mixed-integer feasible set \(F\), a search-exhaustion log consists of a finite rooted branching tree, a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\) of value \(U=c^\top\bar x\) when one exists, and a certificate at every leaf. Each internal node partitions its parent domain into its children. Each leaf certificate verifies exactly one of: infeasibility of its relaxation, a valid lower bound \(L\ge U\), or an integral feasible solution already accounted for with value at least \(U\). If all partitions and leaf certificates verify, every point of \(F\) is covered and no point has objective below \(U\); without an incumbent, infeasibility at every leaf certifies \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified branching coverage and verified pruning at every leaf certify either global optimality of the incumbent or infeasibility of the model.
assumptions_latex: The search tree is finite and every branching disjunction is exhaustive.
All node relaxations and bound calculations have exact checker semantics.
The objective is minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in F\) and \(c^\top\bar x=\min_{x\in F}c^\top x\), or \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Objective value of the certified incumbent.
A certified lower bound at a search node.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically addresses search-exhaustion proof logs.
Treatment of unboundedness and numerical tolerances requires a format-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind fits the leaf and the finite-tree optimality argument is plausible under the stated assumptions. However, no source supports this exact search-exhaustion certificate model, the admissible leaf certificates, or their checker semantics. A format-specific source is also needed to determine whether unboundedness must be represented explicitly.

children.title: Cross-Phase Proof Dependencies
children.top_down_role: Links among transformations, cuts, bounds, and search conclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Phase Proof Dependencies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency condition connecting presolve, cutting, and search certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a solver proof as a directed graph \(G=(V,E)\), whose vertices are logged claims and whose edge \((u,v)\) means that verification of \(v\) uses claim \(u\). Cross-phase verification is well founded precisely when \(G\) is acyclic, every external reference resolves to an authenticated model or previously verified claim, and each claim is checked under the model state produced by all of its predecessors. A topological verification order must therefore place each presolve equivalence before dependent cuts, each cut before dependent node bounds, and each incumbent or bound before pruning claims that cite it. Acceptance requires every reachable dependency to verify.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cross-phase proof is checkable when its dependency graph is acyclic, all references resolve, and every claim is checked after its prerequisites.
assumptions_latex: Each log entry has a unique stable identifier.
Model transformations expose explicit state-transition semantics.
Dependency edges include every premise used by a claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) admits a topological order in which every accepted claim has only authenticated or previously accepted premises.

notation.meaning: Directed dependency graph of proof claims.
Claim v depends on claim u.

review_flags: No supplied source specifies a cross-phase MIP proof dependency model.
Presolve proof-log node is outside this shard and cannot be cited by identifier.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits the leaf, but the claim that cross-phase verification is well founded precisely when the dependency graph is acyclic is framework-dependent and may overstate necessity for systems that validate mutually dependent claims collectively. No source defines the proposed MIP proof-dependency model or supports the exact cross-phase ordering requirements.

children.title: Certificate Exchange-Verification Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces and representations shared by solvers and independent verifiers.

children.title: Certificate Exchange Formats
children.top_down_role: Portable encodings for solver-produced certificates and proof records.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Exchange Formats
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract syntax and semantics required for portable MIP certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate exchange format is a tuple \(\mathcal F=(\Sigma,\mathsf{parse},\mathsf{sem},\mathsf{ver})\). Here \(\Sigma^*\) is the set of serialized byte strings, \(\mathsf{parse}:\Sigma^*\rightharpoonup A\) is a partial parser into abstract syntax \(A\), \(\mathsf{sem}:A\rightharpoonup C\) assigns mathematical certificate objects, and \(\mathsf{ver}:M\times C\to\{0,1\}\) verifies them against models \(M\). The format is semantically adequate for a certificate class \(C_0\subseteq C\) when every \(c\in C_0\) has some serialization \(s\) satisfying \(\mathsf{sem}(\mathsf{parse}(s))=c\). Malformed, ambiguous, or unsupported serializations must be rejected rather than assigned unintended semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A portable format specifies serialization, parsing, mathematical meaning, and verification, with rejection of malformed or unsupported certificates.
assumptions_latex: Parsing and semantic interpretation are deterministic partial functions.
The model and numeric encodings have fixed exact meanings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall c\in C_0\;\exists s\in\Sigma^*:\mathsf{sem}(\mathsf{parse}(s))=c\).

notation.meaning: Finite serialized strings in the exchange alphabet.

review_flags: The supplied source hints do not document MIP certificate exchange formats.
Concrete syntax and supported certificate classes are format-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits the leaf, but the tuple is an abstract design proposed without supporting evidence. Because parse and sem are partial, the adequacy equation also requires an explicit assertion that both compositions are defined. No source in the inventory documents a MIP certificate exchange format with these syntax, semantic, and verification components.

children.title: Independent Certificate Checkers
children.top_down_role: Verifier interfaces for parsing and validating certificate artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Certificate Checkers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification performed independently of the solver that produced the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an encoded model \(m\), certificate \(s\), parser \(P\), and small verification kernel \(K\), independently compute \(M=P(m)\) and \(C=P(s)\); reject if either parse fails. Process certificate claims in dependency order. For each claim \(q_t\), invoke \(K(M,q_t,Q_{<t})\), where \(Q_{<t}\) contains only previously accepted claims; reject upon the first failure. Accept only if all claims verify and the final claim states the requested conclusion, such as infeasibility or optimality. Independence requires that acceptance use neither the producer solver's internal state nor an unverified solver-computed assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent checker reparses the model and certificate, verifies every claim in dependency order, and never trusts hidden producer state.
assumptions_latex: The checker implementation is separate from the certificate-producing solver.
All accepted inference rules are implemented by the verification kernel.
The final claim explicitly identifies the certified result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{Check}(m,s)=1\) only if every certificate dependency and the requested terminal claim are accepted by \(K\).

notation.meaning: Independent parser for models and certificates.
Claims accepted before the current claim.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports an independent MIP certificate-checking algorithm.
Required independence criteria vary across assurance frameworks.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the leaf and the procedure is coherent, but no cited source supports this particular independent-checking algorithm, trusted-kernel interface, or definition of independence. Those details vary materially among certificate systems and assurance frameworks.

children.title: Certificate Canonicalization
children.top_down_role: Stable representations for comparison, archival, and checker interoperability.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Canonicalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving normalization before certificate comparison or checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be certificate abstract syntax with semantic map \(\llbracket\cdot\rrbracket:A\rightharpoonup C\). A canonicalizer \(N:A\rightharpoonup A\) validates an input and then deterministically normalizes numeric encodings, orders commutative collections by a fixed total order, removes permitted syntactic redundancies, and renumbers identifiers by first dependency-respecting occurrence. It must satisfy semantic preservation \(\llbracket N(a)\rrbracket=\llbracket a\rrbracket\), idempotence \(N(N(a))=N(a)\), and uniqueness: whenever \(a\) and \(b\) differ only by the declared syntactic equivalences, \(N(a)=N(b)\). Inputs outside the supported grammar or equivalence theory are rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalization deterministically removes declared syntactic variation while preserving certificate meaning, producing an idempotent normal form.
assumptions_latex: The format defines exact numeric encodings and a total ordering of syntax.
The allowed syntactic equivalences are explicitly enumerated.
Canonicalization occurs only after structural validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\llbracket N(a)\rrbracket=\llbracket a\rrbracket\) and \(N(N(a))=N(a)\) for every supported \(a\).

notation.meaning: Mathematical meaning of syntax object a.

review_flags: No supplied source defines canonicalization for MIP certificates.
Permitted equivalences and identifier normalization are format-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the leaf, but semantic preservation, idempotence, uniqueness, identifier renumbering, and the declared syntactic equivalence relation are format-specific obligations. No source defines these obligations for a MIP certificate format, so the proposed canonicalizer cannot be assessed reliably.

children.title: Format-to-Checker Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Supported pairings between certificate encodings and verification tools.

assumptions_latex: The format profile \(R\) declares all permitted constructs.
Format and checker semantics are deterministic.
Unsupported constructs cause explicit rejection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall s\in R\), successful checking implies \(\llbracket P_K(s)\rrbracket_K=\llbracket s\rrbracket_F\).

notation.meaning: Certificate exchange format with declared semantics.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifies a format-to-checker compatibility relation.
The malformed checker symbol has been repaired; compatibility details remain format- and checker-specific.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition under which a checker soundly consumes an exchange format.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a format \(F\) assign semantics \(\llbracket s\rrbracket_F\) to supported serializations \(s\), and let checker \(K\) implement parser \(P_K\) and verification semantics \(\llbracket\cdot\rrbracket_K\). The pair \((F,K)\) is compatible for profile \(R\) if every \(s\in R\) is parsed or rejected according to \(F\), every successful parse satisfies \(\llbracket P_K(s)\rrbracket_K=\llbracket s\rrbracket_F\), and every inference tag, numeric domain, model feature, dependency convention, and terminal claim used by \(s\) is supported by \(K\). Compatibility is profile-specific; accepting an unknown or differently interpreted construct violates it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checker is compatible with a format profile only when parsing, semantics, numeric domains, inference rules, and terminal claims agree exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Format-to-Checker Compatibility

children.title: Certificate Checker Coverage Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits arising from parsers, formats, reductions, cuts, and plugins lacking checkable interpretations.

children.title: Parser Trust Boundary
children.top_down_role: Reliance on certificate decoding, numeric parsing, and input validation.

knowledge_statements.title: Parser Trust Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound verification fails if serialized input is misinterpreted before kernel checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) map serialized model-certificate pairs \(s\) to internal objects and let \(K\) soundly verify internal objects. End-to-end soundness does not follow from soundness of \(K\) alone: it additionally requires that every accepted \(s\) satisfy \(\llbracket P(s)\rrbracket=\llbracket s\rrbracket_F\), where \(\llbracket\cdot\rrbracket_F\) is the format's declared meaning. If some accepted \(s\) is truncated, rounded, overflowed, ambiguously tokenized, or otherwise mapped to a different mathematical object, then \(K(P(s))=1\) certifies only the misparsed object. Thus the parser lies inside the trusted computing boundary unless its translation is independently validated or certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound kernel cannot compensate for a parser that changes the model or certificate meaning; parsing must be trusted or independently validated.
assumptions_latex: The checker kernel operates only on parsed internal objects.
Certificate claims refer to the mathematical object denoted by the serialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(P(s))=1\) certifies the intended input only if \(\llbracket P(s)\rrbracket=\llbracket s\rrbracket_F\).

notation.meaning: Declared mathematical meaning of serialized input.

review_flags: No supplied source directly addresses parser trust in certificate verification.
Concrete parsing hazards depend on the selected exchange format and implementation language.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf, and the distinction between serialized and parsed semantics is coherent. Nevertheless, the trusted-computing-boundary conclusion and listed parsing hazards require a certificate-system or assurance source; none is cited, and the local inventory does not address parser trust in MIP certificate verification.

children.title: Checker Kernel Trust Boundary
children.top_down_role: Reliance on the minimal verification engine and its arithmetic services.

knowledge_statements.title: Checker Kernel Trust Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual assumptions remaining after all certificate claims have been replayed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the kernel deciding whether parsed model-certificate pairs satisfy the inference rules. Certificate acceptance establishes the advertised mathematical conclusion only relative to the correctness of \(K\)'s implementations of exact arithmetic, inference-rule side conditions, dependency resolution, and terminal-claim interpretation. If there exists an input \(z\) for which \(K(z)=1\) although some accepted inference is invalid under the declared semantics, a producer can embed that inference in a certificate and obtain false acceptance. Consequently, proof logging reduces the trusted base to the parser, kernel, and execution substrate; it does not eliminate trust in those components unless they are themselves formally verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate replay shifts trust into the checker kernel; a bug in any accepted inference rule can permit a false certificate.
assumptions_latex: All solver claims reaching acceptance are replayed by \(K\).
The execution substrate behaves according to the kernel's arithmetic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{Sound}(K)\) is necessary for \(K(z)=1\Rightarrow\mathsf{Valid}(z)\).

notation.meaning: The certificate conclusion is mathematically valid for its model.

review_flags: No supplied source directly characterizes a MIP checker kernel trust boundary.
Formal trusted-computing-base claims require implementation-specific evidence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf, but the exact kernel obligations and assertion that proof logging reduces the trusted base to the parser, kernel, and execution substrate are implementation-specific. No cited source supports this trust-boundary characterization or identifies the actual verified inference kernel.

children.title: Unsupported Solver Reductions
children.top_down_role: Presolve or transformation records lacking a checkable interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Solver Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve or propagation steps outside the checker's transformation calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a solver transform model \(M_0\) through reductions \(M_{t+1}=R_t(M_t)\), and let a checker support a rule set \(\mathcal R_K\). A solver reduction \(R_t\notin\mathcal R_K\) creates a coverage gap whenever later certificate claims are interpreted over \(M_{t+1}\) but no independently checkable witness relates its feasible solutions and objective values to those of \(M_t\). In that case, verification of the residual search proves a statement only about the reduced model. Global infeasibility or optimality for \(M_0\) may be accepted only if the unsupported reduction is disabled, expanded into supported rules, or accompanied by a separately verified equivalence or implication certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified search on a reduced model does not certify the original model unless every reduction has a supported or separately verified justification.
assumptions_latex: The solver performs at least one model-changing reduction.
The terminal claim concerns the original model \(M_0\).
The checker verifies subsequent claims against the reduced state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_t\notin\mathcal R_K\) without a verified linking witness prevents end-to-end certification of \(M_0\).

notation.meaning: Reduction producing the next model state.
Reduction rules supported by the checker.

review_flags: No supplied locator documents proof-producing MIP presolve reductions.
The exact linking obligation depends on whether a reduction preserves feasibility, objective value, or only one implication.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf and the coverage-gap concern is plausible. However, the required linking certificate depends on whether each reduction preserves feasibility, optimal value, or only a directional implication. No source specifies proof-producing presolve semantics or the supported reduction calculus, so the exact claim is not reliable enough to accept.

children.title: Unsupported Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Generated inequalities whose derivations cannot be verified by the checker.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Cut Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts whose validity cannot be reconstructed by the checker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a node relaxation, \(S=P\cap(\mathbb{Z}^I\times\mathbb{R}^{n-|I|})\), and let a solver add \(C=\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\). If the checker lacks a supported derivation establishing \(S\subseteq C\), then later node bounds, pruning decisions, and exhaustion claims computed from \(P\cap C\) are not certificates for \(P\). Even when the cut family is mathematically valid in general, omitted side conditions, scaling, or numerical reconstruction can invalidate the particular row. End-to-end certification therefore requires disabling the family, translating each cut into supported inference steps, or supplying a directly checkable validity witness for every instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unverified cut breaks certification of every later bound or pruning decision that depends on it, even if its cut family is generally valid.
assumptions_latex: The unsupported cut participates in a relaxation used for certified pruning or bounding.
Cut coefficients and right-hand side affect the checked relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq C\) must be verified before conclusions derived from \(P\cap C\) certify conclusions about \(P\).

notation.meaning: Half-space defined by the added cut.

review_flags: The branch-and-cut locator supplied does not specifically support certificate coverage boundaries.
Supported cut families and validity witnesses are checker-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf, and the mathematical inclusion required for a valid cut is clearly stated. The cited inventory contains only general branch-and-cut material, not certificate coverage, supported cut derivations, or per-instance validity witnesses. Those checker-specific claims therefore require a direct source.

children.title: Opaque Plugin Contributions
children.top_down_role: Custom component conclusions lacking portable verification evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Opaque Plugin Contributions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unlogged solver-plugin effects that influence a purportedly certified conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a plugin produce a claim \(q\) or modify model state \(M\) during solving. Its contribution is opaque to a checker when the certificate records neither a supported derivation of \(q\) nor a verified transition from \(M\) to the modified state \(M'\). If any accepted cut, bound, incumbent, branching restriction, reduction, or pruning decision depends transitively on that contribution, replay of the remaining log certifies only a computation conditional on the opaque assertion. End-to-end certification requires that the plugin emit checker-supported witnesses, that its output be independently recomputed, or that all dependent claims be excluded and regenerated without the plugin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unlogged plugin contribution leaves every dependent certificate claim conditional on an unchecked assertion, breaking end-to-end assurance.
assumptions_latex: The plugin can alter solver claims or mathematical state.
At least one terminally relevant claim depends on the plugin output.
The checker does not independently reproduce that output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\leadsto r\) and unchecked \(q\) imply that verification of terminal claim \(r\) is incomplete.

notation.meaning: Terminal claim r depends transitively on plugin contribution q.
Model states before and after a plugin modification.

review_flags: No supplied source treats opaque solver plugins in MIP certificate systems.
Plugin interfaces and their possible mathematical effects are implementation-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf and the conditional-dependency concern is coherent. No source documents opaque plugin contributions in a MIP certificate system, the mathematical effects available through the relevant plugin interface, or the proposed remedies. These implementation-specific semantics require direct evidence.

children.title: Solver Observability
children.top_down_role: Logs, statistics, traces, and event interfaces used to diagnose an individual solve.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Solving Statistics, Display Columns, and Event Handling

children.title: Optimization Progress Log Family
children.top_down_role: Progress views centered on incumbent and relaxation bounds.

children.title: Primal-Bound Progress Logs
children.top_down_role: Incumbent objective changes and feasible-solution milestones.

assumptions_latex: The MIP is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\) and objective \(c^\top x\).
Log events are indexed chronologically by \(k=0,1,\ldots\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recorded sequence \((U_k)\) is nonincreasing whenever incumbent updates are accepted exactly.

notation.meaning: Best objective value among feasible solutions accepted through event k
Accepted incumbent solution at event k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention; infeasibility and numerical acceptance statuses must be logged separately.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At event \(k\), a primal-bound progress log records \(U_k=\min\{c^\top x:x\in F\text{ has been accepted by event }k\}\), with \(U_k=+\infty\) if no feasible incumbent has been accepted. When a newly accepted solution \(x_k^{I}\in F\) satisfies \(c^\top x_k^{I}<U_{k-1}\), the update is \(U_k=c^\top x_k^{I}\); otherwise \(U_k=U_{k-1}\). Each entry should identify the event index and incumbent objective, and may additionally record elapsed time, processed-node count, and incumbent source.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-bound log records the best accepted feasible objective over time; for minimization, its finite values cannot increase.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Bound Progress Logs

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Dual-Bound Progress Logs
children.top_down_role: Global lower- or upper-bound changes during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Progress Logs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound minimization convention with valid, inherited node lower bounds; terminal empty-tree states are logged separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After event \(k\), let \(\mathcal A_k\) contain all active nodes, and let \(\ell_v\) be a valid lower bound for every feasible integer solution in node \(v\). When \(\mathcal A_k\ne\varnothing\), define the global dual bound by \(L_k=\min_{v\in\mathcal A_k}\ell_v\). A dual-bound progress log records \(L_k\), its event index, and preferably elapsed time and processed-node count. If every child or recomputed node bound is no smaller than the bound it replaces, then valid branching and removal of nodes imply \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\) for consecutive events with nonempty active sets. When \(\mathcal A_k=\varnothing\), the solver's terminal status and bound convention are recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-bound log tracks the minimum valid bound over active nodes; it cannot decrease when replacement bounds inherit their predecessors, while an empty active set requires a separate terminal convention.
assumptions_latex: The MIP is a minimization problem, and every active search node \(v\) has a valid lower bound \(\ell_v\).
Log events are indexed chronologically by \(k=0,1,\ldots\).
Every child or recomputed node bound is no smaller than the bound of the node it replaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For consecutive events satisfying \(\mathcal A_k\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal A_{k+1}\ne\varnothing\), the recorded bounds satisfy \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\).

notation.meaning: Set of active, unpruned search nodes after event k
Valid lower bound attached to node v
Global dual bound after event k when the active set is nonempty

children.title: Optimality-Gap Progress Logs
children.top_down_role: Absolute and relative gap evolution across solver time.

assumptions_latex: The MIP is a minimization problem with finite incumbent \(U_k\) and valid dual bound \(L_k\le U_k\).
A positive scaling floor \(\epsilon_s>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The logged absolute and relative gaps are nonnegative and vanish when \(U_k=L_k\).

notation.meaning: Absolute optimality gap at event k
Scaled relative optimality gap at event k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses an explicit symmetric scaling convention; solver-native percentages may differ.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At event \(k\), define the absolute gap by \(g_k^{\mathrm{abs}}=U_k-L_k\) and the relative gap by \(g_k^{\mathrm{rel}}=(U_k-L_k)/\max\{\epsilon_s,|U_k|,|L_k|\}\). An optimality-gap progress log records these quantities with the underlying \((U_k,L_k)\), event index, and scaling convention. If no finite incumbent exists, the gap is reported as infinite or undefined rather than evaluated by the displayed quotient. Under valid bounds, both finite gaps are nonnegative and equal zero when the bounds coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gap log derives absolute and scaled relative distances from the incumbent and dual bounds, while explicitly handling a missing incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Gap Progress Logs

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Bound-Crossover Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Interactions between incumbent improvement and relaxation-bound progress.
