assumptions_latex: The MIP is a minimization problem with logged incumbent \(U_k\) and dual bound \(L_k\).
The solver declares absolute bound tolerance \(\tau_k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An event with \(L_k>U_k+\tau_k\) is a bound-crossover anomaly requiring investigation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic condition, not an optimality theorem; tolerances and bound provenance remain observable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every event having finite bounds, compute \(r_k=L_k-U_k\). Exact valid minimization bounds require \(r_k\le0\). The diagnostic classifies \(0<r_k\le\tau_k\) as a tolerance-scale crossover and \(r_k>\tau_k\) as an anomalous crossover. An anomaly entry records \((k,U_k,L_k,r_k,\tau_k)\), the bound-producing subsystems, and whether values were rounded for display. It does not itself establish which bound is invalid; it flags inconsistency among feasibility acceptance, relaxation validity, numerical tolerances, or reporting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A crossover diagnostic flags when a reported lower bound exceeds the incumbent beyond tolerance, which valid exact minimization bounds cannot do.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Crossover Diagnostics

children.title: Search Processing Statistics Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Search-size and node-processing diagnostic views.

children.title: Search-Tree Statistics
children.top_down_role: Tree size, depth, frontier composition, and pruning summaries.

assumptions_latex: A branch-and-bound run maintains a rooted search tree through observation event \(k\).
Every generated node has one recorded status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The counters satisfy \(N_k^{\mathrm{gen}}=N_k^{\mathrm{open}}+N_k^{\mathrm{proc}}\) under the stated exclusive status convention.

notation.meaning: Number of generated nodes through event k
Number of generated but unprocessed nodes
Number of nodes whose processing has completed

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counters require explicit generated, open, processed, and pruned status conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At event \(k\), search-tree statistics report \(N_k^{\mathrm{gen}}\), \(N_k^{\mathrm{open}}\), \(N_k^{\mathrm{proc}}\), current depth, and maximum attained depth. Under the convention that every generated node is exclusively either open or completely processed, \(N_k^{\mathrm{gen}}=N_k^{\mathrm{open}}+N_k^{\mathrm{proc}}\). Pruned nodes are included among processed nodes and may be partitioned by reason, such as infeasibility, domination by the incumbent, or integrality. The root counts as a generated node unless the log explicitly declares another convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search-tree statistics count generated, open, processed, and pruned nodes and report depth under an explicit counting convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Statistics

children.title: Node-Processing Statistics
children.top_down_role: Node throughput, processing time, and node-status distributions.

assumptions_latex: Each generated search node is processed at most once under the reported accounting convention.
Processing outcomes form disjoint recorded classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sum of outcome counts equals the completed-node count.

notation.meaning: Nodes completely processed through event k
Set of mutually exclusive processing outcomes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies only when processing outcomes are exclusive and exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be an exhaustive set of mutually exclusive completed-processing outcomes, for example infeasible, bound-pruned, integral, or branched. If \(N_{k,q}\) counts nodes assigned outcome \(q\in Q\) by event \(k\), then \(N_k^{\mathrm{proc}}=\sum_{q\in Q}N_{k,q}\). A node-processing report also records total processing time \(T_k^{\mathrm{proc}}\) and, when \(N_k^{\mathrm{proc}}>0\), mean time \(T_k^{\mathrm{proc}}/N_k^{\mathrm{proc}}\). Interrupted or suspended nodes must be excluded or represented by a separate noncompleted status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node-processing statistics partition completed nodes by outcome and relate total processing time to the completed-node count.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Processing Statistics

children.title: Node-Relaxation Statistics
children.top_down_role: Relaxation solves, iterations, failures, and per-node effort.

assumptions_latex: Each recorded node-relaxation solve has a declared relaxation type and termination status.
Work measures use one fixed unit, such as simplex iterations or barrier iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Aggregate relaxation work equals the sum of the recorded per-solve work values.

notation.meaning: Number of node-relaxation solves through event k
Work charged to relaxation solve j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work units must not combine incomparable LP, QP, or NLP iteration measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Through event \(k\), node-relaxation statistics record the number \(R_k\) of relaxation solves and partition them by termination status, such as optimal, infeasible, unbounded, limited, or numerical failure. If \(w_j\ge0\) is the declared work measure for solve \(j\), aggregate work is \(W_k^{\mathrm{rel}}=\sum_{j=1}^{R_k}w_j\), and mean work is \(W_k^{\mathrm{rel}}/R_k\) when \(R_k>0\). Reoptimizations and repeated solves at one node count separately unless the log explicitly aggregates them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node-relaxation statistics count solves, statuses, and comparable work units, including repeated solves when the convention treats them separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Relaxation Statistics

children.title: Tree-to-Relaxation Cost Attribution
children.top_down_role: Allocation of relaxation workload across search-tree regions.

assumptions_latex: Total node-processing time is partitioned by an explicitly declared charging rule.
All attributed times use the same clock and unit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The attributed relaxation fraction lies in \([0,1]\) when the time partition is exhaustive and nonoverlapping.

notation.meaning: Total time charged to node processing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock attribution requires an explicit rule for nesting and parallel execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under an exhaustive, nonoverlapping charging rule, node-processing time decomposes as \(T_k^{\mathrm{node}}=T_k^{\mathrm{rel}}+T_k^{\mathrm{other}}\), where both terms are nonnegative. If \(T_k^{\mathrm{node}}>0\), the relaxation share is \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{rel}}=T_k^{\mathrm{rel}}/T_k^{\mathrm{node}}\in[0,1]\). The report must identify whether the quantities are CPU time, summed thread time, or elapsed time. When relaxation work overlaps other processing or parallel solves overlap each other, equality is valid only after applying the declared attribution rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cost attribution decomposes node-processing time into relaxation and other work, with clock and overlap conventions stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-to-Relaxation Cost Attribution

children.title: Solver Subsystem Statistics
children.top_down_role: Subsystem activity and resource-consumption summaries.

children.title: Presolve Statistics
children.top_down_role: Reduction counts, rounds, timing, and problem-size changes.

assumptions_latex: Presolve transforms an original formulation into a reduced formulation while maintaining a declared recovery map.
Statistics are measured at fixed presolve checkpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each reported reduction is the initial count minus the corresponding remaining count.

notation.meaning: Numbers of removed variables and constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts describe formulation reduction, not by themselves correctness of the recovery map.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Presolve statistics record initial and remaining formulation dimensions and the activity of individual reduction classes. With \(n_0,m_0\) denoting original variable and constraint counts and \(n_p,m_p\) their post-presolve counts, the reported reductions are \(\Delta n=n_0-n_p\) and \(\Delta m=m_0-m_p\). The report should separately count fixed variables, tightened bounds, removed constraints, detected infeasibility, and presolve passes, and should record presolve time. Negative reductions require an explanation when reformulation introduces auxiliary rows or variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve statistics quantify dimension reductions, bound changes, passes, time, and exceptional growth caused by reformulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Statistics

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

children.title: Cutting-Plane Statistics
children.top_down_role: Cut generation, filtering, application, efficacy, and resource use.

assumptions_latex: Each generated inequality is assigned to one cut family and one generation round.
The log distinguishes generated, accepted, and active cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every family and round, the active-cut count cannot exceed the accepted count, which cannot exceed the generated count.

notation.meaning: Generated, accepted, and active cuts for family f in round r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Statistics require exclusive family assignment or an explicit multiple-attribution convention.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each cut family \(f\) and separation round \(r\), let \(G_{f,r}\), \(A_{f,r}\), and \(C_{f,r}\) count generated, accepted into the relaxation, and currently active cuts. Consistent accounting requires \(0\le C_{f,r}\le A_{f,r}\le G_{f,r}\). Cutting-plane statistics also record rounds, separation time, and cuts removed from the relaxation. Aggregation over families is additive only when every cut receives exactly one family label; otherwise the report must declare its multiple-attribution convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cutting-plane statistics track generated, accepted, active, and removed cuts by family and round, together with separation time.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutting-Plane Statistics

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Primal-Heuristic Statistics
children.top_down_role: Heuristic calls, solution discoveries, timing, and success rates.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Heuristic Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A call may return multiple solutions only if the counting convention explicitly permits it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each primal heuristic \(h\), statistics record calls \(K_h\), feasible solutions found \(F_h\), accepted incumbent improvements \(I_h\), and attributed time \(T_h\ge0\). Under a convention allowing at most one returned solution per call, \(0\le I_h\le F_h\le K_h\). If calls may return multiple solutions, only \(I_h\le F_h\) is required. The report should distinguish failure, interruption, infeasible output, nonimproving feasible output, and improving output, and state how shared solutions are attributed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-heuristic statistics count calls, feasible discoveries, incumbent improvements, outcomes, and attributed time under a stated solution-counting convention.
assumptions_latex: Every heuristic invocation has one declared heuristic label and terminal status.
Every accepted heuristic solution is feasible under the solver's acceptance tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every heuristic \(h\), \(0\le I_h\le F_h\); if at most one solution is returned per call, then additionally \(F_h\le K_h\).

notation.meaning: Calls, feasible solutions found, and improving solutions for heuristic h
Execution time attributed to heuristic h

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Plugin Activity Statistics
children.top_down_role: Invocation, timing, memory, and outcome summaries by plugin.

assumptions_latex: Each plugin invocation is assigned a plugin identifier and a terminal status.
Resource measurements use declared units and an explicit attribution rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each plugin, the sum of mutually exclusive terminal-status counts equals its completed invocation count.

notation.meaning: Completed invocations of plugin p having status s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic accounting schema; concrete statuses and resource semantics are solver-interface dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For plugin \(p\), activity statistics record completed invocations \(K_p\), terminal-status counts \(K_{p,s}\), and attributed resource use. If \(S_p\) is exhaustive and its statuses are mutually exclusive, then \(K_p=\sum_{s\in S_p}K_{p,s}\). The record identifies the plugin role, execution phase, number of interrupted or pending invocations, outputs produced and accepted, and the measurement unit for resource use. Nested or concurrent plugin executions require an explicit attribution rule before per-plugin times may be summed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plugin statistics count invocations, outcomes, accepted outputs, and resources while declaring status, nesting, and concurrency conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Activity Statistics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the proposed plugin invocation, status, output-acceptance, or resource-attribution schema. An authoritative solver plugin-interface or statistics reference with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Subsystem Resource Attribution
children.top_down_role: Comparative accounting of time and memory across solver subsystems.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsystem Resource Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive accounting of solver resources across possibly nested MIP subsystems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite set of solver subsystems and \(R\) a set of resource types. A subsystem resource attribution is a map \(a:S\times R\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), together with measured totals \(T_r\), such that \(\sum_{s\in S}a(s,r)\le T_r\) for every \(r\in R\). Equality holds when attribution is exhaustive and subsystem scopes are disjoint; otherwise \(u_r=T_r-\sum_{s\in S}a(s,r)\ge0\) is the unattributed amount. For nested or overlapping scopes, an explicit ownership rule must prevent double counting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource attribution assigns nonnegative resource use to solver subsystems, reconciles it with measured totals, and records any unattributed amount while preventing double counting.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(R\) are finite.
All measurements use a common resource unit and observation interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_r=\sum_{s\in S}a(s,r)+u_r\) with \(u_r\ge0\) for every \(r\in R\).

notation.meaning: resource of type r attributed to subsystem s
measured total consumption of resource r

review_flags: solver-specific accounting semantics require an authoritative implementation or observability reference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The accounting definition is plausible, but no cited source supports additivity, exhaustiveness, ownership, or double-counting conventions for solver subsystems.

children.title: Solver Observation Interface
children.top_down_role: Programmatic observation of solver-state changes.

children.title: Solver Event Tracing
children.top_down_role: Structured capture of solver-state changes and component activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver Event Tracing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured, ordered observation of discrete events during one solver run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a solver run on time domain \(\mathcal T\), an event trace is a finite or countable sequence \(\tau=((t_k,q_k,p_k))_{k\in K}\), where \(t_k\in\mathcal T\) is nondecreasing, \(q_k\) is an event type, and \(p_k\) is a payload valid for that type. Each record must identify the run and preserve a deterministic tie-breaking order among equal timestamps. The trace is complete relative to an event set \(Q\) when every emitted event with type in \(Q\) appears exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver event trace is an ordered sequence of timestamped, typed events with validated payloads and explicit run identity.
assumptions_latex: Each emitted event has a well-defined type and payload schema.
Equal timestamps admit a recorded tie-breaking order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\) defines an ordered observation history, complete relative to \(Q\) exactly when all selected emitted events occur once.
review_flags: trace semantics and completeness conventions require a solver-interface source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed trace model is coherent, but the run-identity, deterministic tie-breaking, and relative-completeness requirements need an authoritative solver-interface source.

children.title: External Monitoring Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Programmatic access to live progress, resource, and status information.

knowledge_statements.title: External Monitoring Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Read-only exposure of solver observations to a process outside the solving core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_t\) be the internal solver state and \(Y\) an externally visible observation space. An external monitoring interface is a read-only map \(M:X_t\mapsto y_t\in Y\), possibly sampled only at times in \(T_M\), together with a serialization and transport convention. It is observational when invoking \(M\) cannot directly alter feasible sets, bounds, incumbent acceptance, branching decisions, or stopping rules; any timing perturbation caused by monitoring must be separately measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external monitoring interface exports serialized observations without directly changing the solver’s mathematical decisions, while exposing or measuring timing perturbations.
assumptions_latex: The solver state and exposed observation schema are specified.
Monitoring calls are separated from control callbacks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) yields externally consumable observations while remaining read-only with respect to solver decisions.

notation.meaning: internal solver state at time t

review_flags: read-only and timing semantics require an authoritative solver-interface source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source establishes the asserted read-only and timing semantics. Moreover, the notation M:X_t\mapsto y_t treats X_t both as a state and as a map domain; a sourced revision should distinguish the state space from its time-indexed elements.

children.title: Trace Filtering Regimes
children.top_down_role: Selection of event classes, verbosity levels, and observation scopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Trace Filtering Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicates defining which solver events are retained or transmitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an event trace \(\tau=(e_k)_{k\in K}\), a trace-filtering regime is a predicate \(F(e_k,h_{k-1})\in\{0,1\}\), where \(h_{k-1}\) is the retained history available before event \(e_k\). The filtered trace is \(\tau_F=(e_k:F(e_k,h_{k-1})=1)\) in original order. A regime is type-static when \(F\) depends only on event type, threshold-based when it also depends on payload values, and stateful when it depends on \(h_{k-1}\). Audit completeness for event set \(Q\) requires \(F(e,h)=1\) whenever the type of \(e\) lies in \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filtering regime retains events satisfying a declared predicate, preserves order, and is audit-complete only for event types it never suppresses.
assumptions_latex: The unfiltered trace has a total event order.
The filter is evaluated before the current event enters retained history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau_F\) is an order-preserving subsequence of \(\tau\), with completeness determined relative to the retained event set.
review_flags: filter classifications and audit-completeness terminology require source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicate construction is mathematically coherent, but the type-static, threshold-based, stateful, and audit-completeness taxonomy is uncited. The record also functions primarily as a definition of a filtering regime rather than merely a condition.

children.title: Monitoring Overhead Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Performance and timing effects introduced by tracing or observation.

knowledge_statements.title: Monitoring Overhead Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits beyond which monitoring materially changes measured solver behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_0,M_0\) denote runtime and peak memory without monitoring, and \(T_M,M_M\) the corresponding quantities under a monitoring regime. For tolerances \(\varepsilon_T,\varepsilon_M\ge0\), the regime lies within the overhead boundary when \(T_M\le(1+\varepsilon_T)T_0\) and \(M_M\le M_0+\varepsilon_M\). It crosses the boundary when either inequality fails. Even inside this boundary, observational equivalence additionally fails if the monitored run changes the solver’s recorded decision sequence under a deterministic execution contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monitoring exceeds its boundary when runtime or memory tolerances are violated; decision-sequence changes can invalidate observational equivalence even below those limits.
assumptions_latex: Baseline and monitored runs use the same instance, configuration, and execution environment.
Runtime and memory measurements use identical conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundary violation occurs iff \(T_M>(1+\varepsilon_T)T_0\) or \(M_M>M_0+\varepsilon_M\).
review_flags: overhead metrics and deterministic-equivalence criterion require empirical or solver documentation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tolerance boundary is a defensible convention and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but neither the selected metrics nor the decision-sequence criterion is supported by a source.

children.title: Reproducibility Record System
children.top_down_role: Per-run records needed to reproduce solver behavior.

children.title: Parameter Snapshots
children.top_down_role: Complete records of effective solver parameter values for a run.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Snapshots
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical record of effective solver parameters at a defined run phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the finite set of effective solver parameters at phase \(t\). A parameter snapshot is a canonical map \(S_t:P\to V\times O\) assigning each parameter its effective value and provenance class, such as default, user-set, or automatically modified. Canonical serialization must preserve parameter names, types, values, units where applicable, and phase identity. Two snapshots are equal exactly when these recorded fields agree for every parameter, independently of serialization order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter snapshot canonically records every effective parameter’s typed value, provenance, units, and run phase, with equality independent of field order.
assumptions_latex: Effective parameter values are queryable at the recorded phase.
Parameter names and types are stable within the recorded solver version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t=S'_t\) iff every parameter has equal recorded value, type, provenance, unit, and phase in both snapshots.
review_flags: canonical snapshot fields require an authoritative reproducibility specification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The required canonical fields need a reproducibility or solver-configuration source. The declared map S_t:P\to V\times O also does not encode all fields later used to define snapshot equality, including type, unit, and phase.

children.title: Run Provenance Records
children.top_down_role: Solver versions, build features, hardware context, and input identities.

knowledge_statements.title: Run Provenance Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity and environment metadata sufficient to distinguish solver executions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A run provenance record is a tuple \(R=(I,H,V,B,E,C,t)\), where \(I\) identifies the mathematical instance, \(H\) is a content digest of its serialized input, \(V\) identifies solver and plugin versions, \(B\) identifies binaries or build options, \(E\) describes the execution environment, \(C\) identifies the effective configuration record, and \(t\) records time and invocation identity. The record is integrity-checkable when recomputing \(H\) from the archived input yields the stored digest.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A provenance record identifies the instance, input digest, software build, environment, effective configuration, and invocation, enabling integrity checks and run comparison.
assumptions_latex: The input has a deterministic byte serialization for digest computation.
Software and environment identifiers are recorded before or during execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recomputed agreement with \(H\) certifies integrity of the archived serialized input, not equivalence of solver outcomes.

notation.meaning: digest of the serialized solver input
identifier of the effective configuration record

review_flags: required provenance fields and digest conventions require a reproducibility standard or solver source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the mandatory provenance fields or digest convention. Digest agreement checks consistency with the archived serialization but should not be described as an unconditional integrity certificate without stated hash assumptions.

children.title: Randomness Records
children.top_down_role: Seeds, randomized component settings, and nondeterministic execution context.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomness Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Record of pseudorandom initialization and stream use during a solver run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomness record is a tuple \(G=(A,\{(j,s_j,c_j)\}_{j\in J},D)\), where \(A\) identifies each pseudorandom generator algorithm and version, \(J\) indexes logical random streams, \(s_j\) is stream \(j\)'s initial seed or state, \(c_j\) records its splitting or consumption convention, and \(D\) records nondeterministic sources not controlled by those streams. Replay equivalence requires identical \(A\), stream initialization, consumption order, and uncontrolled-source behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomness record captures generator identity, stream seeds or states, stream-consumption conventions, and uncontrolled nondeterministic sources needed for replay assessment.
assumptions_latex: All solver-controlled pseudorandom streams can be identified.
Generator state interpretation is tied to a recorded implementation version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matching seeds alone is insufficient for replay unless generator, stream partitioning, consumption order, and external nondeterminism also match.

notation.meaning: initial seed or state of stream j

review_flags: solver-specific stream and nondeterminism semantics require an implementation reference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between seeds, generator identity, stream consumption, and external nondeterminism is plausible, but the solver-specific stream model and replay conditions require authoritative documentation.

children.title: Reproduction Compatibility Checks
children.top_down_role: Comparison of recorded run context with a prospective reproduction environment.

knowledge_statements.title: Reproduction Compatibility Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pre-run predicate for assessing whether two recorded executions are reproducible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For run records \(R\) and \(R'\), define exact-replay compatibility by \(K(R,R')=1\) precisely when their input digests, solver and plugin binaries, effective parameter snapshots, pseudorandom generator identities and stream states, arithmetic mode, thread count and scheduling contract, and declared external dependencies agree. Outcome-comparison compatibility may weaken selected equalities only through an explicit comparison policy. Compatibility is necessary for promised replay under the recorded contract but does not by itself guarantee identical outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-replay compatibility requires matching inputs, binaries, parameters, randomness, arithmetic, concurrency contract, and dependencies; it is necessary but not sufficient for identical outcomes.
assumptions_latex: Both runs provide complete provenance, parameter, and randomness records.
The requested reproduction level is declared before comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(R,R')=1\) is a necessary compatibility certificate for exact replay, not a certificate of equal solver trajectories or outputs.
review_flags: exact replay contract and mandatory compatibility fields require authoritative documentation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the compatibility-check leaf, but the asserted mandatory fields and claim that their equality is necessary for exact replay depend on a presently uncited replay contract.

children.title: Constraint Integer Programming Architecture
children.top_down_role: Constraint-centered solver architecture coordinating semantic handlers with branch-cut-and-price search and extensible plugins.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Overview, Plugin API, and Constraint Handlers
Extending a CIP framework to solve MIQCPs

children.title: Constraint Integer Programming Model
children.top_down_role: Constraint-oriented model representations supporting semantic enforcement, relaxation, propagation, and extension.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Constraint integer programming model and framework

children.title: Semantic-Algebraic Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Coexistence of rich constraint meaning and solver-generated relaxations.

children.title: Constraint Semantic Representations
children.top_down_role: Rich constraint meaning retained by constraint-oriented processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Semantic Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint objects retaining problem structure beyond a flat algebraic encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a variable domain. A semantic constraint representation is a tuple \(C=(\kappa,z,\theta,\Sigma)\), where \(\kappa\) is a constraint class, \(z\) is an ordered tuple of variables, \(\theta\) contains class-specific data, and \(\Sigma\subseteq X\) is the satisfaction set defined by the class semantics. An assignment \(x\in X\) satisfies \(C\) exactly when \(x\in\Sigma\). The representation retains \(\kappa\) so class-specific propagation, separation, enforcement, or reformulation methods may be applied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semantic constraint stores its class, variables, data, and satisfaction set, preserving structure usable by specialized solver procedures.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the joint domain of the declared variables.
The constraint class supplies a well-defined satisfaction predicate on \(X\).
All referenced variables have declared domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\models C\) if and only if \(x\in\Sigma\), while \(\kappa\) remains available for class-specific processing.
review_flags: source may support semantic constraints generally but not the full constraint-integer-programming architecture

children.title: Algebraic Relaxation Representations
children.top_down_role: Rows, bounds, and auxiliary structures exposed to relaxation solvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Relaxation Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic outer approximations used to bound a semantic constraint’s satisfaction set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a semantic constraint have satisfaction set \(\Sigma\subseteq X\), and let \(L:X\to\mathbb R^m\) be an algebraic expression map. An algebraic relaxation representation is a set \(R=\{x\in X:L_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) satisfying \(\Sigma\subseteq R\). For minimization, replacing \(\Sigma\) by \(R\) cannot increase the optimal value. The representation is exact on a domain \(D\subseteq X\) when \(R\cap D=\Sigma\cap D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An algebraic relaxation is an inequality-defined superset of the semantic feasible set; it gives a minimization lower bound and is exact where both sets coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) and \(R\) use the same ambient variable domain \(X\).
The optimization objective is unchanged when the constraint is relaxed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma\subseteq R\), and for minimization \(\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in\Sigma}f(x)\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Semantic-to-Algebraic Translation
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between semantic constraints and generated relaxation artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Semantic-to-Algebraic Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generation of a valid algebraic relaxation from a semantic constraint object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a semantic constraint \(C=(\kappa,z,\theta,\Sigma)\), variable bounds \(D\), and a translation rule \(T_\kappa\). Initialize \(R\leftarrow D\). Generate inequalities \(g_j(z,\theta)\le0\) prescribed by \(T_\kappa\), and update \(R\leftarrow R\cap\{x:g_j(x,\theta)\le0\ \text{for all }j\}\). Validate that \(\Sigma\cap D\subseteq R\); otherwise reject the translation. Output the inequalities and metadata linking them to \(C\). The translation is exact on \(D\) when also \(R\subseteq\Sigma\cap D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The translation rule generates inequalities from a semantic constraint, validates that they contain every feasible assignment, and records whether the resulting relaxation is exact.
assumptions_latex: The semantic satisfaction set \(\Sigma\) is well-defined on \(D\).
The class-specific rule \(T_\kappa\) supplies finitely many algebraic inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted output satisfies \(\Sigma\cap D\subseteq R\); exactness requires \(R=\Sigma\cap D\).

notation.meaning: translation rule for semantic class kappa

review_flags: class-specific translation validation requires stronger constraint-integer-programming documentation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the translation leaf, but the cited general sections on constraint programming and continuous relaxation do not specifically support this class-dependent generation-and-validation algorithm. In particular, no inspectable source establishes how the set inclusion validation is performed.

children.title: Relaxation Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where algebraic surrogates incompletely reflect semantic feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\).
The original and relaxed problems use the same objective and minimization direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq R\Rightarrow \inf_{x\in R}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\); if \(F\nsubseteq R\), this inequality is not guaranteed uniformly over objectives.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the algebraic representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between set-inclusion relaxations that guarantee lower bounds and algebraic surrogates lacking that universal guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a minimization problem have feasible set \(F\subseteq X\) and objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). An algebraic representation with feasible set \(R\subseteq X\) is a set-inclusion relaxation when \(F\subseteq R\); in that case, \(\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). If \(F\nsubseteq R\), then this lower-bound relation is not guaranteed uniformly over objectives: for any \(\bar x\in F\setminus R\), a suitable objective can make the optimum over \(R\) exceed the optimum over \(F\). Conversely, equality of the two optimal values for a particular objective does not imply \(F=R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Containing every original feasible point guarantees that an algebraic representation gives a valid lower bound for every common minimization objective. Without that inclusion the guarantee can fail, while equal optimal values for one objective do not establish exact semantic representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Fidelity Boundaries

children.title: Core CIP Object Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Core objects manipulated by constraint-oriented processing.

children.title: Variable Objects
children.top_down_role: Decision-variable identity, metadata, solver state, and transformed counterparts.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract variable object in a constraint integer programming model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index set \(I\), a variable object \(v_i\) is a record \((i,D_i,c_i,\tau_i)\), where \(D_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) is its current domain, \(c_i\in\mathbb{R}\) is its objective coefficient, and \(\tau_i\in\{\mathrm{continuous},\mathrm{integer},\mathrm{binary},\mathrm{implicit\ integer}\}\) is its type. A solution assignment maps \(v_i\) to a value \(x_i\in D_i\), additionally satisfying \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for an integer type and \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for a binary type.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable object carries identity, current domain, objective coefficient, and type; assigned values must satisfy both its domain and type restrictions.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
Each declared domain is nonempty when the model is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible assignments satisfy \(x_i\in D_i\) and all restrictions encoded by \(\tau_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the Variable Objects leaf, but no source supports the proposed record fields or the semantics of continuous, integer, binary, and implicit-integer types. In particular, the admissibility rule does not explicitly resolve the solver-specific meaning of the implicit-integer type.

children.title: Domain Objects
children.top_down_role: Allowed-value representations, bound state, and domain modifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain object as the solver-maintained admissible-value set of one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A domain object for variable \(v_i\) is a nonempty set \(D_i\subseteq\mathbb R\) represented by bounds and, when supported, excluded values or interval components. A domain update replaces \(D_i\) by \(D_i'=D_i\cap S\) for some restriction \(S\subseteq\mathbb R\). The update is valid on a search region \(Q\) when every feasible assignment represented by \(Q\) satisfies \(x_i\in S\); it detects infeasibility when \(D_i'=\varnothing\). For integral \(v_i\), effective membership is restricted further to \(D_i\cap\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain object stores a variable’s admissible values. Valid propagation intersects it with a necessary restriction, and an empty resulting domain certifies local infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The domain belongs to a declared variable object.
Domain updates are evaluated relative to a specified search region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid update preserves all feasible assignments in \(Q\), while \(D_i'=\varnothing\) proves that \(Q\) contains none.

notation.meaning: Search region where the update is valid.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the Domain Objects leaf, but the representation and propagation semantics have no citation. Defining every domain object as nonempty also conflicts with the later use of an empty updated domain as an infeasibility state; an authoritative solver model is needed to determine whether emptiness is a domain state or only an update outcome.

children.title: Constraint Objects
children.top_down_role: Semantic restrictions, handler associations, flags, and lifecycle state.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic constraint object with a satisfaction predicate and solver operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given variables indexed by \(I
eq\varnothing\), a constraint object \(C\\) consists of a scope \(J_C\subseteq I\), a satisfaction predicate \(P_C:\prod_{i\in J_C}D_i\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\), and implementations of any supported solver operations, such as feasibility checking, propagation, separation, or relaxation generation. An assignment \(x\in\prod_{i\in I}D_i\) satisfies \(C\) exactly when \(P_C((x_i)_{i\in J_C})=\mathrm{true}\). Every generated inference or relaxation must be valid wherever the constraint object declares it valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint object combines a scoped satisfaction predicate with solver operations; every inference or relaxation it generates must respect its declared validity region.
assumptions_latex: Each scoped variable has a declared domain.
Generated artifacts have an explicitly determined validity region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model feasibility requires \(P_C((x_i)_{i\in J_C})=\mathrm{true}\) for every active constraint object \(C\).

notation.meaning: Indices of variables in the constraint scope.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the Constraint Objects leaf, but the claim about supported operations and validity regions is architecture-specific and uncited. The token \(C\\\) contains a malformed or unintended line-break command in math mode and must also be repaired once the sourced formulation is established.

children.title: Solution Objects
children.top_down_role: Candidate assignments, origin metadata, feasibility status, and storage.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment-and-metadata solution object used by a CIP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite variable set \(V=\{v_i:i\in I\}\), a solution object \(s\) contains a partial or total assignment \(x^s:I_s\to\mathbb R\), where \(I_s\subseteq I\), together with provenance and evaluation metadata. It is complete when \(I_s=I\), domain-feasible when \(x_i^s\in D_i\) for all \(i\in I\), and model-feasible when it is complete, domain-feasible, and satisfies every active constraint. Its objective value is \(z(s)=c_0+\sum_{i\in I}c_i x_i^s\) whenever the assignment is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution object stores an assignment and metadata. Feasibility requires completeness, domain compliance, and satisfaction of every active constraint.
assumptions_latex: The objective is linear in the represented variables.
Constraint feasibility is evaluated in one specified model stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete feasible solution has a well-defined value \(z(s)\) and may serve as an incumbent.

notation.meaning: Objective value of a complete solution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the Solution Objects leaf, but partial assignments, stored metadata, stage-relative feasibility, and objective evaluation are solver-specific and unsupported. The conclusion that any complete feasible solution may serve as an incumbent also needs qualification for objective sense, acceptance policy, and the relevant model stage.

children.title: Core Object References
children.top_down_role: References connecting variables, domains, constraints, and stored solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Core Object References
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable logical references among variables, domains, constraints, and solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\) be the set of live solver objects. A core object reference is an identifier \(r\) interpreted through a stage-dependent resolution map \(\rho_t\). It is valid at solver state \(t\) exactly when \(r\in\operatorname{dom}(\rho_t)\) and \(\rho_t(r)\in\mathcal O\). Cross-object relations are represented by such references: a domain refers to its variable, a constraint to its scoped variables, and a solution to the variables whose values it stores. Equality of references denotes logical object identity, not equality of mutable object contents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A core reference resolves an identifier to a live logical object at a given solver stage; identity is distinct from the object’s mutable contents.
assumptions_latex: Solver state \(t\) determines which objects are live.
Resolution does not identify two distinct live logical objects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dereferencing \(r\) is defined precisely when \(r\in\operatorname{dom}(\rho_t)\).

notation.meaning: Reference-resolution map at solver state t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind is plausible for Core Object References, but the identifier-resolution-map model and logical-identity semantics are uncited abstractions rather than established CIP API semantics. The statement also introduces one set of live objects while making resolution stage-dependent without indexing that set by the solver state.

children.title: Search Object Validity-Lifetime Regimes
children.top_down_role: Object validity and lifetime regimes within search.

children.title: Global Objects
children.top_down_role: Objects valid throughout the active search space.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search objects whose mathematical validity covers the entire active search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the rooted search tree and let \(F_u\) denote the feasible assignments compatible with node \(u\in T\). A generated constraint, bound change, or inference object \(g\) is global when its validity region contains every active node: for all active \(u\), every \(x\in F_u\) satisfies \(g\). Equivalently, if \(S_g\) is the set admitted by \(g\), then \(F_u\subseteq S_g\) for every active \(u\). Global validity concerns logical scope and does not by itself require permanent storage or permanent activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global object is valid at every active search node. Global validity does not imply that the solver must retain or activate it permanently.
assumptions_latex: Each search node has a well-defined feasible region.
The object expresses a predicate or restriction on assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\) is global if and only if \(F_u\subseteq S_g\) for every active \(u\in T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Global Objects, but validity only over currently active nodes may be weaker than solver-global validity, which can require validity throughout the problem or all present and future search regions. An authoritative CIP source is needed to fix the intended quantification and distinguish logical validity from activation and storage.

children.title: Local Objects
children.top_down_role: Objects restricted to a node subtree or local search context.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search objects valid only within a designated subtree or search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a rooted search tree. An object \(g\) created at node \(a\in T\) is local to the subtree rooted at \(a\) when every feasible assignment at each descendant \(u\succeq a\) satisfies \(g\), while validity outside that subtree is neither asserted nor required. Writing \(S_g\) for the assignments admitted by \(g\), locality requires \(F_u\subseteq S_g\) for every active descendant \(u\succeq a\). The solver must not use \(g\) to exclude assignments at nodes outside its declared validity region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local object is valid throughout a designated subtree, but cannot safely exclude assignments outside that region without an independent validity argument.
assumptions_latex: Descendant relation \(\succeq\) is defined by the rooted search tree.
The object's creation node or validity root is recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local use is sound only at nodes \(u\) satisfying \(u\succeq a\).

notation.meaning: Root node of the object's validity subtree.
Node u is a descendant of a, including a.
Assignments admitted by the local object.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Local Objects, but the prose first quantifies over every descendant and then the formula quantifies only over active descendants. A solver source is needed to determine whether locality covers the full subtree, only extant nodes, or another recorded validity region.

children.title: Dynamic Objects
children.top_down_role: Objects eligible for aging or adaptive retention during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objects whose solver activation or retention may change according to search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A search object \(g\) is dynamic when the solver may change its operational status over time according to a policy \(A_g(t)\in\{0,1\}\), where \(A_g(t)=1\) means that \(g\) is active at state \(t\). Deactivation may remove \(g\) from propagation, separation, or relaxation processing without changing its declared logical validity region \(V_g\). Reactivation is sound only at nodes lying in \(V_g\). Thus dynamism describes state-dependent use or retention, not whether the object is globally or locally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic object may be activated or deactivated as search evolves. This operational status is independent of whether its validity is global or local.
assumptions_latex: The solver records the object's validity region independently of activation.
Inactive objects do not restrict the current relaxation or propagation state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Use of \(g\) at state \(t\) is permitted only when \(A_g(t)=1\) and the current node lies in \(V_g\).

notation.meaning: Activation indicator for object g at state t.
Declared validity region of the object.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Dynamic Objects, but the proposed activation-indicator semantics are solver-specific and may conflate temporary activation, LP membership, propagation participation, and storage retention. No source establishes the claimed independence or reactivation rules.

children.title: Removable Objects
children.top_down_role: Objects eligible for deletion when no longer useful or active.

knowledge_statements.title: Removable Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objects that may be discarded without invalidating correctness of the represented search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stored search object \(g\) is removable at state \(t\) when deleting its stored representation and ceasing its operational use preserves the solver's correctness invariant: no assignment feasible for the original problem is excluded solely by the deletion, and any bound or infeasibility claim retained afterward remains justified by other live data. Removability is a lifetime property, not a validity property; either a global or local object may be removable. If later reasoning requires \(g\), the solver must regenerate it or retain sufficient information to reconstruct its effect soundly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A removable object may be discarded while preserving all correctness claims. Removability governs storage lifetime, independently of global or local validity.
assumptions_latex: Deletion also removes every unsupported operational effect of the object.
Retained certificates and bounds remain justified after deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing \(g\) preserves the set of correctness-valid conclusions maintained at state \(t\).

notation.meaning: Solver state at which removal is considered.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Removable Objects, but the definition is expressed through an unspecified global correctness invariant and is not tied to an authoritative solver lifecycle model. The effects of deletion, retained bounds, reconstruction, and dependent artifacts are implementation-specific and require a source.

children.title: Validity-Lifetime Interactions
children.top_down_role: Combinations of locality, dynamism, removability, and search-state persistence.

knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Lifetime Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonality and safety conditions connecting logical validity with operational lifetime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each search object \(g\) with a validity region \(V_g\subseteq T\) and a lifetime set \(L_g\) of solver states in which it is live. Sound use at state \(t\) and current node \(u(t)\) requires both \(t\in L_g\) and \(u(t)\in V_g\). Global or local scope determines \(V_g\); dynamic or removable status constrains how \(L_g\) may change. Neither axis determines the other. Deleting or deactivating \(g\) must also retract every relaxation term, inference, or certificate whose validity depends exclusively on \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validity determines where an object may be used; lifetime determines when it exists. Sound use requires both, and deletion must retract unsupported consequences.
assumptions_latex: Every dependent artifact records enough provenance to identify its supporting objects.
The current search node is defined at each operational solver state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sound application of \(g\) implies \(t\in L_g\) and \(u(t)\in V_g\).

notation.meaning: Search-tree validity region of object g.
Set of states during which g is live.
Current search node at state t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the interaction leaf, but the two-axis model and mandatory retraction of every exclusively dependent artifact are uncited architecture claims. Provenance, persistence of derived consequences, and the distinction between deactivation and deletion must be established from a solver-specific source.

children.title: Solver Object Provenance Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Relationships among original, transformed, copied, and solver-owned objects.

children.title: Original-to-Transformed Object Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between user-facing objects and transformed solver objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-to-Transformed Object Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stage-dependent mapping from client-facing model objects to presolved solver objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\) be the original model objects and \(\mathcal T_t\) the live transformed objects at solver stage \(t\). An original-to-transformed mapping is a partial map \(\Phi_t:\mathcal O\rightharpoonup\mathcal T_t\) together with reconstruction data \(R_t\). For an original variable \(v\), its represented value must be recoverable from transformed values by \(x_v=R_{t,v}(y)\). For an original constraint \(C\), transformed feasibility must imply satisfaction of \(C\) after reconstruction. The map may be undefined before transformation or after transformed objects are freed; clients must not treat stale transformed references as live mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stage-dependent map links original objects to transformed ones, while reconstruction recovers original values and feasibility. The map is partial outside transformed-model lifetime.
assumptions_latex: Presolving transformations preserve feasibility under the recorded reconstruction map.
Object identity is distinguished from algebraic equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every transformed-feasible \(y\), the reconstructed assignment \(R_t(y)\) satisfies all original constraints represented by \(\Phi_t\).

notation.meaning: Partial original-to-transformed object map at stage t.
Live transformed objects at stage t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the Original-to-Transformed Object Mapping leaf, but presolving can aggregate, eliminate, or replace objects, so a simple partial object map may not capture the actual API contract. The reconstruction and transformed-feasibility claims, especially for original constraints, require an authoritative solver transformation source with stage and lifetime details.

children.title: Copied-Object Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence across solver copies, subsolvers, and reconstructed instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Copied-Object Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract mapping between corresponding objects in two solver instances during one copy operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) and \(S'\) be distinct solver instances, let \(O(S)\) and \(O(S')\) denote their solver objects, and let \(e\) identify one copy operation. A copied-object mapping is a partial function \(C_e:O(S)\rightharpoonup O(S')\). For every \(o\in\operatorname{dom}(C_e)\), the object \(C_e(o)\) belongs to \(S'\), has the copied semantic role of \(o\), and refers only to objects mapped or created consistently in \(S'\). The mapping is scoped to operation \(e\); it does not identify the source and destination objects or transfer their ownership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A copy operation defines a partial, operation-scoped correspondence from source-solver objects to semantically equivalent destination-solver objects without equating their identities or ownership.
assumptions_latex: \(S\neq S'\).
The copy operation \(e\) specifies which object classes and dependencies are copied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_e:O(S)\rightharpoonup O(S')\) is ownership-preserving and local to \(e\).

notation.meaning: Objects owned or managed by solver instance S.
Partial correspondence created by copy operation e.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the asserted semantic-role, dependency-consistency, scope, and ownership guarantees are solver-API-specific and have no cited authoritative source.

children.title: Solver-Owned Object Lifetimes
children.top_down_role: Retention and disposal responsibilities for solver-managed objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Owned Object Lifetimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for handles to objects whose storage and destruction are controlled by a solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_o\) be a client-held handle to an object \(o\) owned by solver instance \(S\). The handle is usable at time \(t\) only if \(S\) is alive, \(o\) has not been deleted or invalidated, and the current solver stage permits the requested operation. Formally, \[\operatorname{usable}(h_o,t,a)\iff \operatorname{alive}(S,t)\land\operatorname{valid}(o,t)\land\operatorname{allowed}(a,\operatorname{stage}(S,t)).\] Destroying \(S\), deleting \(o\), or crossing an invalidating lifecycle transition makes subsequent dereference through \(h_o\) undefined by this interface model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver-owned object handle is usable only while its solver and object remain valid and the requested operation is permitted in the current solver stage.
assumptions_latex: The client does not independently own the storage of \(o\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of any predicate in the usability condition invalidates use of \(h_o\).

notation.meaning: Client-held handle to solver-owned object o.

review_flags: Lifecycle transitions and permitted stages vary by solver API.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the lifetime leaf, but object invalidation, permitted stages, and the consequences of stale-handle use depend on the solver API and are unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Client-Owned Object Lifetimes
children.top_down_role: Retention and disposal responsibilities for application-managed objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Owned Object Lifetimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for client storage referenced by solver callbacks or object payloads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be client-owned data registered with solver \(S\), and let \(T_d\) be the set of times at which \(S\) may access \(d\), including callback execution and destruction. Correct lifetime management requires \[T_d\subseteq [t_{\mathrm{create}},t_{\mathrm{release}})\] and requires the client not to move, destroy, or mutate \(d\) incompatibly while an access may occur. If ownership is explicitly transferred to \(S\), the client instead relinquishes release authority and the registered destructor becomes responsible for exactly one release.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Client data must remain valid throughout every possible solver access, unless ownership is explicitly transferred and a registered destructor releases it exactly once.
assumptions_latex: The solver retains a pointer, reference, or closure capable of accessing \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every solver access to \(d\) occurs before its unique authorized release.

notation.meaning: Times at which the solver may access client data d.
Time of the unique authorized release.

review_flags: Ownership-transfer and destructor conventions are API-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but ownership transfer, destructor invocation, release authority, and exactly-once destruction are interface-specific claims requiring authoritative lifecycle documentation.

children.title: Stale Mapping Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Invalid references arising from transformation, copying, deletion, or solver-stage changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Mapping Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for provenance mappings retained beyond their defining solver state or copy operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_e\) be an object mapping created during lifecycle epoch \(e\), and let \(h=M_e(o)\). If either participating solver is destroyed, \(o\) or \(h\) is deleted, or a documented transition replaces the represented object without refreshing \(M_e\), then \(M_e(o)\) is stale. A stale entry certifies neither existence nor semantic correspondence. Consequently, dereferencing it, passing it to the wrong solver, or using it to transfer values lies outside the mapping contract; validity must be re-established through a current solver-supported lookup.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping becomes stale after destruction, deletion, or an invalidating transformation; its entries then certify neither object existence nor correspondence and must not be used.
assumptions_latex: \(M_e\) is scoped to a particular lifecycle or copy epoch \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After an invalidating event, \(M_e(o)\) cannot serve as a valid provenance certificate.

notation.meaning: Object correspondence established in epoch e.

review_flags: The precise invalidating transitions depend on the solver implementation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is correct, but the mapping epochs, invalidating transitions, and supported lookup mechanism cannot be validated without solver-specific provenance documentation.

children.title: Constraint Handlers
children.top_down_role: Plugins that own the semantics and solver interactions of constraint classes.

children.title: Candidate Feasibility Enforcement Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for validating candidate solutions and enforcing semantic feasibility.

children.title: Feasibility-Checking Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for validating candidate assignments against constraint semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Checking Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Read-only validation of a supplied candidate against constraints managed by one handler.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a candidate assignment \(x\), a handler-owned constraint family \(\mathcal C_H\), and feasibility tolerances \(\tau\). For each active \(c\in\mathcal C_H\), evaluate its violation measure \(v_c(x)\). Return \(\mathrm{FEASIBLE}\) exactly when \(v_c(x)\leq\tau_c\) for every checked constraint; otherwise return \(\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\) together with an optional violated-constraint diagnostic. The callback validates the supplied candidate and does not, merely by reporting infeasibility, claim that a cut, propagation, or domain reduction has been installed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The checker evaluates every active handled constraint at a candidate and reports feasible only when all violations lie within their prescribed tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Each active constraint \(c\) has a defined violation measure \(v_c\) and tolerance \(\tau_c\).
The supplied candidate provides every value needed by the checker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The result equals \(\mathrm{FEASIBLE}\iff \forall c\in\mathcal C_H,\ v_c(x)\leq\tau_c\).

notation.meaning: Active constraints managed by handler H.
Violation of constraint c at candidate x.

review_flags: Callback result codes and tolerance conventions are solver-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the callback leaf, but requiring every active constraint to be checked and defining an exact FEASIBLE/INFEASIBLE result contract are handler-API-specific claims with no source.

children.title: Integral-Solution Enforcement Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for resolving semantic violations in integral candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Integral-Solution Enforcement Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enforcement response when a candidate is integral but may violate handler-managed constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an integral candidate \(x\) and the active constraints \(\mathcal C_H\) of handler \(H\). If all constraints satisfy \(v_c(x)\leq\tau_c\), return an acceptance result. Otherwise perform a solver-supported action that excludes \(x\) or proves the current search state infeasible, such as adding a valid constraint, separating a valid cut, reducing a domain, or declaring cutoff. Return the result code corresponding to the action actually completed; never return an enforcement-success code when no valid state change or infeasibility conclusion occurred.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integral candidate, the enforcer accepts it if feasible; otherwise it must perform and accurately report a valid exclusion, reduction, or cutoff action.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) satisfies the solver's integrality test.
Every generated constraint, cut, or reduction is valid for the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The callback either accepts \(x\) or produces a valid solver-recognized enforcement outcome.

notation.meaning: Active constraints managed by handler H.

review_flags: Permitted enforcement actions and result codes vary by solver.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the permitted enforcement actions, acceptance semantics, and correspondence between completed actions and result codes require authoritative solver-interface documentation.

children.title: Checker-to-Enforcer Result Mapping
children.top_down_role: Coordination of feasibility outcomes with enforcement responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Checker-to-Enforcer Result Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency relation between candidate validation and enforcement outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)\in\{\mathrm{FEASIBLE},\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\}\) be the checker result and let \(e(x)\) be the integral-enforcer result. A consistent mapping satisfies \[q(x)=\mathrm{FEASIBLE}\Rightarrow e(x)=\mathrm{ACCEPT},\] while \(q(x)=\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\) requires \(e(x)\) to report the concrete valid action performed, such as \(\mathrm{CUTOFF}\), \(\mathrm{SEPARATED}\), \(\mathrm{REDUCEDDOM}\), or \(\mathrm{CONSADDED}\). Infeasibility detected by the checker alone does not determine which nonacceptance code is valid; that code is determined by the enforcer's completed state change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible check maps to acceptance; an infeasible check maps only to the specific exclusion or reduction action that the enforcer actually performs.
assumptions_latex: The checker and enforcer use the same active constraints and feasibility tolerances.
The candidate \(x\) is eligible for integral enforcement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enforcer result is consistent with both \(q(x)\) and the solver action actually completed.
review_flags: Named result codes reflect a SCIP-like interface and require API confirmation.
No supplied source supports the exact checker-to-enforcer mapping.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the mapping leaf, but the named SCIP-like result codes and the asserted feasible-to-ACCEPT implication are exact API semantics unsupported by any citation.

children.title: Candidate Validation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Risks from incomplete checks, inconsistent tolerances, or unsupported candidate states.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate Validation Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a callback result cannot validly certify candidate feasibility or rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Candidate validation is unsound if the checker omits an active handled constraint, reads missing or stale variable values, applies tolerances inconsistent with the solver, or reports feasibility before all required predicates are tested. Rejection is likewise unsupported when the enforcer reports separation, reduction, constraint addition, or cutoff without completing the corresponding valid operation. Thus a result is a certificate only for the candidate, active constraint set, tolerances, and solver state actually examined; changing any of these invalidates reuse of that result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validation fails beyond its contract when required constraints or values are omitted, tolerances disagree, state is stale, or a reported enforcement action was not actually performed.
assumptions_latex: Callback results are interpreted as certificates about a specified candidate and solver state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A result obtained outside the stated validation conditions cannot certify acceptance or rejection.
review_flags: Exact callback preconditions and failure semantics require solver documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but the required checked constraints, tolerance consistency, state validity, and certification effects of result codes depend on an undocumented callback contract.

children.title: Solver-State Enforcement Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for resolving violations in different solver states.

children.title: Relaxation-Solution Enforcement Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for handling semantic violations in relaxation solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Solution Enforcement Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint enforcement at the current LP or other explicit relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the current relaxation solution \(x^R\) and active handled constraints \(\mathcal C_H\). Evaluate violations at \(x^R\). If all satisfy \(v_c(x^R)\leq\tau_c\), report relaxation feasibility. Otherwise attempt a valid enforcement action appropriate to the relaxation state: separate a valid inequality, tighten a domain, add a constraint, or prove node infeasibility. Report exactly the action completed; if no permitted action succeeds, return the interface's designated unresolved result rather than claiming feasibility or successful enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a relaxation solution, the callback checks handled constraints and reports either feasibility, a completed valid enforcement action, or the designated unresolved outcome.
assumptions_latex: \(x^R\) is the solver's current relaxation solution.
Generated inequalities and reductions preserve every feasible integer solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned status faithfully describes feasibility or the enforcement action completed at \(x^R\).

notation.meaning: Active constraints managed by handler H.

review_flags: Supported actions and unresolved result codes are solver-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the supported relaxation state, available enforcement actions, and designated unresolved result are solver-specific and lack an authoritative source.

children.title: Pseudo-Solution Enforcement Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for handling violations when no current relaxation solution is available.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Solution Enforcement Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint enforcement when no explicit relaxation vector is available and bounds define the solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the current local domains \(D=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\) and active handled constraints \(\mathcal C_H\), with no explicit relaxation solution assumed. Determine whether \(D\) can satisfy each handled constraint using domain reasoning. If impossibility is certified, return cutoff; if valid bound tightening or constraint addition is completed, report that action; if all required constraints are certified for the represented state, report feasibility. Otherwise return the designated unresolved result. The callback must not evaluate an unavailable relaxation vector or report a reduction that was not installed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without an explicit relaxation vector, pseudo enforcement reasons from current variable domains and reports only certified feasibility, cutoff, completed reductions, or unresolved status.
assumptions_latex: Current local bounds \(\ell_i,u_i\) are available for every relevant variable.
Domain reasoning is valid for all feasible assignments in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The callback result is justified solely by valid reasoning over \(D\) and completed solver actions.

notation.meaning: Cartesian product of current local variable domains.
Active constraints managed by handler H.

review_flags: The meaning of pseudo solution and allowed results is solver-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but equating pseudo enforcement with reasoning over the Cartesian product of local intervals may not match the solver's pseudo-solution semantics; allowed results also require API documentation.

children.title: Enforcement-State Dispatch
children.top_down_role: Selection of enforcement interfaces according to the active solver state.

knowledge_statements.title: Enforcement-State Dispatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dispatch rule selecting the callback matching the solver's current solution representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the enforcement state be \(s\in\{\mathrm{RELAXATION},\mathrm{PSEUDO},\mathrm{INTEGRAL}\}\). Dispatch to relaxation enforcement when \(s=\mathrm{RELAXATION}\) and an explicit current relaxation vector is available; dispatch to pseudo enforcement when \(s=\mathrm{PSEUDO}\) and only domain or pseudo-state information is available; dispatch to integral-solution enforcement when \(s=\mathrm{INTEGRAL}\) and a complete integral candidate is supplied. The selected callback receives only state-valid data, and its returned status is interpreted under that callback's result contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dispatcher selects relaxation, pseudo, or integral enforcement according to the current solution representation and interprets the result under the matching callback contract.
assumptions_latex: The solver exposes an unambiguous enforcement state \(s\).
A callback is registered for every state the handler claims to support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one state-compatible enforcement interface is invoked for each supported enforcement request.
review_flags: Actual dispatch precedence and state categories vary by solver architecture.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the dispatch leaf, but the three-state partition, claim of unambiguous state exposure, exclusive dispatch, and callback precedence are architecture-specific and unsupported.

children.title: Unsupported Enforcement-State Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Solver states or violation types lacking a sound handler response.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Enforcement-State Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary when a handler cannot enforce constraints in the solver state requesting service.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_H\) be the enforcement states supported by handler \(H\). If the solver requests enforcement in state \(s\notin E_H\), invoking a callback that assumes another state is invalid: relaxation enforcement may read a nonexistent vector, while pseudo enforcement may be too weak to justify acceptance of an explicit candidate. The handler must instead use the solver's declared unsupported or unresolved outcome, or reject registration if the architecture requires total coverage. It must not return feasibility, cutoff, separation, or reduction without the data and action required by that result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a handler lacks support for the current enforcement state, it must report the prescribed unsupported outcome and must not fabricate feasibility or enforcement success.
assumptions_latex: \(E_H\) accurately records the enforcement states implemented by handler \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(s\notin E_H\), no state-specific success result is valid without an independently justified action.

notation.meaning: Enforcement states supported by handler H.
State in which enforcement is requested.

review_flags: Unsupported-state signaling and registration requirements are API-specific.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is correct, but unsupported-state signaling, registration coverage requirements, and the validity of particular result categories depend on the solver interface and need an authoritative citation.

children.title: Domain Reduction Callback Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for semantic domain inference and global reduction.

children.title: Propagation Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for search-time domain inference from semantic constraints.
