knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local domain propagation by a constraint handler.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a search node with domain \(D\) and active handled constraints \(C\), initialize \(D^0=D\). At round \(k\), the propagation callback returns either cutoff or \(D^{k+1}\subseteq D^k\) satisfying \(\{x\in D^k:x\text{ satisfies }C\}=\{x\in D^{k+1}:x\text{ satisfies }C\}\). Repeat applicable callbacks until cutoff, a resource limit, or a round without reduction; output cutoff or the final domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback repeatedly tightens node domains without removing feasible solutions, stopping at cutoff, a resource limit, or a propagation fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the current node domain.
\(C\) is the set of active constraints handled by the callback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is cutoff or a feasibility-preserving domain \(D'\subseteq D\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the callback leaf and the feasibility-preserving propagation contract is plausible, but no inspectable citation supports the callback outcomes, iteration semantics, or resource-limit behavior. An authoritative constraint-handler interface section is required.

children.title: Presolve Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for global reductions before or between search phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global model reductions with postsolve recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a model with feasible set \(F\), a presolve callback returns unchanged, infeasible, or a transformed model with feasible set \(F'\) and recovery map \(\rho\). Every accepted transformation must satisfy \(\rho(F')=F\); this permits globally valid bound reductions, constraint deletion or replacement, and variable substitution. Presolve callbacks are repeated until infeasibility, a prescribed limit, or a round makes no transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve callback globally simplifies the model while preserving recoverable feasible solutions, or certifies infeasibility; rounds stop at stability or a limit.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible set before presolve.
\(\rho\) reconstructs eliminated or substituted original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The result satisfies \(\rho(F')=F\), unless the callback validly certifies \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Feasible sets before and after presolve.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the callback leaf, but the strong equality rho(F')=F asserts recovery of every original feasible solution rather than only sound reconstruction or preservation of relevant optima. No source establishes this exact presolve contract or its callback outcomes.

children.title: Reduction Persistence Across Search
children.top_down_role: Transfer of presolve results into transformed objects and later propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Persistence Across Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifetime rules for global and node-local reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_v\) be the domain at search node \(v\). A reduction proved independently of node assumptions is global and may be applied at every open node. A reduction proved under the assumptions defining \(v\) is local: if it replaces \(D_v\) by \(D'_v\), every descendant \(w\) inherits \(D_w\cap D'_v\), while backtracking outside the subtree rooted at \(v\) restores the domain state preceding that reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global reductions persist throughout search; local reductions persist only in their generating node’s subtree and are undone upon backtracking outside it.
assumptions_latex: The search structure is a rooted tree.
Each local reduction is valid under its generating node's assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A global reduction applies everywhere, whereas a reduction generated at \(v\) applies only to \(v\) and its descendants.

notation.meaning: Search nodes, with w potentially descending from v.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind matches the persistence leaf, and the global-versus-subtree distinction is standard. The precise inheritance and restoration semantics are solver-architecture claims without an inspectable source.

children.title: Inference Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Scope and lifecycle limits on reductions produced by either callback family.

knowledge_statements.title: Inference Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between global and node-conditional inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the global feasible set, \(A_v\) the assumptions defining node \(v\), and \(B\) the set satisfying an inferred bound. The inference is globally valid only if \(F\subseteq B\), and locally valid at \(v\) if \(F\cap A_v\subseteq B\). If \(F\nsubseteq B\) but \(F\cap A_v\subseteq B\), installing the bound outside the subtree of \(v\) can remove a globally feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inference is global only if valid for every feasible solution; a node-conditional inference must remain within that node’s subtree.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the original feasible set.
\(A_v\) contains all assumptions on the root-to-node path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inclusion \(F\cap A_v\subseteq B\) alone does not authorize global installation of the inferred bound.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: logical validity criterion for local and global inference
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the containment criterion is logically coherent. No citation supports its interpretation as the relevant solver-interface boundary or the asserted subtree installation rule.

children.title: Constraint-Relaxation Correspondence Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting semantic constraints to algebraic relaxations.

children.title: Separation Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for generating valid inequalities from semantic violations.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of a relaxation point by valid rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation solution \(\bar x\), feasible set \(F\) represented by the handled constraint, and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the callback searches for inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_i\) such that \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_i\) for every \(x\in F\) and \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b_i+\varepsilon\). It returns such rows, reports that none were found, or reports a resource limit. Accepted rows are added before resolving the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback finds valid inequalities violated by the current relaxation solution, adds them as rows, or reports none or a resource limit.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) solves the current relaxation.
\(\varepsilon\geq0\) is the violation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned row contains \(F\) and separates \(\bar x\) by more than \(\varepsilon\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the separation-callback leaf and the validity and violation conditions are plausible. The permitted return states, tolerance convention, and row-installation behavior are solver-specific and uncited.

children.title: Relaxation Construction Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for supplying alternative or supplemental relaxation structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Construction Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of an outer relaxation for handled constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a handled constraint with feasible set \(F\) on domain \(D\), the callback constructs a tractable set \(R\) using rows, auxiliary variables, or another supported relaxation object. It must ensure \(F\cap D\subseteq R\cap D\). If auxiliary variables are introduced, projecting the extended relaxation onto the original variables must still contain \(F\cap D\). The callback returns the constructed object, reports that none is available, or reports failure without changing the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback constructs an exact or outer relaxation, possibly with linked auxiliary variables, while retaining every feasible point in the current domain.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the handled constraint's feasible set.
\(D\) is the domain where the relaxation is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed relaxation satisfies \(F\cap D\subseteq R\cap D\), after projection when auxiliary variables occur.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the source-free statement blends an original-variable set R with an extended relaxation requiring projection. An authoritative interface source is needed to determine the supported relaxation objects, linking requirements, and exact callback failure semantics.

children.title: Constraint-to-Row Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Links between semantic constraints and generated algebraic rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-to-Row Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set correspondence between a constraint and its relaxation rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a handled constraint define \(F_c=\{x\in D:c(x)\text{ holds}\}\), and let \(\mathcal R_c=\{a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_i:i\in I\}\) be its associated rows. Define \(P_c=\{x\in D:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_i\text{ for every }i\in I\}\). The correspondence is relaxation-valid exactly when \(F_c\subseteq P_c\), and it is exact on \(D\) exactly when \(F_c=P_c\). Otherwise, enforcement or later separation is required to recover the omitted restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Associated rows validly relax a constraint when their intersection contains its feasible set; the correspondence is exact when the sets coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the domain on which correspondence is asserted.
Rows involving auxiliary variables use valid linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation validity is \(F_c\subseteq P_c\), while exactness is \(F_c=P_c\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind matches the correspondence leaf and the containment/equality criteria are mathematically coherent. The claim that enforcement or later separation is required, and the treatment of auxiliary-variable rows, need a specific solver-architecture source.

children.title: Relaxation Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Risks from invalid rows, incomplete surrogates, or stale relaxation state.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for global, local, and extended rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) may be installed globally only if every \(x\in F\) satisfies it. At node \(v\), a row depending on assumptions \(A_v\) is valid only if every \(x\in F\cap A_v\) satisfies it and must remain local to that subtree. Failure of the applicable inclusion permits exclusion of a feasible solution. For an extended formulation, the inclusion is tested after existential projection over correctly linked auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global rows must contain all feasible solutions, while assumption-dependent rows are local; violating either containment condition makes the relaxation unsound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the global feasible set.
\(A_v\) contains the assumptions defining node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global validity requires \(F\subseteq\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\}\); local validity requires the analogous inclusion for \(F\cap A_v\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: set-containment criterion for relaxation validity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the global/local containment distinction is plausible. The locality rule and the stated existential-projection test for extended formulations require an authoritative source and a precise definition of the linked extended feasible set.

children.title: Inference Accountability Callback Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing inference reasons and constraint-direction information.

children.title: Conflict-Explanation Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing reasons for constraint-driven domain inferences.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Explanation Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Antecedent certificate for an inference or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a handled constraint \(c\), recorded inference \(q\), and the historical domain state in which \(q\) was derived, the callback returns antecedent bound literals \(E=\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}\). It is a valid explanation certificate when \(c\land e_1\land\cdots\land e_m\Rightarrow q\). For an infeasibility inference, validity instead requires \(c\land e_1\land\cdots\land e_m\Rightarrow\bot\). The certified antecedents may then support a conflict constraint or nogood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback returns bound antecedents whose conjunction with the responsible constraint implies the recorded inference or infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) identifies a recorded inference.
The supplied historical domain state matches the state in which \(q\) was derived.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The result certifies \(c\land\bigwedge E\Rightarrow q\) or \(c\land\bigwedge E\Rightarrow\bot\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication describes an explanation certificate, but the terminal container is a callback and may require algorithm rather than certificate as its primary kind. The historical-state inputs, callback outputs, and implication contract are solver-specific and cannot be settled without an authoritative interface citation.

children.title: Variable-Lock Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing constraint sensitivity to variable movement directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Lock Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional lock computation for variables in handled constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each handled constraint \(c\) and variable \(x_j\), the callback reports an upward lock if increasing \(x_j\), while holding other variables fixed within their domains, can change satisfaction of \(c\) into violation; it reports a downward lock analogously for decreasing \(x_j\). Locks are accumulated over active constraints. A fixing or rounding operation may use a direction only when the corresponding accumulated lock count is zero, unless feasibility is checked by another valid mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback records whether increasing or decreasing each variable can violate a handled constraint; zero locks identify directions safe from such violations.
assumptions_latex: Each lock is computed over the domain in which the handled constraint is active.
Lock counts include every active constraint capable of being violated in that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero upward or downward lock count certifies that movement in that direction cannot newly violate any counted constraint.

notation.meaning: Variable whose directional locks are computed.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the callback leaf. Directional lock conventions and the conclusion drawn from a zero accumulated count vary with solver definitions, constraint activity, and rounding semantics, so the exact claim requires an authoritative interface source.

children.title: Inference-to-Explanation Mapping
children.top_down_role: Association of propagated domain changes with reusable conflict reasons.

knowledge_statements.title: Inference-to-Explanation Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mapping recorded inferences to sufficient antecedent literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be the set of recorded inferences and \(L\) the set of bound literals. An explanation mapping assigns to each explainable inference \(q\in Q\) a responsible constraint \(c_q\) and a finite set \(E(q)\subseteq L\), reconstructed from the inference identifier and historical domain state, such that \(c_q\land\bigwedge_{e\in E(q)}e\Rightarrow q\). For an infeasibility record, the right-hand side is \(\bot\). This implication is the correctness condition for the mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each recorded inference maps to a responsible constraint and sufficient historical bound literals whose conjunction implies that inference or infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Each explainable inference has a stable identifier.
The historical domain state needed to reconstruct antecedents remains available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every mapped \(q\), the implication \(c_q\land\bigwedge_{e\in E(q)}e\Rightarrow q\) is valid.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: logical mapping underlying conflict analysis
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the mapping leaf and its implication condition is coherent. Stable inference identifiers, historical-domain reconstruction, and responsibility assignment are solver-interface details with no supporting citation.

children.title: Incomplete Explanation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where inference reasons or directional lock information are unavailable or unsound.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Explanation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary when an explanation omits necessary antecedents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an inference \(q\) was derived from constraint \(c\) and antecedents \(E\), but a callback returns \(E'\subsetneq E\). The shortened explanation is usable only if \(c\land\bigwedge E'\Rightarrow q\) remains valid. If some assignment satisfies \(c\land\bigwedge E'\land\neg q\), then a nogood learned from \(E'\) may exclude a feasible assignment. When validity cannot be established, the callback must decline the explanation or the solver must omit explanation-dependent learning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting a necessary antecedent makes an explanation unsound; if sufficiency cannot be established, conflict learning must not rely on that explanation.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is the inference being explained.
\(E'\) is the possibly incomplete returned antecedent set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explanation fails exactly when \(c\land\bigwedge E'\land\neg q\) is satisfiable.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: propositional sufficiency boundary for explanations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the logical insufficiency test is precise. The operational requirement to decline an explanation or suppress explanation-dependent learning is an uncited solver-interface claim and needs authoritative support.

children.title: Constraint Object Lifecycle Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces governing object lifecycle and external representation.

children.title: Transformation Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for creating transformed constraint-handler objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract semantic contract for transforming a constraint object from the original problem into solver space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an original constraint object \(c\) with predicate \(P_c:X\to\{0,1\}\) and a solution-preserving variable transformation \(\tau:X\to Y\), the callback creates a transformed object \(\bar c\), substitutes transformed variable handles, and transfers or duplicates owned data. It must return success only if \[P_{\bar c}(\tau(x))=P_c(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X.\] On failure it returns no registered object and releases every resource allocated during the attempted transformation. The returned object is initialized in the lifecycle state required by the transformed problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback constructs a solver-space constraint whose feasibility predicate agrees with the original constraint under the variable transformation, while preserving ownership and failure atomicity.
assumptions_latex: \(P_c\) is well-defined on the original variable space \(X\).
\(\tau\) preserves the represented solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\bar c}\circ\tau=P_c\).

notation.meaning: Feasibility predicate represented by constraint object c.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic-equivalence, ownership-transfer, failure-atomicity, and lifecycle-state requirements are solver-API-specific and have no cited source. A versioned constraint-handler API specification is required.

children.title: Copy Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for transferring handler objects into solver copies or subsolvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Copy Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic contract for copying constraint objects between compatible solver instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a source constraint object \(c\), a target solver, and a variable correspondence \(\pi:X\to X'\), the copy callback creates \(c'\) using target-side variable and plugin handles. It reports a valid copy only when \[P_{c'}(\pi(x))=P_c(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Mutable data owned by \(c'\) must be independent of mutable data owned by \(c\), unless the interface explicitly designates immutable shared storage. If a complete semantic copy is unavailable, the callback reports failure without leaving a registered partial constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid copy uses target-side handles, preserves the constraint predicate under variable correspondence, and avoids unsafe sharing of mutable owned data.
assumptions_latex: The source and target solver instances support compatible constraint-handler semantics.
\(\pi\) maps every referenced source variable to a target variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{c'}\circ\pi=P_c\), with valid target-side ownership.

notation.meaning: Predicate represented by the source constraint.

children.title: Deletion Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for releasing constraint and handler-specific state.

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource and state contract for destruction of a constraint object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a live constraint object \(c\) with finite set \(R(c)\) of resources owned by its constraint data, the deletion callback releases each element of \(R(c)\) exactly once, removes owned references, and marks the data handle invalid before returning. It must not release borrowed resources. After successful deletion, no later lifecycle callback may dereference the deleted data, and invoking deletion again is either prohibited by the lifecycle state machine or is an explicit no-op. Deleting \(c\) does not alter the mathematical predicates of other live constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion releases exactly the resources owned by a constraint, invalidates its data, preserves borrowed objects, and prevents subsequent dereferencing.
assumptions_latex: Ownership partitions resources into owned and borrowed sets.
\(c\) is in a lifecycle state permitting deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(r\in R(c)\) is released exactly once and the data of \(c\) becomes inaccessible.

notation.meaning: Finite set of resources owned by constraint c.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Exactly-once release, treatment of repeated deletion, handle invalidation, and effects on other constraints depend on the concrete lifecycle and ownership API. No source supports these requirements.

children.title: Printing Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for external textual representation of semantic constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Printing Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic textual representation contract for a constraint object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A printing callback assigns to every printable live constraint \(c\) and print context \(q\) a finite string \(S(c,q)\). The string must identify the constraint-handler syntax and represent all data needed to distinguish the predicate \(P_c\) within the advertised output format. For fixed \(c\) and \(q\), repeated calls satisfy \[S(c,q)=S(c,q),\] independently of transient memory addresses or traversal accidents. Printing is observational: it leaves the lifecycle state, ownership relation, and predicate \(P_c\) unchanged. If the format is declared parseable, parsing \(S(c,q)\) reconstructs an equivalent predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Printing deterministically serializes a live constraint without changing it; a format advertised as parseable must reconstruct an equivalent constraint predicate.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is live and printable in context \(q\).
Any parseability claim is restricted to the declared output grammar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Printing preserves \(P_c\) and all lifecycle state; parseable output satisfies \(P_{\operatorname{parse}(S(c,q))}=P_c\).

notation.meaning: Printed string for constraint c in context q.
Printing context, including format and naming rules.

review_flags: parseability may not be guaranteed by the intended interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality S(c,q)=S(c,q) is tautological and does not formalize repeat-call determinism. Deterministic output, predicate-distinguishing completeness, and round-trip parseability are not generic printing-callback guarantees, and the plain statement omits some of these requirements. The intended API specification is needed.

children.title: Lifecycle Callback Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency of object identity, state, and representation across lifecycle interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifecycle Callback Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-callback semantic and ownership invariants for one constraint-handler implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\), \(C_\pi\), \(D\), and \(S\) denote transformation, copying under correspondence \(\pi\), deletion, and printing. Lifecycle consistency requires: \(T\) and every successful \(C_\pi\) preserve the represented predicate under their variable maps; copying and transformation produce objects whose owned mutable data can be deleted independently; \(D\) is applied only to live owned data and makes that data unreachable; and \(S\) is observational. Whenever both compositions are supported, copying commutes semantically with transformation: \[P_{T(C_\pi(c))}=P_{C_{\bar\pi}(T(c))}\] after identifying corresponding transformed variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Callbacks are consistent when they preserve predicates, obey ownership and state transitions, permit independent deletion, and make copying commute semantically with transformation.
assumptions_latex: All mentioned callback compositions are supported by the handler.
\(\bar\pi\) is the induced correspondence between transformed variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{T(C_\pi(c))}=P_{C_{\bar\pi}(T(c))}\), with no ownership or lifecycle violation.

notation.meaning: Constraint copy operation under variable correspondence pi.

review_flags: callback composition rules may be solver-specific

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Predicate preservation, independent deletion, observational printing, and especially semantic commutation of copying with transformation are solver-specific cross-callback requirements. No lifecycle specification is cited.

children.title: CIP Plugin Architecture
children.top_down_role: Extensible component system for solver algorithms, representations, decomposition interfaces, and application integration.

children.title: Search-Relaxation Plugin Family
children.top_down_role: Plugins that modify search decisions or relaxation content.

children.title: Search Policy Plugin Interface
children.top_down_role: Extension points for search decisions.

children.title: Branching-Rule Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for selecting branching candidates and search partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Rule Plugins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness contract for a branching plugin at an active search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an active node with relaxation solution \(\hat x\) and feasible region \(F\), a branching-rule plugin either declines or returns child regions \(F_1,\ldots,F_k\) with \(k\ge 2\). It may score candidate disjunctions using \(\hat x\), bounds, pseudocosts, or probing information, but an accepted branch must satisfy \[F\cap X_I\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k F_i,\] where \(X_I\) imposes the required integrality conditions. The solver initializes corresponding child nodes, and the callback terminates after reporting the selected branch, its children, or a documented no-branch result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching plugin selects a disjunction whose children cover every integer-feasible solution of the parent node, then returns those children or declines.
assumptions_latex: The active node has well-defined region \(F\) and integrality domain \(X_I\).
Each returned child restriction is representable by the solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap X_I\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k F_i\).

notation.meaning: Set satisfying all required integrality restrictions.
Region assigned to child node i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited branch-and-cut section can support the mathematical coverage condition provisionally, but it does not establish the stated branching-plugin callback outcomes, child initialization, or termination/reporting contract. A versioned plugin API source is required.

children.title: Node-Selector Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for choosing the next open search node.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Selector Plugins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-frontier selection contract for a node-selector plugin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be the finite set of open, unpruned search nodes, each carrying solver-maintained metadata. A node-selector plugin computes or compares priority keys \(\kappa(v)\) and returns some \(v^*\in Q\) that is eligible under the solver state; under strict key selection it satisfies \[\kappa(v^*)=\min_{v\in Q}\kappa(v),\] with a deterministic documented tie rule. If \(Q=\varnothing\), it returns no node. Selection changes the active-node designation but does not itself delete other open nodes or invalidate their bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node selector chooses an eligible open node using a documented priority and tie rule, without silently discarding the remaining frontier.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) contains exactly the open, unpruned nodes.
The comparison key is defined for every eligible node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Q\ne\varnothing\), then \(v^*\in Q\); under strict key selection, \(v^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in Q}\kappa(v)\).

notation.meaning: Current set of open search nodes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited textbook section does not support this exact node-selector interface. Strict minimization, deterministic tie handling, eligibility, and preservation of all other frontier nodes are policy- and API-specific requirements.

children.title: Branching-to-Node-Selection Interaction
children.top_down_role: Effects of branch structure and metadata on subsequent node ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-to-Node-Selection Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frontier update linking a branching decision to subsequent node selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose branching replaces an active parent \(v\) by children \(C(v)=\{v_1,\ldots,v_k\}\), and let \(Q\) be the open frontier immediately before that replacement. After discarding children certified infeasible or dominated by the incumbent bound, the new frontier is \[Q'=(Q\setminus\{v\})\cup C_{\mathrm{live}}(v).\] The node selector is invoked on \(Q'\), not merely on the new children, and returns an eligible member of \(Q'\). Thus branching determines which nodes enter the frontier, while node selection determines the order in which all live frontier nodes are processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching inserts live children into the global frontier; node selection then chooses among those children and all previously open nodes.
assumptions_latex: The processed parent \(v\) belongs to the pre-branching frontier \(Q\).
Only safely pruned children are excluded from \(C_{\mathrm{live}}(v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q'=(Q\setminus\{v\})\cup C_{\mathrm{live}}(v)\), and the next node lies in \(Q'\).

notation.meaning: Open-node frontiers before and after branching.

review_flags: solver scheduling details need API confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global-frontier interpretation and the claim that the active parent belongs to the pre-branching open frontier depend on solver scheduling conventions. The cited general branch-and-cut section is insufficient for this plugin handoff.

children.title: Search-Policy Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of branching strategies with node-selection policies and solver stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Policy Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which branching and node-selection policies preserve exact search correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A branching rule and node selector are correctness-compatible if: every accepted branch covers all integer-feasible solutions of its parent; a node is removed only after processing or a valid pruning certificate; and every open node that remains relevant is eventually selected. Formally, for each parent region \(F\), \[F\cap X_I\subseteq\bigcup_i F_i,\] and the selector is fair: any node that stays open and unpruned from some iteration onward is selected after finitely many further selections. Under finite branching and these conditions, termination with an empty frontier certifies that no unexplored improving integer-feasible solution remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible policies use exhaustive branches, certified pruning, and fair node selection; an empty frontier then leaves no unexplored improving integer-feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: Every node has finitely many children.
Bounds and infeasibility tests used for pruning are valid.
The search is interpreted as an exact finite branch-and-bound or branch-and-cut run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An empty frontier implies that no unprocessed node can contain an improving point in \(X_I\).

notation.meaning: Child regions of parent region F.

review_flags: fairness formulation needs direct source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Exhaustive branching and valid pruning are standard, but the stated fairness condition and its role in plugin compatibility require direct support. The cited textbook locator does not establish this exact interface-level condition.

children.title: Cut Pipeline Plugin Interface
children.top_down_role: Extension points for generating and selecting relaxation rows.

children.title: Separator Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for generating candidate relaxation rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Plugins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity contract for generating cutting planes from a search-node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), its current solution \(\hat x\in R\), and the integer-feasible set \(F\subseteq R\), a separator plugin returns finitely many candidate inequalities \(a_j^{\mathsf T}x\le b_j\) or reports that none was found. Every returned inequality must be valid, \[a_j^{\mathsf T}x\le b_j\quad\text{for all }x\in F.\] A cut intended to separate \(\hat x\) additionally satisfies \(a_j^{\mathsf T}\hat x>b_j+\varepsilon_j\) for its declared numerical tolerance \(\varepsilon_j\ge0\). Returned cuts are candidates; insertion may be deferred to a cut selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator generates finitely many inequalities valid for every integer-feasible point, optionally requiring quantified violation by the current relaxation solution.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
Numerical violation tolerances are fixed before acceptance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each returned cut is valid for \(F\), and each separating cut excludes \(\hat x\) at its declared tolerance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The citation can provisionally support cut validity and separation, but not the exact separator-plugin return contract, finiteness requirement, tolerance convention, or deferred insertion behavior.

children.title: Cut-Selector Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for filtering, ranking, and retaining candidate cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Selector Plugins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection contract for choosing a bounded subset of valid candidate cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite candidate pool \(C\) of valid inequalities, current relaxation solution \(\hat x\), and insertion budget \(m\ge0\), a cut-selector plugin computes documented scores and returns an ordered subset \(S\subseteq C\) with \(|S|\le m\). It may filter cuts by efficacy, parallelism, density, numerical stability, or redundancy. Selection must not alter validity: every selected inequality remains valid for the integer-feasible set \(F\). Under a pure most-violated rule with score \(v(c,\hat x)\), the selected cuts have the largest eligible scores, subject to the budget and deterministic tie handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut selector ranks a valid candidate pool and returns a budgeted subset without weakening validity, using documented scoring and filtering rules.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(C\) is valid for \(F\).
The insertion budget \(m\) and eligibility tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq C\), \(|S|\le m\), and every \(c\in S\) is valid for \(F\).

notation.meaning: Declared violation score of cut c at the relaxation solution.

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

review_flags: general plugin contract exceeds cited selection rule

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited most-violated-cut section is narrower than the proposed general cut-selector contract. It does not support the plugin interface, ordered budgeted subset, listed filters, or deterministic tie handling.

children.title: Separator-to-Selector Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of cut candidates, metadata, and efficacy information between plugin stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator-to-Selector Handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed handoff from cut generation through selection to relaxation insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each invoked separator returns a finite candidate multiset \(C_i\) whose elements carry an inequality, validity scope, origin, and numerical metadata. The solver forms \(C=\bigcup_i C_i\), removes malformed or scope-ineligible entries, and passes the remaining pool with the current solution \(\hat x\) and budget \(m\) to the cut selector. The selector returns \(S\subseteq C\) with \(|S|\le m\); only cuts in \(S\) are scheduled for insertion. For every inserted local cut, its validity scope must contain the current node; every inserted global cut must be valid for the global integer-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separators submit annotated candidate cuts; the solver filters and pools them, and the selector returns the only cuts scheduled for insertion.
assumptions_latex: Every submitted cut declares its validity scope and numerical metadata.
The selector receives only well-formed, scope-eligible candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq\bigcup_i C_i\), \(|S|\le m\), and every inserted cut is valid on its declared scope.

notation.meaning: Candidate cuts returned by separator i.

review_flags: handoff metadata and scheduling require solver API source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Pooling, mandatory metadata, scope filtering, selector invocation, and the claim that only selected cuts are scheduled for insertion are solver-specific pipeline semantics not established by the cited general textbook section.

children.title: Cut-Pipeline Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Invalid, duplicate, incompatible, or excessively costly rows in the cut pipeline.

assumptions_latex: The current node relaxation has feasible set \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
Every accepted cut must be valid for the intended feasible set \(F\subseteq R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure to preserve validity, locality, numerical reliability, or synchronization invalidates the cut-pipeline result.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract mathematical boundary for a separator-to-selector cut pipeline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a separator propose \(a^\top x\leq b\) and let a selector decide whether to add it to the current relaxation. The pipeline is sound only if \(a^\top x\leq b\) holds for every \(x\in F\), its local or global validity scope is preserved, and all transformations applied before insertion preserve the represented inequality. It may fail if an invalid cut is accepted, a local cut is used outside its subtree, scaling or tolerances change its effective feasible halfspace, stale variable mappings are used, or duplicate and nearly parallel cuts exhaust resources without material relaxation improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut pipeline fails when it accepts invalid or mis-scoped cuts, corrupts their representation, uses stale mappings, or spends resources on numerically ineffective cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pipeline Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the solver-specific locality, synchronization, tolerance, or resource-exhaustion claims. The statement also conflates correctness failures with ineffective but still valid duplicate or nearly parallel cuts.

children.title: Nonlinear Relaxation Plugin Interface
children.top_down_role: Extension points for alternative lower-bounding relaxations.

children.title: Relaxator Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for computing alternative lower-bounding relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The original minimization problem has feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f\).
A plugin can solve a relaxation over a superset \(R\supseteq F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid relaxator result supplies a lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), together with an explicit execution status.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract minimization-oriented contract for a relaxation-solving plugin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the current search node, construct or update a relaxation \(R\supseteq F\), solve \(L=\inf\{f(x):x\in R\}\), and return a status describing whether \(L\) is finite, infeasible, unbounded, unavailable, or not solved reliably. If an optimal relaxation point \(\bar x\in R\) is available, return it as auxiliary relaxation information. The solver may use the finite value \(L\) as a node lower bound only when the plugin certifies validity for the current node; otherwise the result must not strengthen the global or local dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxator solves a valid superset relaxation and returns a bound, optional relaxation point, and status that controls whether the solver may use the result.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxator Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxation-bound principle is standard, but the callback result categories and their permitted solver effects require authoritative interface documentation. The record also alternates between the original feasible set and the current node-feasible set.

children.title: NLP-Interface Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points connecting nonlinear relaxations to external NLP solvers.

assumptions_latex: The nonlinear relaxation is represented by an objective and constraints over continuous variables.
A backend solver is available through a stateful interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface result is mathematically usable only when its model revision, solution status, and returned primal or dual data are mutually consistent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent contract for an NLP backend interface plugin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An NLP-interface plugin receives a model of the form \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq 0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and variable bounds, together with incremental model changes and solve requests. It must synchronize the backend model, invoke the nonlinear solver, and translate backend termination into a declared status. Returned values may include \(\bar x\), an objective value, constraint activities, and dual multipliers. Such data are attached to the current model revision only; stale, dimensionally inconsistent, or status-incompatible data must be rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An NLP-interface plugin synchronizes a nonlinear model with a backend, solves it, and returns status-consistent primal and dual data tied to the current model revision.
knowledge_statements.title: NLP-Interface Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected algorithm kind fits the interface leaf, but no source establishes the incremental synchronization, status translation, or returned-data contract. The dimension and domain of the nonlinear decision vector are not explicitly introduced.

children.title: Relaxator-to-NLP Integration
children.top_down_role: Use of nonlinear solver services within alternative relaxation plugins.

assumptions_latex: The relaxator owns a relaxation model \(R_k\) at search state \(k\).
The NLP interface can represent all active nonlinear rows and variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A backend result can update the relaxation bound only after synchronization and validity checks establish that it represents \(R_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-synchronization contract between a relaxator and an NLP backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At search state \(k\), the relaxator maps every active variable, bound, objective term, and nonlinear row defining \(R_k\) into backend model \(M_k\). After applying additions, deletions, and coefficient or bound changes, it requests a solve and translates the backend result. A finite value \(L_k\) may be reported as a valid relaxation bound only if \(M_k\) represents a superset of the node-feasible set and the returned status certifies the claimed bound. Any revision mismatch, unsupported expression, or interrupted solve must yield a nonbinding result unless a separate valid bound certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relaxator must synchronize the current relaxation with the NLP backend and accept a bound only when model revision, representability, and solve status agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxator-to-NLP Integration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integration algorithm is plausible, but the exact synchronization protocol and the statuses that certify usable bounds are solver-specific and unsupported. A source must also clarify how unsupported expressions and interrupted solves are represented.

children.title: Relaxation Status Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Translation of solution, bound, failure, and termination states across plugin interfaces.

assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem.
A relaxation is solved for a set \(R\) containing the node-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each returned status permits only the solver actions justified by its mathematical meaning.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions for consuming nonlinear-relaxation solve statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A status \(s\) is compatible with a solver action only as follows: certified infeasibility of \(R\) permits pruning; certified unboundedness must not be interpreted as infeasibility; a finite certified lower bound \(L\) permits bound strengthening; an optimal status permits use of both \(L\) and an associated solution when supplied; a feasible-but-not-optimal status permits primal-point use but no unproved optimal bound; and unknown, error, numerical-failure, or interrupted statuses permit no inference beyond any separately certified bound. Thus status translation must preserve both termination meaning and the guarantees attached to returned data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation statuses are compatible only with actions they certify: pruning needs infeasibility, bound updates need valid lower bounds, and uncertain termination supports no unsupported inference.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Status Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Authoritative status semantics are required. In particular, a point feasible only for a relaxation is not automatically an original-model primal solution, so “primal-point use” must be limited to auxiliary relaxation use unless original feasibility is separately established.

children.title: Dynamic Decomposition Plugin Family
children.top_down_role: Plugin interfaces for externally owned decomposition, pricing, and cut-generation mechanisms.

children.title: Pricer Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for dynamically generated variables.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master problem contains only a subset of variables.
For a minimization LP master, dual multipliers \(\pi\) define reduced costs of omitted columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pricing terminates exactly when no admissible omitted column has improving reduced cost, up to the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost pricing contract for dynamically generated master variables.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the restricted master and obtain dual multipliers \(\pi\). The pricer searches the admissible column set for a column \(j\) minimizing \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^\top a_j\). If \(\bar c_j<0\), subject to the pricing tolerance, add one or more such variables with their objective coefficients, bounds, types, and constraint coefficients, then reoptimize. If the pricing problem certifies \(\bar c_j\geq 0\) for every omitted admissible column, declare pricing complete. An incomplete or heuristic pricing call may add columns but cannot certify restricted-master optimality for the full master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pricer finds omitted variables with improving reduced cost, adds them to the restricted master, and certifies completion only after exhaustive pricing finds none.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricer Plugins

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost pricing description is mathematically plausible and the algorithm kind fits, but the cited chapter-level locator does not clearly support column pricing or the plugin callback contract. A pricing-specific source with an inspectable section or theorem is required.

children.title: Benders-Decomposition Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for master–subproblem coordination and generated constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders-Decomposition Plugins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical master-subproblem cut-generation contract for minimization, conditional on certified Benders cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a master candidate \((\bar y,\bar\theta)\), solve the subproblem defining \(Q(\bar y)\). If certified infeasibility is accompanied by a valid Benders feasibility cut violated by \(\bar y\), add that cut. If the subproblem has certified finite value \(Q(\bar y)\), \(\bar\theta<Q(\bar y)\) by more than the declared tolerance, and the subproblem certificate supplies a valid optimality cut that underestimates \(Q(y)\) on its declared domain and is violated at \((\bar y,\bar\theta)\), add that cut. Accept the candidate with respect to the decomposition only when subproblem feasibility and \(\bar\theta\geq Q(\bar y)\) are certified within tolerance; otherwise return a nonaccepting status if the required certificate is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Benders plugin solves the subproblem at a master candidate, adds a certified valid feasibility or optimality cut when one is available and violated, and accepts the candidate only after feasible recourse and an adequate recourse estimate are certified.
assumptions_latex: The master decision is \(y\), and the master variable \(\theta\) is constrained to underestimate the recourse value \(Q(y)\).
For each queried master point \(\bar y\), the subproblem procedure either certifies infeasibility, certifies a finite value \(Q(\bar y)\), or reports that no such certificate is available.
Whenever a cut is returned, its certificate establishes validity on the cut's declared master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The plugin adds only certified valid Benders cuts and accepts a candidate only after certifying subproblem feasibility and \(\bar\theta\geq Q(\bar y)\) within tolerance.

notation.meaning: subproblem value function at master decision y

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Decomposition-Specific Constraint Handlers
children.top_down_role: Constraint-centered integration of decomposition semantics.

assumptions_latex: A decomposition relation is represented by a constraint linking master and subproblem semantics.
The handler can test, propagate, separate, and enforce that relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition constraint is correctly handled only if every callback preserves the same feasible set under its declared scope.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-centered consistency requirement for decomposition integration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(y,z)\) denote the decomposition relation represented by a specialized constraint. Its handler may presolve the relation, propagate domains, check candidate solutions, separate valid inequalities, or enforce feasibility by branching or subproblem solution. Every such operation must be valid for the same relation and scope: propagation may remove a value only if no completion satisfies \(D(y,z)\); a generated inequality must hold for every satisfying completion; and acceptance requires that the candidate satisfy the represented decomposition semantics. If exact enforcement is deferred, the handler must return a status that prevents premature feasibility certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposition-specific handler must keep presolving, propagation, separation, and enforcement consistent with one represented master-subproblem relation and must not certify deferred checks as feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Specific Constraint Handlers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind is defensible, but no source establishes the constraint-handler callbacks or deferred-enforcement status semantics. The domain and formal meaning of the abstract relation D are also insufficiently specified.

children.title: Search Progress Plugin Family
children.top_down_role: Plugins responsible for global reduction, domain inference, and feasible-solution search.

children.title: Presolver Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for global model reductions.

assumptions_latex: The original model has feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f\).
A presolve transformation produces a reduced model with feasible set \(F'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A presolver is sound when reduced solutions lift to original solutions and all eliminations preserve infeasibility and objective claims.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global model-reduction contract with explicit solution reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolver inspects the global model, tightens variable bounds, removes redundant constraints, fixes or aggregates variables, or detects infeasibility, producing a reduced feasible set \(F'\) and reconstruction map \(T\). Soundness requires that every \(x'\in F'\) lift to \(T(x')\in F\) with the correctly transformed objective value, and that every original feasible solution relevant to the optimum have a corresponding reduced representative. A declaration of infeasibility requires \(F=\varnothing\). The plugin must record sufficient reverse transformations to reconstruct original-space solutions after solving the reduced model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolver globally reduces a model while preserving relevant feasible solutions and objective values, and records transformations needed to reconstruct original-space solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolver Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but an authoritative source is needed for reconstruction, result codes, and objective-preservation requirements. “Every original feasible solution relevant to the optimum” is not a precise quantified condition.

children.title: Propagator Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for independent domain inference.

assumptions_latex: At a search node, each variable has a current domain \(D_i\).
The active constraints define the node-feasible set \(F_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A propagated domain reduction is valid exactly when it contains every coordinate value attained by a node-feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent node-domain inference with conflict-detection semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A propagator reads the current domains and active constraints, then returns tightened domains \(D_i'\subseteq D_i\), a cutoff, or no reduction. Each tightening must satisfy \(x_i\in D_i'\) for every \(x\in F_N\); a cutoff is valid only if \(F_N=\varnothing\). The propagator may also provide reasons linking each inference to bounds and constraints that imply it. Repeated propagation continues until no scheduled plugin produces a material reduction or infeasibility is detected. The propagator does not need to own the constraints from which its valid inferences are derived.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagator independently tightens node domains or proves cutoff, but every reduction must retain all values used by node-feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The domain-safety condition is mathematically sound, but the scheduling, cutoff, reason-generation, and repeated-propagation claims require an authoritative plugin-interface source.

children.title: Primal-Heuristic Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for feasible-solution construction and improvement.

assumptions_latex: The solver maintains an incumbent feasible solution or no incumbent.
A heuristic may inspect the current relaxation, search state, and incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A heuristic output may improve the primal bound only after complete feasibility and objective validation in the original model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-solution construction and incumbent-improvement contract for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When scheduled, a primal-heuristic plugin constructs or improves a candidate \(\hat x\) using available search information, possibly by rounding, repair, local search, or a restricted auxiliary solve. Before submission, discrete coordinates must satisfy their integrality conditions and all values must lie within variable domains. The solver accepts \(\hat x\) only after verifying \(\hat x\in F\) under feasibility tolerances and evaluating its original objective. For minimization, the incumbent bound is updated from \(U\) to \(f(\hat x)\) only if no incumbent exists or \(f(\hat x)<U\) by the required improvement tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal heuristic constructs or improves candidate solutions, but the incumbent changes only after the solver validates original-model feasibility, integrality, and objective improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Heuristic Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and incumbent-validation principle fit the leaf, but the scheduling, submission, validation, and improvement-tolerance contract is unsupported and solver-specific.

children.title: Solver Integration Plugin Family
children.top_down_role: Plugins supporting data exchange, observation, user control, and problem-specific integration.

children.title: Data Exchange Control Plugin Interface
children.top_down_role: Extension points for data formats and interactive control.

children.title: Reader Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for importing models, solutions, parameters, and auxiliary data.

assumptions_latex: An input instance is encoded in a declared external format.
The solver has an internal model class \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful read must either construct an equivalent internal model or explicitly report unsupported or invalid input.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract correctness contract for model-reader plugins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reader plugin recognizes a declared format, parses an encoding \(E\), and either returns a model \(P(E)\in\mathcal M\) or a status distinguishing unsupported format, malformed input, and read failure. On success, the internal variables, domains, objective, constraints, names, and format-defined metadata must represent the semantics of \(E\), modulo explicitly documented normalization. The plugin must not silently discard unsupported constructs when doing so changes the feasible set or objective. Partial models produced before an error must not be treated as successfully imported unless partial-read semantics are explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reader plugin parses a declared format into an equivalent internal model and reports unsupported, malformed, or failed input without silently changing model semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Reader Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but no source supports the proposed reader statuses, partial-read behavior, or required metadata preservation. Equivalence also depends on a declared external format whose semantics are not specified.

children.title: Writer Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for exporting solver objects and run artifacts.

assumptions_latex: The solver state is represented by an object \(S\), and the requested output format is \(f\).
A writer may inspect \(S\) but must not alter its optimization semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful invocation produces a representation \(y\) satisfying the writer's format contract for \(f\); otherwise it returns an explicit unsupported-format or write-failure status.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers the SCIP writer-plugin interface; authoritative solver documentation is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract contract for serialization plugins in a constraint integer programming solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be the supported format set. A writer plugin is a partial operation \(W_f:S\mapsto (y,r)\), indexed by \(f\in\mathcal F\), where \(y\) is serialized problem or solution data and \(r\) is a status. If \(r=\mathrm{success}\), parsing \(y\) according to \(f\) must recover the information promised by the format contract. Invocation must leave the feasible set and objective represented by \(S\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A writer plugin serializes solver data in a supported format, reports success or failure, and does not change the represented optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Writer Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports the asserted writer status, preservation, or round-trip contract. These implementation-specific guarantees require authoritative SCIP documentation with a precise locator.

children.title: Dialog Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for interactive commands and solver control.

assumptions_latex: The dialog state \(D\) contains a command path, user input, and access to an admissible solver state \(S\).
Each command callback declares the solver stages in which it may execute.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dispatch either executes exactly one admissible callback and returns its successor dialog state, or reports that the command is unavailable or invalid.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers the SCIP dialog-plugin callback and stage contract.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interactive command dispatch through registered dialog plugins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((D,S)\), resolve the next command token sequence to at most one callback \(c\in\mathcal C\). If no callback matches, return an invalid-command status. If \(c\) is not admissible at the current solver stage, return an unavailable-command status. Otherwise invoke \(c(D,S)\), propagate its status, and output the returned successor dialog state \(D'\). Stop when the callback requests termination or no further input is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dialog plugin resolves an interactive command, checks whether it is currently admissible, invokes its callback, and returns the next dialog state or an error.
knowledge_statements.title: Dialog Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The callback uniqueness, stage-admissibility, successor-state, and termination semantics are implementation-specific and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Format Round-Trip Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Preservation of supported model information across reader and writer plugins.

assumptions_latex: A writer \(W_f\) and reader \(R_f\) implement the same format \(f\).
An equivalence relation \(\sim\) specifies which model information the format promises to preserve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Round-trip compatibility holds exactly when every supported state is equivalent to its write-read reconstruction and every successful reconstruction is accepted by the reader.

notation.meaning: writer and reader for format f
states supported by the round trip

review_flags: No supplied source locator defines format-specific preservation guarantees or reader-writer compatibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic, not byte-for-byte, compatibility of a paired reader and writer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For supported states \(\mathcal S_f\), the pair \((W_f,R_f)\) is round-trip compatible relative to \(\sim\) if and only if, for every \(S\in\mathcal S_f\), successful writing gives \(y=W_f(S)\), successful reading gives \(S'=R_f(y)\), and \(S'\sim S\). The relation \(\sim\) must cover all format-promised data, including variable domains, objective sense and coefficients, constraints, and names whenever names are declared preservable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A format round trip is compatible when writing and then reading every supported model preserves all semantics promised by that format.
knowledge_statements.title: Format Round-Trip Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract condition fits the leaf, but the claimed set of format-promised data and reader-writer behavior needs format-specific authoritative documentation.

children.title: Solver Observation Plugin Interface
children.top_down_role: Extension points for observation and progress reporting.

children.title: Event-Handler Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for subscribing to and processing solver events.

assumptions_latex: The solver emits events from a declared event-type set \(\mathcal E\).
Callback execution obeys the solver's stage and mutation restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only subscribed, matching events invoke the handler, and removing the subscription prevents subsequent invocations for that subscription.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers SCIP event filters, subscriptions, or callback restrictions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subscription-based observation of solver lifecycle and search events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An event-handler plugin is a pair \((M,h)\), where \(M:\mathcal E\to\{0,1\}\) is a subscription predicate and \(h(e,S)\) is a callback. When event \(e\) is emitted in state \(S\), the solver invokes \(h\) only if the subscription is active and \(M(e)=1\). The callback may update plugin-owned observation state but may modify solver state only through operations explicitly permitted at that event and solver stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An event-handler plugin subscribes to selected solver events and runs a constrained callback when a matching event occurs.
knowledge_statements.title: Event-Handler Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Subscription filtering, callback invocation, removal behavior, and permitted solver-state mutations depend on the SCIP event API and require a precise source locator.

children.title: Display Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for presenting progress columns and status summaries.

assumptions_latex: The solver exposes an observation state \(O(S)\) at each permitted display update.
Each display column declares an activation rule and a rendering callback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An active display callback returns a bounded-width textual representation of its designated observation without changing the solver state.

notation.meaning: read-only observable projection of solver state

review_flags: No supplied source locator covers SCIP display-column activation, width, or callback semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Read-only progress-column plugins for solver status displays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A display plugin defines metadata \((w,p,a)\) and a callback \(d\), where \(w\in\mathbb N\) is field width, \(p\) is display priority, and \(a(S)\in\{0,1\}\) is an activation predicate. At an eligible update in state \(S\), an active plugin computes \(d(O(S))\), whose rendered width does not exceed \(w\). Evaluation of \(a\) and \(d\) must leave \(S\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A display plugin renders a bounded-width, read-only solver observation when its activation rule and display schedule permit an update.
knowledge_statements.title: Display Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The metadata tuple, activation predicate, width guarantee, scheduling, and read-only behavior are implementation-specific claims without supporting citations.

children.title: Event-to-Display Data Flow
children.top_down_role: Transfer of observed solver state into user-facing progress displays.

assumptions_latex: Event callbacks update plugin-owned observation state atomically with respect to display reads.
Display refreshes occur only at solver-defined safe points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each rendered field reflects a well-defined observation snapshot produced by events no later than its refresh point.

notation.meaning: plugin observation state after event k

review_flags: No supplied source locator documents the synchronization and refresh semantics of SCIP observation plugins.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract pipeline from subscribed solver events to progress-display fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize plugin observation state as \(z_0\). For each subscribed event \(e_k\), apply the handler update \(z_k=H(z_{k-1},e_k)\). At a display refresh occurring after event \(e_j\) and before \(e_{j+1}\), read a consistent snapshot of \(z_j\), evaluate the active display fields \(d(z_j)\), and emit them. Event processing and rendering must not introduce solver-state transitions outside their permitted callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subscribed events update observation state; each display refresh reads a consistent snapshot and renders active fields without independently changing the solver.
knowledge_statements.title: Event-to-Display Data Flow

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted atomic updates, consistent snapshots, event ordering, and safe refresh points cannot be established without authoritative documentation of SCIP execution semantics.

children.title: Observation Overhead Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Runtime and synchronization costs introduced by event or display plugins.

assumptions_latex: A baseline run performs \(T\) solver operations without observation plugins.
There are \(E\) delivered events and \(D\) display refreshes during the observed run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If callback and refresh costs are uniformly bounded, total observation work is additive; without such bounds, plugins can asymptotically dominate the solve.

notation.meaning: numbers of delivered events and display refreshes

review_flags: The bound is an abstract accounting result; no supplied source quantifies SCIP observation overhead.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive work bound for synchronous event handling and display refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a unit-cost RAM model, suppose each delivered event callback costs at most \(c_e\) operations and each display refresh costs at most \(c_d\) operations, including all active fields. Then total work is at most \(T+Ec_e+Dc_d+O(E+D)\), excluding external output latency. Thus observation overhead is \(O(Ec_e+Dc_d)\). If either callback performs unbounded work or synchronous output has unbounded latency, no bound relative to \(T\) follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded callbacks add work proportional to delivered events and display refreshes; expensive callbacks or blocking output can dominate solver time.
knowledge_statements.title: Observation Overhead Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The accounting bound is plausible under its stated model, but its applicability to this solver-observation interface and the assumed synchronous processing model are not sourced.

children.title: Nonlinear Expression Processing Plugin Interface
children.top_down_role: Extension points for nonlinear representation and semantic processing.

children.title: Expression Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for nonlinear expression operators and expression-tree services.

assumptions_latex: Nonlinear formulas are represented by rooted expression trees or directed acyclic graphs.
Each expression kind declares evaluation and derivative capabilities on an explicit domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A registered expression plugin supplies the declared operations for every node of its kind and reports domain or capability failure explicitly.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers SCIP expression-handler callbacks and capability declarations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-level plugins for nonlinear expression representation and computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An expression plugin for operator \(\phi\) defines construction, comparison or hashing as required, evaluation, and any declared differentiation or simplification operations for nodes \(e=\phi(e_1,\ldots,e_k)\). For every \(x\) in the declared domain, evaluation must satisfy \(v_e(x)=\phi(v_{e_1}(x),\ldots,v_{e_k}(x))\). Outside the domain, or when a requested optional operation is unavailable, the plugin must return an explicit failure status rather than an ordinary value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expression plugin represents one nonlinear operator and consistently implements its declared evaluation, differentiation, simplification, and structural operations.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mandatory structural operations, optional capabilities, domain-failure behavior, and callback contract require authoritative SCIP expression-handler documentation.

children.title: Nonlinear-Handler Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension points for detecting and processing nonlinear structure.

assumptions_latex: A nonlinear constraint has an expression representation \(g(x)\) and bounds \(\ell\leq g(x)\leq u\).
Handlers declare a detection predicate and the enforcement capabilities they provide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonlinear-handler plugin may claim an expression only when its detection predicate holds and must implement every capability it claims.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers SCIP nonlinear-handler detection and enforcement contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structure-level handlers for nonlinear constraint detection and enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-handler plugin \(h\) consists of a detection predicate \(P_h\) and callbacks for a declared capability set \(C_h(g)\), such as interval propagation, separation, relaxation initialization, or enforcement. If \(P_h(g)=1\), detection returns the expression components owned by \(h\) and the capabilities claimed for them. For each claimed capability, the corresponding callback must either produce a valid result for \(\ell\leq g(x)\leq u\) or return an explicit non-success status.
