knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear handler recognizes specified expression structures and provides declared propagation, relaxation, separation, or enforcement operations for them.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear-Handler Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Detection ownership, capability declarations, and allowed non-success results are specific to the nonlinear-handler interface and lack a supporting locator.

children.title: Expression-to-Handler Dispatch
children.top_down_role: Assignment of expression structures to compatible nonlinear handlers.

assumptions_latex: A finite ordered set of nonlinear handlers \(\mathcal H\) is registered.
Each handler exposes a detection predicate and a declared priority.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dispatch assigns only detected capabilities, resolves competing claims by the configured ordering rule, and leaves every unclaimed required capability explicitly unsupported.
review_flags: No supplied source locator determines SCIP's exact nonlinear-handler ordering and ownership rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-based assignment of nonlinear expression capabilities to registered handlers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate expression subgraph \(g\), evaluate detection for every eligible \(h\in\mathcal H\) and form \(A(g)=\{h:P_h(g)=1\}\). Order \(A(g)\) by the solver's declared handler priority and deterministic tie rule. Assign each required capability to the first eligible claimant permitted to own or share it, record the resulting ownership, and recurse on unclaimed child subgraphs. If a required capability remains unassigned, return an unsupported-structure status for that capability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dispatch tests registered nonlinear handlers, orders successful detections, assigns claimed capabilities, and reports any required capability left unsupported.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression-to-Handler Dispatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed priority ordering, tie rule, capability ownership or sharing, recursion, and unsupported-status behavior cannot be trusted without exact SCIP dispatch documentation.

children.title: Unsupported Nonlinear Structure
children.top_down_role: Expression forms lacking suitable evaluation, relaxation, propagation, or enforcement support.

assumptions_latex: A nonlinear constraint contains an expression subgraph \(g\).
Correct processing requires a capability set \(C_{\mathrm{req}}(g)\) at the current solver stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If any required capability is absent, the plugin system cannot certify complete processing of that structure and must reject, reformulate, or defer it.
review_flags: No supplied source locator specifies which missing nonlinear capabilities are fatal at each SCIP solver stage.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure criterion for nonlinear structures lacking required plugin capabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After expression-to-handler dispatch, define \(C_{\mathrm{miss}}(g)=C_{\mathrm{req}}(g)\setminus C_{\mathrm{sup}}(g)\). The structure is unsupported at the current stage exactly when \(C_{\mathrm{miss}}(g)\neq\varnothing\). In that case, the solver must not treat processing as complete: it must return an unsupported status, apply a semantics-preserving reformulation accepted by available handlers, or defer the operation to a stage where the missing capability is unnecessary or available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear structure is unsupported when dispatch leaves a currently required capability unprovided; the solver must reject, reformulate, or defer it.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Nonlinear Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition depends on an unspecified stage-dependent required-capability set, while the asserted reject, reformulate, or defer policy is not supported by a source.

children.title: Plugin Lifecycle Coordination System
children.top_down_role: Rules for component registration, scheduling, state ownership, copying, and interaction.

children.title: Plugin Scheduling Calculus
children.top_down_role: Discovery and scheduling of competing components.

children.title: Plugin Registration
children.top_down_role: Discovery, inclusion, naming, and capability metadata for solver components.

assumptions_latex: Each plugin supplies a unique key, type, callbacks, and scheduling metadata.
Registration occurs before the first solver stage requiring that plugin type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful registration inserts exactly one validated plugin descriptor into the appropriate registry; duplicate or invalid descriptors are rejected without partial insertion.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers SCIP plugin inclusion, duplicate-name handling, or registration-stage restrictions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation and insertion of a plugin into a type-specific solver registry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given descriptor \(p\) of type \(t\), first verify that all mandatory callbacks and metadata are present, that \(k(p)\) is valid, and that registration is permitted at the current solver stage. Next require \(k(p)\neq k(q)\) for every \(q\in\mathcal R_t\). If any check fails, return an error and leave \(\mathcal R_t\) unchanged. Otherwise initialize registration-owned data, insert \(p\) once into \(\mathcal R_t\), and return success.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plugin registration validates callbacks, metadata, stage, and key uniqueness before atomically inserting the plugin into its type-specific registry.
knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Registration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Mandatory metadata, key uniqueness, admissible registration stages, atomic failure, and initialization order are implementation-specific registration semantics requiring authoritative documentation.

children.title: Plugin Priority
children.top_down_role: Relative ordering among competing components at shared execution points.

knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Priority
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic priority ordering for plugins eligible at the same solver event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite set of registered plugins and let \(E_t\subseteq P\) be the plugins eligible at event \(t\). A plugin priority is a map \(\pi:P\to\mathbb Z\). The scheduler orders \(E_t\) by decreasing \(\pi\); plugins with equal priority are ordered by a fixed tie-break key \(\tau:P\to\mathbb N\). Thus \(p\) precedes \(q\) exactly when \(\pi(p)>\pi(q)\), or when \(\pi(p)=\pi(q)\) and \(\tau(p)<\tau(q)\). Priority determines consideration order, not eligibility or guaranteed execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eligible plugins run in descending integer priority, with a fixed tie-break rule. Priority controls consideration order but neither eligibility nor guaranteed execution.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite.
\(\tau\) is injective on every equal-priority class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_t\) has a deterministic total execution order.

notation.meaning: plugins eligible at solver event t

review_flags: solver-specific priority direction and tie-breaking require an architecture source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Plugin Priority leaf and is internally precise, but decreasing priority, deterministic tie-breaking, and the distinction between consideration and execution are solver-specific conventions unsupported by any citation.

children.title: Plugin Invocation Frequency
children.top_down_role: Cadence controls for repeated component execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Invocation Frequency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility condition induced by a periodic invocation parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a plugin \(p\), let \(f_p\in\mathbb N_{>0}\cup\{\infty\}\) be its invocation frequency and let \(k\in\mathbb N_0\) index compatible solver events. Its frequency condition is \(F_p(k)\iff f_p<\infty\) and \(k\equiv0\pmod{f_p}\). The scheduler may invoke \(p\) at event \(k\) only if \(F_p(k)\) holds and all independent stage and applicability predicates hold. The value \(f_p=1\) permits every compatible event, whereas \(f_p=\infty\) disables periodic invocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive frequency permits invocation at every corresponding event multiple; infinity disables periodic calls. Other lifecycle and applicability conditions remain necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) counts only events compatible with the plugin class.
Frequency is fixed during the indexed scheduling interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Invocation at event \(k\) implies \(F_p(k)\).
review_flags: frequency conventions vary across solver plugin classes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but the modular event rule, infinity convention, and indexing of compatible events vary among plugin classes and require solver architecture documentation.

children.title: Plugin Execution Timing
children.top_down_role: Solver stages and contexts in which a component may run.

knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Execution Timing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stage and event predicates governing when an eligible plugin may execute.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the finite set of solver stages, \(T_p\subseteq S\) the stages admitted for plugin \(p\), and \(A_p(s,x)\) its applicability predicate at stage \(s\) and solver state \(x\). Execution of \(p\) is timing-valid precisely when \(s\in T_p\), \(A_p(s,x)\) holds, initialization has completed, and cleanup has not begun. Any frequency or priority rule is applied only after this timing-validity test; neither rule can authorize execution outside \(T_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A plugin may execute only in an admitted solver stage, when applicable, after initialization, and before cleanup. Frequency and priority cannot override these boundaries.
assumptions_latex: Solver stages have a defined lifecycle order.
\(A_p\) is evaluated on the current solver state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every valid execution satisfies \(s\in T_p\) and \(A_p(s,x)\).
review_flags: exact stage names and callback permissions are solver-specific

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits execution timing, but the asserted ordering of timing validation, frequency, and priority, together with initialization and cleanup boundaries, is an undocumented solver-specific callback contract.

children.title: Scheduling Conflict Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Starvation, redundant work, or unsafe execution caused by incompatible scheduling controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Conflict Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating deterministic scheduling from order-dependent plugin interference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an event \(t\), model each eligible plugin \(p\) as a partial state transition \(U_p:X\rightharpoonup X\). Two plugins \(p,q\) are conflict-free on a domain \(D\subseteq X\) when both compositions are defined and \(U_p(U_q(x))=U_q(U_p(x))\) for every \(x\in D\). If this condition fails, their simultaneous or unspecified-order execution lies beyond the conflict-free boundary: the scheduler must serialize them by a deterministic order, recompute eligibility after the first update, or reject one invocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plugins are conflict-free when their state updates commute. Otherwise, unspecified ordering can change the solver state, so execution requires serialization, revalidation, or rejection.
assumptions_latex: Each invocation is represented by a partial transition on solver states.
Compared executions begin from the same state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Noncommuting transitions require explicit conflict resolution.

notation.meaning: state transition induced by plugin p
domain on which conflict freedom is tested

review_flags: formal commutativity model is a general abstraction requiring solver-specific validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but commutativity of partial state transitions is a proposed abstraction rather than an established plugin scheduling contract. A source must justify both the model and the stated resolution requirements.

children.title: Plugin State Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Plugin state across solver stages.

children.title: Plugin Initialization
children.top_down_role: Creation and activation of plugin state before solving.

knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifecycle transition that prepares plugin-owned state before operational callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a registered plugin descriptor \(d\), solver context \(c\), and an uninitialized state marker \(\bot\). The initialization callback validates required services, allocates or acquires resources \(R\), constructs plugin state \(z=I(d,c,R)\), and records every ownership or release obligation. It returns either \((\mathrm{ready},z)\) or \((\mathrm{failed},e)\). Operational callbacks are enabled only after a ready return; on failure, all resources acquired during the attempt are released and the plugin remains nonoperational.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialization validates dependencies, acquires resources, constructs state, and records cleanup obligations. Only successful completion enables operational callbacks; failure rolls back acquired resources.
assumptions_latex: The plugin is registered and not already initialized.
Resource acquisition reports failure explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a ready state \(z\) or a failure with no retained attempt-local resources.
review_flags: callback contract and rollback guarantees require solver API documentation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is plausible for initialization, but dependency validation, transactional rollback, resource release, and callback-enablement guarantees require a concrete solver API or architecture source.

children.title: Plugin Transformation
children.top_down_role: Adaptation of plugin state to transformed solver objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Transformation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of plugin state from an original model to its transformed solver representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given original plugin state \(z_o\), a model transformation \(T:M_o\to M_t\), and an object correspondence map \(\phi\), construct transformed state \(z_t=G(z_o,T,\phi)\). Every stored reference to an original object \(a\) that has a transformed counterpart is replaced by \(\phi(a)\); immutable configuration may be copied, while mutable caches are rebuilt or marked invalid. The transformation succeeds only if every required reference has a valid counterpart and all ownership obligations of \(z_t\) are registered; otherwise it returns failure without enabling transformed-stage callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transformation maps plugin state and object references to the transformed model, copying configuration while rebuilding or invalidating caches. Missing required counterparts cause failure.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) has produced the transformed model.
\(\phi\) is defined for every required referenced object.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful output \(z_t\) refers only to valid transformed or explicitly shared objects.
review_flags: transformation semantics and reference-transfer rules are solver-specific

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the transformation leaf, but correspondence mapping, cache treatment, ownership registration, and failure behavior are solver-specific and presently uncited.

children.title: Plugin Cleanup
children.top_down_role: Release or reset of plugin resources at solver-stage transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Cleanup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idempotent lifecycle transition releasing plugin resources and disabling callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given plugin state \(z\) with a finite set \(R(z)\) of outstanding owned resources, cleanup disables new operational callbacks, waits for or cancels permitted in-flight invocations, releases every \(r\in R(z)\) exactly once in reverse dependency order, clears borrowed references, and sets \(z\leftarrow\bot\). Calling cleanup on \(\bot\) has no effect. The output state has no plugin-owned live resource and cannot execute operational callbacks unless a new initialization occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cleanup disables callbacks, resolves in-flight work, releases each owned resource once in dependency-safe order, clears borrowed references, and leaves an inert state.
assumptions_latex: The resource-dependency relation is acyclic.
No new callback begins after cleanup disables invocation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After cleanup, \(R(z)=\varnothing\) and \(z=\bot\).

notation.meaning: outstanding resources owned by the plugin

review_flags: idempotence and in-flight callback behavior require solver API confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits cleanup, but idempotence, cancellation or waiting for in-flight callbacks, reverse dependency release, and exact-once release are strong implementation guarantees needing an authoritative source.

children.title: Cross-Stage State Continuity
children.top_down_role: Persistence and remapping of plugin state across lifecycle transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Stage State Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant relating plugin state before and after a solver-stage transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For consecutive lifecycle stages \(s_i\prec s_{i+1}\), let \(z_i\) be the plugin state before transition and \(z_{i+1}=H_i(z_i)\) afterward. Cross-stage continuity holds when every invariant datum \(a\) has the same semantic value in both states, every stage-specific reference is replaced through the prescribed correspondence map, every carried owned resource remains live with unchanged ownership, and every invalidated cache is marked unusable until recomputed. A callback at \(s_{i+1}\) is admissible only if these conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across stages, invariant data retain meaning, references are translated, ownership remains valid, and stale caches stay disabled. Later callbacks require all continuity conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i\prec s_{i+1}\) is an allowed lifecycle transition.
\(H_i\) is the prescribed state-transfer operation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissibility at \(s_{i+1}\) implies preservation of all declared cross-stage invariants.

notation.meaning: plugin state at lifecycle stage i

review_flags: required invariants depend on the concrete solver lifecycle

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits cross-stage continuity, but the required invariant data, reference correspondence, resource carryover, cache invalidation, and callback admissibility depend on a concrete lifecycle specification.

children.title: Lifecycle Ordering Failures
children.top_down_role: Invalid state caused by missing, repeated, or misordered lifecycle callbacks.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifecycle Ordering Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Illegal callback sequences that invalidate plugin state or resource safety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the legal lifecycle language be \(L=\{\mathrm{register}\,\mathrm{initialize}\,(\mathrm{transform})?\,\mathrm{execute}^{*}\,\mathrm{cleanup}\}\), with optional repeated solve epochs represented by complete initialize-to-cleanup segments. A callback trace outside \(L\) is an ordering failure. In particular, execution before initialization, transformation before required original state exists, execution after cleanup, repeated non-idempotent initialization, or cleanup concurrent with an unprotected callback may access undefined state, stale references, or released resources; no plugin correctness guarantee extends to such traces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Callback traces outside the prescribed lifecycle are failures. They may use absent, stale, or released state, so plugin correctness guarantees no longer apply.
assumptions_latex: Callbacks obey a single trace order, or synchronization induces one.
Repeated solve epochs use distinct complete lifecycle segments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every trace \(w\notin L\), lifecycle safety is not guaranteed.
review_flags: legal trace language is an abstraction requiring solver-specific lifecycle documentation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the proposed legal language fixes one lifecycle sequence and optionality without evidence. Actual plugin types may initialize, transform, solve, exit, and free under different callback traces.

children.title: Plugin Resource Ownership System
children.top_down_role: Coordination of variables, constraints, solutions, and relaxation artifacts.

children.title: Shared Plugin State
children.top_down_role: State exchanged across callbacks, components, solver stages, or related objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Plugin State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State intentionally accessible by multiple plugins or solver objects under a synchronization contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Shared plugin state is a tuple \((z,A,M,\sigma)\), where \(z\) is a mutable state object, \(A\) is a nonempty set of authorized clients, \(M:A\to 2^{\{\mathrm{read},\mathrm{write}\}}\) assigns access modes, and \(\sigma\) is a synchronization protocol. An access by \(a\in A\) is valid only if its mode belongs to \(M(a)\), the lifetime of \(z\) covers the complete access, and the execution satisfies \(\sigma\). Conflicting accesses are a pair involving at least one write and must be ordered by \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared state has authorized clients, access modes, a covering lifetime, and a synchronization protocol. Any pair of conflicting accesses must be ordered.
assumptions_latex: Clients access \(z\) only through the declared contract.
The synchronization protocol defines ordering for conflicting accesses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every valid conflicting access pair is ordered by \(\sigma\).
review_flags: concurrency and sharing contracts require solver implementation documentation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits shared plugin state, but its authorization, lifetime, and synchronization contract is a generic concurrency model rather than a sourced property of the target solver architecture.

children.title: Reference Counting
children.top_down_role: Retention accounting for solver objects referenced by plugins.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference Counting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-lifetime invariant for solver objects retained by multiple clients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an object \(o\), let \(H(o)\) be the finite set of live owning handles and let \(c(o)\in\mathbb N_0\) be its reference count. The reference-counting invariant is \(c(o)=|H(o)|\). Creating or copying an owning handle increments \(c(o)\) once; destroying or releasing such a handle decrements it once. The object may be destroyed exactly when a decrement changes \(c(o)\) to zero. Borrowed handles do not change the count and must not outlive an owning handle that guarantees the object's lifetime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reference count equals the number of live owning handles. Ownership acquisition increments it, release decrements it, and zero permits destruction.
assumptions_latex: Every owning-handle operation updates the count atomically with ownership transfer.
Each owning handle is released exactly once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(o)>0\) preserves \(o\), while a transition to \(c(o)=0\) permits destruction.
review_flags: standard systems invariant but solver-specific capture and release semantics need a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits reference counting and the invariant is standard, but the candidate supplies neither a standard systems source nor solver documentation supporting atomic updates, borrowed-handle rules, and destruction semantics.

children.title: Object Ownership
children.top_down_role: Allocation, mutation, transfer, and disposal responsibilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Object Ownership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusive responsibility for maintaining and releasing a solver resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a live resource \(r\) and clients \(A\), an ownership assignment is a partial function \(\omega:R\rightharpoonup A\) such that \(\omega(r)=a\) designates the unique client responsible for preserving and eventually releasing \(r\). Ownership transfer from \(a\) to \(b\) is an atomic update \(\omega(r):a\mapsto b\) that invalidates the transferring owner's release right. A client holding only a borrowed reference may access \(r\) within its declared scope but may neither release it nor retain it beyond the owner's lifetime guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each owned resource has one responsible client. Transfer atomically moves release authority; borrowed references neither release the resource nor outlive its guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Each live owned resource has at most one exclusive owner.
Transfers occur before the former owner's release.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every instant, at most one client has authority to release \(r\).
review_flags: ownership model and transfer operations require solver API documentation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits object ownership, but exclusive ownership, atomic transfer, release authority, and borrowing constraints are one possible resource model and require documentation for the intended solver API.

children.title: Aliasing Across Solver Objects
children.top_down_role: Shared references among variables, constraints, solutions, and relaxation artifacts.

assumptions_latex: Solver instances \(S\) and \(T\) expose handles to mutable plugin resources.
Each resource has an identity and a declared ownership and synchronization policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Alias}_{S,T}(h_S,h_T)\) is safe only under the stated shared-lifetime protocol.

notation.meaning: resource-resolution map for solver instance U

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines safe aliasing of mutable plugin resources across solver instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_S\) and \(h_T\) be handles exposed by solver instances \(S\) and \(T\), with resource-resolution maps \(\rho_S\) and \(\rho_T\). Define \(\operatorname{Alias}_{S,T}(h_S,h_T)\) by \(\rho_S(h_S)=\rho_T(h_T)\). Such aliasing is lifetime-safe only if the common resource is immutable, or if a shared-ownership protocol keeps it alive until both instances release it and every mutation is synchronized. Otherwise the handles must resolve to distinct resources, even when their initial states are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two solver handles alias when they resolve to one resource; mutable cross-instance aliasing is safe only with synchronized access and a lifetime spanning all users.
knowledge_statements.title: Aliasing Across Solver Objects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the aliasing leaf and is internally coherent, but its ownership, synchronization, and mandatory resource-distinction rules are architecture-specific and have no cited evidence.

children.title: Lifetime Safety Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Leaks, premature disposal, stale references, and conflicting ownership claims.

assumptions_latex: Every plugin resource has a set of authorized users and a destruction event.
Callbacks may access a resource only while their solver stage is active.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every authorized access time \(t\) satisfies \(t_c\le t<t_d\).

notation.meaning: number of outstanding owning references at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the temporal invariant preventing use-before-creation and use-after-destruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a resource created at \(t_c\) and destroyed at \(t_d\), lifetime safety requires every callback access at time \(t\) to satisfy \(t_c\le t<t_d\). If ownership is reference-counted, destruction is permitted only when \(n(t_d)=0\), and no new owning reference may be acquired at or after \(t_d\). Before copying, resetting, or freeing a solver, every borrowed handle whose validity depends on that solver must either be invalidated or rebound to an independently live resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource may be accessed only after creation and before destruction; solver teardown must invalidate or safely rebind every dependent borrowed handle.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifetime Safety Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifetime condition fits the leaf, but the callback-stage, reference-counting, invalidation, and rebinding requirements need an inspectable solver-architecture source.

children.title: Cross-Instance Solver Interface
children.top_down_role: Component behavior in auxiliary solvers and repeated solves.

children.title: Subsolver Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Component integration with auxiliary solver instances.

assumptions_latex: A parent instance has model \(M\), incumbent bound \(U\), and a finite resource budget.
A submodel transformation records maps between transferable parent and subsolver objects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only independently validated subsolver results may alter the parent solver's valid state.

notation.meaning: objective cutoff inherited from the parent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies a validity-preserving parent-to-subsolver call protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a parent model \(M\), construct a subsolver model \(M'\) by an explicit restriction, relaxation, or reformulation and record its object maps. Transfer the cutoff \(U\), relevant parameters, and a finite resource budget; solve \(M'\) until its stopping condition holds. Map a returned solution \(x'\) to \(x\) only when \(x\) is defined for all parent variables and is checked feasible for \(M\). Import a bound, cut, or conflict only after verifying that its validity assumptions hold for the parent state; otherwise discard it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subsolver receives a mapped model, cutoff, parameters, and budget; returned solutions, bounds, cuts, or conflicts enter the parent only after validity checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Subsolver Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate kind, but the proposed transfer and validation protocol combines several solver-specific interface guarantees without a source.

children.title: Solver-Copy Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Transfer of plugin configuration, state, and supported objects into solver copies.

assumptions_latex: A source solver \(S\) contains a model, plugins, parameters, and stage-dependent state.
The destination solver \(T\) is newly initialized and independent of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The copy is successful only if \(T\) is semantically equivalent on the declared copied state and owns its mutable resources safely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes construction of an independent, semantically mapped solver copy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an empty destination solver \(T\) from source solver \(S\). Copy supported plugins and parameters, then create destination variables and constraints while recording an object map \(\phi\). Transfer only stage-independent or explicitly copyable state, rewriting every transferred reference through \(\phi\). Mutable resources must be deep-copied or governed by a declared shared-ownership protocol. Return success only if every required object was copied and all mapped incidences, bounds, domains, and objective coefficients agree; otherwise report a partial or failed copy without treating \(T\) as equivalent to \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver copy recreates supported components, maps all references, and transfers only copyable state; success requires semantic agreement and safe ownership of mutable resources.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Copy Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the solver-copy leaf, but supported plugin copying, copyable stages, equivalence checks, and partial-copy semantics depend on a concrete solver API and require evidence.

children.title: Reoptimization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Component behavior across related solves with retained solver state.

assumptions_latex: A previously solved model \(M_0\) is changed to \(M_1\).
Retained artifacts carry enough provenance to test their validity for \(M_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reoptimization state contains exactly the retained artifacts valid for \(M_1\), together with newly initialized replacements.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives an invalidate-then-reuse protocol for repeated solves after model changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given previous state \(\Sigma_0\) for model \(M_0\) and an edit producing \(M_1\), classify each stored incumbent, bound, cut, basis, conflict, and search-tree record by its dependencies. Retain an artifact only if those dependencies are unchanged or its validity is re-established for \(M_1\); remap retained object references and invalidate all others. Initialize missing state, apply the new objective and domains, and resume optimization. The interface must report whether the resulting conclusion concerns \(M_1\), rather than silently reusing a certificate valid only for \(M_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reoptimization reuses prior artifacts only after dependency-based validation for the modified model; invalid state is discarded before solving resumes.
knowledge_statements.title: Reoptimization Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The invalidate-and-reuse algorithm is plausible, but validity rules differ among artifact types and solver implementations; no source supports the stated comprehensive protocol.

children.title: Cross-Instance Object Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence of plugin-owned and solver-owned objects across instances.

assumptions_latex: Solver instances \(S\) and \(T\) contain corresponding model objects.
Each transferable object has semantic data and incidence relations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid map \(\phi\) preserves object type, semantic data, and mapped incidences.

notation.meaning: transferable objects owned by solver U

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes semantic object correspondence between distinct solver instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cross-instance object mapping is a typed partial function \(\phi:\mathcal O_S\rightharpoonup\mathcal O_T\), never an identification by memory address. For each mapped object \(o\), the object \(\phi(o)\) has the same declared type and copied semantic data, subject to the stated transformation. For mapped incidences, \((o_1,o_2)\in I_S\) implies \((\phi(o_1),\phi(o_2))\in I_T\). Any transferred expression or state record must replace every source reference \(o\) by \(\phi(o)\); if a required image is undefined, that record is not transferable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cross-instance map is a typed semantic correspondence, not pointer equality; it must preserve relevant data and incidences and cover every transferred reference.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Instance Object Mapping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct role, but preservation of all declared semantic data and incidences is an architecture-dependent mapping contract without cited support.

children.title: State Transfer Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Missing, incompatible, or stale component state in copied or repeated solves.

knowledge_statements.title: State Transfer Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when source-local validity makes transferred solver state unsound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let artifact \(a\) be valid for every point in source context \(D\), but not globally valid. Transferring \(a\) as unrestricted state to target context \(D'\) is sound only if \(D'\subseteq D\), or if \(a\) is weakened or revalidated for \(D'\). Thus a node-local cut, conflict, propagation, basis status, or bound may not be imported after its defining fixings, rows, columns, objective, or tolerances have changed. Missing object images and incompatible numerical conventions are additional hard transfer boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State valid only in a source-local context cannot be transferred to a broader or incompatible target context without weakening or revalidation.
assumptions_latex: A state artifact \(a\) is valid only under source context \(D\).
The target instance uses context \(D'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(D'\not\subseteq D\), unrestricted transfer of \(a\) is invalid.

children.title: Branch-Cut-Price Solver Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Architectural integration of constraint enforcement, branching, separation, pricing, propagation, and primal search.

children.title: Enforcement-Search Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coordination between semantic feasibility and tree search.

children.title: Constraint Enforcement
children.top_down_role: Semantic feasibility processing at candidate and relaxation states.

assumptions_latex: A search node has relaxation candidate \(\bar x\) and active constraints \(\mathcal C\).
Each constraint handler can test feasibility and return only validity-preserving actions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node accepts \(\bar x\) only if \(c(\bar x)=\mathrm{true}\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\).

notation.meaning: feasibility predicate represented by constraint c

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the node-level enforcement loop for constraint-handler architectures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node, obtain a relaxation candidate \(\bar x\) and query every relevant constraint \(c\in\mathcal C\). If all predicates satisfy \(c(\bar x)=\mathrm{true}\), accept \(\bar x\) as constraint-feasible. Otherwise apply a handler action that is valid for the node: declare cutoff, add a valid separating row, tighten domains by valid inference, repair and recheck the candidate, or return a branching disjunction covering all feasible completions. Repeat after every state-changing action; never accept the candidate while an active constraint remains unenforced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint enforcement checks every active constraint and responds to violations by cutoff, separation, propagation, repair, or exhaustive branching before accepting a candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Enforcement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits constraint enforcement, but the exhaustive handler query and permitted response protocol are specific to constraint-handler solver architectures and lack cited support.

children.title: Enumerative Search
children.top_down_role: Tree-based partitioning and exploration of unresolved solution space.

knowledge_statements.title: Enumerative Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exhaustive-search formulation with valid pruning and covering branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal L\) with a root node whose domain is the original search domain. Repeatedly remove a node \(v\) from \(\mathcal L\). Prune it only by a valid infeasibility certificate or, when an incumbent exists, by a valid bound showing that \(v\) cannot improve that incumbent; record any feasible incumbent found. Otherwise generate finitely many children satisfying \(D_v\cap F\subseteq\bigcup_{w\in\operatorname{child}(v)}D_w\), where \(F\) is the feasible set, and add them to \(\mathcal L\). Stop when \(\mathcal L=\varnothing\); return the best incumbent, or report infeasibility if none exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerative search partitions unresolved domains and prunes only by valid infeasibility or bound certificates; exhausting all live nodes establishes optimality or infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The initial feasible search domain is finite or admits a finite exhaustive partition tree.
Every unresolved node is eventually selected unless it is validly pruned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When no live nodes remain, every feasible assignment has either been covered by the search or ruled out as infeasible or unable to improve the returned incumbent by a valid certificate.

children.title: Enforcement-to-Branching Escalation
children.top_down_role: Transition from detected semantic violations to additional search partitioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Enforcement-to-Branching Escalation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when failed enforcement may escalate to exhaustive branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\bar x\) violates an active constraint at node \(v\), and no valid cutoff, domain inference, separating row, or accepted repair resolves the violation. An enforcement handler may return branches \(D_1,\ldots,D_k\) only when they cover every feasible completion, \(F_v\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k D_i\), while excluding the unresolved candidate, \(\bar x\notin\bigcup_{i=1}^k D_i\). Each child inherits the parent restrictions and its branch restriction. Failure to provide either another valid enforcement action or such a covering disjunction leaves the node unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When other enforcement actions fail, branching must cover every feasible continuation while excluding the violating candidate; otherwise enforcement remains unresolved.
assumptions_latex: A candidate \(\bar x\) violates an active constraint.
Separation, propagation, cutoff, and valid repair do not resolve the violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching is admissible only if \(F_v\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k D_i\) and \(\bar x\notin\bigcup_{i=1}^k D_i\).

notation.meaning: feasible completions of the current node

children.title: Search Completeness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Risks when enforcement responses or branching coverage leave violations unresolved.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Completeness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite deterministic completeness conditions for enforcement-coupled branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization over \(F\), enforcement-coupled search is complete when every branch has finite arity and covers all feasible descendants, node selection is fair, pruning uses only valid infeasibility or lower-bound certificates, and every accepted incumbent belongs to \(F\). If the resulting tree is finite, exhaustion returns either no incumbent, certifying \(F=\varnothing\), or an incumbent \(x^*\) satisfying \(f(x^*)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in F\). These conditions do not provide a completeness guarantee when branches leave feasible descendants uncovered, constraints remain unenforced, pruning certificates are invalid, live nodes are permanently starved, or refinement produces a nonterminating tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under covering finite branching, fair node processing, valid pruning, full enforcement, and a finite search tree, exhaustion certifies global optimality or infeasibility; the stated guarantee does not apply when these safeguards fail.
assumptions_latex: Branching has finite arity and covers all feasible completions at each expanded node.
Node selection is fair, and every pruning decision has a valid certificate.
All required constraints are eventually enforced to the prescribed exact feasibility convention.
The resulting search tree is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustion certifies either a globally optimal incumbent or infeasibility under the stated conditions.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the original problem

children.title: Dynamic Relaxation Management System
children.top_down_role: Coordination of dynamically changing rows, columns, and relaxation state.

children.title: Separation Management
children.top_down_role: Coordination of candidate row generation, filtering, insertion, and removal.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-pool management for valid inequalities separating the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F\subseteq P\) and \(\bar x\in P\), invoke separation routines to produce inequalities \(a_j^\top x\le b_j\) satisfying \(a_j^\top x\le b_j\) for every \(x\in F\) and \(a_j^\top\bar x>b_j\). Reject invalid, numerically unacceptable, or redundant candidates; rank the remainder and select a finite set \(J\). If \(J\ne\varnothing\), add the selected rows to form \(P'=P\cap\bigcap_{j\in J}\{x:a_j^\top x\le b_j\}\), reoptimize, and repeat until no accepted separator is found or a prescribed round, time, or improvement limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation management validates, filters, ranks, and adds inequalities that preserve all feasible points while excluding the current relaxation candidate, then reoptimizes under explicit limits.
assumptions_latex: A relaxation polyhedron \(P\) contains the intended feasible set \(F\).
A candidate \(\bar x\in P\) is available to a separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(J\ne\varnothing\), every selected row is valid for \(F\) and excludes \(\bar x\), so \(F\subseteq P'\subsetneq P\), where \(P'=P\cap\bigcap_{j\in J}\{x:a_j^\top x\le b_j\}\).

notation.meaning: finite index set of selected separating inequalities

children.title: Pricing Management
children.top_down_role: Coordination of dynamic variable generation and restricted-master updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master pricing for a minimization formulation with dynamically generated columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a restricted column set \(J\), solve \(\min\{c_J^{\mathsf T}x_J:A_Jx_J=b,\ x_J\ge 0\}\) and obtain a dual solution \(\pi\). A pricing oracle computes \(j^*\in\arg\min_{j\in\mathcal J\setminus J}\{\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\}\), subject to all current branching restrictions. If \(\bar c_{j^*}<0\), add one or more negative-reduced-cost columns to \(J\), mark the restricted relaxation unsolved, and reoptimize. If every admissible omitted column satisfies \(\bar c_j\ge 0\), the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full current LP relaxation. Terminate pricing only after this certificate or an explicitly recorded nonexact stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the restricted master, add admissible negative-reduced-cost columns, and stop exactly only when no omitted column can improve the current LP relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The full column family \(\mathcal J\) is finite or admits an exact pricing oracle.
The restricted master is feasible and strong LP duality applies.
All current branching restrictions are enforced by the pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact termination certifies \(\bar c_j\ge 0\) for every admissible \(j\in\mathcal J\setminus J\), hence full-relaxation optimality.

notation.meaning: columns currently present in the restricted master

children.title: Relaxation-State Management
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of relaxation contents, basis state, solution status, and validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-State Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-validity protocol for a dynamically changing node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a relaxation state \(S=(R,C,\ell,u,B,z,v)\), containing active rows, active columns, variable bounds, an optional basis, a relaxation solution, and validity flags. After any mutation \(\Delta\), update \(R,C,\ell,u\); invalidate every cached object whose defining data changed; and classify the state as unsolved, primal-feasible, dual-feasible, or certified optimal. Before using \(z\) as a node bound, require a current dual-feasibility or optimality certificate for the same \((R,C,\ell,u)\). Before separation or primal heuristics use a relaxation point, require current primal feasibility. Reoptimize whenever the requested consumer's validity predicate is false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track the exact relaxation version behind every solution, basis, and bound, invalidating and recomputing objects whenever a relevant row, column, or bound changes.
assumptions_latex: Every relaxation mutation is recorded before a cached result is consumed.
The LP solver reports primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and optimality status separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cached relaxation result is consumed only when its validity flag matches the current state \((R,C,\ell,u)\).

notation.meaning: validity flags for cached relaxation objects

review_flags: No supplied locator directly documents solver-level relaxation-state validity and invalidation semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope fit, but no inspectable source supports the proposed state categories, cache invalidation predicates, or conditions for consuming node bounds and relaxation points.

children.title: Row-Column Interaction
children.top_down_role: Mutual effects of generated rows and columns on the active relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Column Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual invalidation effects between cutting-plane separation and column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the restricted relaxation \(P(R,C)=\{x_C:A_{R,C}x_C\ge b_R,\ x_C\ge0\}\), adding a valid row \(r\) replaces it by \(P(R\cup\{r\},C)\subseteq P(R,C)\) and may change the dual multipliers and every omitted column's reduced cost. Adding columns \(D\) replaces it by a relaxation represented over \(C\cup D\); its new optimum may differ, so separation conclusions based on the former primal optimum must be recomputed. Consequently, after a row addition, pricing must use updated dual multipliers, and after a column addition, separation must use an updated primal solution; neither previous oracle conclusion is automatically current.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: New rows can change pricing reduced costs, while new columns can change the point requiring separation; each operation may invalidate the other oracle's conclusion.
assumptions_latex: All added rows are valid for the intended full formulation.
All added columns satisfy the current branching restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Row insertion invalidates price conclusions tied to old dual multipliers, and column insertion invalidates separation conclusions tied to the old primal optimum.

children.title: Stale Relaxation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Invalid or inconsistent relaxation state after dynamic structural changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Relaxation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary beyond which cached LP certificates cannot justify pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization restricted master with dual certificate \(\pi\) and value \(z\). If a newly admissible column \(j\) has \(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j<0\), then \(\pi\) is not dual feasible for the enlarged master, so \(z\) cannot be retained as a certified lower bound for that enlarged relaxation. More generally, a cached solution or certificate becomes stale when rows, columns, bounds, objectives, or branching restrictions used in its defining feasibility conditions change. It may be reused for pruning only after direct validation against the new state or reoptimization; version equality alone is unnecessary only when a monotonicity argument explicitly preserves the required bound direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached bound crosses its validity boundary when model changes destroy its supporting certificate; negative reduced cost is a concrete invalidation witness after column addition.
assumptions_latex: The node problem is a minimization problem.
The cached value is justified by the displayed dual certificate rather than by an independent global argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j<0\), the old certificate cannot justify pruning in the enlarged relaxation.

children.title: Search Information Feedback System
children.top_down_role: Exchange of inference, learning, and incumbent information.

children.title: Propagation Coordination
children.top_down_role: Scheduling and exchange of domain inferences among solver components.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queue-based coordination of sound domain reductions at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize variable domains \(D=(D_i)_{i=1}^n\) from the node bounds and enqueue every constraint affected by their changes. Repeatedly select an enqueued propagator \(p\), compute a sound contraction \(D' = p(D)\subseteq D\), record an explanation for each removed value or tightened bound, and enqueue every propagator whose inputs changed. If some \(D_i'\) is empty, output infeasibility with the accumulated explanations. Stop when the queue is empty, returning the common fixed point reached under the chosen schedule. Any relaxation, branching, or conflict module receiving these domains must be notified of every committed contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run sound propagators to a queue-fixed point, retain explanations for all reductions, detect empty domains, and notify every module affected by tightened domains.
assumptions_latex: Each propagator is contracting and preserves every feasible assignment in its input domain.
Committed domain reductions are communicated to all dependent propagators and solver modules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output domains contain every node-feasible assignment, or an empty domain certifies node infeasibility relative to sound explanations.
review_flags: No supplied locator covers constraint-propagation scheduling and explanation management.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the queue and explanation protocol. Moreover, contraction and soundness alone do not guarantee finite termination or a schedule-independent common fixed point; suitable finite-domain, descending-chain, fairness, monotonicity, or termination hypotheses must be established by an authoritative reference.

children.title: Conflict Coordination
children.top_down_role: Collection, retention, and reuse of explanations or learned restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction, validation, and insertion of learned constraints after node infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When propagation or relaxation processing derives contradiction \(\bot\) under local decisions \(L=\{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\}\), traverse recorded explanations backward until obtaining a subset \(L'\subseteq L\) sufficient for the contradiction. Construct a nogood \(N(L')\) that excludes simultaneous satisfaction of all literals in \(L'\). Validate that every explanation used is globally valid or attach the strongest search context in which it is valid. Insert \(N(L')\) into the corresponding constraint store, compute a backjump level from its decision literals, invalidate affected relaxation state, and resume propagation at that level. Discard or localize any learned object whose validity context cannot be established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace an infeasibility through recorded reasons, learn a context-valid nogood, backjump, update the relaxation, and propagate the learned information.
assumptions_latex: Every inference contributing to \(\bot\) has a checkable explanation.
The learned nogood is stored only in a context where all explanations remain valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned constraint \(N(L')\) excludes the conflicting assignment while preserving every feasible solution in its declared validity context.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports conflict analysis, contextual validity, and backjump coordination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Conflict Coordination, but no citation supports explanation traversal, contextual validity, nogood construction, backjump-level selection, and relaxation invalidation as one coordinated protocol.

children.title: Primal-Search Coordination
children.top_down_role: Sharing of candidate solutions, incumbents, and feasibility information.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Search Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinated invocation and acceptance of MIP primal heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with relaxation point \(x^{LP}\), domains \(D\), incumbent value \(U\), and resource budget \(B\), select eligible primal heuristics according to their preconditions and deterministic priorities. Give each selected heuristic the current state and an allocated subbudget. For every returned vector \(\hat x\), independently verify variable domains, integrality, and all original constraints. If \(\hat x\) is feasible and \(c^{\mathsf T}\hat x<U\), set \(U\leftarrow c^{\mathsf T}\hat x\), store \(\hat x\), broadcast the new cutoff, and invalidate consumers depending on the former incumbent. Stop when eligibility, budget, or improvement criteria terminate the schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schedule eligible primal heuristics within a budget, independently verify candidates, and broadcast every improving incumbent and its tighter cutoff.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization MIP with objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).
Candidate acceptance checks the original model, not merely a presolved or relaxed representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted \(\hat x\) is MIP-feasible and updates the valid primal bound to \(U=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x\).

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

review_flags: The source supports primal-bound search but may not document solver scheduling mechanics.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited primal-bounds section is relevant to heuristic solution search, but it does not adequately support the detailed eligibility scheduling, deterministic priorities, subbudget allocation, independent original-model validation, broadcast, and cache-invalidation protocol stated here.

children.title: Inference-to-Conflict Flow
children.top_down_role: Transfer of propagation reasons into conflict analysis and learned information.

knowledge_statements.title: Inference-to-Conflict Flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explanation chain converting propagated inferences into a verifiable conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let decisions \(L_0\) imply successive bound literals \(L_1,\ldots,L_m\), where each inference has a recorded valid implication \(R_t\land L_{i_1}\land\cdots\land L_{i_q}\Rightarrow L_t\). If the accumulated literals imply both \(x_i\le a\) and \(x_i\ge b\) with \(a<b\), composing the recorded implications yields \(L'\Rightarrow\bot\) for some subset \(L'\subseteq L_0\). The nogood \(\neg\bigwedge_{ell\in L'}\ell\) is then a certificate excluding the conflicting decisions. Verification consists of checking each local implication, the terminal bound contradiction, and the validity context of every reason \(R_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compose recorded inference reasons until contradictory bounds arise; the responsible decisions yield a verifiable nogood when every reason is valid in context.
assumptions_latex: Every propagated literal has an explicit, checkable reason.
All reasons are valid in the context where the nogood is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The composed explanation certifies \(L'\Rightarrow\bot\), hence validates the learned nogood \(\neg\bigwedge_{ell\in L'}\ell\).

notation.meaning: decisions retained in the conflict explanation

review_flags: No supplied locator covers explanation-based conflict certificates in constraint integer programming.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed explanation certificate. In addition, both displayed nogood formulas use the undefined token sequence `ell` rather than the introduced literal symbol `\ell`, so the mathematical notation is not internally consistent.

children.title: Incumbent Feedback Flow
children.top_down_role: Effects of primal discoveries on propagation, learning, pruning, and search priorities.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feedback Flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of an improved primal bound through a minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization MIP, a newly verified feasible solution \(\hat x\) establishes the global primal bound \(U=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x\). Every open node with a certified lower bound \(L_v\ge U\) may be pruned. At remaining nodes, the cutoff inequality \(c^{\mathsf T}x<U\), or \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le U-1\) when the objective is integral, may be supplied to propagation, relaxation, and primal-search modules. Any priority, gap, or stopping quantity depending on the former incumbent must be recomputed. Feasibility of \(\hat x\) must be checked before any such global feedback is committed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified improving incumbent tightens the global cutoff, prunes nodes whose lower bounds cannot beat it, and updates all incumbent-dependent solver state.
assumptions_latex: The MIP is a minimization problem.
The incumbent candidate \(\hat x\) is feasible for the original model.
Each node bound \(L_v\) used for pruning is currently certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nodes satisfying \(L_v\ge U\) cannot contain a solution improving upon \(\hat x\) and may be pruned.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound at node v

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

review_flags: The locator supports primal bounds; explicit solver-feedback semantics remain to be checked.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pruning implication from a verified incumbent and certified node lower bound is correct, but the cited primal-bounds section does not establish the full solver-feedback protocol. The use of the strict cutoff inequality in relaxation and propagation modules also needs a precise representability or tolerance convention; the integral-objective alternative requires an explicitly integer-valued objective scale.

children.title: Solver Context Coordination Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Architectural coordination across primary solver execution contexts.

children.title: Root-Node Coordination
children.top_down_role: Component scheduling and information exchange during root processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Node Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root processing to a coordinated relaxation and inference fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the root domains, active formulation, incumbent \(U\), and relaxation state. Repeat: propagate domains; solve the current relaxation; separate violated globally valid inequalities; price admissible negative-reduced-cost columns; and run eligible primal heuristics. After each modification, invalidate affected primal, dual, pricing, and separation certificates before their reuse. Continue until propagation is at a fixed point, no selected separator adds a row, exact pricing finds no improving column, and the relaxation is certified optimal, or until an explicit resource limit is recorded. Output the root bound, incumbent, globally valid learned objects, and a versioned state from which branching may safely begin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the root, coordinate propagation, relaxation, separation, pricing, and primal search until certified stability or a recorded limit, then initialize branching state.
assumptions_latex: All imported cuts and columns are valid for the root context.
Every relaxation mutation triggers the required certificate invalidations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact termination yields a root state with fixed-point propagation, certified relaxation optimality, and no improving admissible priced column.
review_flags: Supplied locators cover individual relaxation mechanisms but not the complete root-node coordination protocol.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Root-Node Coordination, but no cited source supports the complete interleaving, invalidation rules, exact stopping conditions, and versioned handoff to branching.

children.title: Search-Tree Coordination
children.top_down_role: Component scheduling and state management across non-root nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global coordination of node selection, processing, branching, and pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an open-node set \(Q\), incumbent value \(U\), and for each node \(v\) a local context and certified lower bound \(L_v\). Select \(v\in Q\), restore its context, coordinate propagation and relaxation processing, and then: prune it if infeasible or if \(L_v\ge U\); accept and verify an integral feasible relaxation solution; or create children whose branching disjunction covers every feasible solution remaining at \(v\). Insert surviving children into \(Q\), broadcast globally valid incumbents and learned objects, and keep local objects confined to their validity subtrees. Terminate when \(Q=\varnothing\) or a declared stopping limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select and process versioned nodes, prune by valid bounds or infeasibility, branch exhaustively, and share only information valid in each receiving context.
assumptions_latex: Every branching disjunction covers the feasible set remaining at its parent.
Only certified node bounds are used for pruning.
Shared learned objects preserve validity in every receiving context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Q=\varnothing\) without a resource-limit termination, the incumbent is globally optimal or infeasibility has been certified.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound at node v

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the complete search-tree coordination and context-valid sharing protocol.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and leaf placement are appropriate, but the global-optimality conclusion depends on a complete exact branch-and-bound coordination invariant, including exhaustive node processing and context-valid sharing. No inspectable source is supplied for those claims.

children.title: Subsolver Coordination
children.top_down_role: Information transfer between the primary solver and auxiliary solver instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsolver Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe exchange between a parent MIP search and auxiliary solver instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From a parent context \(K\), construct a subproblem \(P_K\) together with an explicit mapping \(\phi\) between parent and subsolver variables, constraints, and objective values. Run the subsolver under a declared resource budget. For every returned solution, bound, cut, conflict, or domain reduction, map it through \(\phi\) and independently verify both its mathematical validity and its scope. Import feasible solutions after checking the parent model; import bounds or learned constraints only when their assumptions hold in the receiving context. Keep subsolver-local state isolated, record provenance, and invalidate affected parent caches after each accepted import.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map parent data into a budgeted subsolver, validate and scope every returned object, import only sound information, and isolate all remaining local state.
assumptions_latex: The mapping \(\phi\) preserves the declared correspondence between parent and subproblem objects.
Every imported object has a checkable validity scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted imports preserve correctness of the parent search; objects lacking a verified parent-valid interpretation remain isolated.

notation.meaning: mapping between parent and subsolver representations

review_flags: No supplied locator documents subsolver mapping, isolation, provenance, and safe import requirements.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches Subsolver Coordination, but no source supports the representation mapping, validation obligations for each returned object type, scope checks, provenance requirements, isolation rules, and parent-cache invalidation protocol.

children.title: Cross-Context State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Movement of bounds, solutions, cuts, conflicts, and configuration across execution contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Context State Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for transferring solver state between root, tree, and subsolver contexts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let contexts \(C_s\) and \(C_t\) represent formulations with feasible sets \(F_s\) and \(F_t\), and let \(T\) translate source objects into the target variable space. A source bound \(L_s\), incumbent \(x_s\), or inequality \(a_s^\top x\le b_s\) is transferable only when its translated counterpart is valid for \(F_t\): respectively \(L_s\le \inf_{x\in F_t}c^\top x\), \(T(x_s)\in F_t\), or \(T(a_s)^\top x\le b_s\) for every \(x\in F_t\). Transferred state must be rejected or revalidated whenever variable mappings, local assumptions, or objective conventions differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds, incumbents, and cuts may cross solver contexts only after translation and validation against the target formulation and its local assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(C_s\) and \(C_t\) have an explicit variable and objective mapping \(T\).
The target feasible set \(F_t\) incorporates all assumptions active in the target context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every imported object is valid for \(F_t\) under the target context's conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence supports the proposed cross-context protocol. The target objective vector and its relation to the source objective are not defined, so the bound-transfer condition is not reliable across differing objective conventions.

children.title: Context Isolation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Risks from leaking local or instance-specific state into incompatible contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Context Isolation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic boundary separating globally valid solver information from context-local state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a solver context \(C\), partition maintained state as \(S(C)=G(C)\mathbin{\dot\cup}L(C)\), where objects in \(G(C)\) are valid for the context's global formulation and objects in \(L(C)\) depend on local branching decisions, temporary constraints, transformed variables, or context-specific parameters. An object \(q\in L(C)\) may affect another context \(C'\) only if a validation predicate \(V(q,C')=1\) establishes its validity for the formulation represented by \(C'\). Destruction or rollback of \(C\) must not alter state owned by \(C'\) except through an explicitly validated transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local branching, temporary constraints, transformed data, and parameters remain isolated; another context may use them only after explicit validity checking.
assumptions_latex: Each maintained object has identifiable ownership and validity scope.
\(V\) tests validity relative to the receiving formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unvalidated context-local state cannot modify or certify another solver context.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The state partition, ownership semantics, rollback behavior, and validation predicate are architecture-specific claims without cited evidence.

children.title: CIP Extension Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem classes and solver roles enabled by constraint handlers and plugin composition.

children.title: MILP as a CIP Regime
children.top_down_role: Constraint-oriented realization of mixed-integer linear optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: MILP as a CIP Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MILP represented by linear constraint handlers within a constraint-integer-programming architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-integer linear program is represented as \[\min\{c^\top x: Ax\le b,\; \ell\le x\le u,\; x_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }i\in I\}.\] In a constraint-integer-programming regime, each row \(a_j^\top x\le b_j\), each bound, and each integrality restriction is a constraint object whose enforcement may include feasibility checking, propagation, relaxation-row generation, separation, and branching support. The represented feasible set remains exactly \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ell\le x\le u,x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\}\), irrespective of which valid enforcement operations are activated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MILP is a CIP instance whose linear, bound, and integrality constraints are handled as structured constraint objects without changing its feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c,\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The CIP representation has the same feasible set and objective as the stated MILP.

notation.meaning: linear constraint matrix and right-hand side

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited branch-and-bound/cut section can support the MILP formulation but does not establish that rows, bounds, and integrality restrictions are all CIP constraint objects with the listed handler operations. In particular, integrality may be represented as a variable property rather than a constraint object.

children.title: Nonlinear Quadratic CIP Regime Family
children.top_down_role: CIP extensions incorporating nonlinear and quadratic constraint semantics.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Extending a CIP framework to solve MIQCPs

children.title: MINLP CIP Regimes
children.top_down_role: Constraint-oriented processing for mixed-integer models with general nonlinear structure.

knowledge_statements.title: MINLP CIP Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General finite-dimensional mixed-integer nonlinear regime with explicit constraint semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-integer nonlinear programming CIP regime represents problems of the form \[\min\{f(x): g_j(x)\le 0\ (j=1,\ldots,m),\; \ell\le x\le u,\; x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i\in I)\},\] where \(f,g_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) may be nonlinear. Each nonlinear relation is retained as a constraint object capable of checking candidate solutions and supplying sound domain propagation, relaxations, or branching information. Every generated relaxation must contain the feasible points of the represented problem on the current node domain; convexity is not required unless invoked by a particular relaxation procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MINLP CIP regime retains nonlinear constraints as enforceable objects and requires every node relaxation to contain all locally feasible mixed-integer points.
assumptions_latex: All functions are defined on the variable box \([\ell,u]\).
\(I\subseteq\{1,…,n\}\) identifies integer variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime represents the stated MINLP while permitting only sound relaxations and domain reductions.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_refs.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The textbooks support the MINLP formulation and relaxation concepts, but the assertion that every nonlinear relation is retained as a CIP constraint object with the stated capabilities requires an architecture-specific source. The assumption also uses a Unicode ellipsis rather than standard TeX notation.

children.title: MIQCP CIP Regimes
children.top_down_role: Constraint-oriented processing for mixed-integer quadratically constrained models.

knowledge_statements.title: MIQCP CIP Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer quadratically constrained regime, including convex and nonconvex quadratic objectives and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-integer quadratically constrained programming CIP regime represents \[\min\{x^\top Q_0x+c^\top x: x^\top Q_jx+a_j^\top x\le b_j\ (j=1,\ldots,m),\;\ell\le x\le u,\;x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\}.\] Each matrix may be replaced by its symmetric part without changing the corresponding quadratic form. A constraint function \(x\mapsto x^\top Q_jx+a_j^\top x-b_j\) is convex when the symmetric part of \(Q_j\) is positive semidefinite, and the objective is convex when the symmetric part of \(Q_0\) is positive semidefinite. If these curvature conditions fail, global certification requires globally valid relaxation bounds; such bounds may be constructed using valid underestimators, spatial branching, or other globally valid mechanisms. Quadratic constraint objects may retain their algebraic structure while contributing valid relaxation constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An MIQCP has quadratic objective and constraint functions together with integer variables. Positive-semidefinite symmetric parts give the corresponding convex functions; nonconvex cases require globally valid bounds, without prescribing one exclusive bounding method.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_j\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) for \(j=0,\ldots,m\), \(a_j,c,\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b_j\in\mathbb R\).
\(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime represents the stated MIQCP and distinguishes convex quadratic functions from quadratic functions requiring nonconvex global bounding mechanisms.

source_refs.locator: The MILP road to MIQCP p. 373

source_witnesses.locator: The MILP road to MIQCP p. 373

children.title: Quadratic-to-General Nonlinear Transition
children.top_down_role: Changes in representation and handler coverage when quadratic structure becomes general nonlinear structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-to-General Nonlinear Transition
