knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding quadratic constraints into the general nonlinear CIP interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every quadratic expression \(q(x)=x^\top Qx+a^\top x-b\) is a differentiable nonlinear expression with \(\nabla q(x)=(Q+Q^\top)x+a\) and \(\nabla^2q(x)=Q+Q^\top\). Hence an MIQCP instance embeds into the MINLP regime by replacing each quadratic constraint with \(g_j(x)=x^\top Q_jx+a_j^\top x-b_j\le0\). The transition preserves feasible points and objective values. Specialized quadratic recognition may nevertheless be retained because it permits direct curvature tests, quadratic propagation, and structure-specific relaxations unavailable to an opaque general expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic models embed exactly into general nonlinear models, while retaining recognized quadratic structure enables stronger specialized analysis and relaxations.
assumptions_latex: All quadratic expressions are defined on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The same variable bounds and integrality restrictions are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic and nonlinear representations define identical feasible sets and objective values.

source_refs.locator: The MILP road to MIQCP p. 373

source_witnesses.locator: The MILP road to MIQCP p. 373

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact quadratic-to-nonlinear embedding and derivative formulas are correct, but the cited MIQCP section does not establish the architecture-specific claims about quadratic recognition, propagation, and unavailable opaque-expression relaxations.

children.title: Nonlinear Relaxation Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Availability and interoperability of nonlinear relaxations across the two regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Relaxation Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness condition for nonlinear relaxations used within node-based CIP search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node with domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(F_D=\{x\in D:g_j(x)\le0\text{ for all }j\}\). A relaxation \(R_D\) is compatible with the nonlinear constraint system exactly when \(F_D\subseteq R_D\). If the solver minimizes \(f\), a relaxation objective \(\underline f_D\) must satisfy \(\underline f_D(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_D\). Consequently, \(\inf_{x\in R_D}\underline f_D(x)\) is a valid node lower bound; infeasibility of \(R_D\) certifies infeasibility of \(F_D\). Numerical or local approximations lacking these containment inequalities cannot support global pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear node relaxation is compatible only if it contains every locally feasible point and underestimates the objective wherever feasibility holds.
assumptions_latex: The optimization problem is a minimization problem.
The relaxation is interpreted over the current node domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in R_D}\underline f_D(x)\le\inf_{x\in F_D}f(x)\), and \(R_D=\varnothing\) implies \(F_D=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: nonlinear feasible set on the node domain

children.title: Custom Combinatorial Constraint Regimes
children.top_down_role: Application-specific constraint semantics integrated without flattening all structure into generic rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Custom Combinatorial Constraint Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CIP regime retaining application-specific combinatorial constraint semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the variable domain and let a custom combinatorial constraint be specified by a predicate \(P:X\to\{0,1\}\). Its feasible set is \(F_P=\{x\in X:P(x)=1\}\). A sound constraint handler may implement feasibility checking, propagation, separation, or branching directly from \(P\), without first replacing \(F_P\) by generic linear rows. Every inferred domain reduction must preserve \(F_P\), every generated relaxation inequality must hold for all \(x\in F_P\), and acceptance of a complete candidate requires \(P(x)=1\). Multiple custom constraints define feasibility by intersection of their predicate sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A custom combinatorial constraint keeps its predicate semantics and may propagate, separate, or branch directly, provided every inference preserves its feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is decidable on complete candidate assignments.
Handler operations are interpreted relative to the current variable domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All handler inferences are valid for \(F_P\), and complete candidates are accepted exactly when \(P(x)=1\).

notation.meaning: feasible set defined by the predicate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicate model is coherent, but the claims about direct CIP feasibility checking, propagation, separation, and branching are architecture-specific and have no cited source.

children.title: Dynamic Generation Decomposition Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Extensible integration of dynamic rows, columns, and subproblems within search.

children.title: Branch-Cut-Price Regimes
children.top_down_role: Integrated dynamic-row and dynamic-column generation within tree search.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Cut-Price Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact node search combining branching, row separation, and dynamic column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a mixed-integer master formulation whose valid rows and variables may be generated dynamically. Initialize a restricted master at the root. At each active node, repeatedly solve its relaxation, add violated valid cuts, and add columns having negative reduced cost for minimization until neither oracle finds an improving object. If the relaxation is infeasible, prune; if its bound is dominated by an incumbent, prune; if its solution is feasible and integral, update the incumbent; otherwise branch using disjunctions that preserve exhaustive coverage. Output the best incumbent when no active nodes remain, provided separation and pricing termination certify the full node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-cut-price alternates relaxation solves, valid-cut separation, and reduced-cost pricing at each node, then prunes, accepts, or branches using certified bounds.
assumptions_latex: Cut and pricing oracles are valid for every node where invoked.
Branching decisions preserve exhaustive coverage and remain compatible with pricing.
Oracle termination certifies the full node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon exhaustion of the active-node set, the returned incumbent is globally optimal, or infeasibility is certified.

notation.meaning: reduced cost of a candidate master column

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited source covers branch-and-cut rather than branch-cut-price. It does not support exact pricing, pricing-compatible branching, full node-relaxation certification, or the combined algorithm's global termination claim.

children.title: Decomposition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Master-subproblem architectures with externally coordinated subproblem information.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination of linking decisions and structured subordinate problems, with formulation-dependent cut and column validity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\left\{d(y)+\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x_k,y): y\in Y,\;x_k\in X_k(y)\ \text{for }k=1,\ldots,K\right\},\] where all cross-component coupling is represented by \(y\) and the master constraints defining \(Y\). A decomposition regime coordinates decisions in \(y\) with subordinate problems over the sets \(X_k(y)\). A cut-based master relaxation yields a valid lower bound for this minimization problem only when its cuts remove no projection of a globally feasible solution and its value approximations are global underestimators. A restricted-column master generally represents a subset of a full master formulation; a feasible restricted-master solution that lifts to feasible subordinate solutions gives an upper bound, while a valid pricing certificate is needed to establish optimality or a bound for the full master relaxation. Thus cut and column information must be interpreted according to its respective containment direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposition coordinates linking variables with subordinate problems. Outer-approximation cuts must preserve every feasible projection to give lower bounds, whereas restricted columns describe only part of a full master and require pricing certification for full-master optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(Y\) is the master domain, and \(X_k(y)\) is the feasible set of component \(k\) at \(y\).
All cross-component coupling is represented by \(y\) and constraints in the master formulation.
Any reported feasible master solution can be lifted to compatible points \(x_k\in X_k(y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid decomposition bounds follow from the containment direction of the chosen master representation; cut relaxations and restricted-column formulations cannot be assigned the same generic bound interpretation.

notation.meaning: feasible set of component k at linking decision y

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Pricing-Based Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition variants centered on dynamically generated variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master column generation using a reduced-cost pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the linear master \(\min\{\sum_{p\in P}c_p\lambda_p:A\lambda=b,\lambda\ge0\}\) with a potentially large column set \(P\). Initialize \(P'\subseteq P\) so the restricted master is feasible. Solve it to obtain a dual vector \(\pi\), then call a pricing oracle minimizing \(c_p-\pi^\top a_p\) over \(p\in P\). If the minimum reduced cost is negative, add one or more such columns to \(P'\) and repeat. Otherwise stop and return the restricted-master solution, which is optimal for the full linear master under exact pricing and strong linear-programming duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column generation repeatedly solves a restricted master and adds negative-reduced-cost columns; exact absence of such columns certifies full-master LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The initial restricted master is feasible.
The pricing oracle globally minimizes reduced cost over \(P\).
The primal and dual linear programs attain equal finite optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(c_p-\pi^\top a_p\ge0\) for every \(p\in P\), the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master.

notation.meaning: dual multiplier for the master equality

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and reduced-cost certificate are standard and internally consistent, but the broad decomposition-chapter locator does not specifically support the stated restricted-master column-generation algorithm and its exact pricing certificate.

children.title: Cut-Based Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition variants centered on dynamically generated master restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master refinement by globally valid feasibility and subordinate-value cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{d(y)+\phi(y):y\in Y\},\qquad \phi(y)=\inf\{f(x,y):x\in X(y)\},\] with \(\phi(y)=+\infty\) when \(X(y)=\varnothing\). Initialize a master problem with \(y\in Y\), a variable \(\theta\), and a valid global lower-bounding model for \(\phi\). At iteration \(t\), solve the master to obtain a lower bound \(L_t\) and a point \((y^t,\theta^t)\). Solve the subordinate problem at \(y^t\). If \(X(y^t)=\varnothing\), add a feasibility cut that excludes \(y^t\) but no \(y\) with \(X(y)\ne\varnothing\). Otherwise compute \(U_t=d(y^t)+\phi(y^t)\), update the incumbent upper bound, and add a valid cut \(\theta\ge h_t(y)\) satisfying \(h_t(y)\le\phi(y)\) for every \(y\in Y\). Repeat until the incumbent upper bound \(U\) and master lower bound \(L\) satisfy \(U-L\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut-based decomposition solves a lower-bounding master, queries the subordinate problem, and adds globally valid feasibility or value-function cuts until the feasible incumbent and master bounds differ by at most the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
Every feasibility cut preserves all \(y\in Y\) for which \(X(y)\ne\varnothing\).
Every optimality cut satisfies \(h_t(y)\le\phi(y)\) for all \(y\in Y\).
The master and subordinate problems are solved accurately enough to validate the reported bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), the incumbent is feasible and has objective value at most \(\varepsilon\) above the global optimum; before termination, \(L\) is a valid lower bound.

notation.meaning: subordinate feasible set at the master decision
master lower estimate of the subordinate value
current global lower and incumbent upper bounds

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Nested Search Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of primary search with pricing, separation, or auxiliary subproblem solves.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a mixed-integer optimization problem.
Each search instance \(S_k\) has a valid local domain \(D_k\), incumbent bound \(U_k\), and dual bound \(L_k\).
Information transferred between instances is globally valid or explicitly tagged with its validity domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U:=\min_k U_k\) is a valid global primal bound, while a child result may update a parent dual bound only when it certifies the parent's entire unresolved domain.

notation.meaning: search instance at nesting level k
domain assigned to search instance k
primal and dual bounds of search instance k

review_flags: CIP-specific authoritative source and exact coordination contract are needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic coordination of recursively invoked MIP searches with validity-aware information exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a parent search \(S_0\), select an unresolved subdomain \(D_1\subseteq D_0\) and initialize a child search \(S_1\) with inherited globally valid constraints and incumbent \(U_0\). Run \(S_1\) until it proves \(D_1\) infeasible, finds an incumbent, reaches a prescribed resource limit, or completely solves \(D_1\). Transfer any feasible solution to every ancestor by setting \(U_j\leftarrow\min\{U_j,f(x)\}\). Transfer cuts, deductions, or bounds only to ancestors whose domains are contained in their validity domains. Mark \(D_1\) resolved only after a complete certificate for that subdomain; otherwise return it to the parent's unresolved set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested search may share incumbents broadly, but it may prune or strengthen an ancestor only with information valid on the ancestor's relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Search Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the nested-search leaf, but its bound-sharing, ancestor-transfer, and subdomain-resolution rules require an authoritative CIP source. The minimization convention and objective function used by the incumbent updates are also not introduced explicitly.

children.title: Plugin Assurance Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Correctness, performance, numerical, and maintainability risks introduced by extensible solver components.

children.title: Feasibility Coverage Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Semantic constraints whose checking or enforcement coverage is incomplete.

children.title: Incomplete Feasibility Checking
children.top_down_role: Cases where plugin checks omit relevant candidate solutions, search states, or constraint violations.

assumptions_latex: The solver declares a candidate \(x\) feasible exactly when every invoked checking routine accepts it.
The intended feasible set is \(F=\bigcap_{i\in I}F_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There can exist \(x\notin F\) that the solver accepts as feasible, so incumbent validity and any primal bound derived from that incumbent are unsound.

notation.meaning: feasible set of constraint family i
indices of all required constraint families

review_flags: A source specifying completeness requirements for CIP feasibility callbacks is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by omitting or weakening a required constraint-family feasibility check.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\subsetneq I\) be the constraint families actually checked, so the implemented acceptance set is \(\widehat F=\bigcap_{j\in J}F_j\). Incomplete feasibility checking occurs when \(\widehat F\nsubseteq F\); equivalently, there exists \(x\in\widehat F\setminus F\). Such an \(x\) passes every invoked check while violating at least one omitted family \(F_i\), with \(i\in I\setminus J\). If the solver installs \(x\) as an incumbent, the reported solution is infeasible for the intended model and its objective value is not a valid primal bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If checking omits a required constraint family, an infeasible point can be accepted as an incumbent, invalidating the reported solution and primal bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Feasibility Checking

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and set-theoretic characterization fit the leaf, but the required completeness contract for CIP feasibility checking is uncited. The assertion about an invalid primal bound also requires an explicit optimization sense.

children.title: Incomplete Constraint Enforcement
children.top_down_role: Cases where detected violations do not trigger sufficient rejection, propagation, separation, or repair.

assumptions_latex: At a search node with domain \(D\), valid solutions must lie in \(F\cap D\).
The solver relies on plugins to separate, propagate, branch on, or otherwise enforce violated constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solver may retain an invalid relaxation point or terminate without establishing feasibility, and pruning based on the resulting state need not be sound.
review_flags: A source specifying enforcement obligations of CIP constraint handlers is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a constraint plugin to eliminate or resolve detected violations during search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(D)\subseteq D\) denote the points that remain admissible after all implemented enforcement actions at node domain \(D\). Constraint enforcement is incomplete if there exists \(x\in E(D)\setminus F\) for which no valid cut removes \(x\), no propagation proves its exclusion, no branching separates it into exhaustive subdomains, and no terminal infeasibility or rejection result is produced. Consequently, the search can treat a node containing a known constraint violation as resolved or can use an invalid point in subsequent bounding and pruning decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A detected violation must trigger a valid eliminating or resolving action; otherwise the search can retain invalid points and make unsound decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Constraint Enforcement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record appropriately describes an enforcement failure rather than a definition, but the claimed obligations and consequences for CIP constraint handlers need authoritative support.

children.title: Checking-Enforcement Coverage Gaps
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between the states examined by a plugin and the states where corrective intervention is available.

assumptions_latex: Checking accepts precisely the set \(C\subseteq X\).
Enforcement guarantees eventual resolution only for points in \(E\subseteq X\).
The intended feasible set is \(F\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sound coverage requires \(C=F\) and \(X\setminus F\subseteq E\); failure of either inclusion creates an acceptance or unresolved-violation gap.

notation.meaning: intended feasible set in ambient candidate space X

review_flags: A source formalizing checking-enforcement coverage in CIP architectures is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic boundary separating complete feasibility recognition from complete violation resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A checking-enforcement coverage gap exists if either \(C\nsubseteq F\) or \(X\setminus F\nsubseteq E\). In the first case, some \(x\in C\setminus F\) is falsely accepted as feasible. In the second, some \(x\in(X\setminus F)\setminus E\) is infeasible but has no guaranteed enforcing response. Even when every enforced point is correctly rejected, the second gap permits an unresolved violation; even when enforcement covers every violation, the first gap permits an invalid incumbent if the terminal checker is weaker than the intended model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checking must reject every infeasible candidate, and enforcement must resolve every possible violation; a gap in either coverage condition breaks solver assurance.
knowledge_statements.title: Checking-Enforcement Coverage Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, and the two coverage gaps are internally coherent, but the abstract sets C and E and their asserted correspondence to CIP checking and enforcement require a supporting architectural source.

children.title: Plugin Scope Integrity Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Plugin artifacts persisting beyond their valid search scope.

children.title: Invalid Plugin Locality
children.top_down_role: Plugin artifacts applied outside the node, subtree, probing context, or solver stage where they remain valid.

assumptions_latex: A plugin artifact \(a\) is derived under a local search domain \(D_v\).
The artifact is valid exactly on a stated validity domain \(V(a)\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Using \(a\) at \(w\) is sound only if \(D_w\subseteq V(a)\); otherwise it may exclude a feasible point or justify an invalid deduction.

notation.meaning: search domains at nodes v and w

review_flags: A source for CIP plugin locality and artifact-validity rules is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Misuse of node-local plugin artifacts outside the domains in which they are valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Invalid plugin locality occurs when an artifact \(a\), such as a cut, bound change, inference, or conflict explanation, is installed at a search node \(w\) although \(D_w\nsubseteq V(a)\). Concretely, if there exists \(x\in D_w\setminus V(a)\) that satisfies the original model but violates the restriction imposed by \(a\), then applying \(a\) at \(w\) can remove a feasible solution. An artifact proved only under \(D_v\) is therefore not automatically valid at an ancestor, sibling, restarted search, or independent nested search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local cut, bound, or inference becomes unsafe when applied at a node whose domain is not contained in the artifact's validity domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Plugin Locality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The domain-containment criterion is plausible and fits the locality failure leaf, but the treatment of cuts, bound changes, inferences, and conflicts under one validity-domain rule needs a CIP-specific source.

children.title: Plugin State Leakage
children.top_down_role: Transient plugin data or effects that persist into unrelated search contexts.

assumptions_latex: A plugin maintains mutable state \(s_v\) associated with scope \(v\).
Distinct scopes may require different correct states \(s_v^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If leaked state changes a solver decision, the resulting cut, inference, feasibility verdict, or bound can be invalid in the receiving scope.

notation.meaning: plugin state stored for scope v
state required for correctness in scope v
plugin decision computed from state and scope

review_flags: A source describing plugin state ownership and reset obligations is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-scope contamination by mutable plugin data that should have been isolated, copied, restored, or reset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Plugin state leakage occurs when execution in scope \(u\) mutates state later read in a distinct scope \(v\), producing \(A(s_u,v)\neq A(s_v^*,v)\), although no valid state-transfer rule identifies the two states. Typical leaked data include cached local bounds, flags, temporary constraints, reference counts, and incumbent-dependent conclusions. If the differing decision affects mathematical search state, then the receiving scope can inherit an artifact whose derivation assumptions do not hold there, even when the underlying plugin routines are individually correct for properly initialized state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mutable data from one search scope must not influence another unless an explicit valid transfer rule applies; otherwise mathematical solver decisions can be corrupted.
knowledge_statements.title: Plugin State Leakage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the state-isolation, reset, and transfer obligations are implementation-contract claims without cited support.

children.title: Scope-Transition Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures arising when plugin artifacts cross node, restart, probing, transformation, or subsolver boundaries.

assumptions_latex: Each scope \(v\) has a required invariant \(I_v(s)\) for plugin state \(s\).
A transition \(T_{u\to v}\) moves or transforms state from scope \(u\) to scope \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transition failure occurs when \(I_u(s)\) holds but \(I_v(T_{u\to v}(s))\) does not, making subsequent plugin conclusions uncertified.
review_flags: A source specifying scope-transition invariants for CIP plugins is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to preserve plugin invariants when entering, leaving, copying, restoring, or restarting a search scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every permitted scope transition \(u\to v\), correctness requires \(I_u(s)\Rightarrow I_v(T_{u\to v}(s))\). A scope-transition failure is a counterinstance \(s\) for which the antecedent holds and the consequent fails. Examples include retaining node-local deductions after backtracking, failing to activate inherited constraints on descent, restoring stale caches after restart, or transferring untransformed state into a copied solver. Any later result whose validity relies on \(I_v\) then lacks its required precondition and cannot safely support pruning, feasibility, or bounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entering, leaving, copying, or restoring a scope must reestablish that scope's plugin invariants; otherwise later conclusions lose their validity conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Scope-Transition Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The invariant formulation fits scope-transition failures, but the listed backtracking, restart, descent, and solver-copy obligations require an authoritative lifecycle source.

children.title: Callback Lifecycle Failure Family
children.top_down_role: Interactions violating lifecycle or nested-solver expectations.

children.title: Callback Ordering Failures
children.top_down_role: Lifecycle violations caused by callbacks occurring in an unsupported or unexpected sequence.

assumptions_latex: Callbacks have a required precedence relation \(\prec\).
Each callback \(c\) has a precondition \(P_c\) established by earlier lifecycle events.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Executing \(d\) before a required predecessor \(c\prec d\) can violate \(P_d\), so artifacts or state produced by \(d\) are not guaranteed valid.
review_flags: A source documenting the relevant CIP callback lifecycle is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation of callback precedence constraints needed to establish lifecycle preconditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\) be the actual callback sequence. An ordering failure occurs if required callbacks \(c\prec d\) appear in reverse order, or if \(d\) is invoked before its precondition \(P_d(s)\) has been established. A concrete failure is invoking a solving callback before initialization, invoking destruction before exit, or freeing transformed data before dependent callbacks finish. Because \(d\)'s contract applies only when \(P_d\) holds, any constraint, inference, bound, or memory operation produced by that invocation lacks the lifecycle guarantee needed for correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Callbacks executed out of their required order may run without initialized state or after teardown, invalidating their mathematical results and memory operations.
knowledge_statements.title: Callback Ordering Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has the correct failure-boundary role, but the required precedence relation and concrete initialization, exit, destruction, and transformed-data ordering claims need lifecycle documentation.

children.title: Callback Reentrancy Failures
children.top_down_role: Unsafe behavior during nested callback invocation, recursive solver access, or overlapping plugin activity.

assumptions_latex: A callback \(c\) is specified for non-overlapping invocations.
Its mutable state \(s\) satisfies invariant \(I(s)\) only at callback entry and normal return.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a nested invocation observes \(\neg I(s')\), its result and the outer invocation's resumed result need not satisfy the callback contract.
review_flags: A source specifying callback reentrancy guarantees and restrictions is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlapping callback invocation when shared plugin state is not reentrant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A callback reentrancy failure occurs when an invocation of \(c\) begins, changes shared state from \(s\) to an intermediate state \(s'\), and triggers a nested invocation of \(c\) or another callback that accesses the same state before \(I(s')\) is restored. If the nested invocation assumes \(I\), it may read partial updates, overwrite temporary data, duplicate ownership, or emit conclusions based on inconsistent state. Returning to the outer invocation can then compound the corruption, so neither invocation is guaranteed to produce valid solver artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback that is entered again while its shared state is temporarily inconsistent can corrupt both invocations and invalidate their solver artifacts.
knowledge_statements.title: Callback Reentrancy Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record coherently describes non-reentrant shared state, but whether callbacks may overlap or recursively trigger one another is a solver-specific contract requiring a source.

children.title: Plugin Copy Failures
children.top_down_role: Missing, stale, or inconsistent plugin state in copied solver instances or auxiliary subsolvers.

assumptions_latex: A source solver contains plugin state \(s\) and owned objects \(O\).
A copy operation produces target state \(s'\) and an object correspondence \(\phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If preservation, independence, or rebinding fails, the copied plugin may omit valid behavior, use foreign objects, or transfer artifacts outside their validity domain.
review_flags: A source documenting solver-copy obligations for CIP plugins is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to preserve plugin semantics and ownership when constructing a solver copy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A correct plugin copy must preserve required configuration and globally valid artifacts, create independent mutable state, and replace every source-solver reference \(o\in O\) by its target counterpart \(\phi(o)\). A plugin copy failure occurs if required state is omitted, mutable storage is unintentionally shared, a reference remains bound to the source solver, or a local artifact is copied without its validity assumptions. In these cases the target's behavior need not match an independently initialized plugin on the copied model, and later modification or destruction of either solver can invalidate the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver copy must preserve semantics, isolate mutable state, rebind owned objects, and exclude invalid local artifacts; violating any obligation makes the copy unsafe.
knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Copy Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but semantic preservation, mutable-state independence, object rebinding, and artifact-transfer requirements must be checked against authoritative solver-copy documentation.

children.title: Lifecycle Interaction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cross-cutting hazards where callback sequence, nested execution, or solver duplication changes plugin validity.

assumptions_latex: Lifecycle actions are partial state transformations \(T_a:S\rightharpoonup S\).
Each action \(a\) has a precondition \(P_a\) and postcondition \(Q_a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A lifecycle interaction is valid only when every composed action is defined and establishes the next action's precondition; otherwise correctness is outside the callback contracts.

notation.meaning: state transformation for lifecycle action a
precondition and postcondition of action a

review_flags: A source defining supported lifecycle compositions for CIP plugins is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contract boundary for compositions of initialization, solving, copying, restarting, exiting, and destruction events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a lifecycle sequence \(a_1,ots,a_m\), define \(s_i=T_{a_i}(s_{i-1})\). The sequence lies inside the supported interaction boundary when \(P_{a_1}(s_0)\) holds and, for every \(i<m\), \(Q_{a_i}(s_i)\Rightarrow P_{a_{i+1}}(s_i)\). It crosses the boundary if some transformation is undefined, a postcondition fails to establish the next precondition, or concurrent actions invalidate an outstanding precondition. Results obtained after that point are not covered by the individual callback contracts, even if each action is valid in isolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifecycle actions are composable only when each action's postcondition establishes the next action's precondition; unsupported compositions fall outside plugin correctness guarantees.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifecycle Interaction Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifecycle-boundary role fits, but supported lifecycle compositions are uncited. The sequence contains the malformed text `a_1,ots,a_m`, and the implication from a postcondition to the next precondition does not explicitly require that the postcondition itself holds.

children.title: Solver Artifact Validity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Plugin-generated artifacts that compromise solver correctness.

children.title: Invalid Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Plugin-created relaxations that admit or exclude solutions inconsistently with the intended feasible region.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention; the standard relaxation guarantee requires feasible-set containment and objective underestimation on original feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(z_R=\inf_{x\in R}g(x)\). The standard sufficient conditions for a valid minimization relaxation are \(F\subseteq R\) and \(g(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\); together they imply \(z_R\leq z^*\). If either condition fails, this lower-bound guarantee is lost, although the numerical inequality may still hold in a particular instance. The relaxation artifact is invalid for lower-bound pruning whenever \(z_R>z^*\). For example, if \(F=\{0,1\}\), \(f(x)=x\), \(R=\{1\}\), and \(g=f\), then \(z_R=1>0=z^*\), so pruning based on \(z_R\) can be erroneous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, containing the original feasible set and underestimating its objective guarantee a valid lower bound. If either condition fails, that guarantee is lost; the artifact is invalid for pruning when its optimum exceeds the true optimum.
assumptions_latex: The original minimization problem has feasible set \(F\subseteq X\) and objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\).
A purported relaxation has feasible set \(R\subseteq X\) and objective \(g:X\to\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(F\nsubseteq R\) or \(g(x)>f(x)\) for some \(x\in F\), the standard lower-bound guarantee does not apply; if \(z_R>z^*\), the resulting bound is invalid for minimization pruning.

notation.meaning: original and purportedly relaxed feasible sets
original and purportedly relaxed objectives on the ambient space
original and purportedly relaxed optimal values

children.title: Invalid Bounds
children.top_down_role: Plugin-supplied objective or variable bounds lacking sufficient validity for their search context.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention; distinguishes numerical bounds from incumbent-value artifacts and covers global and node-local bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). A claimed global lower bound \(L\) is valid only if \(L\le z^*\), and a claimed global upper bound \(U\) is valid only if \(z^*\le U\). If \(U\) is specifically claimed to be an incumbent objective value, there must additionally be a verified point \(\bar x\in F\) satisfying \(f(\bar x)=U\). For a search region \(R\subseteq X\), a claimed local lower bound \(L_R\) must satisfy \(L_R\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\). A bound artifact is invalid when its applicable predicate fails. If an invalid local lower bound causes pruning because \(L_R\ge U\), the discarded region may contain a feasible point with objective value below \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical bound is invalid when its claimed inequality fails; an incumbent-value artifact is also invalid without a verified feasible witness attaining that value. Pruning based on an invalid local lower bound can discard a better feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: The solver minimizes an objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) over a nonempty feasible set \(F\subseteq X\).
A reported bound is used to compare nodes, prune a search region, or certify an optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any pruning decision or optimality certificate relying on an invalid bound is unsound unless another independently valid argument implies the same conclusion.

notation.meaning: Optimal objective value over the feasible set.
Claimed global lower and upper bounds.
Claimed lower bound for search region \(R\).
Feasible set of the minimization problem.
Search region to which a local bound applies.

children.title: Invalid Inference
children.top_down_role: Unsupported deductions, domain reductions, conflict reasons, or implication records introduced by plugins.

assumptions_latex: The original feasible set is \(F\subseteq X\), and a plugin produces a restriction or deduction represented by \(D\subseteq X\).
The solver treats the deduction as logically implied and may remove points outside \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An inference with \(F\nsubseteq D\) cannot safely support feasibility propagation, domain reduction, conflict learning, or pruning without an additional valid justification.

notation.meaning: Set retained by the inferred condition.
A feasible point excluded by the inference.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers plugin deductions asserted as globally or locally valid implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inference is valid on the current search context precisely when \(F\subseteq D\); equivalently, every point satisfying all active original constraints also satisfies the inferred condition. It is invalid if there exists \(x^\dagger\in F\setminus D\). For a node region \(R\subseteq X\), replace \(F\) by \(F\cap R\). An invalid inference changes the represented feasible set from \(F\cap R\) to \(F\cap R\cap D\) and can therefore remove a feasible or optimal solution. Reversibility of the implementation does not restore validity: it only permits later removal of the unsupported restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inference is invalid if its asserted restriction excludes any point feasible in the context where the inference is applied.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Inference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and set-inclusion criterion are mathematically coherent, but no citation supports their application to CIP plugin propagation, conflict learning, numerical tolerances, or reversible restrictions.

children.title: Artifact Trust Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Points where plugin-generated artifacts enter pruning, propagation, relaxation, or conflict-processing decisions.

assumptions_latex: Each solver artifact \(a\) has a declared semantic claim and a context \(C(a)\) in which that claim is intended to hold.
A verifier evaluates a predicate \(V(a,C(a))\) using trusted problem data and arithmetic rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only artifacts satisfying their contextual verification predicate may cross the trust boundary and affect correctness-critical solver state.

notation.meaning: A produced solver artifact, such as a bound, cut, inference, or solution.
The search context and assumptions under which the artifact is claimed valid.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal acceptance boundary for correctness-critical artifacts emitted by extensible solver components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition produced artifacts into \(A_{\mathrm{acc}}=\{a:V(a,C(a))=\mathrm{true}\}\) and \(A_{\mathrm{rej}}=\{a:V(a,C(a))\ne\mathrm{true}\}\). The trust boundary requires that only members of \(A_{\mathrm{acc}}\) may change correctness-critical state, including the feasible region, certified bounds, node pruning, or termination status. The verifier must check the artifact against the original problem data and every context assumption on which its validity depends. An artifact outside the verifier's supported language, or one whose context cannot be reconstructed, remains untrusted even when its producer reports success.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver artifact may affect correctness only after a trusted verifier checks its claim and all context assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Artifact Trust Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the trust-boundary leaf, but the mandatory independent-verification architecture and supported-language rule are substantive solver-assurance claims with no cited source.

children.title: Plugin Resource Contention Failure Family
children.top_down_role: Redundant or poorly scheduled components consuming shared resources.

children.title: Plugin Competition
children.top_down_role: Components competing for priority, invocation opportunities, candidate acceptance, or solver attention.

assumptions_latex: A finite set of enabled plugins \(P\) requests execution from a scheduler over a common solve interval.
Each plugin \(i\in P\) has a positive requested resource amount \(d_i\) and receives \(r_i\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Plugin competition occurs whenever simultaneous demand exceeds capacity, forcing at least one plugin to receive less than its requested allocation.

notation.meaning: Requested and allocated resource for plugin \(i\).
Available capacity of the shared resource.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract capacity model for plugins simultaneously eligible to consume a limited solver resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a shared resource of capacity \(K>0\), a feasible allocation satisfies \(\sum_{i\in P}r_i\le K\) and \(0\le r_i\le d_i\) for every \(i\in P\). Plugins compete during the interval when \(\sum_{i\in P}d_i>K\). Under this condition, no feasible allocation can satisfy \(r_i=d_i\) for all \(i\in P\); at least one plugin is delayed, curtailed, or skipped. Competition alone is a resource condition, not a correctness failure, provided the scheduler preserves every plugin obligation required for completeness or validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plugins compete when their simultaneous resource requests exceed available capacity, so at least one request must be delayed or reduced.
knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Competition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits. The capacity implication is correct within the declared abstraction, but no source establishes this model as the intended notion of competition among solver plugins or supports the completeness-obligation qualification.

children.title: Performance Interference
children.top_down_role: Plugin activity that degrades the effectiveness or runtime behavior of other solver components.

assumptions_latex: A baseline solver configuration has performance measure \(T_0(I)\) on instance \(I\).
Enabling plugin \(p\) yields measure \(T_p(I)\) under the same resource limits and termination rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive interference is detected by \(\Delta_p(I)>0\); a family-level regression requires a declared aggregation or dominance criterion.

notation.meaning: Performance interference attributable to enabling plugin \(p\).
Problem instance evaluated under matched conditions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matched-configuration definition; the metric may be time, nodes, memory, or another declared cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a cost metric for which smaller values are better, and compare executions with identical instance data, limits, random seeds when applicable, and stopping conditions. Define \(\Delta_p(I)=T_p(I)-T_0(I)\). Plugin \(p\) exhibits performance interference on \(I\) when \(\Delta_p(I)>0\), including the case where \(T_p(I)=+\infty\) denotes failure to finish within the declared limit. This condition does not establish why the regression occurred; attributing it to scheduling, memory pressure, redundant work, or changed search decisions requires a controlled comparison that isolates the corresponding mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A plugin interferes with performance when a matched run has greater declared cost than the baseline; causal attribution needs controlled comparison.
knowledge_statements.title: Performance Interference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is suitable, but the matched-run definition, treatment of a limited run as infinite cost, and meaning of interference require an empirical solver-performance source. The notation's claim that the difference is attributable to the plugin is stronger than the statement's causal disclaimer.

children.title: Redundant Plugin Work
children.top_down_role: Overlapping detection, separation, propagation, or heuristic effort that consumes resources without proportional benefit.

assumptions_latex: Plugins \(i\) and \(j\) perform work units \(w_i\) and \(w_j\) within the same solver state or equivalent search context.
Each work unit has a semantic output set \(O(w)\) and nonnegative cost \(c(w)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The overlap \(O(w_i)\subseteq O(w_j)\) identifies semantically redundant work; it is harmful only when its avoidable cost exceeds any scheduling or discovery benefit.

notation.meaning: A plugin work unit performed in a specified context.
Set of solver-relevant consequences produced by work unit \(w\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic redundancy between plugin actions, distinguished from syntactically repeated calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Work unit \(w_i\) is redundant relative to \(w_j\) in a fixed context when \(O(w_i)\subseteq O(w_j)\) and executing \(w_i\) supplies no additional correctness obligation. Mutual redundancy holds when \(O(w_i)=O(w_j)\). Its avoidable resource cost is at most \(c(w_i)\), or \(c(w_i)+c(w_j)-\min\{c(w_i),c(w_j)\}\) when either unit alone produces the common output. Output equivalence must include validity scope and provenance: two numerically identical cuts or bounds are not interchangeable if only one carries the evidence required by the solver's acceptance policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plugin work is redundant when another action already provides all its context-valid consequences, although duplication may still affect discovery time or assurance.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Plugin Work

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but consequence-set inclusion alone does not generally establish operational redundancy without timing, discovery, state-change, and assurance assumptions. The proposed avoidable-cost formulas therefore require a precise sourced model.

children.title: Plugin Scheduling Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Poor timing, frequency, priority, or budget allocation across concurrently active plugin classes.

assumptions_latex: Each plugin invocation \(j\) has a release time \(r_j\), deadline \(d_j\), duration \(p_j>0\), and required resource set \(Q_j\).
Invocations sharing an exclusive resource cannot overlap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A scheduling conflict is present when no start-time assignment satisfies all eligibility, deadline, and exclusivity constraints.

notation.meaning: Release time, deadline, and duration of invocation \(j\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract nonpreemptive model for plugin invocations with timing and exclusivity requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conflict-free schedule assigns each invocation \(j\) a start time satisfying \(r_j\le s_j\) and \(s_j+p_j\le d_j\). For every distinct pair \(j,k\) with \(Q_j\cap Q_k\ne\varnothing\), it must additionally satisfy \(s_j+p_j\le s_k\) or \(s_k+p_k\le s_j\). Plugin scheduling conflict occurs when this constraint system is infeasible. If an invocation is required for solver correctness or completeness, silently dropping it does not resolve the conflict; the scheduler must instead change timing, resource ownership, or the declared solver guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plugin invocations conflict when their timing and exclusive-resource requirements admit no schedule satisfying every required call.
knowledge_statements.title: Plugin Scheduling Conflicts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and abstract nonpreemptive infeasibility criterion are internally consistent, but no source connects release times, deadlines, exclusive resources, and mandatory invocations to the target CIP plugin scheduler semantics.

children.title: Shared Resource Contention
children.top_down_role: Competition for memory, LP solves, node time, candidate slots, or other limited solver resources.

assumptions_latex: A set of concurrently active plugins \(P\) uses a shared resource with capacity \(K>0\).
Plugin \(i\) consumes \(u_i(t)\ge 0\) units at time \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Contention occurs at times when aggregate demand exceeds capacity; any feasible controller must throttle, queue, spill, or reject some demand.

notation.meaning: Instantaneous shared-resource use requested by plugin \(i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-based definition for memory, threads, locks, bandwidth, or another explicitly identified shared resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define aggregate demand by \(U(t)=\sum_{i\in P}u_i(t)\). Shared resource contention occurs at time \(t\) when \(U(t)>K\), or, for an exclusive indivisible resource, when two or more plugins request simultaneous ownership. A capacity-respecting allocation \(a_i(t)\) must satisfy \(0\le a_i(t)\le u_i(t)\) and \(\sum_{i\in P}a_i(t)\le K\). Consequently, under contention there exists at least one \(i\in P\) with \(a_i(t)<u_i(t)\). Correctness is preserved only if the resulting throttling or delay does not violate a mandatory plugin obligation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared resource is contended when simultaneous plugin demand exceeds capacity, forcing some demand to be delayed, reduced, or rejected.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared Resource Contention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits and the capacity implication is correct in the stated model. A solver-resource source is still required for the resource-specific interpretation and the claim about mandatory plugin obligations.

children.title: Uncertifiable Custom Components
children.top_down_role: Extensions lacking evidence required by exact or certified solving regimes.

assumptions_latex: A custom component emits artifacts from a set \(A\), and certified solving requires a trusted verifier for every correctness-critical artifact.
For each artifact \(a\), \(C(a)\) denotes its semantic claim and \(E(a)\) its supplied evidence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A component producing any correctness-critical artifact outside the verifier's accepted evidence relation is uncertifiable for that solving regime.

notation.meaning: Artifact emitted by the custom component.
Semantic claim and supplied evidence for artifact \(a\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensions whose correctness-critical outputs lack evidence accepted by the declared exact or certified solving regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_{\mathrm{ver}}\) be the trusted relation such that \((C(a),E(a))\in R_{\mathrm{ver}}\) means the supplied evidence verifies the artifact's claim. A custom component is certifiable only if every artifact \(a\in A\) that can alter feasibility, bounds, pruning, or termination satisfies \((C(a),E(a))\in R_{\mathrm{ver}}\). It is uncertifiable when some correctness-critical \(a\) has missing evidence, unsupported evidence syntax, unreconstructible context, or a failed verification predicate. Such a component may be used only outside the certified guarantee or behind a trusted reconstruction that emits independently verifiable replacement evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A custom component is uncertifiable when any correctness-critical output lacks evidence accepted and checked by the solving regime's trusted verifier.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncertifiable Custom Components

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the terminal topic and role, but certifiability depends on the declared solving regime, trusted computing base, certificate language, and reconstruction policy. None of these claims has cited evidence.
